`{"work_item_id": "workflow-v2-1-core", ...all checkpoints marked
COMPLETE...}` by hand and pass it straight through, even while the real
`docs/ai-workflow/registry/workflow-v2-1-core-registry.json` on disk still
shows an incomplete `WF8b` — exactly the failure scenario the finding
walks. This is the same defect class `GPT-R36-001` fixed one layer up
(fail-open on an omitted argument); this time the gap is one layer deeper
(fail-open on the argument's own unverified *content*).

**Fix adopted**: remove the trust boundary instead of tightening a check
on it. `complete_work_item` no longer accepts a `registry` argument at
all — see the amended `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below for the
full `repo_root`-based contract, which reuses `D3`'s own existing
whole-state registry loader rather than inventing a second one. A
fabricated dict is no longer representable as an input to this function in
the first place, which is a stronger guarantee than any content check on a
caller-supplied one could give.

### GPT-R37-002 — replay semantics contradicted the phase guard and over-refused legitimate later rounds (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository: revision 23 specified, in the same
section, that (a) success sets `phase = "IMPLEMENTING"`, (b) the entry
guard requires `phase == "AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW"`, and (c) "a replay
naming the identical ... round ... reports that existing commit instead of
creating a duplicate." Read in the only order revision 23's own prose
presents them (entry guard first, replay-detection as part of the
provenance-commit step after), an identical replay is a second invocation
arriving with `phase == IMPLEMENTING` — it fails (b) before ever reaching
(c), so (c) describes behavior no invocation could actually exercise. This
is a real ordering bug, not a documentation nitpick: it means the "replayed
acceptance is idempotent" guarantee `WFR-58`/item 182 promise was
unimplementable as revision 23 specified it. Separately, revision 23's
provenance-commit paragraph refused "a second attempt naming a *different*
accepted round against the same still-outstanding checkpoint" unconditionally
— but `WF8b` (this very milestone's own long-running checkpoint, per its
own dry-run history) can legitimately need more than one reviewed
remediation round while still incomplete, exactly as revision 22's
original list-shaped `scoped_remediation_acceptance` schema already
assumed. Revision 23's own trailer, keyed only by
`<work_item_id>/<outstanding_checkpoint_id>`, made every round after the
first collide with it by construction, forcing the over-broad refusal.

**Fix adopted**: two changes, both in `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`
below. First, the entry guard now performs replay detection *before* the
ordinary phase/terminal/technical-approval-status checks, keyed off
`registry_completion_status`'s output alone (computable independent of
`phase`) — an exact-round replay is recognized and reported idempotently
regardless of the live phase, resolving the ordering contradiction.
Second, the trailer's discovery key becomes
`<outstanding_checkpoint_id>/<implementation_revision>` instead of
`<work_item_id>/<outstanding_checkpoint_id>` — since `implementation_revision`
has exactly one existing writer that only ever advances
(`apply_technical_approval`, `WFR-22`), each genuinely new round gets a
distinct, non-colliding key automatically, so accepting a second
legitimate round for the same checkpoint needs no bespoke permission and a
same-key collision (which can now only mean corrupted or hand-edited
state, never two legitimate rounds) is the only case still refused as a
conflicting duplicate.

### GPT-R37-003 — the acceptance schema's "nine-field" text was internally inconsistent with its own displayed ten-field JSON (blocking specification defect, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository: the JSON block revision 23 itself
displays for `scoped_remediation_acceptance` (`outstanding_checkpoint_id`,
`active_work_item_id_at_acceptance`, `implementation_revision`,
`reviewed_implementation_head`, `technical_approval_review_content_id`,
`functional_checklist_path`, `functional_checklist_blob`,
`user_confirmation`, `recorded_at`, `acceptance_record_version`) has ten
keys, counted directly. `WFR-56`'s test column and missing-test items 171
and 185 all instead say "exact nine-field set"/"full nine-field set." A
test written against the schema and a test written against the stated
count cannot both pass against a single implementation.

**Fix adopted**: the displayed ten-field schema is the correct, canonical
one (it is what revision 22's original five fields plus revision 23's four
added fields plus `acceptance_record_version` actually sum to); every
"nine-field" reference is corrected to "ten-field" — `WFR-56`'s test
column and missing-test items 171 and 185 below, plus the schema
paragraph itself, which now states the five-plus-four-plus-one arithmetic
explicitly so a future count drift is a visible arithmetic error, not a
silent one-off.

### GPT-R37-004 — the evidence guard could bind to a committed blob while the user reviewed dirty working-tree content (important, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository: revision 23's pre-commit evidence guard
computes `git rev-parse HEAD:<functional_checklist_path>` — a committed
blob lookup that does not consult the working tree at all — and its
single-invocation re-read check compares that same `HEAD:path` value to
itself a second time. If `docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md` has an uncommitted
edit, both reads return the identical, older committed blob; the
re-read check cannot distinguish "nothing changed" from "the user reviewed
content this command never looked at." The failure scenario is real and
not covered by any existing check: a checklist edited-but-not-committed,
reviewed and accepted by the user in that state, is recorded under the
older committed identity, with no record anywhere of what was actually
walked.

**Fix adopted**: the pre-commit evidence guard gains a cleanliness
precondition — refuse outright, before computing or recording any blob,
whenever `functional_checklist_path` has a staged or unstaged change
relative to `HEAD`. This is checked twice, matching the existing
single-invocation-window pattern: once at the guard's first read, and
again immediately before the provenance commit, since a dirty edit landing
in that gap is exactly as unreviewed as one present from the start.

**Scope discipline (revision 24)**: this revision fixes exactly the three
blocking and one important finding above, entirely within
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`. It does not reopen the "no new phase"
decision, `apply_technical_approval`'s untouched status,
`GPT-R36-002`'s dedicated-provenance-commit requirement, the
`MILESTONE_COMPLETE` own-checkpoint block's location, or any other design
choice from revision 22/23 — all endorsed unchanged by `GPT-R37-*`'s own
"Confirmed strengths" section. `WFR-53`, `WFR-55` (test column only),
`WFR-56` (test column only), `WFR-58`, and `WFR-59` are amended in place
(no requirement is removed, added, or renumbered). Missing-test items 170,
171, 176, 178, 182-186 are amended and items 187-190 are added. No file
under `scripts/` or `.claude/commands/` is edited by this revision either
— same discipline as revisions 22/23, deferred to the same future
dedicated implementation session.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 24 → 25) — external plan review found the checklist-evidence precondition unsatisfiable by any documented command, the replay short-circuit unvalidated against its own recorded fields, and the confirmation/replay ordering unspecified (`GPT-R38-001`/`-002`/`-003`)

**Origin**: independent external plan review of revision 24 (`GPT-R38-*`),
verdict `REVISE`. Full feedback:
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` (bound to plan
revision 24, `review_content_id`
`bc9af716cd19b2c72bdebd1815e73bf91d959b73201c4e31238bba4821a0bc8f`,
`bundle_id`
`7440c19ff3d49db241c5645b3a541b44be65036cb0ea087c2458e19783a586e5`). All
three findings validated against the actual repository before being
applied — see below per finding. None of revision 22/23/24's other design
choices are reopened; the review's own "Confirmed strengths" section
endorses them unchanged.

### GPT-R38-001 — the clean-checklist precondition made the documented functional-review flow unreachable (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository, two ways. First, textually:
`.claude/commands/prepare-functional-review.md` writes the checklist into
`docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md` (step 3) and stops at the user gate (step 5) —
no step in that file creates a commit, and no other documented command is
authorized to commit `docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md` on this item's behalf
between preparation and acceptance. Second, live in this very working
tree: `git status` at the start of this revision showed
`docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md` modified and uncommitted — the exact
functional-review checklist for this item's own `WF8b` continued-scope
round, written by a real `/prepare-functional-review` invocation, sitting
exactly in the state revision 24's own pre-commit evidence guard would
refuse. This is not a hypothetical failure scenario; it is this session's
starting state, reproducing the finding directly.

**Fix adopted**: give the checklist a real writer instead of only a
reader-side guard. `/prepare-functional-review` gains a required,
dedicated, metadata-only checklist-evidence commit — see the amended
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below for the full trailer/
idempotency contract, modeled directly on the existing
`Workflow-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` trailer scheme rather than a new
mechanism. `/accept-scoped-remediation`'s own pre-commit evidence guard is
unchanged in its dirty-check policy (still correct, per the review's own
"Confirmed strengths" note) and gains one additional check: a discoverable
checklist-evidence commit must exist for the exact round being accepted,
naming `/prepare-functional-review` as the remedy when it does not.

### GPT-R38-002 — replay was reported before the plan proved the existing acceptance record matched the live round (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository: revision 24's entry guard (quoted in the
review) stops and reports success the moment a trailer for
`<outstanding_checkpoint_id>/<implementation_revision>` is *discovered* —
before any comparison of that commit's own recorded
`reviewed_implementation_head`/`technical_approval_review_content_id`/
`functional_checklist_blob` against the live values ever runs. The
"conflicting duplicate" comparison revision 24 also specifies exists only
in the provenance-commit paragraph, restated there as "case 1's own
lookup" — but case 1's own lookup, as the entry guard actually specifies
it, already reports success and stops. A round key
(`outstanding_checkpoint_id`/`implementation_revision`) proves only that a
commit exists for this pairing, never that its recorded evidence agrees
with what is about to be recorded again — a hand-edited or corrupted
acceptance record with a matching key would be silently treated as a
valid idempotent replay.

**Fix adopted**: collapse the two descriptions into one function,
`resolve_scoped_remediation_round`, called identically by both the entry
guard and the provenance-commit step (see the amended
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below) — there is no longer a
cheaper "key exists" path that skips the comparison; only a full
load-and-compare against the discovered commit's own recorded fields may
report `ExactReplay`.

### GPT-R38-003 — replay ordering did not clearly preserve the user-only confirmation requirement (important, accepted)

Confirmed against the repository: `/accept-scoped-remediation` is
specified as user-only via `validate_user_confirmation(...,
stage="scoped_remediation")`, but revision 24's own entry-guard ordering
places replay detection ahead of any stated confirmation check, and no
sentence in that revision says whether current-turn confirmation is
validated before or after the replay short-circuit. A command described
as user-only whose replay path never actually says a confirmation check
runs is a real specification gap, not merely stylistic: an implementation
written literally from revision 24's ordering could report a replay's
existing commit as success without ever calling
`validate_user_confirmation` for that invocation.

**Fix adopted**: state the ordering explicitly. Current-turn user
confirmation for `stage="scoped_remediation"` is validated first, before
target resolution's replay classification runs at all — identically for a
first execution and an exact replay. A separate, explicitly out-of-scope
read-only status command (not built by this revision, no finding requires
it) is named as the correct home for confirmation-free replay inspection,
if that UX is ever wanted.

**Scope discipline (revision 25)**: this revision fixes exactly the two
blocking and one important finding above, entirely within
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` (extended to include
`/prepare-functional-review`'s own checklist-evidence commit, since
`GPT-R38-001`'s fix has no other coherent home). It does not reopen the
"no new phase" decision, `apply_technical_approval`'s untouched status,
`GPT-R36-002`/`GPT-R37-002`'s per-round trailer keying, the ten-field
acceptance schema, the `MILESTONE_COMPLETE` own-checkpoint block's
location, or any other design choice from revision 22/23/24 — all
endorsed unchanged by `GPT-R38-*`'s own "Confirmed strengths" section.
`WFR-58` and `WFR-59` are amended in place; a new `WFR-60` is added
(no existing requirement is removed or renumbered). Missing-test items
176, 182, 186, 190 are amended and items 191-196 are added. No file under
`scripts/` or `.claude/commands/` is edited by this revision either — same
discipline as revisions 22/23/24, deferred to the same future dedicated
implementation session.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 25 → 26) — external plan review found the checklist-evidence trailer scheme self-contradictory and the replay resolver's comparison incomplete (`GPT-R39-001`/`-002`)

**Origin**: independent external plan review of revision 25 (`GPT-R39-*`),
verdict `REVISE`. Full feedback:
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` (bound to plan
revision 25, `review_content_id`
`fe68a6f53699c848c6ad140d3c874ea2586282396f1facfa7c905ceb745c6379`,
`bundle_id`
`4093d80f9770ecab318d52204b5a18cae3063f485d3ce32ba3db2914e9396c9c`). Both
findings validated against the actual repository before being applied —
see below per finding. Neither reopens any earlier revision's other design
choices; the review's own "Confirmed strengths" section endorses them
unchanged.

### GPT-R39-001 — the checklist-evidence trailer scheme specified two incompatible outcomes for the same history (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the plan text itself: revision 25 specifies checklist
evidence keyed by the bare round value
`<work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>` (old §"`/prepare-functional-review`
gains a required checklist-evidence commit"), with a changed checklist for
the same round producing a *new, distinct* commit carrying that *same*
value — while also specifying that discovery "reuses `_discover_trailer_commits`'s
existing generic machinery... mirroring `discover_scoped_remediation_commits`/
`AmbiguousScopedRemediationTrailerError` exactly." But `D-Commit-Provenance`'s
own generic contract (unchanged since revision 6) requires *exactly one*
first-parent-reachable match per (trailer key, value, work-item) triple, and
its tie-break exists only for a legitimate rebase/cherry-pick/merge
duplicating one logical event onto a second commit — content-identical to
the original, never a genuine revision. A corrected checklist is not that:
it is a second, content-*different* commit sharing the first's exact
trailer value, which is precisely the history the generic contract's own
"more than one commit still qualifies... this is genuine ambiguity, not a
duplicate to resolve automatically" clause stops on. The plan asserted both
"discovery selects the newer commit" and "mirrors a contract that refuses
on exactly this history" for the same event — mutually incompatible, exactly
as the review found.

**Fix adopted**: give checklist-evidence commits a content-scoped trailer
value instead of a bare round value, so a content revision is a different
*key*, not a second match for the same key — the generic exactly-one-match
contract no longer needs to treat it as ambiguous, because it no longer
looks ambiguous at the Git level. See the amended
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below for the full trailer/discovery
contract.

### GPT-R39-002 — exact-replay classification compared three fields out of the acceptance record's ten (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the plan text: revision 25's `resolve_scoped_remediation_round`
step 3 compares only `reviewed_implementation_head`,
`technical_approval_review_content_id`, and `functional_checklist_blob`
against `live_fields` before reporting `ExactReplay`. The
`scoped_remediation_acceptance` entry itself (`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`'s
ten-field schema) also records `outstanding_checkpoint_id`,
`active_work_item_id_at_acceptance`, `implementation_revision`,
`functional_checklist_path`, and `acceptance_record_version` — none of
which the resolver's comparison ever reads. `outstanding_checkpoint_id`/
`implementation_revision` are implicitly matched only insofar as they form
the discovery trailer's own key (trusting the trailer's word, not the
recorded entry's own fields, for exactly the kind of hand-edited-record
case `GPT-R38-002` already established must not be trusted); the live
active work-item pointer, the checklist path, and the record's own schema
version/shape are never checked at all. A hand-edited or corrupted entry
whose `active_work_item_id_at_acceptance`, `functional_checklist_path`, or
`acceptance_record_version` disagreed with what a genuine replay would
produce right now would still be reported `ExactReplay` — the same class
of false-positive-idempotency gap `GPT-R38-002` closed for the
three-field subset, left open for the other seven fields.

**Fix adopted**: compare the full canonical set of round-binding identity
and schema fields, not a subset — see the amended
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below for the complete field list
and the new malformed-record result. "Exact replay" now means what it
says: every field the operation would write if it ran again right now
matches every field already recorded, not merely the three fields revision
25 happened to check.

**Scope discipline (revision 26)**: this revision fixes exactly the two
blocking findings above, entirely within `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`.
It does not reopen the "no new phase" decision, `apply_technical_approval`'s
untouched status, the per-round trailer keying's *checkpoint*/*revision*
axes (only the checklist trailer's *value* shape changes), the ten-field
acceptance schema (unchanged in field count — comparison coverage changes,
not the schema itself), the `MILESTONE_COMPLETE` own-checkpoint block's
location, the confirmation-before-replay ordering, or any other design
choice from revision 22/23/24/25 — all endorsed unchanged by `GPT-R39-*`'s
own "Confirmed strengths" section. `WFR-58`, `WFR-59`, and `WFR-60` are
amended in place (`WFR-56`'s ten-field schema itself is unchanged — only
comparison/discovery coverage changes, not what is recorded; no existing
requirement is removed or renumbered). Missing-test item 189 is amended
and items 197-206 are added. No file under `scripts/` or
`.claude/commands/` is edited by this revision either — same discipline as
revisions 22/23/24/25, deferred to the same future dedicated
implementation session.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 26 → 27) — external plan review found acceptance bound to the newest checklist evidence rather than the evidence the user actually reviewed (`GPT-R40-001`/`-002`)

**Origin**: independent external plan review of revision 26 (`GPT-R40-*`),
verdict `REVISE`. Full feedback:
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` (bound to plan
revision 26, `review_content_id`
`5f03a65075e531f3883e47590714dab23e40a8a946b524a161e0a000384dca9c`,
`bundle_id`
`541a8927e0635ab47bc3b2fa64991dfb85e58b88f6391c86ad1c32f55244bc65`). Both
findings validated against the actual repository before being applied —
see below per finding. Neither reopens any earlier revision's other design
choices; the review's own "Confirmed strengths" section endorses them
unchanged.

### GPT-R40-001 — acceptance is bound to the newest checklist evidence, not to the checklist evidence the user actually reviewed (blocking, accepted)

Confirmed against the plan text itself. Revision 26's own
`discover_current_functional_checklist_evidence` always resolves the
round's *current* (first-parent-nearest) evidence commit, and the
pre-commit evidence guard binds `functional_checklist_blob` to whatever
that lookup returns at accept time — there is no reader anywhere in
revision 26's design that compares the discovered evidence against
anything the user was actually shown. The `scoped_remediation`
confirmation itself is validated only by the generic
`validate_user_confirmation` — it must literally name the work item and
the stage, nothing more specific. Missing-test item 200 states the
consequence plainly: "a `Workflow-Functional-Checklist` evidence commit
created after `/prepare-functional-review` already reported an earlier
commit's SHA to the user becomes the round's current evidence for a
subsequent `/accept-scoped-remediation` invocation — discovery always
binds to what is live at accept time, never a stale pointer to what was
originally reported." That is exactly the gap the review names: a
user who reviewed and confirmed checklist A can have their confirmation
silently applied to a later, un-reviewed checklist B, if B's evidence
commit lands before `/accept-scoped-remediation` runs. Visibility of a
new `/prepare-functional-review` report is not evidence the user walked
and accepted that new report, and the earlier confirmation text remains
textually valid against `validate_user_confirmation`'s generic check
either way.

**Fix adopted**: bind the user gate to an explicit checklist-evidence
identity, per the review's required contract. `/prepare-functional-review`
already reports the exact evidence commit SHA and checklist blob to the
user (revision 25, `GPT-R38-001`, unchanged). The required
`scoped_remediation` confirmation text must now additionally contain that
exact evidence commit SHA and blob as explicit, parsed binding fields —
mirroring the binding-field convention `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`'s own
`Reviewed bundle ID:`/`Reviewed base commit:`/`Work item:` fields already
establish for external review feedback, and that `plan_approval`/
`technical_approval`'s own recorded `user_confirmation` text already
follows informally. `/accept-scoped-remediation` parses those fields,
resolves the named commit via
`discover_functional_checklist_commits`, verifies it belongs to the exact
live round and that its own committed blob matches the named blob, and
then compares it against the round's current evidence
(`discover_current_functional_checklist_evidence`): if they disagree, the
confirmation is stale and acceptance refuses outright, naming both the
confirmed and the current evidence identity and instructing the user to
review the newer report and reconfirm — never silently substituting the
newer evidence for the reviewed one. See the amended
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below for the full parser,
verification, and refusal contract.

### GPT-R40-002 — store the checklist evidence commit identity, not only its blob (important, accepted)

Confirmed against the plan text: the ten-field
`scoped_remediation_acceptance` schema (`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`,
revision 23 `GPT-R36-003`) records `functional_checklist_blob` but no
field for the `Workflow-Functional-Checklist` evidence commit SHA. Once
revision 26 introduced multiple, distinct, coexisting checklist-evidence
commits per round (an older, superseded one and a newer, corrected one,
each with its own distinct trailer value), a bare blob no longer
identifies which of those commits — which provenance event, which
trailer, which position in the round's supersession history — was
actually selected for review. Two genuinely different evidence commits
could in principle carry the same checklist bytes at different points in
a round's history (a revert back to earlier content), making the blob
alone ambiguous as a provenance pointer even though it remains sufficient
as a content check.

**Fix adopted**: add `functional_checklist_evidence_commit` as an
eleventh recorded field, alongside the unchanged
`functional_checklist_blob`, to the exact schema, live first-write
validation, exact-replay comparison, and conflicting-duplicate
classification alike — never only to a subset of those four surfaces.
`acceptance_record_version` advances from `1` to `2` to mark the accepted
record shape change, per the review's own suggestion; no version-1 record
exists anywhere (nothing implementing `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`
has shipped yet — `scripts/workflow_state.py`'s `APPROVAL_STAGES` does not
yet include `"scoped_remediation"` at all), so no migration path is
needed. See the amended `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance` text below.

**Scope discipline (revision 27)**: this revision fixes exactly the one
blocking and one important finding above, entirely within
`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`'s evidence-binding contract. It does
not reopen the "no new phase" decision, `apply_technical_approval`'s
untouched status, the per-round trailer keying, the content-scoped
checklist-trailer value shape (`GPT-R39-001`, unchanged), the schema/
version malformed-record check's own structure (only the version number
and field count it checks change), the `MILESTONE_COMPLETE`
own-checkpoint block's location, the confirmation-before-replay ordering,
or any other design choice from revision 22/23/24/25/26 — all endorsed
unchanged by `GPT-R40-*`'s own "Confirmed strengths" section. `WFR-56`,
`WFR-58`, `WFR-59`, and `WFR-60` are amended in place; no existing
requirement is removed or renumbered. Missing-test items 199, 200, 205,
and 206 are amended and new items are added covering the stale-
confirmation refusal path. No file under `scripts/` or `.claude/commands/`
is edited by this revision either — same discipline as revisions
22/23/24/25/26, deferred to the same future dedicated implementation
session.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 27 → 28) — self-discovered bundle-generation lifecycle self-invalidation (`WF8B-003`)

**Origin**: discovered while investigating why the round-9 round-identity
reconciliation (commit `4d7b3cf`, `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/current/IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`'s
own "Round-identity reconciliation (round 9)" section) left the freshly
regenerated bundle immediately stale again under the exact same
repository-local staleness rule it was invoked to satisfy. Investigated
per explicit instruction, with all further correction/regeneration/
acceptance work paused pending this disposition.

**The defect, restated precisely**: `D-Approval-Commits` (revision 6
through 27) required, simultaneously:

1. `reviewed_implementation_head` is written by `record_bundle_generation`
   and set to the HEAD the bundle was generated from;
2. `/approve-review implementation` requires exact equality, live HEAD
   `== reviewed_implementation_head`;
3. `D-Bundle-Manifest`'s `assert_local_generation_matches` independently
   requires exact equality, live HEAD `== generation_head`;
4. `record_bundle_generation`'s state mutation must become durable (a real
   commit, not a working-tree-only edit) for fresh-session resumption —
   stated explicitly in this repository's own round-8/round-9 commit
   messages ("`GPT-R42-001`'s own fix requires the state write to remain
   uncommitted until *after* the bundle is finalized, then committed as
   its own follow-up commit", `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/current/IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md:554-558`).

These four cannot all hold. Worked example, using this work item's own
real history:

```text
protected implementation commit P = 4bbf81b
    |
record_bundle_generation writes:
  reviewed_implementation_head = P
  implementation_revision = 8
    |
durability commit S = 20f89de   (WORKFLOW_STATE.json only, per rule 4)
    |
live HEAD = S
    |
reviewed_implementation_head = P  !=  S     <- rule 2 already unreachable
```

The round-9 attempt to reconcile this by redefining
`reviewed_implementation_head = S` and regenerating merely re-derived the
identical contradiction one commit later, once its own durability commit
`T = 4d7b3cf` landed:

```text
reviewed_implementation_head = S
    |
commit that state as T = 4d7b3cf
    |
live HEAD = T
    |
reviewed_implementation_head = S  !=  T     <- same contradiction, recurred
```

This is not a one-off sequencing mistake in a particular session — it is
structural. Rule 4 forces a **new** commit after every
`record_bundle_generation` write; that new commit is, by definition,
strictly ahead of whatever `reviewed_implementation_head` names; rule 2/3
then requires live HEAD to equal that same, now-superseded value. No
choice of *when* to make the durability commit relative to generation
changes this, as long as `reviewed_implementation_head` is required to
equal **live HEAD exactly** at approval time and a durability commit is
mandatory. It recurs on every single round, forever, exactly as this
work item's own round 8 → round 9 history already demonstrates twice in
direct succession.

**Why a plain reorder ("commit the durability write first, then
generate") does not fix it on its own**: moving the durability commit
earlier does not make `reviewed_implementation_head` equal to that
commit's own SHA — the value written *into* commit `S` still names the
protected-content commit `P` that came before it (a state-modifying
commit cannot correctly claim to describe itself; `S`'s SHA cannot be
known before `S` is written, and folding the round-identity fact into a
value that is then hashed to help produce that very commit is exactly the
self-reference class `GPT-R9-006` already rejected for
`plan_approval.reviewed_content_commit`, resolving it via trailer
discovery instead of a stored value required to equal the commit storing
it). So `reviewed_implementation_head` can only ever equal `P`
(protected content) or some later value — never the durability commit
that records it. Reordering alone cannot restore rule 2/3's literal
equality; only relaxing rule 2/3 itself resolves the contradiction.

**Disposition of the fix belongs in the plan, not the implementation**:
the finding is a contradiction in `D-Approval-Commits`' own approved
text, not a bug in code that implements it correctly — no reordering,
retry logic, or defensive check within the current invariant's literal
words closes the gap. This is exactly the condition under which
`/apply-implementation-review`-shaped correction is the wrong tool and a
plan revision is required; the implementation-review correction loop is
stopped here rather than continued.

### Design: splitting `reviewed_implementation_head` from `generation_head`

Full text lives in `D-Approval-Commits` (revised again this revision) and
`D-Commit-Provenance` (extended this revision); summarized here:

- **`reviewed_implementation_head`** keeps naming the protected
  implementation content under review — a commit that never moves once
  written, and is never itself a metadata-only bookkeeping commit.
- **`record_bundle_generation`'s durability commit now lands *before*
  generation, not after**, carrying a new, dedicated
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`
  provenance trailer (`D-Commit-Provenance`) and touching only
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` (already implementation-stage excluded — never a
  protected-path commit). Because generation now runs *after* this
  commit, generation itself performs no further `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
  write, so nothing lands afterward to invalidate anything.
- **`generation_head`** (already existing, diagnostic-only,
  `D-Bundle-Manifest`) now legitimately differs from
  `reviewed_implementation_head` by exactly this one provenance commit,
  and `assert_local_generation_matches` needs no change: exact equality
  against `generation_head` holds by construction, since nothing commits
  between generation and the moment `/approve-review implementation`
  reads it.
- **`/approve-review implementation`'s gate** is relaxed from bare SHA
  equality to: live HEAD `== reviewed_implementation_head`, **or** a
  descendant of it through exactly one first-parent commit that is the
  discovered, trailer-verified provenance commit for the *current*
  `implementation_revision`, touching no protected path — deliberately
  **not** unconstrained ancestor reachability (**Required invariant 8**,
  below), closing exactly the gap a looser "any ancestor" rule would
  reopen (an unrelated intervening protected-path commit silently treated
  as authorized).
- **`implementation_revision` advancement** is rebound to a genuine change
  in the protected implementation-stage `review_content_id` against the
  previously durable round — never to "live HEAD differs from the stored
  value," which is what forced round 9's revision bump for a round that
  added zero new reviewable content (`review_content_id` was
  byte-identical, `619911d7...`, before and after). The authoritative
  comparison source is `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` plus the durable provenance
  commit, **never** `.ai-review/current/MANIFEST.md`, which remains
  disposable, regeneratable bundle content.

### Interaction with `GPT-R44`

`REVIEW_FEEDBACK.gpt-r44.md` reviewed the round-8 bundle (base `c132185f`,
head `4bbf81b`, revision 8) and returned `REVISE`
(`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/current/IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md:512-526`).
It is **not applied by this revision** — the round-9 session already
correctly refused to apply it against an already-superseded bundle, and
this revision does not reopen that refusal. The feedback file itself is
not currently present on disk in this repository (`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/`
holds no `gpt-r44` copy at the time of this revision) — only its
existence, target bundle, and two finding topics are known, the second
via the round-9 commit message and the first as characterized directly by
the user this session. Per the standing instruction not to silently mark
either resolved:

- **`GPT-R44-002`** (implementation_revision relying on
  `current/MANIFEST.md` as an authority): this topic is independently
  corroborated by this repository's own artifacts — `GPT-R43-001`'s
  guard, as actually built, "compares the live `implementation_revision`
  against the value the *previous* bundle's own `MANIFEST.md` recorded"
  (`scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh`, per the `c98e7e6` commit message), and
  this is exactly what forced round 9's spurious revision bump for
  zero new content. **Resolved by this revision's `WFR-61` redesign**
  (round identity bound to `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` + the durable provenance
  commit, never `MANIFEST.md` — acceptance criterion 29, missing-test item
  225), not by a narrower independent patch.
- **`GPT-R44-001`** (whole-plan approval freshness): no independent copy
  of this finding's exact text is available to verify or fix against in
  this repository. **Explicitly deferred, not resolved and not rejected**:
  the fresh external plan review this revision requires should be asked
  to re-supply or re-paste `GPT-R44`'s exact text (or confirm it no longer
  applies against this revision's `D-Approval-Commits`/`D-Bundle-Manifest`
  changes) so it can be dispositioned on its actual content rather than a
  second-hand characterization.

### Required invariants (verbatim from this revision's own design brief, preserved as the acceptance bar for the eventual implementation)

1. `reviewed_implementation_head` identifies the implementation/protected-
   content revision under review, not a later metadata-only bookkeeping
   commit.
2. `generation_head` identifies the exact repository state from which the
   final external-review bundle was generated.
3. A metadata-only workflow-state/provenance commit after the
   implementation content must not create a new implementation revision
   by itself.
4. `implementation_revision` advances exactly once for a genuinely new
   reviewed implementation round.
5. Exact same protected content/regeneration is idempotent.
6. The final bundle-generation operation performs no state write requiring
   a later durability commit.
7. `/approve-review implementation` must accept `HEAD ==
   reviewed_implementation_head`, or `reviewed_implementation_head` as an
   allowed ancestor of HEAD. **(superseded, revision 29, `GPT-R45-003` —
   the bare-equality disjunct is removed; see "WF8b finding disposition
   (revision 28 → 29)" below.)**
8. **Not** unconstrained ancestor reachability — every commit in
   `reviewed_implementation_head..HEAD` must satisfy first-parent
   provenance, excluded-paths-only changes, no protected-path change, the
   required trailer, correct `work_item_id`, correct
   `implementation_revision`/round identity, and no ambiguous duplicate
   provenance.
9. `generation_head` remains subject to repository-local staleness
   checking — before technical approval, live repository state must still
   correspond to the exact generated bundle state the lifecycle permits.
10. "Is this still the implementation that was externally reviewed" and
    "is this still the repository state the review bundle was generated
    from" are two distinct questions, never represented by the same SHA
    equality.

**Scope discipline (revision 28)**: this revision is deliberately
design-only. No file under `scripts/`, `.claude/commands/`, or
`docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md` is edited — all three are
implementation-stage protected, and per this same investigation's own
instruction, implementing this distinction changes an approved
`D-Approval-Commits`/`D-Bundle-Manifest` invariant and therefore belongs
in a plan revision, not a silent implementation change. `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s
own `reviewed_implementation_head`/`implementation_revision`/
`technical_approval` fields are likewise left exactly as recorded by round
9 (`20f89de3c030ebd89d69bcd5afffb830096f8c2b`, revision 9) — this revision
neither advances nor reinterprets that round's own recorded identity; it
only changes what future rounds require. No other `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`
design choice from revisions 22 through 27 is reopened.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 28 → 29) — external plan review found four blocking gaps in the round-identity/provenance redesign (`GPT-R45-001`/`-002`/`-003`/`-004`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 28 bundle (`GPT-R45-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) returned
`Status: REVISE`, four blocking findings. All four independently verified
against this repository before being accepted — `GPT-R45-001` directly
against `scripts/workflow_state.py:1763-1887`
(`resolve_own_registry_completion_status`/
`_assert_registry_covered_by_current_plan_approval`, both already present
in the codebase from the revision-24/27 `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`
work), `GPT-R45-002`/`-003`/`-004` against this document's own revision-28
`D-Approval-Commits`/`D-Commit-Provenance` text. No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R45-001` — registry-derived terminality did not require a genuinely current, durable plan approval

This re-supplies the previously-deferred `GPT-R44-001` (revision 28 could
not disposition it — no independent copy of its text was available at the
time; the external reviewer has now re-supplied it as `GPT-R45-001`).

Confirmed directly: `_assert_registry_covered_by_current_plan_approval`
(`scripts/workflow_state.py:1846-1886`) proves only that (a)
`plan_approval.status == "CURRENT"`, a plain string on a runtime-mutable
file, and (b) the registry file's live blob equals whatever blob the
live, equally runtime-mutable `plan_approval.review_content_manifest`
entry happens to record for `registry_path` — never that the manifest
entry itself is the one a durable `Workflow-Plan-Approval` commit actually
approved, and never that any *other* plan-stage protected document
(`WORKFLOW_V2_PLAN.md`, the mapping file, `TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md`, the
audit doc) still matches what was approved. Both failure scenarios the
finding describes are real against this exact code: a protected-but-not-
registry document can drift after approval while the registry-blob check
alone still passes (Failure scenario A), and a `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`-only
edit to the manifest entry can forge agreement with a rewritten registry
with no reachable approval commit ever having covered it (Failure
scenario B) — a mutable state record cannot authenticate itself.

**Fix**: `_assert_registry_covered_by_current_plan_approval`'s
registry-blob comparison is retired outright — not kept alongside a new
check, since it becomes strictly redundant with the replacement.
`resolve_own_registry_completion_status` now requires, before trusting
any loaded registry's completion status:

1. the durable `Workflow-Plan-Approval` provenance commit for
   `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id` is discovered
   (`discover_plan_approval_commit`) and reachable from live HEAD — never
   merely a `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` status string;
2. the canonical `approval_is_current(repo_root, work_item, stage="plan",
   base_commit=work_item["base_commit"], head="HEAD")` — the same
   full plan-stage protected-path recomputation `IMPLEMENTING`'s own
   entry check (`implementing_entry_reachable`) already uses — returns
   `True` against live HEAD.

Because `registry_path` is already one of the five plan-stage protected
paths that full recomputation covers byte-for-byte, step 2 alone already
proves the registry's live blob matches the durably approved one exactly;
no separate blob comparison is needed to "also" prove it. This closes
both failure scenarios: scenario A is caught because step 2 recomputes
the *whole* protected projection, not only the registry; scenario B is
caught because step 1 requires a genuinely reachable, durable approval
commit, not a mutable state field's own say-so. `complete_work_item`,
`milestone_complete_gate_reachable`, and `scoped_remediation_gate_reachable`
all consume `resolve_own_registry_completion_status`'s result (directly or
via the `is_terminal` value a caller derives from it), so the fix is a
single shared choke point, not three separate patches. See `WFR-53`
(amended below) for the requirement text and required-tests list.

### `GPT-R45-002` — no single authoritative source for "the previously durable round's protected `review_content_id`"

Confirmed directly against this document's own revision-28 text
(`D-Approval-Commits`, "`reviewed_implementation_head`'s sole writer"):
it names the comparison source as "the new provenance record below,"
but `D-Commit-Provenance`'s `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record:
<work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>` trailer carries only the
revision number, never a content hash — there was in fact no field
anywhere in the documented `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` schema (`D3`) holding
the prior round's protected `review_content_id`, exactly as the finding
states. This matters most for a `REVISE` round with no `technical_approval`,
where `technical_approval.approved_review_content_id` is not a universally
available fallback.

**Fix**: one explicit source, requiring no new stored field and no
provenance-commit discovery of its own. `reviewed_implementation_head`
(`D3`) already durably names an immutable commit, written unconditionally
by every round regardless of its eventual review outcome. "The value the
previously durable round recorded" is defined as: the protected
implementation-stage `review_content_id` recomputed directly from the
commit `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s own `reviewed_implementation_head` field
currently names, using the same protected-path set and artifact
declaration the new candidate projection uses — never a separately stored
content-id field, and never `.ai-review/current/MANIFEST.md`.
`reviewed_implementation_head` absent (no round has ever been recorded
for this work item) is treated as vacuously differing: the first-ever
round always advances from no revision to revision 1. This resolves every
edge case the finding names:

- **first-ever round**: no `reviewed_implementation_head` to recompute
  from — vacuously new, as above;
- **previous `REVISE` round with no `technical_approval`**:
  `reviewed_implementation_head` was still written unconditionally by
  that round's own `record_bundle_generation` call, so the recomputation
  works identically regardless of the review outcome;
- **exact retry after the provenance commit**: `reviewed_implementation_head`
  and the candidate projection are computed from the same commit, so the
  comparison is trivially equal — idempotent, no bump;
- **malformed/missing previous provenance, or a deleted previous review
  directory**: irrelevant to this comparison, which never reads a
  provenance-commit trailer or `.ai-review/current/` at all — it recomputes
  directly from the durable, immutable commit `reviewed_implementation_head`
  already names;
- **artifact-classification change between rounds**: not specially
  handled, deliberately — like every other protected-path projection in
  this document, the comparison always uses the currently governing
  classification rules, so a classification change can itself produce a
  genuine revision bump for otherwise byte-identical file content. That
  is intended (a classification change is itself a content-relevant
  design change requiring fresh review), not a gap this fix needs to
  paper over.

### `GPT-R45-003` — the `HEAD == reviewed_implementation_head` branch bypasses the mandatory generation-record provenance

Confirmed directly against this document's own revision-28
`D-Approval-Commits` ordering rule: the provenance-commit-before-generation
requirement is unconditional — "that durability commit is made **before**
bundle generation runs, never after" — for **every** round, without
exception. Under that rule, live HEAD immediately after a legitimate
round's bundle generation is always the durability commit `S`, one
first-parent commit ahead of `reviewed_implementation_head` — never equal
to it. Revision 28's own worked example already established this ("could
never hold once the durability commit... is required to exist"), yet the
gate as written still accepted bare equality as a live alternative,
meaning a state that can only arise from the mandatory durability commit
never having run would be silently approved. Missing-test item 216 tested
only the *unequal*-with-missing-provenance case; there was no test for
equal-with-no-provenance-record.

**Fix**: the bare-equality disjunct is removed from `/approve-review
implementation`'s gate, not narrowed to a migration exception — nothing in
this repository's own history needs it preserved. The one already-recorded
round predating this trailer type entirely (this work item's own round 9,
`reviewed_implementation_head = 20f89de3c030ebd89d69bcd5afffb830096f8c2b`,
`technical_approval` still `null`) was never approved under the old
equality rule in the first place — that is exactly the defect `WF8B-003`
discovered and left `blocking_decisions`-blocked. It remains unable to
reach approval as-is; `WF8b` resumption regenerates a fresh round under
this revision's gate rather than attempting to grandfather the old one in.
Removing the branch is therefore a strictly narrower gate than revision
28's text, not a lost capability: it drops only an already-dead code path.

### `GPT-R45-004` — no recovery path once a later legitimate commit stales the bundle without changing protected content

Confirmed as a genuine, previously-undocumented gap: the workflow
explicitly supports concurrent work items with many implementation-stage
*excluded* paths (`D-Fingerprint-Generalization`), so a legitimate,
unrelated commit `U` can land after a round's durability commit `S` and
move HEAD without touching this work item's protected implementation
content at all. `D-Approval-Commits`' one-commit provenance interval then
correctly refuses (`P → S → U` is two first-parent commits, not one), and
nothing in revision 28's text describes how to get back to a reviewable
state without either fabricating a second, ambiguous provenance commit for
the same round or incorrectly treating unchanged content as a new
implementation round.

**Fix**: a dedicated re-provenance recovery operation, distinct from
ordinary bundle regeneration, reusing `D-Commit-Provenance`'s existing
genuine-ambiguity recovery mechanism (`Workflow-Supersedes:`, already
defined for the rebase/cherry-pick duplicate-trailer case, `OPUS-R6-022`)
rather than inventing a second one:

1. **Precondition, checked first, before any commit is made**: the
   protected implementation-stage `review_content_id` recomputed at the
   candidate HEAD must be byte-identical to the one recomputed at
   `reviewed_implementation_head` (`GPT-R45-002`'s recomputation, above).
   If it is not identical, this is not recovery at all — it is a
   genuinely new round, handled by the ordinary path, and the recovery
   operation refuses outright.
2. Once confirmed identical, the operation creates **exactly one** new
   commit `S2`, touching only `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, carrying **both**
   the unchanged `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record:
   <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>` trailer value as `S` — this
   is not a new round, `implementation_revision` does not change — **and**
   a `Workflow-Supersedes: <S-sha>` trailer naming `S` explicitly.
3. `D-Commit-Provenance`'s trailer lookup, on finding two matches for the
   same `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` trailer key/value,
   already resolves genuine ambiguity via a `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer
   rather than stopping (existing revision-6 recovery text) — this fix
   states explicitly that a content-verified `Workflow-Supersedes` match
   (the superseding commit itself touches no protected path, same check
   every other trailer discovery already performs) resolves the
   resulting duplicate deterministically: `S` is treated as superseded,
   `S2` as current. Without a `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer, two matching
   provenance commits remain genuine, refused ambiguity — missing-test
   item 221 is unchanged and continues to cover exactly that case.
4. Bundle generation then runs from `S2`, and `/approve-review
   implementation` re-evaluates against the ordinary one-commit interval
   `reviewed_implementation_head → S2` — no separate approval code path
   for a recovered round.

This satisfies every constraint the finding names: no protected or
unclassified intervening content is ever permitted (precondition 1,
enforced before any commit); the recovery is fail-closed by construction
(refuses outright rather than guessing); first-parent ancestry stays
deterministic; current/superseded generation-record identity is explicit
(`Workflow-Supersedes`); there is no duplicate ambiguity once the trailer
is present, and no silent auto-pick when it is absent; `implementation_revision`
never changes for unchanged protected content; same-content regeneration
stays idempotent (recovery is itself idempotent — retrying it against the
same `S`/candidate HEAD reuses the same `S2` decision); and
`generation_head`'s exact local-staleness check is unaffected — it still
checks exact equality against whatever HEAD generation actually ran from.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 29 → 30) — external plan review found three blocking gaps in `WFR-62`'s stale-`generation_head` recovery design (`GPT-R46-001`/`-002`/`-003`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 29 bundle (`GPT-R46-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) returned
`Status: REVISE`, three blocking findings, confirming `GPT-R45-001`/`-002`/`-003`
closed while finding revision 29's `GPT-R45-004` fix (`WFR-62`) does not
actually restore approval reachability. All three independently verified
against this document's own revision-29 `D-Commit-Provenance`/`D-Approval-Commits`
text before being accepted. No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R46-001` — the recovery commit `S2` cannot become the one first-parent child of `reviewed_implementation_head`

Confirmed directly against this document's own revision-29 text: the
recovery operation creates `S2` as a new commit on live HEAD, whose parent
is necessarily `U` (the intervening excluded-only commit), not `P`
(`reviewed_implementation_head`) — ordinary Git commit semantics, not a
bug in any code. Revision 29's own text then claimed `/approve-review
implementation` "re-evaluates against the ordinary one-commit interval
`reviewed_implementation_head → S2`," but that interval does not exist in
the graph revision 29 itself describes (`P → S → U → S2`, three commits,
not one). `Workflow-Supersedes` resolves which of two duplicate trailer
matches is authoritative; it was never capable of rewriting ancestry or
making `S2` a child of `P`. The gate as revision 29 specified it (WFR-61's
"exactly one first-parent commit") would therefore refuse every recovered
round, making the entire recovery mechanism unable to restore approval
reachability — the exact failure the mechanism exists to prevent.

**Fix**: adopt the reviewer's own proposed minimal model. `D-Commit-Provenance`'s
single-commit provenance rule is generalized to a **bounded, fully
enumerated and classified first-parent interval** (new "Provenance
interval" definition, above) rather than an exactly-one-commit interval.
`D-Approval-Commits`' `/approve-review implementation` gate is restated
against this generalized interval. The real topology `P → S → U → S2` is
now accepted **as that graph** — never misdescribed as a one-commit
`P → S2` interval — because every non-terminal member (`S`, `U`) is
individually classified excluded-only and the terminal member (`S2`)
carries the current trailer and touches no protected path. An ordinary,
non-recovered round is the `n = 1` special case of the same definition, so
no existing acceptance test (215-230) changes behavior.

### `GPT-R46-002` — endpoint `review_content_id` equality does not prove no protected or unclassified commit occurred in the recovery interval

Confirmed directly: revision 29's precondition compared only the protected
projection at the two interval *endpoints* (`reviewed_implementation_head`
and candidate HEAD) and concluded from that equality that "every commit in
[the interval] ... has touched no protected implementation path." That
implication is false in general — a content identity function proves the
final projection matches, not that the history between the two points
never touched protected content. Both of the reviewer's counter-examples
are real against revision 29's text as written: (A) a protected-path
commit followed by a byte-for-byte revert of that same path leaves
endpoint content identical while the interval contains a commit the
recovery must refuse; (B) a transient unclassified path added then removed
before candidate HEAD leaves endpoint content identical while the interval
contains a commit the fail-closed classifier should never let through.
Revision 29's text would have let an implementation that follows it
literally skip the required history scan entirely.

**Fix**: the precondition now explicitly requires **both** endpoint
content equality (kept, as a cheap fast-refusal check for the genuinely
common "this is actually a new round" case) **and** an exhaustive
first-parent, commit-by-commit classification of the *entire* candidate
interval, inspecting each commit's own diff against its own first parent
rather than inferring historical cleanliness from the endpoints. This is
not a separate, redundant mechanism from `GPT-R46-001`'s fix — it is the
same per-commit classification the generalized "Provenance interval"
definition already requires the approval gate to perform, reused here as
a precondition so the recovery operation refuses *before* committing
rather than only being caught later at approval time.

### `GPT-R46-003` — the recovery operation had no defined command, authorization boundary, or state mutation

Confirmed directly: revision 29 described the recovery commit's trailer
content but never named which command invokes it, what phase it runs
from, whether explicit user authorization is required (despite
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s pre-existing generic `Workflow-Supersedes` rule
already requiring exactly that for the general case), which
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` fields it writes, or how a retry recognizes an
already-completed recovery. Left this open, independent implementers could
reach materially different authority, replay, and audit behavior while
each honestly believing they followed revision 29's prose.

**Fix**: a full operation contract is now specified — a new dedicated
command (`/recover-implementation-provenance <work_item_id>`), its
allowed source phase, mandatory explicit user confirmation (preserving,
not narrowing, `D-Commit-Provenance`'s existing user-approval requirement
for `Workflow-Supersedes`), the exact (minimal) `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
mutation, pre- and post-commit validation, interruption safety, and
replay/idempotency discovery — see the "Operation contract" subsection of
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s stale-`generation_head` recovery paragraph, above.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 30 → 31) — external plan review found three blocking lifecycle/security gaps and two plan/bundle consistency defects (`GPT-R47-001` through `-005`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 30 bundle (`GPT-R47-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) returned
`Status: REVISE`, three blocking findings plus two consistency findings
labelled important/blocking-plan-consistency. All five independently
verified against this repository/document's own revision-30 text before
being accepted — `GPT-R47-001`/`-002` against `D2`'s `EXTERNAL_APPROVE`
exact-`bundle_id`-match rule and `docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`'s
own phase enumeration (confirming `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
is a real, distinct phase preceding `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`),
`GPT-R47-003` directly against this document's own revision-30
"Provenance interval" condition 4 text, `GPT-R47-004` directly against
`workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json` and the Requirements traceability table
(confirmed: `WFR-53` diverged, table/JSON both already at 62 rows, item
166's "52 rows" claim stale), `GPT-R47-005` directly against the bundle's
own `PLAN.md` (confirmed: still headed "Revision 29," a real omission —
revision 30 updated `REVIEW_REQUEST.md` but never regenerated `PLAN.md`).
No finding was rejected. `GPT-R45-001`/`-002`/`-003` and `GPT-R46-001`/
`-002`/`-003` were independently reconfirmed closed by the reviewer's own
"Confirmed strengths" section.

### `GPT-R47-001` — recovery creates a new bundle identity but defines no return to external implementation review

Confirmed directly against `D-Approval-Commits`' `D2` text: `EXTERNAL_APPROVE`
requires the current `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`'s `Reviewed bundle ID:` to equal
the just-recomputed `bundle_id` **exactly**. Regenerating from `S2` changes
`generation_head` and the bundled `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`/provenance
content, so `bundle_id` necessarily changes even though the protected
`review_content_id` does not. Revision 30 left the phase at
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` after recovery and wrote no field but
`state_revision`/`last_transition`, defining no path back through fresh
external review — the pre-recovery feedback for `B1` cannot legitimately
authorize `B2`, but nothing in revision 30 said so or routed around it.

**Fix**: recovery now always transitions the item to
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` on success, mandating a fresh
external review of the regenerated bundle before `EXTERNAL_APPROVE` can
apply — see the "Post-recovery phase transition" subsection of
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s recovery paragraph, above. Stale pre-recovery
feedback is correctly, automatically inert under the existing `WFR-03`/
`D2` exact-bundle-id-match rule; this fix states that consequence
explicitly rather than leaving it implicit and unenforced by a phase that
never asked for it.

### `GPT-R47-002` — the recovery command is unavailable when staleness happens before the technical-approval phase

Confirmed directly against `docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`:
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` is a real, named phase preceding
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` in the ordinary implementation-review cycle.
A legitimate excluded-only commit can stale a generated bundle's
`generation_head` while the item is still in that earlier phase, and
revision 30's phase-restricted command (`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`
only) had no legal action available — a dead-end state, exactly as the
finding's failure scenario shows.

**Fix**: `/recover-implementation-provenance`'s allowed source phase is
widened to both `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` and
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` — the only two phases in which a generated
implementation bundle can exist without a current technical approval
already recorded — with `GPT-R47-001`'s fix supplying a single,
uniform post-recovery phase (`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`)
regardless of which of the two the command ran from, exactly matching the
reviewer's own "prefer one recovery operation with phase-specific exits"
guidance (collapsed to one exit, since both source phases converge on the
same fresh-review requirement).

### `GPT-R47-003` — the generalized approval interval does not fail closed on an unclassified terminal provenance commit

Confirmed directly against this document's own revision-30 "Provenance
interval" condition 4 text: non-terminal commits were classified against
both protected **and** unclassified paths (condition 3), but the terminal
commit `T` was checked only for "touches no protected implementation
path" — no unclassified-path check, and no check that `T`'s mutation
matches its own role's exact contract. A fabricated or malformed terminal
commit carrying the correct trailer plus an unrelated unclassified file
change would pass condition 4 as literally written.

**Fix**: condition 4 is rewritten to classify `T` exactly as strictly as
every non-terminal commit (no protected, no unclassified path) **plus** an
additional role-specific mutation check — an ordinary round's `T` must
touch only `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` and carry only the
`Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` trailer; a recovery round's `T` (`S2`)
must touch only `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s `state_revision`/`last_transition`/
`phase` and carry both the unchanged `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
value and a `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer. An ordinary, well-formed round
is unaffected (`S` already only ever touched `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` with
the one trailer); a fabricated terminal commit with an extra unclassified
mutation now refuses.

### `GPT-R47-004` — the protected requirements mapping is already out of sync with the plan, and item 166's historical claim is stale

Confirmed directly: `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json`'s `WFR-53` entry had
diverged from its table row (missing the `GPT-R45-001` amendment text the
table already carried), and missing-test item 166 still asserted "All 52
rows are already synced" against a document that has carried 62 rows
since revision 29. Both are plan-stage protected paths under active
review, so this is a real consistency defect in the content being
approved, not a cosmetic note.

**Fix**: `WFR-53`'s JSON description is resynced to its table row exactly
(zero mismatches now verified across all 62 rows, mechanically, using the
conformance test's own normalization function). Item 166's stale "52
rows"/historical framing is corrected below the table. The conformance
test's own hardcoded `len(table_rows) == 60` sanity assertion
(`scripts/workflow_integration_test.py`) is **not** edited by this
plan-only revision — `scripts/` remains implementation-stage protected,
outside this revision's declared scope, same discipline as every prior
`WF8b` plan revision — but item 166 now explicitly names the fix that
revision owes: replace the hardcoded literal with a check derived from
the live requirement count (`len(mapping["requirements"])`), never a
magic number that silently drifts on the next requirement addition.

### `GPT-R47-005` — the bundle's required `PLAN.md` still described Revision 29

Confirmed directly: revision 30 updated `REVIEW_REQUEST.md` but never
regenerated the bundle's hand-maintained `PLAN.md`, which still opened
with "**(Revision 29)**" and summarized the 28→29 change only — a real
process omission in the previous session, not a finding about the design

(`MANIFEST.md`'s `plan_revision`, `REVIEW_REQUEST.md`, `PLAN.md`, and the
plan doc's own title) must all agree before a bundle is handed to a
reviewer — restated as part of step 5 of `/apply-plan-review` going
forward, not a new mechanism.

`GPT-R48-002` directly against `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Provenance

### `GPT-R48-001` — `D-States` still requires the pre-WF8B exact-HEAD equality that revision 28-31 explicitly removed

Confirmed directly against `D-States`' own text: the
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` entry condition required "current committed
content matches `reviewed_implementation_head` exactly" — the same bare
equality `WFR-61` explicitly states is "never accepted, not even as an
alternative, since the mandatory provenance commit makes that state
unreachable for any genuinely new round." A work item finishing an
ordinary implementation round could never satisfy `D-States`' own entry
gate for the phase `/approve-review implementation` is supposed to run in,
since live HEAD is always the durability commit `T`, one commit past
`reviewed_implementation_head`, by the time the round is ready for
technical approval.

**Fix**: `D-States`' entry condition is rewritten to require the same
provenance-interval round-validity predicate `WFR-61`/`D-Commit-Provenance`
already define for `/approve-review implementation` itself — a current
`T`, live HEAD exactly equal to `T`, and the bounded interval
`reviewed_implementation_head..T` validating completely — rather than an
independent, contradictory bare-equality check. See `D-States`'
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` entry, above.

### `GPT-R48-002` — the terminal recovery-commit mutation contract omits the mandatory `phase` write, making valid recovery fail its own approval gate

Confirmed directly against `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Provenance interval"
condition 4 and its recovery "Topology" paragraph: both named only
`state_revision`/`last_transition` as the recovery commit `S2`'s allowed
mutation, omitting `phase` even though the "Operation contract"
subsection's own "Exact `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` mutation" paragraph, `WFR-62`'s
table row, and missing-test items 254/255 all already required
`phase`/`state_revision`/`last_transition`. A correctly-performed recovery
from `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` (which the operation contract requires
to write `phase`) would then fail the terminal-commit classification's own
role-specific mutation check, since that check's allowed-field list did
not include the field the recovery is required to write.

**Fix**: condition 4 and the "Topology" paragraph both now name
`phase`/`state_revision`/`last_transition` as the recovery commit's
allowed mutation, matching the "Operation contract" subsection, `WFR-62`'s
row, and missing-test items 254/255 exactly. No behavioral change to the
`WFR-62` operation itself — it already wrote `phase` — this fix only makes
the interval-validation definition text agree with the contract it is
supposed to be checking, closing a self-inflicted approval-gate rejection
for well-formed recovery from `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`.

### `GPT-R48-003` — recovery replay text describes an impossible partial state and an undefined uncommitted phase repair

Confirmed directly against the recovery "Replay/idempotency" paragraph:
it described a replay path that "confirms `phase` reads
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` on this replay path, in case an
interrupted first attempt committed `S2` but never reached that state
write (a fresh session's resume path completes the phase transition
without re-committing)." The immediately preceding "Interruption behavior"
paragraph states the operation is a single atomic commit with "no partial
state, including the `phase` write, which lands in the same commit as the
trailers" — if `S2` exists, `phase` is already part of it; there is no
committed-but-not-transitioned state to complete, and completing one
without a commit would itself be an uncommitted, non-durable state
mutation this document's standing "a durable commit, not a mutable state
field, is the authority" principle forbids.

**Fix**: the impossible partial-state branch is deleted. Replay now
verifies the discovered `S2`'s own committed state directly — if it
satisfies the required mutation, reports exact replay/idempotent success
with no write; if it does not (a hand-edited or corrupted historical
commit, never an in-progress recovery, since the commit is atomic),
refuses as malformed/conflicting recovery provenance rather than repairing
it. See the "Replay/idempotency" paragraph, above. New missing-test items
260-261 cover exact replay (no write) and the malformed-`S2` refusal;
`WFR-62`'s verification column extended to name both.

### `GPT-R49-001` — the ordinary/recovered "carries only" trailer contracts never named the `Workflow-Work-Item` trailer their own scoped discovery requires

Confirmed directly: `D-Commit-Provenance`'s opening paragraph states
discovery is "`Workflow-Work-Item`-scoped" (unchanged since revision 6,
reused verbatim for this trailer), and missing-test item 219 exercises
exactly that scoping against a wrong-work-item trailer. But condition 4
said an ordinary `S` "carries only the `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
trailer," and the recovery "Topology" paragraph named only
`Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` plus `Workflow-Supersedes` for `S2` —
neither ever named `Workflow-Work-Item`. Taken literally, a correctly
scoped, discoverable commit (carrying `Workflow-Work-Item`) would fail
its own terminal-commit "carries only" check, while a commit satisfying
the "carries only" check literally (omitting `Workflow-Work-Item`) would
never be discovered by the scoped lookup that check's own document
section requires. Every other provenance-commit type in this document
(`Workflow-Plan-Approval`, `Workflow-Technical-Approval`,
`Workflow-Checkpoint`, `Workflow-Functional-Checklist`,
`Workflow-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`) already states it carries the
ordinary `Workflow-Work-Item` trailer alongside its own — this trailer
type was the one exception, unintentionally.

**Fix**: `D-Commit-Provenance` gains an explicit "Canonical provenance
trailer set" subsection defining the exact two-trailer ordinary set and
three-trailer recovered set, each including `Workflow-Work-Item`.
`D-Approval-Commits`' durability-commit paragraph, condition 4, and the
recovery "Topology" paragraph are all corrected to reference this same
set. `WFR-61`/`WFR-62`'s row text and their mirrored
`workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json` descriptions are amended identically.
New missing-test items 262-265 cover positive discovery of both
correctly-trailered roles and negative non-discovery of both
incorrectly-trailered variants.

### `GPT-R49-002` — the ordinary generation-record commit had no exact field-level mutation contract, unlike the recovered commit

Confirmed directly: condition 4's recovered-role clause names an exact
field list (`phase`/`state_revision`/`last_transition`), but its
ordinary-role clause only said "touches only `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`" — a
file-level classification, not a field-level one. An ordinary `S` that
also mutates, in the same commit, `technical_approval`, `plan_approval`,
`active_work_item_id`, a `checkpoints` entry, `functional_acceptance_status`,
or another work item's own state would still satisfy "touches only
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json`" (all of those live inside that one file), so the
terminal-commit classification had no specification requiring it to
refuse — reopening, inside one excluded file, the same "unexpected
mutation rides through a valid provenance commit" class `GPT-R47-003`
closed at the path level.

**Fix**: `D-Approval-Commits`' durability-commit paragraph and
`D-Commit-Provenance` condition 4's ordinary-role clause both now name
the exact allowed field set — `reviewed_implementation_head`,
`implementation_revision`, `state_revision`, `last_transition`, and no
other field — matching `record_bundle_generation`'s own implementation
exactly (confirmed against `scripts/workflow_state.py`'s
`record_bundle_generation`, which writes precisely these four fields and
no others). `WFR-61`'s row text and its mirrored mapping description are
amended identically. New missing-test items 266-267 cover a valid
ordinary `S` and an ordinary `S` that additionally mutates each
representative forbidden field.

### `GPT-R49-003` — no defined semantics for a second or later legitimate recovery of the same round

Confirmed directly: the "Stale-`generation_head` recovery" subsection's
precondition, topology, and operation-contract paragraphs are all stated
in terms of exactly one recovery (`P → S → U → S2`). Nothing addresses
what happens if `S2`'s own regenerated bundle goes stale again before
`technical_approval` is recorded — a scenario the recovery mechanism's
own purpose (tolerating concurrent excluded-only commits) makes entirely
plausible to recur. Without an explicit rule, a second recovery's
resulting three-provenance-commit set (`S`, `S2`, `S3`, all carrying the
same `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` value) has no stated current-tip
computation, fork rule, or cycle rule.

**Fix**: `D-Commit-Provenance` gains a "Multiple sequential recoveries /
supersession chain" subsection, applied within the existing
"Stale-`generation_head` recovery" section: the same operation, run
again, treats the prior `S2` as the new `S`; supersession is scoped to
one `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` pair, forms a simple linked
list (never a tree or cycle), and the current tip is the unique commit
never named by another commit's `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer — a fork
(two commits naming the same target) or a cycle both refuse as malformed
provenance. `WFR-62`'s row text and its mirrored mapping description are
amended identically. New missing-test items 268-271 cover a two-recovery
end-to-end round-trip, the full-chain interval validation, a forked
supersession, and a cyclic/malformed one.

re-verified directly against this repository's own revision-33 text
before being accepted — `GPT-R50-001` against `D-Approval-Commits`'
durability-commit paragraph (confirmed: its exact allowed mutation set is
`reviewed_implementation_head`/`implementation_revision`/`state_revision`/
`last_transition` — four fields, `phase` excluded — while
`docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`'s own `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`

`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`, and no other commit exists anywhere in the
mandatory one-commit ordinary interval to carry it), `GPT-R50-002` against
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Provenance interval" condition 3 (confirmed: it
classifies every non-terminal commit as generic excluded-only regardless
of whether that commit itself carries a `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
trailer for this exact round — after one recovery, `S` is non-terminal;
after two, `S` and `S2` both are — so a malformed historical generation-
record commit is checked only for "no protected/unclassified path," never

as "carrying only the generation-record trailer" and a valid recovered
`S2` as "carrying both trailers" — the exact one-/two-trailer framing
