### `GPT-R50-001` — the ordinary generation-record commit cannot also perform the required transition into external implementation review

Confirmed directly against `D-Approval-Commits`' durability-commit
paragraph and `docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`'s state reference.
The ordinary commit `S` is the sole commit the mandatory one-commit
`P -> S` interval permits between the last protected implementation
commit and bundle generation, yet its exact allowed mutation set omits
`phase`, and the workflow's own state machine requires a durable
`phase == AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` transition before that
point. No other legal place exists to carry it: writing `phase` in `S`
itself violates the exact-field contract as revision 33 left it; a
separate pre-`S` phase-only commit breaks the mandatory one-commit
topology and trips missing-test item 218's untrailed-metadata-commit
refusal; a post-generation write moves live HEAD past `generation_head`,
immediately staling the bundle; and folding the transition into the final
protected commit `P` is not a documented command contract and is not
generally achievable (self-review/testing can finish after `P` already
exists, and history is never rewritten merely to insert phase
bookkeeping). This is the exact ordinary-path analogue of the `phase`-field
gap revision 32 (`GPT-R48-002`) already fixed for recovery `S2`.

**Fix**: `D-Approval-Commits` gains a new "Ordinary bundle-publication
phase transition" subsection: `S`'s exact allowed `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
mutation grows from four fields to five — `phase`,
`reviewed_implementation_head`, `implementation_revision`,
`state_revision`, `last_transition` — with `phase`'s own legal source
phases (`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` for the round's first bundle,
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` for a `post-fix` bundle), exact target phase
(always `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`), value-wise-unchanged-
on-retry behavior, and post-commit validation stated explicitly, mirroring
the same shapes `WFR-62`'s recovery `phase` write and replay contract
already use rather than inventing new ones. `D-Commit-Provenance`
condition 4's ordinary-role clause and `WFR-61`'s row text are corrected
to the same five-field set. New missing-test items 273-277 cover the
end-to-end phase transition from both legal source phases, refusal from
an illegal source phase, refusal of a wrong target phase value, and
idempotent retry.

### `GPT-R50-002` — after recovery, prior generation-record commits are downgraded to generic excluded-only commits and can hide malformed provenance

Confirmed directly against condition 3's text ("every non-terminal commit
... is classified implementation-stage excluded-only") and the recovery
"Topology"/"Multiple sequential recoveries" paragraphs, both of which
describe `S` (and, after a second recovery, `S2`) as merely
"excluded-only-classified" once superseded. Condition 4's role-specific
contract — the same one that already makes the *terminal* commit's own
malformed mutation refuse — was never extended to a *historical*
generation-record commit, so `GPT-R50-002`'s two worked scenarios both
hold: a malformed `S` (an extra forbidden field mutation) followed by an
otherwise-valid `U -> S2` reaches `/approve-review implementation`
because `S` is only ever checked as "touches no protected/unclassified
path," never against its own exact field/trailer contract once `S2`
exists; the same recurs for a malformed `S2` hidden by a valid `S3` after
a second recovery.

**Fix**: `D-Commit-Provenance` condition 3 is redefined by role rather
than by terminal/non-terminal position: any commit carrying a
`Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` trailer for this exact
`(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` pair — necessarily historical/
superseded when non-terminal, since the pair's current record is always
`T` — must satisfy condition 4's role-specific contract (ordinary or
recovered, matching whichever trailer set it carries) exactly as strictly
as condition 4 already requires of `T`; every other commit (no such
trailer) remains classified excluded-only exactly as before. Condition 4
itself is reframed as the shared definition condition 3 now references,
rather than a terminal-only check. The recovery "Topology" paragraph, the
"Multiple sequential recoveries" paragraph, and the "Stale-`generation_head`
recovery" precondition 2 are all corrected to apply this same role-based
rule — precondition 2 in particular, since a second or later recovery's
own candidate interval already contains a prior round's `S`/`S2` as a
non-terminal member before the new commit is even created. `WFR-61`/
`WFR-62`'s row text is corrected to state that every generation-record
member of the interval, not only the terminal one, is role-validated.
New missing-test items 278-281 cover a malformed historical `S` hidden by
an otherwise-valid recovery, a malformed historical `S2` hidden by an
otherwise-valid second recovery, a canonical multi-recovery chain with
every generation-record member independently role-valid, and an unrelated
excluded-only commit remaining permitted without any role-specific
obligation of its own.

### `GPT-R50-003` — missing-test item 255 still asserts the pre-revision-33 trailer sets

Confirmed directly: item 255 described a valid ordinary `S` as "carrying
only the generation-record trailer" and a valid recovered `S2` as
"carrying both trailers" — the exact framing `GPT-R49-001`/revision 33
replaced with the canonical two-trailer ordinary and three-trailer
recovered sets, already correctly tested by items 262-265. Implemented

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35) — external plan review found three blocking post-approval lifecycle/provenance gaps plus one important stale-test-obligation finding (`GPT-R51-001` through `-004`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 34 bundle (`GPT-R51-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id`, confirmed `GPT-R50-001`/`-002`/
`-003` resolved, and returned `Status: REVISE`, three blocking findings
plus one important finding against the *next* boundary revision 34's own
fix exposed. All four independently re-verified directly against this
repository's own revision-34 text before being accepted — `GPT-R51-001`
against `D-States`' `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` paragraph and
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s recovery "Allowed source phase" precondition
(confirmed: `D-States` describes the gate with the same "Entry"/"Exit"
framing this document uses for every other, literally durable `phase`
value, and the recovery precondition literally names
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` as a checkable legal source phase — which
only makes sense if it is a real, durably stored value — while no
paragraph anywhere states a durable writer for the transition into it, or
states that it is never durably stored; the reviewer's read that a
separate durable phase-transition commit is required, and therefore
structurally impossible without re-staling the just-reviewed bundle
exactly as the worked five-step contradiction shows, is a defect in what
this plan actually says, not a misreading of it), `GPT-R51-002` against
`D-States`' edge summary (`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK → AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL →
AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`) and the "Ordinary bundle-publication phase
transition" subsection's "Target phase: always
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`" sentence revision 34 itself
just added (confirmed: both are verbatim as quoted, and jointly describe
two different, incompatible destinations for the same
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` exit), `GPT-R51-003` against the
"`reviewed_implementation_head`'s sole writer" bullet's idempotency
sentence (confirmed: "regenerating against an unchanged
`reviewed_implementation_head` and unchanged `review_content_id` reuses
the existing revision, idempotently" names no live-HEAD-position
condition at all, so a live HEAD that has moved past the recorded `S`
through legitimate excluded-only commits since `S` was made is handled
identically to an exact retry, discovering and reporting the now-historical
`S` as if it were still current), and `GPT-R51-004` against missing-test
item 12 (confirmed: it still requires `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`
reachable "for a `REVISE`-with-findings-resolved round," the exact claim
`GPT-R51-002`'s own fix, below, makes false for the implementation stage —
every post-fix regeneration now returns through external review by
construction, so no `REVISE` round can reach a technical-approval-eligible
state on the strength of its own, superseded feedback). No finding was
rejected.

### `GPT-R51-001` — no durable transition from an externally approved bundle to `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` that preserves that bundle's validity

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above. The underlying cause is
that `AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` was always designed as a **computed gate
state** — D2 already says entry to it "never reads" the approval record,
and no paragraph anywhere names a commit that durably writes
`phase: AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` (the plan-approval commit's own exit
target, `IMPLEMENTING`, is written directly, per `D-Approval-Commits`'
"`/approve-review plan`" bullet) — but `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` was
never given the same explicit treatment, and revision 31's recovery-phase
fix (`GPT-R47-002`) then actively treated it as a real, checkable, durably
stored value, contradicting the computed-gate design its sibling gate
already uses without ever saying so.

**Fix**: state the computed-gate design explicitly, symmetrically, for
both gates, and correct the one place (`D-Commit-Provenance`'s recovery
precondition) that assumed otherwise. Applied below:

- `D-States` gains a new shared paragraph, immediately before the
  `AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` paragraph, stating plainly: neither
  `AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` nor `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` is ever a
  durably stored `phase` value. Entry to each is evaluated live, every
  time, from repository/state content (`plan_approval_gate_reachable`/
  `technical_approval_gate_reachable`, already the shared-reachability
  functions this document names). The literal `phase` field remains at
  the immediately preceding durable phase —
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_PLAN_REVIEW` / `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
  respectively — for the gate's entire duration. The approval command's
  own single commit (`/approve-review plan` / `/approve-review
  implementation`) is the **sole** writer that ever touches `phase` on
  this path, and it writes the successor durable phase directly —
  `IMPLEMENTING` / `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW` — in the same atomic
  commit that also records `plan_approval`/`technical_approval`. No
  commit ever durably writes `phase: AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` or
  `phase: AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`; both remain legal validator enum
  values (no code change — an enum listing a value no writer this design
  defines ever produces is not itself a defect) but are never observed in
  a conforming `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`. This resolves the reviewer's
  five-step contradiction directly: the "exit" `/approve-review
  implementation` performs is the *same* commit whose precondition
  requires live HEAD `== T` — that equality is checked and satisfied
  immediately before the commit is created, and nothing after it ever
  needs to re-satisfy the same equality against a later, different
  commit, because there is no later, different commit on this path.
- `D-States`' `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` paragraph's "Exit" bullet is
  restated to name the field-mutation contract explicitly (previously
  implicit): the metadata-only technical-approval commit touches only
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, and within it changes exactly `technical_approval`,
  `phase` (`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` →
  `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`), `state_revision`, and `last_transition` —
  no other field — mirroring the exhaustive-field-set discipline
  `GPT-R49-002`/`GPT-R50-001` already established for the generation-record
  commits. `D-Approval-Commits`' `/approve-review implementation` bullet
  is amended identically.
- `D-Commit-Provenance`'s recovery "Allowed source phase" collapses from
  two legal source phases to **one**: `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`.
  `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` is removed as a legal source phase because
  it can no longer be durably observed at all — every case revision 31
  introduced it to cover (a bundle staled after receiving a matching
  `APPROVE`, before the user invoked `/approve-review implementation`) is
  now already covered by the sole remaining phase, since `phase` never
  left `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` in the first place. This
  is a pure simplification, not a coverage loss: recovery's own mechanics
  never depended on knowing whether a matching `APPROVE` existed for the
  bundle being recovered (the "Post-recovery phase transition" paragraph
  already establishes that any pre-recovery feedback is automatically
  inert against the regenerated bundle regardless of its verdict).
- The "Post-recovery phase transition" paragraph's "regardless of which of
  the two legal source phases the command ran from" clause is simplified
  to name the sole remaining phase; its value-wise-unchanged/real-transition
  distinction ("may be value-wise unchanged when the recovery's source
  phase was already `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, and is a
  real transition when the source was `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`") is
  replaced with a single sentence: the recovery commit's `phase` mutation
  is now always value-wise unchanged (`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
  → `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`), since that is now the only
  legal source and target — still part of `T`'s allowed mutation set, not
  an extra field, so a future design reintroducing a phase-varying
  recovery path would not need to change this field list again.
- Missing-test item 250 (the phase-scope regression guard added revision
  31) is corrected in place to name the single remaining legal phase and
  to add the now-illegal-source-phase case (`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`
  is refused identically to any other wrong phase, since it can never be
  durably observed).

### `GPT-R51-002` — revision 34's state edges still contradict the new post-fix publication flow

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above — the two quoted
statements are both present verbatim and jointly incompatible.

**Fix**: define the two verdict-specific transitions explicitly, replacing
the single ambiguous edge:

- **Current external `REVISE`**: `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
  → `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` → a regenerated bundle (`record_bundle_generation`,
  `post-fix` stage, `GPT-R51-003`'s corrected branching below) → durably
  back to `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` — always, regardless of
  whether the regeneration advanced `implementation_revision` or reused it
  (`GPT-R51-003`). No path from a current `REVISE` ever makes
  `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` reachable on the strength of that `REVISE`
  round's own feedback.
- **Current external `APPROVE`**: the (computed, `GPT-R51-001`)
  `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` gate becomes reachable against the current,
  matching bundle; the user invokes `/approve-review implementation`; its
  single commit durably transitions `phase`,
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` → `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`
  (`GPT-R51-001`).
- `D-States`' edge summary sentence is rewritten to state both explicitly,
  replacing `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK → AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL →
  AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`.
- `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`'s own entry-condition paragraph is
  narrowed: "the most recently reviewed current bundle's status was
  `REVISE` or `APPROVE`" becomes "...was exactly `APPROVE`" for the
  **implementation** stage only — the plan stage's own
  `AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` entry condition is deliberately unchanged
  (`REVISE` or `APPROVE`, never `BLOCK`), because the plan stage has no
  analogous "every regeneration mandatorily returns to review" rule: a
  locally-fixed plan `REVISE` may still reach `AWAITING_PLAN_APPROVAL` and
  be approved via `USER_OVERRIDE` without a forced re-review round, per
  this very command's (`/apply-plan-review`) own step 6 discretion. The
  implementation stage has no equivalent discretion once revision 34's
  "target phase: always `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`" rule is
  in force, so narrowing only its own entry condition is not an
  inconsistency between the two gates — it is each gate correctly
  reflecting its own, already-different, regeneration contract.
- `technical_approval_gate_reachable`'s prose description (D-States) is
  updated to require `latest_round_status == "APPROVE"` exactly, dropping
  the shared `approval_gate_reachable` primitive for this one call site —
  the plan-stage call site is unaffected.
- The `D-States` sentence naming `apply-plan-review.md`/
  `apply-implementation-review.md`'s exit-step amendments is corrected: it
  no longer says `apply-implementation-review.md`'s exit step names
  `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` as its target — that command's exit target,
  for every regenerated bundle regardless of verdict, is durably
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` (set by `record_bundle_generation`
  itself, never by the command directly), matching `apply-plan-review.md`'s
  own "stop, report next state, never self-declare readiness" discipline.

### `GPT-R51-003` — same-content post-fix publication incorrectly reuses the historical generation record and cannot produce a current reviewable bundle

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above, and independently
worked through against `WFR-62`'s existing recovery machinery: the
scenario the reviewer describes (`P → S → U...`, protected content
unchanged, live HEAD moved) is structurally identical to the staleness
`WFR-62` recovery already handles — the only genuine gap is that
`record_bundle_generation`, invoked at `post-fix` stage, never checks for
it, and `/recover-implementation-provenance` is not legally invocable from
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` (not one of its two, now one after
`GPT-R51-001`, legal source phases) to fill the gap either.

**Fix**: `record_bundle_generation`, at `post-fix` stage, splits its single
idempotency check into three cases, all reusing `WFR-62`'s existing
byte-identity-plus-exhaustive-interval-classification machinery rather
than inventing a parallel one, exactly as the reviewer's own required
correction directs:

1. **Genuinely new round** (protected `review_content_id` differs from the
   value recomputed from the commit `reviewed_implementation_head`
   currently names): the existing ordinary path, unchanged — create `S`,
   advance `implementation_revision` by exactly one.
2. **Exact retry** (live HEAD is itself the already-recorded,
   content-verified current `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit `T`
   for the work item's current `implementation_revision` — i.e. nothing
   has been committed since `T`): create nothing, report existing success
   — the only case the pre-revision-35 text actually covered correctly.
3. **Same-content republication** (protected `review_content_id` is
   unchanged **and** live HEAD differs from `T`): run `WFR-62`'s existing
   two-part recovery precondition — (a) content at live HEAD is
   byte-identical to content at `reviewed_implementation_head`; (b) an
   exhaustive, first-parent, commit-by-commit classification of the entire
   `T..HEAD` interval finds no protected or unclassified commit, and any
   generation-record commit found in the interval satisfies its own
   role-specific contract — over the interval `T..HEAD`. If both pass,
   create **exactly one** new commit, shaped identically to `WFR-62`'s
   recovery commit `S2` (first-parent child of live HEAD; touches only
   `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s `phase`/`state_revision`/`last_transition`;
   carries the unchanged `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` value, a
   `Workflow-Supersedes: <T-sha>` trailer, and the ordinary
   `Workflow-Work-Item` trailer — the same recovered-role canonical
   trailer set `D-Commit-Provenance` already defines) — the sole
   difference from a `/recover-implementation-provenance`-authored `S2` is
   **who authors it and from which phase**: here it is
   `record_bundle_generation` itself, authorized identically to its own
   already-established ordinary-`S` authority (D-Approval-Commits), legal
   only when invoked at `post-fix` stage from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` —
   never a separate command, never requiring the additional user
   confirmation `/recover-implementation-provenance` requires, because
   this is not exceptional out-of-band staleness recovery, it is the
   ordinary, in-band outcome of applying review feedback whose findings
   were rejected with evidence or resolved entirely in excluded content.
   Its `phase` mutation is `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` →
   `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` — always a real transition
   here, never value-wise unchanged (unlike a recovery-authored `S2`,
   which is always value-wise unchanged after `GPT-R51-001`) — both are
   legal for a recovered-role commit, distinguished by, and only by, which
   of the two writers is legally invocable from the phase the repository
   is actually in, never ambiguous since exactly one writer is legal per
   phase. If precondition (b) fails (a protected, unclassified, or
   role-invalid commit is found in `T..HEAD` despite byte-identical
   endpoint content — the revert/transient-path scenarios `GPT-R46-002`
   already named), `record_bundle_generation` refuses outright, naming the
   offending commit — this should not be reachable through any documented
   `/apply-implementation-review` disposition path, and exists as a
   fail-closed backstop, not an expected outcome.

`implementation_revision` and `reviewed_implementation_head` are unchanged
by case 3, exactly as they already are by a `WFR-62` recovery — satisfying
the reviewer's "do not silently increment `implementation_revision` merely
to obtain a new trailer key" instruction directly. `WFR-62`'s own
supersession-chain rules (linked list, no fork, no cycle, unique current
tip) are extended, not duplicated: a chain link may now be authored by
either `/recover-implementation-provenance` (source phase
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`) or `record_bundle_generation`
(source phase `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`, case 3 above) — the chain
mechanics themselves (uniqueness, tie-break, interval validation at
approval time) do not distinguish which writer produced which link, only
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Operation contract" paragraph, amended below,
names which writer is legal from which phase.

### `GPT-R51-004` — standing state-machine tests still encode the pre-re-review `REVISE → technical approval` rule

**Fix**: missing-test item 12 is split into two clauses, matching

receive a fresh external review before technical approval can be reached,
never directly. New items 282-283 (below) exercise this split directly as
regression guards distinct from item 12's own state-reachability
assertion.

### `GPT-R52-001` — the recovered-role mutation contract does not permit revision 35's new same-content republication commit

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: `D-Commit-Provenance` condition 4's recovered-role clause is
rewritten to state the two legal recovered-role writer/source
combinations exactly, replacing the value-wise-unchanged/`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`
pairing:

- value-wise unchanged (`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` →
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`) when the commit was written
  by `/recover-implementation-provenance`;
- a real transition (`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` →
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`) when the commit was written
  by `record_bundle_generation`'s same-content-republication branch
  (`D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Same-content post-fix republication"
  subsection);
- a durable source phase of `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` is never legal
  for either writer — that value is never durably stored under revision
  35's computed-gate design (`GPT-R51-001`), so a historical recovered-role
  commit whose parent state names it is malformed provenance, refused
  identically to any other role-contract violation.

The validator distinguishes which of the two combinations applies from the
commit's own parent `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` state (the committed pre-state's
`phase`), then validates the exact corresponding transition — never
inferred from which command happened to run, since a fresh-session replay
or an independently-authored commit is checked against committed state
alone, the same discipline every other role-specific check in this
document already uses. The "Same-content post-fix republication"
subsection's own claim ("both are legal phase sources ... under condition
4") now points at a contract that actually says so.

Four new tests (below) exercise: the recovery writer's own value-wise-unchanged
transition; the republication writer's own real transition; a
historical recovered-role commit sourced from a hand-edited or corrupted
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` refusing outright; and either writer
producing the *other* writer's phase transition (a recovery-authored
commit performing a real `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` transition, or a
republication-authored commit staying value-wise unchanged from
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`) refusing as a role-contract
mismatch, since each writer is legal only from its own disjoint phase.

### `GPT-R53-001` — the implementation-stage `USER_OVERRIDE` basis is unreachable under the `APPROVE`-only computed technical-approval gate

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`'s entry condition (`D-States`) is
restated as basis-neutral, matching the plan stage's own never-narrowed
shape: reachable whenever the current, bundle-matching feedback (if any)
is not `BLOCK` — `BLOCK` alone bars the gate, unchanged and consistent
with D2's own "`BLOCK` never reaches either basis" rule. Feedback that is
missing entirely, bound to a stale (non-current) bundle, current `REVISE`,
or current `APPROVE` all make the gate reachable identically; which of
D2's two bases `/approve-review implementation` actually selects — exact
`EXTERNAL_APPROVE` only for the exact-match-`APPROVE` case, `USER_OVERRIDE`
requiring literal, stage-and-work-item-named confirmation text otherwise —
remains entirely D2's decision, unchanged by this fix. This restores D2's
own, never-revised implementation-stage override contract without
reopening what `GPT-R51-002` actually fixed: that revision's real target
was `D-States`' edge summary and the "Ordinary bundle-publication phase
transition" subsection jointly describing two incompatible destinations
for `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`'s exit — a contradiction resolved entirely
by the verdict-specific edge summary (a `REVISE` round always durably
republishes through `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, never
through a durably stored `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`, which is never a
`phase` value at all per `D-States`' revision-35 "computed gate" rule).
That fix needs no help from an `APPROVE`-only entry condition: D2's own
exact-bundle-match rule already guarantees a `REVISE` round's feedback can
never, by itself, select `EXTERNAL_APPROVE`, and only an explicit,
literal, human `USER_OVERRIDE` — never silent, never automatic — can move
a gate reached on a current `REVISE`'s strength forward. The edge-summary
paragraph (`D-States`) is updated to state this explicitly, so a reader
does not have to re-derive it. `WFR-19` and missing-test item 12 are
updated to match (below); four new items (297-300) exercise: gate

### `GPT-R53-002` — `record_bundle_generation`'s "exact retry" outcome is unreachable from either of its own legal source phases

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above — worked through
independently for both crash scenarios (interruption after an ordinary
`S`, interruption after a same-content-republication `S2`) and found to
recur identically in each: the function's own legal-source-phase gate
and its "exact retry" classification can never both hold at once.

**Fix**: `record_bundle_generation`'s own decision algorithm is narrowed to
its two genuinely reachable outcomes — a genuinely new round (create `S`,
advance `implementation_revision`) or same-content republication (create
`S2`, `implementation_revision` unchanged) — removing the "exact retry"
branch entirely from the function's own body. The crash-recovery case that
branch existed to serve (a fresh session resumed after `S`/`S2` landed but
before the bundle's on-disk files were written) is redefined as a new,
separate, non-phase-gated **bundle-publication resume** contract
(`D-Approval-Commits`, new subsection): the caller-level decision of
whether to invoke `record_bundle_generation` at all, made *before* that
function's phase gate is ever reached — if live HEAD already equals the
round's current, content-verified tip `T`, the resume contract writes the
bundle's files directly and never invokes `record_bundle_generation`;
otherwise, `record_bundle_generation` runs from the current phase (subject
to its own, unchanged legal-source-phase refusal) and produces one of its
two remaining outcomes. This is not a new capability — every revision
since 28 already stated that generating the bundle's files performs no
further `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` write and is therefore, itself, already
non-phase-gated by construction (`D-Approval-Commits`' "The bundle is then
generated from the live HEAD..." paragraph, unchanged); this fix only
names that already-true separation explicitly and gives the interrupted-
resume case an operation that can actually run in the exact state it needs
to run in. `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Same-content post-fix republication"
subsection's "Operation" paragraph, the "Authority and source phase"
paragraph's "third branch" framing (now the second and last outcome, not a
third), and `WFR-61`'s row text are updated to match (below). Six new items
(301-303, plus consequential amendments to 224, 227, 277, 286, 291 — see
`GPT-R53-003` immediately below) exercise: the real crash boundary from
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION`; the same boundary from
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` after a same-content republication; and a
hand-constructed attempt to invoke `record_bundle_generation` directly at
live-HEAD-equals-`T`, confirming the ordinary legal-source-phase check
alone already refuses it, with no special-case branch required inside the
function.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 37 → 38) — external plan review found two blocking security/lifecycle gaps normative sections revision 37 itself left unsynchronized, plus one important atomicity gap (`GPT-R54-001` through `-003`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 37 bundle (`GPT-R54-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, `read-only bundle inspection`), confirmed the plan/mapping's
62-row normalization holds with zero description mismatches, confirmed
`GPT-R53-001` through `-003` correctly fix the direct revision-36 defects,
and returned `Status: REVISE`, two blocking findings plus one important
finding. Both blocking findings were independently re-verified directly
against this repository's own revision-37 text before being accepted.
`GPT-R54-001` against `D-States`' `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` entry
condition and D2 jointly (confirmed: revision 37's "not `BLOCK`" entry
condition made the gate reachable whenever current feedback was missing
entirely, bound to a stale bundle, current `REVISE`, or current `APPROVE`
— treating "missing" and "genuinely not `BLOCK`" as the same predicate.
But `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` is mutable review-workspace state — this
repository's own history already records multiple canonical/archive
feedback-file inversions requiring manual repair — so a current `BLOCK`
could be converted into the exact "missing feedback" state the gate
treats as override-eligible merely by deleting, renaming, or overwriting
its feedback file, with no further Git action. D2 still states `BLOCK`
never reaches either basis; revision 37's rule made that guarantee
depend on evidence that does not durably persist). `GPT-R54-002` against
`D-Approval-Commits`' general two-outcome `record_bundle_generation`
algorithm and `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Same-content post-fix
republication" subsection's "Authority and source phase" paragraph
jointly (confirmed by direct derivation: `D-Approval-Commits`' own
"Identical ... → same-content republication" branch is stated
generically, for either legal source phase, with no phase restriction of
its own; but `D-Commit-Provenance`'s restatement of that exact branch
says it is "legal only when invoked at `post-fix` stage from
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`" — strictly narrower than the branch it
restates. A work item entering `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` whose
protected implementation projection is byte-identical to the value
recomputed at `reviewed_implementation_head` — a no-op implementation
pass, a plan-only correction that ultimately requires no protected
implementation change, or any implementation session whose attempted fix
is reverted before publication — is classified "identical" by the general
algorithm, which requires the same-content-republication outcome; but the
narrower restatement refuses that same invocation, since
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` is not `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`. A
conforming implementation must violate one normative section or the
other for that exact repository state). `GPT-R54-003` against
`D-Approval-Commits`' "Bundle-publication resume" contract (confirmed:
both of its branches say only "write the bundle's files directly
from live HEAD" / "write the bundle's files from the resulting HEAD,"
with no atomicity contract, while `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh` — the
bundled implementation this contract's own text describes — rewrites
`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current/` in place: `CHANGED_FILES.txt`,
`COMMITS.txt`, `DIFF.patch`, deletion/recreation of `current/files/`, and
`MANIFEST.md`, before finally creating the archive. An interruption after
some but not all of those files are rewritten leaves `current/`
representing neither the prior bundle nor a complete new one, directly
contradicting the contract's own "idempotent, safe to run any number of
times" claim — this reopens the same canonical-current principle
`GPT-R43-003` already established: the directory is "the bundle currently
under review," not a scratch workspace). No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R54-001` — a current `BLOCK` can be converted into an override-eligible "missing feedback" state by removing the mutable feedback file

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`'s entry condition (`D-States`) is
narrowed from revision 37's basis-neutral "not `BLOCK`" rule to an
explicit positive-membership test: the current external
`REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` is read and, using `WFR-03`/`D2`'s existing exact
three-field binding check plus a successful `Status:` parse, classified
into exactly one of five states — current `APPROVE`, current `REVISE`,
current `BLOCK`, bound to a stale/different bundle, or missing/
unparseable. The gate is reachable for exactly the first two and refuses
for the other three identically — `BLOCK`, stale/mismatched, and missing/
unparseable feedback all now produce the same outcome, closing the gap
where losing a `BLOCK` file's evidence silently converted it into an
override-eligible state. `GPT-R53-001`'s own restoration (implementation-
stage `USER_OVERRIDE` reachable against a current `REVISE`, mirroring D2's
never-revised, never-stage-scoped override contract) remains fully
intact: a current `REVISE` still reaches the gate and D2's `USER_OVERRIDE`
basis is still reachable against it, exactly as `GPT-R53-001` restored —
this fix only removes the two cases (missing, stale/mismatched) that
restoration never needed to cover. `D-States`, `WFR-19`, and missing-test
items 12/297/298 are updated to match (below); six new items (304-309)
exercise: current `BLOCK` refuses; deleting/renaming/overwriting that
exact `BLOCK` feedback still refuses; current `REVISE` with no override
text refuses; current `REVISE` with exact override text succeeds as
`USER_OVERRIDE`; and missing/stale feedback both refuse identically to
`BLOCK`.

### `GPT-R54-002` — `record_bundle_generation`'s two-outcome algorithm has no legal identical-content outcome from `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION`

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: the "Same-content post-fix republication" subsection's "Authority
and source phase" paragraph (`D-Commit-Provenance`) is widened from
"legal only... from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`" to legal from **either**
of `record_bundle_generation`'s own two legal source phases —
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` or `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` — matching
the general algorithm's own never-phase-restricted "Identical" branch
(`D-Approval-Commits`, unchanged by this fix — it was already correct;
the contradiction was entirely in this subsection's own narrower
restatement of it). The resulting commit's `phase` mutation is a real
transition either way — `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` →
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` when invoked from that phase
(new), `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` → `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
when invoked from that one (unchanged) — so condition 4's recovered-role
"carries only" contract (`D-Commit-Provenance`) widens from two to three
named legal writer/source combinations: `/recover-implementation-provenance`
(value-wise unchanged), `record_bundle_generation` from
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` (a real transition), and
`record_bundle_generation` from `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` (a real
transition, new). `WFR-61`/`WFR-62`'s row text is updated to match
(below); the "Provenance interval" definition's closing "sole mechanism"
sentence, ambiguous once a second source phase for the same writer
exists, is rewritten to name both authorized producers of a longer
interval explicitly (the important consistency note the reviewer raised
alongside this finding). Four new items (310-313) exercise:
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` with genuinely changed content routing
to the unchanged ordinary path; `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` with
unchanged content producing the new same-content-republication outcome;
both legal source phases producing commits distinguished only by their
own real phase transition; and a source/writer combination crossed
incorrectly refusing as a role-contract mismatch.

## Important finding

### `GPT-R54-003` — "Bundle-publication resume" is not atomic and can leave the canonical `current/` bundle partially rewritten

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: the "Bundle-publication resume" contract's shared bundle-file-
writing step (`D-Approval-Commits`) is redefined as a new "Atomic
bundle-file publication" operation, invoked identically by both of the
resume contract's branches: construct the complete candidate bundle in a
temporary sibling directory, never `current/` itself; populate and
validate every required artifact inside the candidate only; write the
candidate's `MANIFEST.md` and independently reproduce
`review_content_id`/`bundle_id` against it before promotion is attempted;
only once every check passes, atomically promote the candidate to
canonical `current/` via a single directory rename — the only moment
canonical content ever changes; on any failure or interruption before
promotion, canonical `current/` is left byte-identical to its
pre-publication state, and a retry reconstructs the same candidate
deterministically; the archive is generated from the verified
candidate/canonical content with its own temp-file-plus-rename
discipline, so a failed archive write never replaces the previously valid
archive. `WFR-61`'s row text is updated to reference this contract
(below). Five new items (314-318) exercise interruption after partial
candidate population, after manifest write but before promotion, during
the promotion step itself, a post-success retry, and an interrupted
archive write — each proving canonical `current/` is always either the
complete old bundle or the complete new one, never a partial mix.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 38 → 39) — external plan review found the revision-38 promotion primitive unimplementable and the `BLOCK` durability fix still incomplete, plus two normative-consistency gaps and one bundle-consistency gap (`GPT-R55-001` through `-005`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 38 bundle (`GPT-R55-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository), confirmed the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with
zero description mismatches, confirmed revision 38 correctly resolves the
direct local contradictions from `GPT-R54`, and returned `Status: REVISE`,
two blocking findings plus three important findings (two normative-
consistency, one bundle-consistency). Both blocking findings were
independently re-verified directly against this repository's own
revision-38 text before being accepted, and both important normative
findings were independently re-verified against the live acceptance
criterion / missing-test text before being accepted. No finding was
rejected.

`GPT-R55-001` against `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file
publication" contract (confirmed by direct derivation, not merely taken
on the reviewer's word: `current/` is, in ordinary operation, an
existing, non-empty directory holding the previous complete bundle —
exactly the state every prior bundle in `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/`
is in right now. A plain `rename`/`os.replace` call cannot atomically
replace an existing non-empty directory with another; on this repository's
own Linux environment that operation raises `OSError: [Errno 39] Directory
not empty`. The two-step `current → backup`, `candidate → current`
fallback the reviewer's own failure scenario rules out is correct to
reject: it leaves an observable interval where `current` is missing, and
an interruption between the two renames can leave the canonical name
absent entirely — worse than revision 38's own claimed guarantee, not
equivalent to it). `GPT-R55-002` against `D-States`'
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` entry condition and D2 jointly (confirmed:
revision 38's positive-membership test reads only the current,
freshly-parsed `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` — there is no durable record anywhere
in this design of what an implementation-stage review verdict *was* the
first time it was observed. Editing a current, correctly-bound `BLOCK`
file's `Status:` line to `REVISE`, and nothing else, produces a file that
is, by every predicate `D-States`/D2 check, indistinguishable from a
legitimate current `REVISE` — same `Reviewed bundle ID:`, same `Reviewed
base commit:`, same `Work item:`, parse-valid. Missing-test item 15
("a `BLOCK` status cannot reach either approval state by any path") and
D2's own "`BLOCK` never reaches either basis" sentence both state a
guarantee revision 38 alone cannot substantiate against this exact
mutation). No finding was rejected for either blocking item.

### `GPT-R55-001` — the "single directory rename over `current/`" atomic promotion is not an implementable replacement operation for an existing non-empty directory

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: the "Atomic bundle-file publication" contract (`D-Approval-Commits`)
is redesigned around immutable, versioned bundle directories
(`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>/`) plus a canonical `current`
that is itself a **symlink**, never a directory holding content. Promotion
becomes a single `rename`/`os.replace` of the `current` symlink name onto
a freshly created symlink pointing at the newly built, fully verified
versioned directory — a rename of one symlink name onto another existing
name is a single directory-entry update on every POSIX filesystem this
tooling runs on, unlike replacing a populated directory. Symlink creation
or replacement failing for any reason aborts the promotion without
touching `current` and without any non-atomic fallback. `WFR-61`'s row
text and missing-test items 314-317 are corrected in place to test the
actual selected primitive (existing non-empty `current`, promotion success,
interruption at the symlink-rename boundary, cleanup/replay); item 318 is
unchanged (the archive's own temp-file-plus-rename discipline was never
the defective part); a new item 319 exercises symlink-unsupported
fail-closed behavior.

### `GPT-R55-002` — revision 38 still does not durably protect a `BLOCK` verdict from same-bundle status mutation

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: a new durable, append-only, git-committed ledger,
`technical_review_block_pins` (new `D2a` design element), records
`{bundle_id, review_content_id, recorded_at}` the first time any workflow
command observes a current, bundle-matching, parse-valid `BLOCK` for the
implementation stage. `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`'s entry condition
(`D-States`, `WFR-19`) gains a second, independent refusal predicate: the
gate refuses whenever a pin exists for the current `bundle_id`, regardless
of what `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` currently says — closing exactly the gap
`GPT-R55-002` raised, since a pin, once recorded against an actually-
observed `BLOCK`, survives any later status-preserving edit of the mutable
file. This is Option A of the three the reviewer offered ("`BLOCK` is
genuinely non-overridable"), chosen over Option B (accept the file as the
sole trusted verdict, weaken D2's "`BLOCK` never reaches either basis"
claim) because: (1) that claim, and missing-test item 15's identical
claim, predate `GPT-R54-001` and are not new inventions this lineage can
casually retreat from; (2) `GPT-R54-001` itself was raised and fixed
specifically because a `BLOCK` verdict, once genuinely issued, must not
become reachable again by any means short of a genuinely regenerated
bundle — Option B would just relocate the same hole one edit later, not
close it; (3) the mechanism costs no new abstraction beyond what this
document already uses everywhere else for evidence that must outlive a
mutable file — a small, git-committed, append-only record, the same shape
`blocking_decisions` and every provenance trailer already take. Option C
(remove implementation-stage `BLOCK` non-overridability entirely) was
rejected for the same reason as (2): it is not a bug fix, it is reversing
a foundational design invariant this document has never previously
questioned. A pin is scoped to its exact `bundle_id` permanently — a
genuinely regenerated bundle (new `bundle_id`, only producible through the
ordinary `record_bundle_generation`/recovery lifecycle) is never affected
by a prior pin. Three new items (320-322) exercise: a pinned `BLOCK`
surviving a status-preserving overwrite; a pin not affecting a later,
genuinely distinct `bundle_id`; and idempotent (non-duplicating) pin
recording.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 39 → 40) — external plan review found the revision-39 symlink redesign's steady-state primitive correct but its one-time migration and archive contract missing, plus two hardening gaps and one bundle-evidence gap (`GPT-R56-001` through `-005`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 39 bundle (`GPT-R56-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, re-confirmed again while applying this disposition), confirmed
the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with zero description
mismatches, confirmed revision 39 correctly resolves the direct local
contradictions from `GPT-R55-001` (steady-state case)/`-002` (normal
command-driven operation)/`-003`/`-004`, and returned `Status: REVISE`,
two blocking findings plus three "important"/"bundle consistency"
findings. All five were independently re-verified directly against this
repository's own revision-39 text and the actual `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh`
tar invocation before being accepted. No finding was rejected.

`GPT-R56-001` against `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file
publication" contract (confirmed by direct derivation: every scoped
bundle presently under `.ai-review/` — including `workflow-v2-1-core`'s
own — has `current/` as a real, non-empty directory holding the previous
complete bundle, exactly the pre-symlink representation revision 39's own
step 5 assumes is never the case; revision 39 defined the promotion
rename only for the case where `current` already resolves through a
symlink, and named no transition into that representation at all — the
first attempted promotion would still call `os.replace(temp_symlink,
"current")` against an existing, non-empty, non-symlink directory, which
fails closed exactly as `GPT-R55-001` already proved for the pre-symlink
design). `GPT-R56-002` against the same contract's step 10 (confirmed
directly against `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh:360-361`: the archive line
reads exactly `tar -czf "$ARCHIVE" -C "$ROOT_DIR" current`, with no `-h`/
`--dereference` flag; GNU/POSIX `tar` does not follow symlinks by
default, so once `current` is a symlink this invocation archives one
symlink member, `current -> bundles/<token>`, and nothing else — an
external reviewer extracting the archive outside `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/`
finds a dangling link and no bundle content at all). No finding was
rejected for either blocking item.

### `GPT-R56-001` — no transition is defined from the existing non-empty `current/` directory to the new `current` symlink representation

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: a new named subsection, "One-time `current/`-to-symlink
migration," is added to `D-Approval-Commits`, immediately before "Atomic
bundle-file publication," which that contract's own step 1 now
references as a precondition:

- **When it runs**: automatically, as the first thing any "Atomic
  bundle-file publication" attempt does, for any work item whose
  `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current` currently exists and is a real
  directory (`os.path.islink` false, `os.path.isdir` true) rather than
  already a symlink. This is a one-time, per-work-item event — once
  `current` is a symlink, this precondition is never true again for that
  work item — requiring no separate command, opt-in flag, or explicit
  user action, the same automatic-on-first-access precedent `WFR-27`'s
  own flat-to-scoped migration already set for this exact directory tree.
  No migration runs, and none is needed, when `current` is already a
  symlink or is entirely absent (a work item that has never published a
  bundle at all — the ordinary, already-legal empty state).
- **Mechanism**: two ordinary POSIX renames, in order, both onto
  previously-absent target names — never a copy, and never the
  operation `GPT-R55-001`/`GPT-R56-001` proved impossible (replacing an
  existing non-empty directory):
  1. `os.rename`/`os.replace` the existing `current/` directory itself
     onto a fresh, collision-free `bundles/<token>/` path (same `<token>`
     scheme "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1 already defines) —
     renaming an existing directory onto an *absent* target path is a
     single, ordinary, atomic directory-entry update on every POSIX
     filesystem this tooling runs on, unlike replacing a *populated*
     target, which is the operation that fails. After this step, the
     name `current` does not exist on disk at all, and the former
     `current/` directory's complete content — whatever it was, exactly
     byte-identical, since a rename moves an inode without touching its
     contents — is preserved intact under the new versioned path.
  2. Immediately create the `current` symlink pointing at that same
     `bundles/<token>/` path, via the identical temporary-symlink-then-
     atomic-rename primitive step 5 of "Atomic bundle-file publication"
     already uses (create at a temporary path, then `os.replace` it onto
     the name `current` — now legal, because step 1 above already made
     `current` absent, so this is a rename onto a non-existent name, not
     a populated directory).
- **Interruption window**: steps 1 and 2 above are two separate
  filesystem operations — no single POSIX syscall can rename a directory
  and create a symlink atomically together — so there is a real, but
  narrow and synchronous, interval between them where `current` is
  observably absent from the filesystem. This is the "short no-current
  interval... explicitly allowed because migration occurs only at a
  quiescent, user-gated boundary" option the review offered: this
  tooling is a local, single-operator CLI with no concurrent-process
  access to `.ai-review/` claimed or required anywhere else in this
  design, migration runs synchronously inside the one command already
  performing a publication the user initiated, and the window spans only
  the two syscalls themselves, with no candidate-bundle construction (the
  slow part of publication) permitted to start until migration, if
  needed, has already completed — see the ordering guarantee below.
- **Fresh-session recovery**: because an *ordinary* (non-migration)
  promotion only ever replaces one symlink name with another — a single
  atomic `os.replace` that POSIX guarantees is indivisible — `current`
  being observably absent from the filesystem is a state reachable
  **only** from an interrupted migration (steps 1/2 above) or from a work
  item that has never published a bundle at all. A fresh session
  resuming any publication attempt therefore classifies this exactly:
  - `bundles/` absent or empty: never migrated, never published — the
    ordinary, already-legal "no bundle exists yet" state; no recovery
    action, proceed directly to ordinary candidate construction (which
    itself needs no pre-existing `current` to build from).
  - Exactly one `bundles/<token>/` directory exists and `current` is
    absent: this is step 1 having completed and step 2 not yet run (or
    interrupted mid-way) — recovery completes **only** step 2 (create the
    `current` symlink pointing at this directory); step 1 (the directory
    rename) is never re-attempted or re-verified for content
    completeness, because a completed rename is, by POSIX's own atomicity
    guarantee, either fully done with the source directory's exact prior
    content or not done at all (visible as the "`bundles/` absent" case
    above) — there is no partial-rename state to detect or repair.
  - More than one `bundles/<token>/` directory exists while `current` is
    absent: unreachable in conforming operation, since ordinary
    candidate-directory construction (steps 1-4 of "Atomic bundle-file
    publication") is never permitted to begin while `current` is missing
    — migration must complete (or be detected-and-resumed to completion)
    strictly before any new candidate is built, by this same
    fresh-session check running first. A command encountering this state
    anyway (e.g., a hand-edited or externally corrupted `.ai-review/`
    tree) fails closed and reports the inconsistency rather than
    guessing which directory is authoritative — the same "never trust an
    unexplained filesystem/state shape" discipline this design applies
    to every other multi-step recovery it defines.
- **Once migration completes** (`current` resolves to a symlink), the
  ordinary "Atomic bundle-file publication" contract runs completely
  unmodified from its existing step 1 onward — migration is strictly a
  one-time precondition, never a recurring step, and the newly-migrated
  versioned directory becomes an ordinary superseded version the instant
  the very next promotion completes.
- Item 314 (already amended, revision 39) needs no further change — it
  already only describes the steady-state candidate-construction
  interruption, unaffected by migration timing. New items 323-324
  (below) cover the migration mechanism and its own interruption/recovery
  path end to end.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file
publication" contract (new subsection), `WFR-61`, missing-test items
323-324.

### `GPT-R56-002` — the archive contract does not specify symlink dereferencing, so the existing tar path would archive only the `current` symlink and produce an unusable review bundle

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 10 is restated with one
exact, concrete archive representation instead of the prior "resolved
through the symlink" prose: the archive is generated with GNU `tar`'s
dereferencing mode — `tar -czf review-bundle.tar.gz -C
.ai-review/<work_item_id> -h current` (the `-h`/`--dereference` flag
added to the existing invocation) — which follows the top-level `current`
symlink and archives the directory it points to, storing its contents
under the symlink's own archived name (`current/...`), never the
versioned directory's own `bundles/<token>/...` name. This is a
deliberate, minimal restatement of the *existing* command
(`scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh:360-361`), not a new archival mechanism:
one flag, no new dependency, no change to the temp-file-plus-rename
discipline step 10 already specifies for the archive file itself
(unaffected, still correct, `GPT-R54-003`). The resulting archive
contains only ordinary regular files and directories under a top-level
`current/` name — no symlink whose target exists only in the source
worktree survives into the archive, satisfying the review's portability
requirement directly: an archive extracted anywhere, on any machine, into
an empty directory, is immediately a self-contained, ordinary `current/`
bundle directory, exactly as every reader upstream of the symlink
redesign already assumes. New item 325 (below) extracts a generated
archive into an unrelated empty temporary directory and independently
reproduces `bundle_id` from the extracted content, proving the round trip
end to end — the same standard this design already holds every other
identifier-reproduction claim to.

**Affected areas:** "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 10,
`scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh` (design contract only — the actual `-h`
flag addition is `WF8b` implementation work, not this plan-only
revision), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 325.

## Important findings

### `GPT-R56-003` — atomic symlink replacement does not by itself give multi-file readers snapshot consistency, and opportunistic cleanup can invalidate a reader's old target

**Severity:** important (hardening/concurrency, not a likely manual
happy-path failure — the plan explicitly claimed this guarantee, so the
gap is real even though this tooling's normal single-operator usage
rarely exercises it).

**Confirmed**: `compute_bundle_id` (`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py`)
enumerates and reads multiple paths under the bundle root across one
logical operation; nothing in revision 39's text requires resolving
`current` only once for that operation, and step 9's cleanup rule
("eligible for cleanup, opportunistically... never required to be atomic
with promotion") states no retention guarantee for a version directory a
slower reader might still be using.

**Fix**: two changes to "Atomic bundle-file publication":

- A new "Reader snapshot semantics" clause: every reader of bundle
  content — `compute_bundle_id`, manifest regeneration, `/approve-review`'s
  local generation-head check, and any future multi-path consumer of
  `current/` — resolves `current` to its concrete `bundles/<token>/`
  target **exactly once**, at the start of its operation, and performs
  every subsequent file read for that operation against the resolved,
  pinned path directly, never through the `current` name a second time
  and never re-resolving mid-operation. A promotion may replace the
  `current` pointer concurrently with an in-progress read; because the
  reader already pinned a concrete target before that happened, its own
  view stays internally consistent regardless (either entirely the old
  bundle's content or entirely the new one's, per whichever target it
  resolved first — never a mix).
- Step 9 (cleanup) is narrowed from "eligible for cleanup,
  opportunistically, by a later promotion or an explicit maintenance
  step" to: **automatic cleanup of superseded version directories is
  removed from ordinary publication entirely.** No promotion ever deletes
  a `bundles/<token>/` directory as a side effect of publishing a new one.
  Cleanup, if ever performed, is a separate, explicit, later maintenance
  action, run only when no workflow command is active — trading
  unbounded local disk growth under `bundles/` (accumulated superseded
  versions) for the simplest correct concurrency story, with no
  reader-registration or reference-counting protocol needed. `.ai-review/`
  is fully gitignored and local-only (`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`), so this is a
  disk-hygiene tradeoff, never a correctness or repository-size one; a
  human clearing `bundles/` by hand between rounds remains available and
  loses nothing, since only the `current` symlink's own target is ever
  canonical. This closes the reader/cleanup interaction directly, rather
  than trying to define a reader-lifetime rule against a cleanup policy
  that could still race it.

New item 326 (below) exercises the reader-pinning guarantee directly
(pin the old target, promote, finish reading the old target
consistently, confirm a fresh reader started after promotion sees only
the new target); new item 327 confirms ordinary publication never
deletes a superseded version directory.

**Affected areas:** "Atomic bundle-file publication" (new "Reader
snapshot semantics" clause; step 9 narrowed), `WFR-61`, missing-test
items 326-327.

### `GPT-R56-004` — `technical_review_block_pins` is called append-only/permanent, but the validator does not prevent pin deletion or mutation

**Severity:** important (requires a tracked `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` edit,
not merely editing the gitignored feedback file, so materially less
likely than `GPT-R55-002`'s original scenario — but it contradicts the
explicit append-only/permanent governance guarantee `D2a` states, and
this design already treats hand-edited/malformed tracked state as
something validators must fail closed on everywhere else).

**Confirmed**: `D3`'s validator rule (added revision 39) rejects only
"two `technical_review_block_pins` entries for the same `bundle_id`
within one work item" — a later tracked edit that removes an existing
pin, changes an existing pin's `bundle_id`/`review_content_id`/
`recorded_at`, or replaces the array wholesale produces a state file
with **zero** duplicate `bundle_id`s, which that rule alone cannot
distinguish from a legitimately smaller or edited, but still
duplicate-free, array.

**Fix**: append-only monotonicity is made an enforced invariant of every
state write that touches `technical_review_block_pins`, not merely a
prose claim: the candidate array is compared against the first-parent
committed pre-state's array (the same first-parent-comparison idiom
`D-Commit-Provenance`'s provenance-interval checks already use elsewhere
in this design, not a new validation mechanism) and the write is rejected
unless every pin present in the pre-state remains present in the
candidate, field-identical (`bundle_id`, `review_content_id`,
`recorded_at` all unchanged) and in the same relative order, with the
**only** legal difference being the append of zero or one new,
previously-unseen-`bundle_id` pin at the end (`PinLedgerMonotonicityError`,
naming convention matching this document's other fail-closed validator
errors). `D2a`'s own writer already only ever appends one new pin per
observation (unchanged); this check is defense in depth against any
*other* tracked-state write — hand-edited or otherwise — that might
disturb the array, closing exactly the gap `GPT-R56-004` raised without
introducing a second source of truth (a Git-provenance-discovered ledger,
the review's alternative option, was considered and rejected: it would
duplicate information the tracked JSON array already carries reliably
once this comparison exists, for no added guarantee this design's other
first-parent checks don't already provide). This is checked at every
state write, not only at `D2a`'s own pin-recording moment, so a
later, unrelated commit that happens to also touch this field is caught
identically.

New item 328 (below) exercises all four review-specified sub-cases in
one integration test: delete an existing pin → refused; mutate an
existing pin's `bundle_id`/other field → refused; append one valid new
pin → succeeds; a duplicate-`bundle_id` append (the pre-existing revision
39 check) continues to refuse.

**Affected areas:** `D3`'s validator (strengthened rule), `D2a`
(cross-reference to the strengthened rule), `WFR-61`, missing-test item
328.
