## WF8b finding disposition (revision 40 → 41) — external plan review found the revision-40 one-time migration contract correct in concept but unrunnable on this repository's own actual starting shape, plus a second concrete recovery-ambiguity gap, two further hardening gaps, and one non-blocking observation (`GPT-R57-001` through `-005`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 40 bundle (`GPT-R57-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, re-confirmed again while applying this disposition), confirmed
the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with zero description
mismatches, confirmed revision 40 correctly fixes the steady-state archive
dereference rule, reader-pinning intent, reviewer evidence count, and the
ordinary command-driven `BLOCK`-pin mutation cases raised in `GPT-R56-*`,
and returned `Status: REVISE`, two blocking findings plus three
"important"/"hardening" findings and one explicitly non-blocking
observation. All five findings were independently re-verified directly
against this repository's own revision-40 text — including reproducing
`GPT-R57-001`'s exact failure with a live Python `os.rename` call against
this repository's actual `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/` directory
(`current/` present, `bundles/` absent, confirmed via `ls`) — before being
accepted. No finding was rejected.

`GPT-R57-001` against the "One-time `current/`-to-symlink migration"
subsection's step 1 (confirmed by direct reproduction: this repository's
own `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/` presently has `current/` as a real,
non-empty directory and no `bundles/` directory at all — exactly the
starting shape the recovery classifier's own "`bundles/` absent or empty:
never migrated, never published" branch says is the normal, expected
precondition — and revision 40's migration step 1 renames `current/`
directly onto `bundles/<token>/` with no earlier step that creates
`bundles/`; Python's `os.rename`/`os.replace` does not create a missing
parent directory, so this call raises `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No
such file or directory` against exactly this shape). `GPT-R57-002`
against the same subsection's fresh-session recovery classifier
(confirmed by direct derivation: "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1,
unchanged by revision 40, builds the candidate directly inside
`bundles/<token>/`, so an ordinary first-ever publication — a work item
that has never published a bundle, `current` absent from the start —
interrupted after step 1 creates `bundles/<token>/` but before step 5
promotes it produces exactly the filesystem shape "`current` absent,
exactly one `bundles/<token>/` directory" the recovery classifier treats
as proof that migration step 1 completed and only step 2 remains; the
classifier's own justification for skipping re-verification — "a
completed rename is, by POSIX's own atomicity guarantee, either fully
done with the source's exact prior content or not done at all" — is true
only of content that arrived via a completed rename of an already-valid
source directory, which describes migration's own step 1 but not an
ordinary candidate still being incrementally populated and validated by
steps 2-4; recovery would therefore promote a partial, unverified
candidate as canonical, violating the core publication guarantee that
`current` never names unverified content). No finding was rejected for
either blocking item.

### `GPT-R57-001` — the migration renames onto `bundles/<token>/` before the plan ever creates the `bundles/` parent directory

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above, including a live
reproduction of the exact `FileNotFoundError` against this repository's
own current on-disk shape.

**Fix**: both the migration subsection and "Atomic bundle-file
publication" gain a shared, idempotent precondition — **"Version-store
parent directories"** — run at the very start of either operation, before
anything is ever renamed onto a `bundles/<token>/` or `staging/<token>/`
path: `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/` and
`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/staging/` (the latter new, see `GPT-R57-002`
below) are each created via an idempotent directory-creation call
(`os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)`), safe to call unconditionally on
every invocation, including when the directory already exists from a
prior round. If either path already exists but is not itself a real
directory (a stray file or a symlink left by external tampering), the
operation refuses outright and fails closed, reporting the inconsistency
— the same "never trust an unexplained filesystem shape" discipline this
design already applies to the migration recovery classifier's own
"more than one `bundles/<token>/`" branch. With this precondition in
place, migration step 1's rename always targets a path whose parent
directory already exists, on every invocation, including the very first
one against this repository's own actual current shape.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "One-time `current/`-to-symlink
migration" subsection (new precondition), "Atomic bundle-file
publication" (same precondition, shared), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 329
(new, below).

### `GPT-R57-002` — "`current` absent, exactly one `bundles/<token>/`" is not unique to an interrupted migration; an interrupted first-ever candidate build produces the identical shape

**Confirmed**, per the "Origin" verification above.

**Fix**: "Atomic bundle-file publication" adopts the review's Option A —
a separate staging namespace — collapsing the ambiguity structurally
rather than trying to distinguish the two origins after the fact. Step 1
no longer builds the candidate directly inside `bundles/<token>/`;
instead it builds inside a new, sibling
`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/staging/<token>/` directory (same `<token>`
scheme, never itself treated as canonical by any reader, exactly as
`bundles/` entries are canonical only through `current`). Steps 2-4
(populate/validate every required artifact, write `MANIFEST.md`,
independently reproduce `review_content_id`/`bundle_id`) operate against
the staging directory exactly as before, unchanged in substance. Only
once every one of steps 2-4 passes does a new step — **step 4a,
"Promote candidate to version store"** — rename the now fully verified
`staging/<token>/` directory onto `bundles/<token>/`: an ordinary rename
onto a previously-absent target, identical in kind to the migration
subsection's own step 1 rename and covered by the same POSIX atomicity
argument, so this rename can never leave a partially-built
`bundles/<token>/` on disk. Only after step 4a does promotion (the
symlink swap, former step 5, renumbered step 5 unchanged in mechanism)
proceed.

This establishes one invariant every reader and every recovery path can
now rely on: **a `bundles/<token>/` directory, once it exists, is always
complete and identity-verified — never a partial, in-progress candidate**
— regardless of whether it arrived via the migration subsection's
validated-legacy-directory rename (`GPT-R57-003` below) or via this
staged-candidate promotion. The fresh-session recovery classifier is
restated accordingly, and simplifies rather than grows: "`current`
absent, exactly one `bundles/<token>/` directory present" now has exactly
one legal recovery action — complete the symlink-creation step pointing
at that directory — regardless of whether the directory arrived through
migration or through an interrupted-then-resumed ordinary publication,
because both origins now guarantee the same completeness property before
a directory is ever placed under `bundles/`. No re-verification of
`bundles/<token>/` content is performed in this branch, exactly as
revision 40 already argued for the migration-only case — the argument
now applies unconditionally because the precondition it relies on (a
completed rename of already-valid content) is now true for every entry
under `bundles/`, not only migrated ones.

An interruption still mid-`staging/` (before step 4a's promotion rename)
leaves `current` **unchanged** for every round after the first (only the
final symlink swap ever touches `current`, and step 4a's rename touches
neither `current` nor `bundles/`'s existing entries), so no new ambiguity
is introduced there; for a genuinely first-ever publication interrupted
at this same point, `current` is absent and `bundles/` remains absent or
empty — the pre-existing, unchanged "never migrated, never published"
branch, safe as before. A retry after any staging-phase interruption
builds a fresh candidate under a new `<token>` in `staging/`, never
reusing or resuming the interrupted attempt's own directory — the
identical "never reused or resumed in place" rule this design already
applies to an interrupted promotion retry (unchanged, `GPT-R55-001`). An
abandoned `staging/<token>/` directory is never treated as canonical by
any reader and needs no special cleanup guarantee beyond the one
`bundles/` already has (safe to leave in place; cleanup, if ever
performed, is the same separate, explicit, later maintenance action step
9 already defines, extended to cover `staging/` for consistency, not a
new policy).

New item 330 (below) exercises the disambiguation directly: an
interrupted first-ever publication (partial `staging/<token>/`, `current`
absent, `bundles/` absent) resumes by discarding the stale staging
attempt and building fresh, never promoting partial content; a
migration-interrupted state (`current` absent, exactly one verified
`bundles/<token>/`) resumes by completing only the symlink step, exactly
as before, now justified unconditionally rather than by a migration-only
argument.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file publication"
contract (new `staging/` namespace, new step 4a, renumbered steps), "One-time
`current/`-to-symlink migration" subsection (recovery classifier
restated, simplified), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 330 (new, below);
items 323-324 amended in place (below).

## Important findings

### `GPT-R57-003` — the migration explicitly refuses to validate the legacy `current/` bundle, so a pre-atomic partial directory could be canonized as an immutable version

**Severity:** important (this repository's own uploaded revision-40
bundle is complete and reproducible, so the immediate activation instance
is unaffected in practice; the gap is in the migration contract's claimed
general recovery semantics for other/future repository states, including
any `.ai-review/` directory that predates the candidate-build/
atomic-promotion redesign `GPT-R54-003` introduced).

**Confirmed**: revision 40's migration text argues only that the step-1
*rename itself* is atomic and content-preserving (true, and unaffected by
this fix) — it never claims, and cannot from that argument alone, that
the *source* `current/` directory was already complete and valid before
the rename. A `current/` directory written in place under the pre-
`GPT-R54-003` regime could have been left partial or mixed by an
interruption that predates this design's own atomic-promotion guarantees
entirely; migrating such a directory verbatim would preserve, not detect,
that pre-existing corruption, and canonize it as an immutable version.

**Fix**: migration's step 0 (preceding step 1's rename) gains a
**legacy-content validation** requirement: before the existing real
`current/` directory is eligible for the step-1 rename, it is validated
using the identical completeness/identity check "Atomic bundle-file
publication" steps 2-4 already require of every candidate before
promotion — every required artifact present, `MANIFEST.md` present and
well-formed, and `review_content_id`/`bundle_id` independently reproduced
from the directory's own content and confirmed to match `MANIFEST.md`'s
recorded values. Only a `current/` directory that passes this exact check
proceeds to step 1. A `current/` directory that fails it is **not**
migrated, not moved, not deleted, and not silently repaired — migration
refuses outright and fails closed, reporting the specific validation
failure and leaving the legacy directory completely untouched for
explicit operator inspection and recovery, the same fail-closed,
no-automatic-data-loss discipline this design already applies to the
recovery classifier's own "more than one `bundles/<token>/`" branch and
to `GPT-R57-001`'s new parent-directory-type check above. No automatic
quarantine, discard, or rebuild is performed — fabricating a destructive
recovery policy for data an operator may still need to inspect is a
larger risk than stopping and asking.

New item 331 (below) exercises both branches: a well-formed legacy
`current/` migrates exactly as before; a legacy `current/` with a missing
required artifact, a missing/corrupt `MANIFEST.md`, or a
`review_content_id`/`bundle_id` mismatch against its own content refuses
migration outright, leaves the directory byte-for-byte untouched, and
reports the specific failure.

**Affected areas:** "One-time `current/`-to-symlink migration" subsection
(new legacy-validation precondition), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 331
(new, below).

### `GPT-R57-004` — a symlink-unavailable failure during migration violates the plan's own "abort without touching `current`" guarantee

**Severity:** important (low-likelihood on this repository's documented
Linux/POSIX environment, where symlinks are expected to work — but it
directly contradicts the explicit fail-closed unsupported-filesystem
behavior revisions 39/40 already claim for the steady-state case).

**Confirmed**: "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 8's "abort without
touching `current`" guarantee is true only once `current` already
resolves through a symlink — an ordinary promotion never removes the
existing `current` symlink until the moment it atomically replaces it
with a new one. During migration, that precondition does not hold: step
1 moves the *real* `current/` directory away first, so `current` is
already absent by the time step 2 attempts symlink creation; if step 2
fails or the platform does not support symlinks at all, the workflow is
left with `current` missing and no path back to the previously valid
canonical directory, on a filesystem that can never complete the
documented fresh-session recovery either.

**Fix**: migration's step 0 gains a **symlink-capability preflight**,
run before step 1's rename ever touches the real `current/` directory:
create a disposable, uniquely-named temporary symlink at a fresh,
collision-free path inside `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/` (pointing at an
arbitrary existing target, such as the `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/`
directory itself), then immediately remove it — proving `os.symlink` is
supported and functional on this filesystem's own mount before the point
of no return. If this preflight raises `OSError`, `NotImplementedError`,
or any other failure, migration aborts immediately, having performed no
rename of the real `current/` directory at all — the identical
"abort without touching `current`" guarantee step 8 already provides for
steady-state promotion, now also true for migration's own irreversible
first step. Only once the preflight succeeds does step 1's rename
proceed, immediately followed by step 2's symlink creation, which by
construction can no longer fail for capability reasons (having just been
proven to work on the same filesystem moments earlier) — an ordinary
`OSError` from a transient cause (e.g., disk full) between preflight and
step 2 is still possible and still leaves `current` missing with no
automatic rollback, but this is now a narrow, already-inherent
interruption-recovery case the migration subsection's existing
fresh-session classifier already handles (an incomplete migration is
detected and resumed on the next invocation), not an unsupported-platform
case with no recovery path at all.

New item 332 (below) exercises the preflight directly: a simulated
symlink-unsupported filesystem (`OSError`/`NotImplementedError` from the
preflight's own temporary symlink attempt) aborts migration before the
real `current/` directory is touched, leaving it byte-identical to its
pre-migration state; a working filesystem proceeds through preflight,
rename, and symlink creation exactly as revision 40 already specified.

**Affected areas:** "One-time `current/`-to-symlink migration" subsection
(new symlink-capability preflight precondition), `WFR-61`, missing-test
item 332 (new, below).

### `GPT-R57-005` — the archive step bypasses revision 40's own "pin `current` once" reader-snapshot rule

**Severity:** important (concurrency hardening, not a likely manual
happy-path failure — this tooling's normal single-operator sequential
usage rarely exercises a concurrent promotion during archive creation,
but revision 40 explicitly promised this guarantee for every multi-file
reader, and the archive command is one).

**Confirmed**: the "Reader snapshot semantics" clause (revision 40)
requires every multi-file reader of bundle content to resolve `current`
to its concrete `bundles/<token>/` target exactly once, at the start of
its own operation, and read only against that pinned path thereafter.
Step 10's exact archive command, `tar -czf review-bundle.tar.gz -C
.ai-review/<work_item_id> -h current`, hands `tar` the mutable `current`
name directly — `tar` itself resolves that name (once, via `-h`'s
dereference), but nothing in the surrounding contract requires the
*caller* to have already pinned a concrete target before invoking `tar`,
so the archive operation does not itself follow the same pin-once
discipline required of `compute_bundle_id` and every other reader in the
same section.

**Fix**: step 10 is restated to resolve `current` to its concrete target
exactly once, via the same "Reader snapshot semantics" rule the same
section already requires of every other reader, and then archive that
already-resolved, concrete `bundles/<token>/` directory **directly**,
remapping its top-level path component to the fixed archive name
`current` via `tar`'s member-name transform, rather than handing `tar` a
name to resolve itself:

```
tar -czf review-bundle.tar.gz -C .ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles \
    --transform 's,^<token>,current,' <token>
```

where `<token>` is the concrete directory name `current` resolved to at
the start of this archive operation (the pinning step), not re-resolved
at any point during the `tar` invocation itself. Because the path handed
to `tar` is now the already-resolved real directory rather than the
mutable `current` symlink, no dereference flag is structurally needed any
longer — there is no symlink left in the path being archived at all —
which is not a regression of `GPT-R56-002`'s own portability requirement:
the resulting archive still contains only ordinary regular files and
directories under a top-level `current/` name (via the `--transform`
rename), still self-contained, still extracts anywhere into an ordinary
`current/` bundle directory, and item 325's existing extract-and-
reproduce-`bundle_id` test continues to verify this end to end unchanged.
The `-h`/`--dereference` mechanism revision 40 specified is superseded by
this more robust mechanism precisely because `GPT-R57-005` shows
dereferencing the mutable name at `tar`-invocation time does not, by
itself, satisfy the concurrent-reader pin-once contract revision 40 itself
introduced in the same revision — the *guarantee* (portable,
self-contained, ordinary `current/`-named archive) is unchanged; only the
concrete mechanism producing it is.

New item 333 (below) exercises the concurrency property directly: pin
`current`'s target, initiate archive creation from that pinned target,
promote to a new target mid-operation, confirm the resulting archive
still reproduces the originally pinned bundle's `bundle_id` exactly (not
the post-promotion target's) — the same pattern item 326 already
established for `compute_bundle_id`, now also proven for archive
creation.

**Affected areas:** "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 10 (restated
archive mechanism), `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh` (design contract
only — the actual command change is `WF8b` implementation work, not this
plan-only revision), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 333 (new, below).

## Non-blocking observation — not applied this revision

The reviewer's own feedback separately raised a hardening observation
about `technical_review_block_pins`' "permanent even against hand-edited
tracked state" claim: a single immediate first-parent comparison
(`GPT-R56-004`'s fix, unchanged this revision) cannot prove permanence
against arbitrary later Git history — a manual pin-deletion commit
followed by an unrelated commit before the next workflow validation would
present a shortened ledger as the new immediate first-parent state. The
reviewer explicitly stated this "requires direct tracked-state tampering
plus additional Git history and is well outside normal operation" and
declined to make it an additional blocking finding for revision 40,
offering it only as something to consider if the word "permanent" is
meant to cover arbitrary committed tampering rather than
workflow-command-mediated writes. This revision makes the same choice the
reviewer's own text anticipated: not applied, since `D2a`/`D3`'s existing
first-parent monotonicity check already covers every write path this
design's own commands ever produce, and defending against arbitrary
hand-crafted Git history that bypasses every command in this workflow
entirely is outside this design's threat model, consistent with how every
other validator in this document (`D-Commit-Provenance`'s trailer checks,
`D3`'s other invariants) is scoped to workflow-command-mediated state, not
to unbounded tracked-state forgery. No `D2a`/`D3` text changes as a result
of this observation.

### `GPT-R58-001` — the canonical `current` symlink's exact target representation is undefined; the obvious repo-relative implementation produces a broken symlink

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: neither the "One-time
`current/`-to-symlink migration" subsection's step 1.2 nor "Atomic
bundle-file publication" step 5 ever stated the literal string passed to
`os.symlink`, only prose such as "that same `bundles/<token>/` path."
Every other mention of the target directory in this document uses the
fuller `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>` spelling, which is not
a legal relative-symlink payload for a link living at
`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current`: POSIX/Python resolve a relative
symlink target against the link's own parent directory
(`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/`), not the repository root, so that spelling
resolves to the nonexistent, duplicated-prefix path
`.ai-review/<work_item_id>/.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>` —
independently reproduced directly against this repository's own
Python/Linux environment while applying this disposition, matching the
reviewer's own reproduction exactly.

**Fix**: a new "Canonical `current` symlink target payload" contract
states one exact form — link payload exactly `bundles/<token>` (relative,
no repository/worktree prefix), every temporary symlink en route to
`current` created directly inside `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/` so the same
payload resolves identically once renamed into place, and a mandatory
resolve-and-verify check (absolute/`..`-escaping/cross-work-item/broken
targets all fail closed) before any such symlink is ever renamed onto the
name `current`. Both migration step 1.2 and "Atomic bundle-file
publication" step 5 now cross-reference this single contract rather than
each independently describing the target in prose. New item 334 exercises
`os.readlink(current)` directly after both migration and ordinary
promotion, proving the exact payload and its resolution, plus the
fail-closed rejection of a corrupted target.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "One-time `current/`-to-symlink
migration" subsection (step 1.2), "Atomic bundle-file publication" (new
named contract, step 5), `WFR-61`, missing-test item 334 (new, below).

### `GPT-R58-002` — the fresh-session `current`-absent recovery classifier is specified, but `Atomic bundle-file publication` does not actually invoke it when `current` is absent

**Severity:** important.

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: revision 41's numbered "Atomic
bundle-file publication" step 1 branched only on "`current` exists and is
a real directory" (migration) versus "otherwise" (build a new staging
candidate) — collapsing "`current` is already a symlink" and "`current` is
absent" into the same unconditional "otherwise" branch. The fresh-session
recovery classifier immediately above it was fully specified in prose but
never referenced from step 1's own control flow, so a literal reading of
the numbered algorithm never reaches it: a fresh session finding `current`
absent with exactly one already-verified `bundles/<token>/` directory
waiting would fall through step 1's "otherwise" branch and begin building
a redundant new staging candidate rather than completing the one-bundle
symlink recovery the classifier itself defines.

**Fix**: step 1 is restructured into three explicit, ordered branches —
1a (`current` a real directory: run migration, fall through to 1c), 1b
(`current` absent: run the now explicitly-named "Fresh-session
`current`-absent recovery classifier" immediately above; its one-bundle
branch completes the symlink step and returns immediately without
entering steps 2-4a; its zero-bundle branch falls through to 1c; its
multi-bundle branch fails closed), 1c (`current` already a symlink,
including having just fallen through from 1a or 1b: construct a new
staging candidate, as before). No case's actual recovery *behavior*
changes — revision 41 already specified the correct action for each
filesystem shape — only the numbered algorithm's own control flow now
provably reaches the classifier before candidate construction, closing the
gap between the narrative description and the authoritative numbered
steps. Item 330 is amended in place to describe this same scenario as
driven through step 1's own branches rather than as an unwired,
free-standing description.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file publication"
step 1 (restructured into 1a/1b/1c), "Fresh-session `current`-absent
recovery classifier" (labeled as its own named subsection), `WFR-61`,
missing-test item 330 (amended in place, below).

### `GPT-R59-001` — `current`-absent one-bundle recovery restores the pointer and returns before determining whether publication itself is complete

**Severity:** blocking.

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: the "Fresh-session `current`-absent
recovery classifier"'s "exactly one `bundles/<token>/`" branch and "Atomic
bundle-file publication" step 1b both specified an unconditional
create-symlink-then-return-immediately action for *any* directory found
alone under `bundles/`, regardless of whether that directory's own content
is the round the caller is actually trying to publish. Both worked failure
scenarios reproduce directly against the live text: (A) an interrupted
migration leaves the *previous* round's content as the sole
`bundles/<token>/` entry; recovery would link and return without ever
constructing the *new* round the caller was trying to publish; (B) an
interrupted first-ever publication after step 4a leaves the
current-round candidate correctly placed, but recovery still returned
without ever reaching step 10's archive generation, so
`review-bundle.tar.gz` could remain absent or stale despite `current`
resolving correctly. Neither scenario was distinguishable under the prior
text, which treated "exactly one verified `bundles/<token>/` directory
exists" as sufficient proof of "the requested publication is complete" —
two genuinely different claims, exactly as the reviewer's finding argued.

**Fix**: the one-bundle branch is split into pointer recovery (create the
symlink) followed by an explicit **current-round binding check** comparing
the restored bundle's own `MANIFEST.md` identity (`stage`, `work_item_id`,
the stage's own round field, protected `review_content_id`) against the
round the caller is currently trying to publish — never `generation_head`
alone, since two genuinely different rounds can legitimately share a
`generation_head`. A match means the restored bundle already **is** the
requested round: the operation continues through the remaining
publication-completion steps (9-10, including archive
generation/replacement) before returning success. A mismatch means the
restored bundle is a valid but older round: pointer recovery is complete as
representation recovery only, and the operation falls through to ordinary
candidate construction (step 1c onward) for the round actually requested,
leaving the older directory as an ordinary superseded version. "Atomic
bundle-file publication" step 1b, `WFR-61`'s row text, and items 324/330
are updated to match; new item 335 exercises all three scenarios the
reviewer's "Required tests" list specifies end to end.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "Fresh-session `current`-absent
recovery classifier" (split into pointer recovery + binding check), "Atomic
bundle-file publication" step 1b, `WFR-61`, missing-test items 324, 330
(amended in place), 335 (new, below).

### `GPT-R59-002` — the stated symlink validation cannot reject an absolute payload that points to the correct directory unless the raw link payload is checked

**Severity:** important.

**Confirmed**, by direct reasoning matching the reviewer's own reproduction:
`os.path.realpath` resolves both `bundles/<token>` and
`/absolute/.../bundles/<token>` to the identical real directory when both
genuinely name it, so a resolved-target-equality check alone validates
*where the link points*, never the required canonical *spelling of the
link payload itself* — a corrupted-but-correctly-resolving absolute
payload would pass the prior text's single check.

**Fix**: the "Canonical `current` symlink target payload" contract now
requires two independent checks before any promotion: (1) the raw
`os.readlink` payload equals exactly `bundles/<token>` — rejecting any
non-canonical spelling regardless of where it resolves; (2) the resolved
target equals exactly the intended real directory — rejecting a
canonically-spelled-but-wrong-target payload, an escape, or a
broken/dangling target. Item 334 is amended to inspect both the raw payload
and its resolution, and to exercise a deliberately corrupted absolute
target that resolves correctly but must still be rejected by check 1.

**Affected areas:** `D-Approval-Commits`' "Canonical `current` symlink
target payload" contract, `WFR-61`, missing-test item 334 (amended in
place, below).

### `GPT-R59-003` — Revision 42's live WFR/test inventory still contains pre-fix publication wording

**Severity:** important plan-consistency defect.

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check against both sub-claims: `WFR-61`'s
own row text, inside its revision-41 `GPT-R57-002` clause, still read
"resumes by discarding the stale attempt and building fresh" — the exact
"discard" verb revision 42's own step 7/step 9 reconciliation replaced
everywhere else, missed in this one surviving occurrence; missing-test item
316 still read "the promotion step is a single atomic rename of the
`current` symlink itself onto a freshly built, fully verified versioned
directory" — the pre-`GPT-R57-002` (revision 39-era) model, describing the
opposite rename direction from the authoritative revision-41+ mechanism (a
temporary symlink is renamed onto the name `current`; a directory is never
the rename target of that operation).

**Fix**: `WFR-61`'s surviving "discarding the stale attempt" replaced with
"leaving the stale staging attempt unreferenced," matching step 9's rule;
item 316 rewritten to state the exact current primitive (create validated
temporary symlink → atomically rename/replace that symlink entry onto the
name `current` → `current` resolves to the already-existing verified
`bundles/<token>/` directory). No other live "discard(ed/ing)" or
wrong-direction symlink-rename wording was found in `WFR-61`'s row or items
314-334 on a full re-read of both.

**Affected areas:** `WFR-61` (wording), missing-test item 316 (rewritten in
place, below).

Applied alongside the four findings above, though not itself a `GPT-R59-*`
finding: migration step 1.2 said symlink creation there is "guaranteed to
succeed" once the capability preflight (step 0.3) has passed, while this
same design's own recovery classifier exists precisely because a later
`OSError` remains possible even after a successful preflight. Restated to
say the preflight rules out the known unsupported-symlink capability class,
not that the later syscall is literally guaranteed to succeed — wording
only; the recovery mechanism this note references was already correct and
required no change.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 43 → 44) — external plan review confirmed `GPT-R59-001` through `-004` resolved but found the revision-43 current-round binding check's four-field comparison deliberately excludes `generation_head`, letting a stale same-round bundle be mistaken for the requested publication, plus two important findings against `WFR-61`'s stale wording and an unvalidated pre-existing `current` symlink (`GPT-R60-001` through `-003`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 43 bundle (`GPT-R60-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, re-confirmed again while applying this disposition), confirmed
the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with zero description
mismatches, confirmed `GPT-R59-001` resolved structurally (pointer
recovery and publication completion no longer treated as the same event),
`GPT-R59-002` resolved for symlinks created by conforming
migration/publication, and `GPT-R59-003`/`-004` resolved, and returned
`Status: REVISE`, one blocking finding plus two important findings. All
findings were independently re-verified directly against this
repository's own revision-43 text — re-reading the "Current-round binding
check," the "Fresh-session `current`-absent recovery classifier," step
1c of "Atomic bundle-file publication," and `WFR-61`'s own Verification
cell — before being accepted. No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R60-001` — the current-round recovery binding deliberately omits `generation_head`, allowing a stale bundle from the same protected round to be mistaken for the requested publication

**Severity:** blocking.

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: the "Current-round binding check"
compared only `stage`, `work_item_id`, the stage round number, and
protected `review_content_id`, and its own prose stated `generation_head`
is "deliberately not part of this comparison," reasoning that
`generation_head` equality alone cannot distinguish two different rounds.
That premise is correct — this design's own D-Bundle-Manifest already
gives `generation_head` one precise meaning, "the exact repository HEAD
the bundle was generated from," and same-content republication
(D-Commit-Provenance's own subsection) exists specifically for the case
where two bundles share every round/content field while
`generation_head` legitimately differs, because an excluded-only commit
advanced live HEAD without changing protected content. But the reviewer's
conclusion does not follow from that premise: `generation_head`
insufficiency *alone* is an argument for requiring it *conjunctively*
with the round/content fields, not for omitting it from the comparison
entirely. The worked failure scenario reproduces directly against the
live text: a valid bundle B0 at generation head H0 is superseded by a
required republication at H1 for the identical round (implementation
revision, protected `review_content_id`); if the one-time
representation-migration recovery path is entered while only B0 exists as
the sole `bundles/<token>/` directory, the four-field check reports a
match against B0 even though the caller is trying to publish the H1
bundle, skips candidate construction, and completes the operation
reporting success against a bundle whose own `MANIFEST.md` still records
H0 — later caught only by `assert_local_generation_matches`'s
repository-local staleness check, not by the recovery operation itself,
which is exactly the "publication reports success against a stale
bundle" defect the revision-43 binding check exists to prevent.

**Fix**: the "Current-round binding check" (`D-Approval-Commits`) widens
from four fields to seven — `stage`, `work_item_type`, `work_item_id`,
the stage round number, `base_commit`, protected `review_content_id`,
and `generation_head` — all required to match exactly, with the
**expected** `generation_head` supplied by the publication caller already
in progress (the durable current generation-record tip `T` for
implementation-stage publication, or live repository HEAD at the start
of the attempt for plan-stage publication), never re-derived from the
restored directory. `work_item_type`/`base_commit` are added alongside
`generation_head` because the prior four-field set, despite its own
"full identity binding" label, silently left them out entirely — an
omission distinct from, but adjacent to, the `generation_head` gap.
`WFR-61`'s Verification cell gains a matching acceptance clause; missing-
test items 324/330 (already describing binding-check outcomes) are
amended in place to note their `generation_head` conjunct explicitly, and
item 335 (the binding check's own dedicated scenario item) gains two new
lettered sub-scenarios: (d) same round/content fields, stale
`generation_head` → mismatch, fresh candidate built; (e) a lone
`base_commit`/`work_item_type` disagreement → mismatch, confirming both
newly named fields actually participate in the comparison.

### `GPT-R60-002` — `WFR-61` still contains revision 42's unconditional "restore symlink and return" acceptance statement

**Severity:** important (plan-consistency defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: `WFR-61`'s Verification cell's
revision-42 `GPT-R58-002` clause stated, unconditionally, that a fresh
session with `current` absent and exactly one `bundles/<token>/`
directory "completes only the symlink-creation step and returns without
entering steps 2-4a." Revision 43 correctly replaced that unconditional
behavior with the pointer-recovery-then-binding-check split, and added
its own later acceptance clause describing the new match/mismatch
outcomes, but never revisited the earlier revision-42 sentence still
sitting in the same live cell — leaving two directly contradictory
statements about the same operation's outcome in one machine/test-
authoritative row, with no historical/superseded label distinguishing
them (unlike the row's own `tar -h`/`--dereference` clause, which
revision 42 explicitly marked historical).

**Fix**: the revision-42 `GPT-R58-002` clause is rewritten in place
(matching the reviewer's preferred remedy over accumulating another
historical exception) to state the current two-outcome behavior directly
— completes the symlink-creation step and then, per the binding check,
either returns after completing archive generation/replacement or falls
through into steps 2-4a to build a fresh candidate — with an inline
citation noting the correction and its revision. Items 323-336 were
re-read in full for any other unconditional "one bundle → return"
wording predating the binding check; none was found beyond the one
corrected here.

### `GPT-R60-003` — an existing `current` symlink is treated as trusted steady state without validating the canonical payload/target contract

**Severity:** important (hardening gap).

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: the "Canonical `current` symlink
target payload" contract's raw-payload and resolution checks apply only
to a *temporary* symlink, before it is ever promoted (renamed) onto the
name `current`. "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1c's own text, for
the case where `current` is *already* a symlink, treated that as
"the ordinary steady-state case" and proceeded directly into candidate
construction with no entry validation of the existing link at all —
inconsistent with this design's repeated fail-closed treatment of
unexplained filesystem shapes elsewhere in the same algorithm (step 1d's
refusal of an unexpected non-symlink/non-directory object at `current`,
immediately below).

**Fix**: step 1c now validates an already-existing `current` symlink,
before treating it as steady state, using the same two checks (raw
`os.readlink` payload equals exactly `bundles/<token>`; resolution names
a real directory inside this work item's own `bundles/`) the creation-
time contract already requires — refusing outright, before any staging
directory is built or existing content is read, on an absolute,
`..`-escaping, cross-work-item, or dangling existing link, and leaving it
untouched either way. New missing-test item 337 exercises a canonical
existing symlink (proceeds normally) against each of the four refusing
shapes (absolute-but-resolving, `..`-escaping, cross-work-item, dangling).
`WFR-61`'s Verification cell gains a matching acceptance clause and its
item range extends to 310-337.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 44 → 45) — external plan review confirmed `GPT-R60-001` through `-003` resolved but found the revision-44 current-round binding check still omits `worktree_root`, letting a bundle from another or relocated worktree be mistaken for the requested local publication, plus two important findings against existing-`current` validation strictness and stale migration-match wording (`GPT-R61-001` through `-003`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 44 bundle (`GPT-R61-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, re-confirmed again while applying this disposition), confirmed
the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with zero description
mismatches, confirmed `GPT-R60-001` resolved for `generation_head`
staleness specifically, `GPT-R60-002` resolved for the sentence it
targeted, and `GPT-R60-003` resolved for symlinks already conforming to
the canonical target payload, and returned `Status: REVISE`, one blocking
finding plus two important findings. All findings were independently
re-verified directly against this repository's own revision-44 text —
re-reading the "Current-round binding check," the "Canonical `current`
symlink target payload" contract, step 1c of "Atomic bundle-file
publication," missing-test items 324/330/335, and `WFR-61`'s own
Verification cell — before being accepted. No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R61-001` — the current-round recovery binding still omits `worktree_root`, so a bundle from another/moved worktree can be accepted as the requested local publication

**Severity:** blocking.

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: the "Current-round binding check"
(revision 44) compared exactly `stage`, `work_item_type`, `work_item_id`,
the stage round number, `base_commit`, protected `review_content_id`, and
`generation_head` — seven fields, none of them `worktree_root`. This
design's own `D-Bundle-Manifest` section ("Worktree/HEAD staleness check,"
resolving `OPUS-R6-016` against the actual first-party Milestone-8
incident) already establishes that `generation_head` equality alone
cannot distinguish a genuinely current local bundle from a stale one
generated in a *different* worktree at the identical repository HEAD —
that is precisely why `assert_local_generation_matches` checks both
`worktree_root` and HEAD together, never HEAD alone. The revision-44
binding check added `generation_head` but not its local-staleness
partner. The worked failure scenario reproduces directly: two worktrees
at the same commit `H`, same protected content, same work item, same
round number; bundle B, generated in worktree A
(`worktree_root = /path/A`, `generation_head = H`), is copied, moved, or
otherwise becomes the sole recovered `bundles/<token>/` directory under
worktree B (or worktree A itself is relocated after B was generated); the
revision-44 recovery comparison in worktree B sees all seven compared
fields match and treats B as the requested publication, completing
archive generation and reporting success — only for `/approve-review`'s
own pre-existing `assert_local_generation_matches` check to then, later
and correctly, reject that same bundle as stale. Publication has reported
success for a bundle the workflow's own next local gate already knows is
stale — exactly the class of defect the current-round binding check
exists to prevent, one field short.

**Fix**: the "Current-round binding check" (`D-Approval-Commits`) widens
from seven fields to eight, adding `worktree_root` as a required
conjunct, never a standalone distinguisher (the same non-standalone
argument already made for `generation_head` applies identically: two
different worktrees can share every round/content field and even
`generation_head`, which is exactly the case `worktree_root` alone
distinguishes). Rather than reimplementing the comparison, recovery
reuses `D-Bundle-Manifest`'s existing `assert_local_generation_matches`
predicate directly against the restored directory's `MANIFEST.md` for the
`worktree_root`/`generation_head` portion (treating a raised staleness
error as "mismatch," never a hard failure of the recovery attempt), so
the two call sites — this classifier and `/approve-review` — can never
diverge on what "the same worktree and HEAD" means; the remaining six
round/content fields continue to be compared independently. This check
stays repository-local only, exactly like `assert_local_generation_matches`
itself (`D-Bundle-Manifest`'s portability split, `WFR-17`) — an external
reviewer consuming a portable archive is never asked about
`worktree_root`. `WFR-61`'s Verification cell gains a matching acceptance
clause; item 335 (the binding check's own dedicated scenario item) gains
two new lettered sub-scenarios: (f) same round/content fields and
`generation_head`, different `worktree_root` → mismatch, fresh candidate
built; (g) a relocated worktree's old bundle, recording the previous
absolute `worktree_root` → mismatch against the caller's current root.
Item 335(b)'s existing positive first-publication-origin case is amended
to note it also satisfies the new `worktree_root` conjunct by
construction, covering the reviewer's third required test without a
fourth new sub-scenario.

### `GPT-R61-002` — existing-`current` validation is weaker than the canonical creation-time target contract

**Severity:** important (hardening gap).

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check: the creation-time "Canonical
`current` symlink target payload" contract's resolution check required
resolving to *exactly* the intended `bundles/<token>/` directory the
creating step already knew from its own fresh token. Revision 44's step
1c entry validation of an *already-existing* symlink, despite its own
text claiming "the same two checks," instead required only that
resolution land *somewhere inside* this work item's `bundles/` — a
strictly weaker property. Without a stated token grammar or a check that
`bundles/<token>` is itself a real, non-symlink directory, a raw payload
naming a nested path, or `bundles/<token>` itself being an alias
(`bundles/A -> bundles/B`), could satisfy the literal revision-44 wording
without matching creation time's actual strictness. A conforming
publisher never produces these states, so this is primarily a
fail-closed corruption/tampering gap, not a reachable defect in ordinary
operation — but the two validation call sites had already drifted apart
in strictness once, which is exactly the drift a single shared
implementation prevents from recurring.

**Fix**: the "Canonical `current` symlink target payload" contract is
restated as one canonical, four-check predicate — token grammar (one
non-empty path component, never `.`/`..`, no `/`), raw payload check,
a new direct-child reality check (`lstat` on `bundles/<token>` identifies
a real directory, never a symlink), and a resolution check tightened to
require exact equality with that same direct-child directory, not merely
containment inside `bundles/`. Step 1c now invokes this identical
predicate against `current` itself, rather than its own narrower, ad hoc
two-check copy. New missing-test item 338 exercises the grammar and
direct-child checks directly (a nested-path token; a `bundles/A ->
bundles/B` alias); item 337 (already exercising creation-time-conforming
and corrupted existing symlinks) is amended to describe the token grammar
and direct-child check explicitly rather than the superseded two-check
version.

### `GPT-R61-003` — live missing-test/`WFR-61` text still conflates migration recovery with the first-publication match case, and retains one wrong-direction promotion sentence

**Severity:** important (plan-consistency defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct textual check, in three places:

- Item 324 derived "the binding check confirms the restored directory
  already matches the round being published" from "no new round has been
  requested since migration began, so no repository commit has landed."
  That implication does not hold: migration runs *inside* publication, so
  the publication request can already be for a genuinely newer round the
  moment migration begins, while the real legacy `current/` directory
  being migrated is older — no additional commit or request needs to
  occur *after* migration begins for a mismatch, exactly the scenario
  item 335(a) already exercises.
- Item 330 correctly established "always confirms a match" for the
  step-4a first-publication-interrupted origin (the candidate was built
  for exactly this request), then extended that same "always matches"
  claim to the migration origin as an equivalent case — true for the
  former, not generally true for the latter.
- `WFR-61`'s own revision-39 sub-bullet still read "the only atomic
  operation is the rename of that symlink onto a freshly built, verified,
  immutable versioned directory" — backwards relative to the actual,
  currently authoritative mechanism (a temporary symlink pointing *at*
  the already-built directory is what gets renamed *onto the name*
  `current`), a wrong-direction sentence surviving from before the
  `staging/`-then-`bundles/` redesign that item 316 was already corrected
  for in revision 43 (`GPT-R59-003`) but this older sub-bullet was not.

**Fix**: item 324 is rewritten to state that migration recovery always
restores the pointer unconditionally, with the binding check then
determining match vs. mismatch from the actual comparison, never from
request timing; item 330's "always matches" is scoped explicitly to its
own step-4a origin, with an explicit cross-reference noting it does not
extend to the migration origin (item 324/335(a)'s own scenario); `WFR-61`'s
revision-39 sub-bullet is corrected in place to state the rename's actual
direction, with an inline citation. Items 314-337 were re-read in full
for any other request-timing-derived match claim or wrong-direction
promotion wording beyond the three corrected here; none was found.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 45 → 46) — external plan review confirmed `GPT-R61-001` through `-003` resolved but found the revision-45 eight-field binding check's own reused helper is permissive about missing metadata, plus two important findings against a mis-stated `worktree_root` source and an under-constrained archive-command token grammar (`GPT-R62-001` through `-003`)

**Origin**: external plan review of the revision 45 bundle (`GPT-R62-*`,
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`) independently
reproduced `bundle_id`/`review_content_id` (both confirmed exact matches
against a fresh `python3 scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` run against this
repository, re-confirmed again while applying this disposition), confirmed
the plan/mapping's 62-row normalization holds with zero description
mismatches, confirmed `GPT-R61-001` resolved for every case where the
compared local-generation metadata is actually present, `GPT-R61-002`
resolved for ordinary canonical tokens/targets, and `GPT-R61-003` resolved
in the inspected migration/promotion text, and returned `Status: REVISE`,
one blocking finding plus two important findings. All three findings were
independently re-verified directly against this repository's own bundled
`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` implementation and its bundled test
suite — never merely against the plan's own prose — before being
accepted; the tar-token finding was additionally reproduced independently,
live, against this repository's own environment. No finding was rejected.

### `GPT-R62-001` — the reused local-staleness helper explicitly treats missing `worktree_root`/`generation_head` as success, so the claimed eight-field binding is not actually eight-field fail-closed

**Severity:** blocking.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of the bundled implementation:
`assert_local_generation_matches` (`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py`)
compares `worktree_root` only `if "worktree_root" in recorded`, and
`generation_head` only `if "generation_head" in recorded` — an absent or
unparseable field is simply not compared, never a mismatch. This is not
an oversight: the bundled test
`test_missing_manifest_metadata_is_not_a_local_mismatch` states and
verifies exactly this contract, and independently running it confirms it
passes. Revision 45's own "Current-round binding check" text said "all
eight fields above must match exactly" while its own "Implementation
note" directed recovery to satisfy the `worktree_root`/`generation_head`
pair by invoking this same permissive function unmodified. The two
statements are incompatible: a legacy or otherwise metadata-less
`bundles/<token>/` directory — a real, reachable state given this design's
own migration path for pre-existing `current/` content — would pass the
"eight-field" check while never having recorded, let alone matched, two
of those eight fields.

**Fix**: `assert_local_generation_matches` (`D-Bundle-Manifest`) gains a
`require_metadata: bool = False` keyword argument. The default preserves
today's unchanged permissive behavior at every existing call site,
including `/approve-review`'s own repository-local staleness check, for
which legacy tolerance is the deliberate, correct contract. The
current-round binding check (`D-Approval-Commits`) is the sole caller
using `require_metadata=True`, under which exactly one well-formed
`worktree_root:` line and exactly one well-formed, 40-hex
`generation_head:` line must be present — zero or more than one of either
is itself a mismatch — before both are compared, as before, against the
caller's own current live Git worktree root/HEAD. This is still one
function, one raised `WorktreeOrHeadMismatchError` type, reused directly
rather than reimplemented, so the two call sites cannot drift apart on
what "the same worktree and HEAD" means; only the presence requirement
now differs by caller. `D-Bundle-Manifest` gains a new "Strict
local-generation metadata mode" paragraph stating this contract
authoritatively; the "Current-round binding check"'s own Implementation
note is rewritten to invoke `require_metadata=True` explicitly and state
why the permissive default cannot be reused here. Item 335 gains four new
lettered sub-scenarios, (h)-(k), covering missing-`worktree_root`-only,
missing-`generation_head`-only, both-absent, and malformed/duplicate
metadata, each a mismatch under the strict mode; new item 339 confirms
the permissive default is unaffected at its own legacy call site.

### `GPT-R62-002` — revision 45 names `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` as the source of `worktree_root` even though the bundled implementation derives it from Git

**Severity:** important (normative source-of-truth defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of the bundled implementation: both
`D-Bundle-Manifest`'s original "Worktree/HEAD staleness check" paragraph
and revision 45's own "Current-round binding check" text named
`.ai-review/runtime/WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` (`D3`) as the source
`worktree_root` is read from. The bundled `current_worktree_root_and_head`
function — the one function both manifest generation and
`assert_local_generation_matches` actually call — runs `git rev-parse
--show-toplevel`/`git rev-parse HEAD` directly; it does not read
`WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` at all. The distinction is behaviorally load-
bearing, not merely a documentation nit: `D3` refreshes
`WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` only on a dirty-`IN_PROGRESS`-checkpoint
transition, with no stated refresh-on-every-publication contract, so a
worktree relocated after its last such write would leave that file
pointing at the old path while `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` reports the
new one immediately — exactly the relocation item 335(g) already requires
detecting correctly. The existing implementation already has the correct,
safer behavior; only the plan's own prose pointed somewhere else.

**Fix**: both paragraphs are corrected in place to name the live Git
worktree (`current_worktree_root_and_head`) as the authoritative source,
and to state explicitly that `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` serves
dirty-checkpoint resume safety only and is never authoritative for
bundle-generation/local-staleness identity. New item 340 confirms
relocation is detected via live Git even when `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json`
still names, or never named, the prior path, and confirms dirty-checkpoint
resume itself is unaffected and continues reading that file for its own
purpose.

### `GPT-R62-003` — the version-token grammar is broader than the exact `tar --transform` command that later consumes the token

**Severity:** important (fail-closed hardening gap).

**Confirmed**, independently reproduced against this repository's own
environment: the token grammar ("one path component, never `.`/`..`, no
`/`") admits a token such as `--version`, which the exact archive command
`tar -czf review-bundle.tar.gz -C .ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles
--transform 's,^<token>,current,' <token>` then interprets as the `tar
--version` option — `tar` prints its own version, exits successfully, and
creates no archive. A conforming publisher's own token generator never
produces this, so this is a fail-closed corruption/tampering gap (an
already-existing `current` symlink reaching this state despite step 1c's
validation, or a hand-placed `bundles/` entry), not a reachable defect in
ordinary operation — but it is inconsistent with this design's own
increasingly strict fail-closed treatment of exactly this class of state
elsewhere (step 1d, the direct-child reality check, `GPT-R59-002`'s raw
payload check).

**Fix**: the token grammar narrows to `^[0-9a-f]{32}$` — the exact form
`uuid.uuid4().hex` produces — closing the vulnerability by construction,
since no character with meaning to the shell, to `tar --transform`'s
sed-style expression, or to any other filename-adjacent parser survives
that grammar. The archive command additionally gains a `--` before its
positional `<token>` operand, defense in depth beyond the grammar fix
alone. The one other prose example of token generation
("e.g. a UUID4 or `<pid>.<monotonic-timestamp>`") is restated to name the
same canonical `uuid.uuid4().hex` form. New item 341 exercises the
tightened grammar directly (a leading-dash and a delimiter/metacharacter
token both rejected by the canonical symlink validator, before archive
generation is ever reached) and confirms a conforming token's archive
round trip is unaffected.

### `GPT-R63-001` — the portability paragraph and `WFR-17` still name `/approve-review` as the sole local caller, even though revision 46 itself added a second, live caller and this validation pass found a third, already-live one neither the reviewer nor the plan had ever named

**Severity:** important (normative-consistency defect, not a mechanism
defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of this document's own revision-46 text:
the "Portability vs. local staleness" paragraph (`D-Bundle-Manifest`)
stated the worktree/HEAD equality check is enforced "exclusively by
repository-local commands — specifically `/approve-review`," and `WFR-17`
stated "only repository-local commands (`/approve-review`) stop." Both
sentences predate revision 46 unchanged. Revision 46's own new "Strict
local-generation metadata mode" paragraph, and `D-Approval-Commits`'
"Current-round binding check," both explicitly describe a **second**
caller of the same `assert_local_generation_matches` function —
using `require_metadata=True` — added in that same revision. The two
sentences were never updated to match, so the document contradicted
itself the moment revision 46 landed: one paragraph said "one local
caller, `/approve-review`," while another, a few paragraphs below, added
a second. The bundled implementation's own docstring
(`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py:1776`, "Repository-local commands only
(`/approve-review`)") carries the identical stale claim, confirming this
is not merely a plan-prose slip but a caller-inventory statement this
design intends to bind an eventual implementation to. `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json`'s
`WFR-17` description mirrors the same stale single-caller claim, so the
mapping normalization claim ("no description change needed") that
accompanied every revision since 37 is, for `WFR-17` specifically, no
longer true as of revision 46.

**Self-discovered widening, applying this finding**: the reviewer's own
finding text names exactly two callers (`/approve-review` and
`D-Approval-Commits`' not-yet-built binding check). Per
`/apply-plan-review` step 2's own validation requirement ("validate it
against the actual repository ... do not take the finding's premise on
faith"), every actual call site was grepped directly, rather than trusting
that two-caller framing: `grep -rl assert_local_generation_matches
.claude/commands/` finds **two** command files, not one —
`.claude/commands/approve-review.md` (the expected caller) **and**
`.claude/commands/review-plan.md`, built by the already-`COMPLETE`
`WF4a-iv` checkpoint (`D-Plan-Review-Stages`, the two-stage
local-then-manual-external plan-review protocol) as part of this same
work item's own prior scope. `review-plan.md`'s own text (step 5) already
says "This command also runs inside a real, current worktree, so also
call `workflow_fingerprint.assert_local_generation_matches(repo_root,
<bundle_dir>/MANIFEST.md)` ... (`D-Bundle-Manifest`, `WFR-17`)" — citing
this exact paragraph and this exact requirement as its own authority.
Neither the "Portability vs. local staleness" paragraph nor `WFR-17` nor
`D-Plan-Review-Stages`' own section had ever named `/review-plan` as a
caller, at any revision — this is not a regression introduced by revision
46; it predates it. Applying `GPT-R63-001` literally (adding only the
design-only `D-Approval-Commits` caller) would have left the correction
still wrong — undercounting by one, in the opposite direction from
revision 46's own gap, and for a caller that has been live and calling
this exact function since `WF4a-iv` completed.

**Failure scenario**: `WF5` is implemented literally from `WFR-17`'s
description and the portability paragraph as written, even after a
naive two-caller fix. An implementer either constrains the eventual
helper/docstring/conformance test to the two named callers — silently
making `/review-plan`'s own already-shipped call non-conforming, or
forcing a conformance test to either omit `/review-plan` (false pass) or
fail against a caller that has always been correct — or wires all three
while leaving `WFR-17`/the mapping/the docstring stating a caller
inventory that is still false for one of them. Either way, the
requirement, as literally written, would not match the actual, already-
running command set this design itself shipped.

**Fix**: the "Portability vs. local staleness" paragraph and `WFR-17` are
both corrected in place to name **three** repository-local callers — two
already live, `/approve-review`'s own pre-existing staleness check and
`/review-plan`'s own staleness check, plus one design-only future one,
`D-Approval-Commits`' current-round binding check, not yet built — while
preserving the paragraph's actual invariant unchanged: the check is
repository-local only, never asked of an external reviewer consuming a
portable archive. `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json`'s `WFR-17` description
is mirrored to match exactly. `D-Approval-Commits`' own revision header
gains a revision-47 clause naming this correction. New missing-test item
342 adds a conformance assertion enumerating `assert_local_generation_matches`'s
actual call sites and confirming the set is exactly the three named ones
— the two live commands plus, once `WF5` lands, the current-round binding
check — so a future fourth local caller (or a caller outside the
repository-local command set) cannot be added again without the same
requirement/mapping drift recurring silently.

### `GPT-R63-002` — item 335(k)'s strict-mode duplicate/malformed coverage is `worktree_root`-only, with no symmetric `generation_head` case, and no case distinguishing "duplicate" from "duplicate where one line is malformed"

**Severity:** important (test-coverage gap with a concretely identified
blind spot, not a design-mechanism defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of the bundled implementation: `read_manifest_generation_metadata`
(`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py:1758-1772`) has two independent branches,
`_WORKTREE_ROOT_LINE_RE.search(content)` and
`_GENERATION_HEAD_LINE_RE.search(content)`, each returning only the first
regex match found — neither branch itself rejects a second occurrence of
its own field name. Revision 46's own text requires `require_metadata=True`
to treat "zero matches or more than one of either [field]" as a mismatch,
but item 335, the scenario list this design uses to specify that
behavior concretely, exercised duplication only for `worktree_root` (its
sub-scenario (k)); no sub-scenario exercised a duplicate `generation_head:`
line. An implementation that added duplicate-detection for `worktree_root`
only — the exact field item 335(k) names — while leaving `generation_head`
on its existing first-match `.search()` behavior would satisfy every
enumerated scenario while still accepting a manifest with two
`generation_head:` lines, using whichever the regex happens to match
first. A second, related blind spot: if duplicate-detection were
implemented by counting well-formed regex matches rather than counting
line occurrences independently of grammar, a manifest with one
well-formed line plus one additional malformed line for the same field
would still show "one match," silently passing as "exactly one" when it
is actually two lines, one of them corrupt.

**Fix**: `D-Bundle-Manifest`'s "Strict local-generation metadata mode"
paragraph gains a new "Symmetric per-field grammar and occurrence checks"
subsection, stating explicitly, for the first time, a well-formed grammar
for `worktree_root:` (a single absolute-path line) symmetric with
`generation_head:`'s existing 40-hex grammar, and requiring two
independent sub-checks per field — occurrence (exactly one line for that
field name, counted independently of value grammar) and grammar (that
sole line's value matches the field's own grammar) — closing the
match-counting blind spot by construction. Item 335 gains five new
lettered sub-scenarios, (l)-(p): duplicate-valid `generation_head`
(symmetric with existing (k)); one well-formed plus one malformed
duplicate line, for each field independently; and a lone malformed line
with correct occurrence, for each field independently. `D-Approval-Commits`'
own revision header gains the same revision-47 clause naming this
correction (shared with `GPT-R63-001` above). `WFR-61`'s acceptance/test
cell gains a revision-47 clause describing the symmetric coverage; its
description column is unaffected (the fix is `D-Bundle-Manifest`
mechanism detail the description references by contract name, not a
change to `D-Approval-Commits`' own current-round binding check
behavior).

### `GPT-R64-002` — the required `WF5` caller-documentation synchronization is still not an implementation obligation, so item 342 can pass while active operator/helper documentation remains false

**Severity:** important (implementation-acceptance/documentation gap).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of the three named active surfaces:
`docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s generation-diagnostic-metadata
section describes the local side of the portability split only as "A
**repository-local command** (`/approve-review`)"; `WorktreeOrHeadMismatchError`'s
docstring (`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py`) says the exception is
"Raised by a **repository-local** consumer (`/approve-review`)"; and
`assert_local_generation_matches`'s own docstring says "**Repository-local
commands only** (`/approve-review`)." None of the three has been edited
by any plan-only revision — that staleness is expected, not itself the
defect. The defect is that revision 47's fix, which added item 342 (an
executable call-site enumeration) and corrected the protected plan/mapping
text, added no obligation requiring these three active surfaces to be
corrected when `WF5` actually implements the three-caller split. Item 342
proves the call-site *set*; it says nothing about caller-facing
*documentation* of that set.

**Failure scenario**: `WF5` implements `require_metadata`, the strict
binding call, and item 342's call-site assertion exactly. Item 342 passes
— three real callers, correct mode split. No acceptance criterion requires
`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, the error docstring, or the helper docstring to
change, so all three continue stating or implying `/approve-review` is the
sole local consumer indefinitely. A later maintainer, reading only the
active documentation (never this plan's historical disposition prose),
follows the stale single-caller story and reintroduces the exact
caller-inventory drift item 342 exists to prevent.

**Fix**: new missing-test item 343 adds the explicit `WF5`
implementation-acceptance obligation: once the three-caller
`require_metadata` split lands, `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s generation-
diagnostic-metadata section, `WorktreeOrHeadMismatchError`'s docstring,
and `assert_local_generation_matches`'s own docstring must no longer state
or imply `/approve-review` is the sole repository-local consumer — a
non-exclusive phrasing ("repository-local callers such as ...") or an
exhaustive three-name list both satisfy it, but a phrasing that reads as
excluding `/review-plan` or the current-round binding check does not.
Item 343 is deliberately scoped to *active* mechanism/operator/API
documentation only; this plan's own historical `## WF8b finding
disposition` prose is explicitly out of scope and is never rewritten.
`D-Approval-Commits`' own revision header gains the same revision-48
clause naming this addition (shared with `GPT-R64-001` above).

### `GPT-R65-001` — item 343 makes `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` a `WF5` implementation-acceptance surface, but the implementation-stage artifact declaration still excludes it, so the required correction is not durably bound by technical approval

**Severity:** important (approval-durability and artifact-classification
inconsistency, not a mechanism defect).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of `workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json`:
`implementation_stage.excluded_paths` still contained
`docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, with the rationale "plan-stage-
governed workflow documentation, not an implementation deliverable" —
exactly contradicting revision 48's own new item 343, which requires this
file's caller-facing wording to agree with the corrected three-caller
model as a `WF5` implementation-acceptance obligation. Reproduced
independently in an isolated scratch repository using the bundled
classifier/fingerprint code: with the pre-fix declaration,
`classify_path_implementation_stage("docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md",
...)` returned `excluded`, and a commit changing only that file left the
implementation-stage `review_content_id` exactly unchanged, while a
control file under the protected `scripts/` prefix changed it as expected.

**Failure scenario**: `WF5` implements the three-caller split, updates all
three item-343 documentation surfaces (including `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`),
item 343's own conformance check passes, and the implementation bundle
receives external `APPROVE`. At a later committed maintenance step,
`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` alone regresses to the stale `/approve-review`-only
wording, with every other protected implementation-stage path unchanged.
Because `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` was excluded, the implementation-stage
`review_content_id` recomputes identically, so `approval_is_current(stage=
"implementation")` continues to report the technical approval as current
even though one of item 343's own explicitly required surfaces no longer
satisfies the approved contract — active operator documentation can
silently diverge from `WFR-17`/item 342/the real call sites again, with no
durability gate ever noticing. A changed `bundle_id` does not close this
hole, since `WFR-04` makes `review_content_id`, not the historical
`bundle_id`, the future approval-durability gate.

**Fix**: `workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json` moves
`docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` from `implementation_stage.excluded_paths`
to an exact `implementation_stage.protected_paths` entry, with a rationale
naming item 343's own obligation as the reason (never the removed "not an
implementation deliverable" claim); the file's existing self-referential
implementation-stage protection is untouched, so this classification
change is itself technical-approval-bound. Re-verified, same isolated-
scratch-repository method: with the fix, `classify_path_implementation_stage`
returns `protected`, a `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`-only edit now changes the
implementation-stage `review_content_id`, and the two item-343 Python
docstring surfaces remain protected through the pre-existing `scripts/`
prefix, unaffected. The plan-stage classification of `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`
is deliberately left unchanged — this finding is about implementation-stage
durability, never a request to make the file plan-stage protected. New
missing-test item 344 adds the direct classification/fingerprint/approval-
staleness coverage the finding's own "Required tests" list calls for;
`WFR-61`'s acceptance/test cell gains a matching revision-49 clause and its
"owed" item range widens to include item 344; description column, and
therefore `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json`, unaffected.

### `GPT-R67-001` — the plan-approval commit's four-file contract omits the work item's own artifact declaration, so a pending, bundle-reviewed classification edit to it can survive external approval yet never become durable Git history

**Severity:** important (approval-durability and bootstrap-consistency
defect, not a mechanism defect in the fingerprint/classification code
itself).

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of `.claude/commands/approve-review.md`
step 6 and `D-Approval-Commits`' own "`/approve-review plan`" bullet
(pre-fix text): both enumerate exactly four commit members — approved plan
doc(s), registry JSON + generated Markdown view, `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`,
requirements mapping file — and neither names
`docs/ai-workflow/registry/workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json`. Confirmed
independently that this file is presently, concretely dirty in this
repository's own working tree (revision 49's `GPT-R65-001`
reclassification, moving `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` from
`implementation_stage.excluded_paths` to `implementation_stage.protected_paths`),
that this exact edit is part of the current bundle both `bundle_id` and
`MANIFEST.md` were computed over, and that `docs/ai-workflow/registry/` is
a plan-stage excluded prefix — so the edit is real, bundle-reviewed
content that nonetheless never touches the plan-stage `review_content_id`
the four-file contract was scoped against.

**Failure scenario**: Revision 49 is externally approved; `/approve-review
plan workflow-v2-1-core` is invoked; the command validates the current
bundle and plan-stage `review_content_id` (both still match, since the
artifact declaration is plan-stage excluded); it creates the documented
four-file commit; `workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json` remains modified,
uncommitted, because it is outside that set; the plan-stage post-approval
manifest check (`WFR-06`) still passes, since it only verifies the four
protected/named files; the working tree is consequently *not* clean
immediately after the command returns, contradicting `D-Approval-Commits`'
own immediate-clean-tree postcondition; before any later checkpoint or
technical approval ever binds the declaration at the implementation stage,
an ordinary `git stash`/`reset`/`checkout`/worktree recreation can discard
the uncommitted change, silently reverting `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` to its
stale, `GPT-R65-001`-reopened classification with no gate ever having
noticed.

**Fix**: `D-Approval-Commits`' "`/approve-review plan`" bullet gains a
conditional fifth commit member — the work item's own concrete
`<work_item_id>-artifacts.json` — included in the same single commit
exactly when (a) its working-tree bytes differ from HEAD and (b) those
bytes are byte-identical to the copy the just-recomputed current
`bundle_id` already covers; an unchanged declaration is never gratuitously
added, and a declaration that changed again after bundle generation causes
`/approve-review plan` to refuse outright rather than commit unreviewed
bytes. Because this repository's own `workflow-v2-1-core` work item is
permanently Workflow-v1-governed and its installed
`.claude/commands/approve-review.md` predates this correction — with no
future checkpoint scheduled to update that command file before this work
item's own next plan approval runs — a new "Revision-50 bootstrap approval
procedure" paragraph states the explicit, plan-recorded one-time manual
procedure that next approval must follow, exactly parallel to
`D-Bootstrap`'s own WF0 one-time commit contract. The permanent fix to
`.claude/commands/approve-review.md`'s own prose is deferred to the next
checkpoint that touches implementation content, consistent with this
document's unbroken revision-28-through-49 practice of never editing
`scripts/`/`.claude/commands/` content during a plan-only revision, and is
tracked by new missing-test item 347 so the obligation is not silently
dropped. New missing-test items 345-346 add the one-commit/clean-tree/
trailer, freshness-refusal, and no-gratuitous-inclusion coverage the
finding's own "Required tests" list calls for.
