### `GPT-R68-001` — the revision-50 bootstrap procedure's "manually extended" step has no defined execution surface, and directly contradicts the installed command's own "steps 1-7 execute exactly as written" `"1"`-branch text

**Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH / important immediate-approval bootstrap defect.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of `.claude/commands/approve-review.md`
step 0 (`governing_workflow_version: "1"`: "steps 1-7 execute exactly as
written") and step 6 (plan stage: "one commit containing the approved plan
doc(s), registry JSON + generated Markdown view, `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`,
and the requirements mapping file together" — four members, no
cross-reference to any other document, no bootstrap branch, no bootstrap
argument or mode): the installed command, exactly as written, gives no
place from which a plan-doc-defined "manual extension" of its own step 6
could be applied, and no pause exists between state write (step 5), commit
creation (step 6), and post-approval verification (step 6a) into which
such an extension could be inserted after the fact. Confirmed directly
against `D-Approval-Commits`' own revision-50 text: its bootstrap
procedure's step 2 said only that the commit "is manually extended, in
that same commit" — naming no concrete precondition/action, no bootstrap
input or mode, and no amend-before-step-6a mechanism, any one of which the
finding's own candidate mechanisms would have required to be executable
and deterministic.

**Failure scenario**: revision 50 receives external `APPROVE`; the user
invokes the currently installed `/approve-review plan
workflow-v2-1-core`; the command resolves a permanently-`"1"` item and
therefore follows steps 1-7 "exactly as written"; step 6 stages/commits
the four named approval members only; nothing in the command creates a
pause or invokes the plan's manual fifth-member extension; whether a
separately staged declaration happens to enter the commit depends on
unspecified Git mechanics chosen by whichever model executes the command
that session; if it is omitted, step 6a can still pass, since the
declaration is plan-stage excluded, reproducing the exact durability
window `GPT-R67-001` found revision 50 was meant to close; if the operator
notices only after the command returns, adding it requires a later
amend/commit after step 6a has already verified and step 7 has already
reported success — outside the single approval transaction and in direct
conflict with `D-Approval-Commits`' own no-second-commit rule.

**Fix**: the revision-50 "Revision-50 bootstrap approval procedure" is
replaced by a "Bootstrap plan-approval procedure" that does not attempt to
locally override the installed command's own step 6 at all. Instead it
replaces *invoking* `/approve-review plan workflow-v2-1-core` outright,
for as long as the installed command file remains unupdated, with a fully
self-contained transaction that inlines that command's own steps 1-5 and
6a unchanged (gate reachability, fresh recomputation plus the local
worktree/HEAD staleness check, basis resolution, record building, state
write; then, after commit creation, the unchanged
`verify_post_approval_manifest_match` call) and restates only commit
creation with the corrected conditional five-file set explicit and
inline, adding a new post-commit declaration-content check (`git show
<commit>:<path>` byte-compared against the bundle's own captured copy)
that closes the gap left by the pre-existing plan-stage manifest check,
which never covers a plan-stage-excluded path. This is exactly parallel
in kind to `D-Bootstrap`'s own WF0 one-time commit contract ("There is no
`/approve-review` to invoke it with"), so the "steps 1-7 execute exactly
as written" clause is never contradicted — it is simply never invoked for
a round this procedure covers. The procedure's own user-only guard is
stated explicitly (the same literal confirmation text `/approve-review`'s
own mechanism (2) requires), so the command's user-only safety property is
preserved even though the command itself is not invoked. The finding's own
scope ambiguity ("this work item's own Revision 50 approval only" vs.
"any later bundle, for as long as the installed command file remains
unupdated") is resolved to the latter, stated once. New missing-test item
348 records the bootstrap procedure's own live-execution checklist, since
it is a documented manual transaction with no `scripts/`/`.claude/commands/`
implementation of its own; item 347's wording is updated to name the
renamed procedure. The top-of-document title/status block, found stale
during this validation (bumped to "Revision 50" without ever updating its
own "Status:" summary or inserting a "**Revision 50**" historical
paragraph for the revision-49-to-50 transition), is corrected in the same
pass — a bundle/document-consistency gap this revision's own validation
surfaced, not a premise of the reviewer's finding.

### `GPT-R69-001` — the bootstrap persists `plan_approval` and transitions to `IMPLEMENTING` before its declaration-freshness refusal, so the documented "no partial state" failure path is impossible

**Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH / important bootstrap failure-atomicity
inconsistency.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of revision 51's own step ordering:
step 2 performed the read-only gate-reachability/recompute-plus-
staleness/basis-resolution/record-building sub-steps *and* the state write
(`apply_plan_approval` plus persisting `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`) together,
before step 3 ever evaluated the artifact-declaration's pending-change and
freshness conditions. Step 3's own text required that a freshness
violation "refuse outright, before any commit is created ... no commit, no
partial state" — a guarantee about state, not only about commits, that
revision 51's own ordering could not satisfy: by the time step 3 ran,
`docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` had already been rewritten by
step 2. Confirmed directly against the bundled `workflow_state.py`: calling
`apply_plan_approval(...)` is not a tentative/read-only operation — it
returns a work item with `phase` set to `IMPLEMENTING` and a new `CURRENT`
`plan_approval` record, which step 2 then persisted.

**Failure scenario**: revision 51 receives a binding external `APPROVE`;
the user supplies the required literal confirmation and starts the
bootstrap; steps 1-4 (gate reachability, staleness check, basis resolution,
record building) succeed; step 2 executes `apply_plan_approval(...)` and
persists the result, so the work item now durably claims `IMPLEMENTING`/
`CURRENT`; `workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json` has meanwhile changed
relative to the bundle copy, so the following step detects the freshness
violation and refuses before any commit is created, exactly as designed —
but the repository is now left with a persisted state transition the
procedure simultaneously promised would not exist. A fresh-session
`implementing_entry_reachable(...)` check still fails closed, since no
matching durable plan-approval commit exists, so this is not an approval
bypass — but it is a recovery problem the documented refusal path was
supposed to make impossible, and a retry cannot be treated as if nothing
happened, since `phase`/`plan_approval`/`state_revision`/`last_transition`
have already been modified.

**Fix**: revision 51's step 2 is split into a read-only sub-step (gate
reachability, recompute-plus-staleness, basis resolution, record building —
producing the approval record in memory, writing nothing) and the
artifact-declaration freshness evaluation is moved immediately after it,
still before any write. The state write (`apply_plan_approval` plus
persisting `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`) and commit creation are deferred to a new
step 4, reached only once the freshness check clears — so a freshness
refusal now occurs while `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` is still byte-identical to
its pre-procedure state, and the documented "no commit, no partial state"
guarantee is literally true rather than aspirational. This preserves
revision 51's self-contained bootstrap architecture and its
command-supersession lifetime unchanged — the fix is purely a reordering of
already-specified sub-steps, not a new mechanism — and requires no rollback
machinery, since the known freshness condition is now evaluated before, not
after, the write it would otherwise have to undo. Missing-test item 348 is
strengthened to require proving `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s byte-identical
non-mutation (not merely "no commit"/"no reported success") on the
freshness-refusal branch, per the finding's own "Required tests" items 1-2.

### `GPT-R70-001` — the fifth member's binding is proven only after the approval commit is already durable and discoverable, so an interruption between commit creation and that check leaves a bad commit fresh-session-valid

**Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH / important approval-durability and
crash-recovery gap.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of revision 52's own step ordering and the
bundled recomputation functions: step 4 writes `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` and
creates the approval commit; step 5 (the only mechanism that byte-verifies
the fifth member against the reviewed bundle copy) runs strictly after.
Because `implementing_entry_reachable(...)`'s fresh-session check recomputes
only the plan-stage projection — which, by the fifth member's own
plan-stage-excluded classification, never includes
`workflow-v2-1-core-artifacts.json` — a fresh session that discovers the
step-4 commit but never observes step 5 complete (interruption, or a
detected mismatch left unresolved) has no way to distinguish a
correctly-bound commit from one whose fifth member was omitted or wrong.
The gap is narrow — it requires a declaration race or a commit-construction
defect between step 3's freshness check and step 4's commit, plus an
interruption or incomplete recovery — but once triggered, the one mechanism
`GPT-R67-001` through `GPT-R69-001` built specifically to bind the reviewed
declaration bytes never actually ran to completion before the commit became
authoritative.

**Failure scenario**: step 3 clears (the declaration is bundle-fresh);
between that check and commit construction, the declaration's bytes are
altered or the commit-construction step stages the wrong content; step 4
persists `CURRENT`/`IMPLEMENTING` and creates the commit carrying the normal
approval trailers; execution is interrupted before step 5 verifies the
declaration, or step 5 detects the mismatch but no defined recovery
completes. In a fresh session, `discover_plan_approval_commit(...)` finds
the commit, `plan_approval.status == CURRENT`, and the plan-stage
`review_content_id` still matches (the declaration is excluded from that
projection) — so `implementing_entry_reachable(...)` accepts the approval
even though the fifth-member binding never completed.

**Fix**: the declaration check is moved from post-commit to pre-commit and
made load-bearing *before* the commit exists, rather than being the sole
mechanism that establishes correctness only afterward. A new step 4 stages
the fifth member's exact bytes (`git add`) — the only write it performs,
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` still untouched — and byte-compares the staged index
entry against the bundle's own captured copy before any state write or
commit. A mismatch unstages the path (`git restore --staged`, restoring the
index to its exact pre-step state) and refuses outright, symmetric with
step 3's own "no commit, no partial state" guarantee — now extended to "no
commit, no partial state, no partial index" as well. A match leaves the
pinned index entry untouched through the rest of the transaction: the new
step 5 (formerly step 4) stages only the four ordinary files and creates
the commit, which is therefore guaranteed by construction to carry the
correct fifth-member bytes the moment it becomes reachable. The former
post-commit check (new step 6) is retained as a redundant defense-in-depth
audit — reachable in ordinary operation only via a transaction-invariant
violation (something outside the procedure mutating the pinned index entry
between step 4 and step 5) — with an explicit, deterministic recovery
(`git add` the correct bytes, `git commit --amend --no-edit`, identical
trailers, re-verify against the amended SHA) replacing the prior ambiguous
"resolve manually, e.g. `git reset`" instruction. This requires no rollback
machinery for `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` itself, since the declaration binding is
now fully established before that file is ever written — exactly the same
structural pattern revision 52 already used to make the freshness check
pre-write. Missing-test item 348 is strengthened to require proving the
fifth member's binding is established and load-bearing before the approval
commit becomes reachable, deterministic index-rollback on a step-4 refusal,
and the defined step-6 amend recovery, per the finding's own "Required
tests" items 1-4 and 6-7.

### `GPT-R71-001` — the bootstrap's fifth-member guarantee assumes an isolated Git index but never requires or preserves one, so its rollback is not exact and plausible commit forms either absorb unrelated staged content or bypass the pinned declaration blob

**Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH / important approval-transaction and provenance
defect.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of revision 53's own step 4-6 text and by
the three independent Git reproductions above. Revision 53's step 4 claims
`git restore --staged <path>` on mismatch "restor[es] the index to its
exact pre-step state," and step 5/6 claim the resulting commit contains
exactly the applicable four/five-file set and that a step-6 amend recovery
leaves "the rest of the committed tree unchanged." None of these three
claims is backed by a stated precondition on the index's starting state, a
pre-commit assertion of the complete staged set, or an exact commit
invocation that excludes a pathspec form — so all three are true only for
the single Git usage pattern the document's prose implicitly assumed
(clean index beforehand; no-pathspec commit; no working-tree edit between
pin and commit), and false for other equally ordinary Git states or
invocation choices, as reproduced above.

**Failure scenario**: a legitimate pre-existing staged change (the
declaration itself from prior manual Git work, or an unrelated plan-stage
excluded path) is present when the bootstrap begins; step 4 (old
numbering) stages the declaration on top of it; either a mismatch triggers
`git restore --staged`, which resets to `HEAD` rather than the user's
pre-existing staged content (data loss the procedure never warned about),
or the declaration matches and step 5 (old numbering) proceeds — a
no-pathspec commit then silently absorbs the unrelated staged path into the
provenance-bearing approval commit (undetected, since plan-stage
verification never hashes excluded-path content), or a pathspec-limited
commit form rereads newer, unreviewed working-tree bytes for the
declaration path instead of the pinned index blob, reproducing the exact
`GPT-R70-001` gap one mechanism later.

**Fix**: the bootstrap gains an explicit, checked Git index transaction
rather than an implicit one. A new step 3 (index-isolation precondition)
requires the whole index to equal `HEAD` before any staging begins,
refusing outright and naming every already-staged path otherwise — this
alone makes the (renumbered) step 5 mismatch rollback's "exact pre-step
state" claim true by construction, since the only path step 5 ever stages
is the one path being pinned, from a starting point already proven equal to
`HEAD`. The (renumbered) step 6 gains two new pre-commit assertions run
immediately before commit creation: the complete staged path set must equal
exactly the applicable four/five-member set, and, when the fifth member
applies, its staged blob must still match the reviewed bundle copy. The
commit itself is required to be a plain, pathspec-free `git commit` — never
a pathspec form naming the approval paths — since a pathspec form is
exactly the mechanism reproduced above to bypass the pin. The (renumbered)
step 7 amend recovery gains matching otherwise-clean-index/
single-corrected-path assertions before amending, making "leaving the rest
of the committed tree unchanged" a checked property instead of an assumed
one. Missing-test item 348 is strengthened to require proving index
isolation before staging, the exact pre-commit staged-set assertion, the
pathspec-free commit invocation, and the hardened amend recovery, per the
finding's own "Required tests" items 1-10.

### `GPT-R72-001` — the bootstrap's final pre-commit assertions and its commit operation run after the approval-state write, and no failure path among them has a rollback, so a refusal or commit failure leaves persisted `CURRENT`/`IMPLEMENTING` state with no durable approval commit

**Severity:** MEDIUM-HIGH / important approval-transaction failure-atomicity
defect.

**Confirmed**, by direct reading of revision 54's own step 6 against the
bundled implementation, not on the reviewer's text alone.
`scripts/workflow_state.py`'s `apply_plan_approval(...)` deep-copies the
state, sets the work item's `plan_approval` record, sets `phase` to
`IMPLEMENTING`, increments `state_revision`, and writes `last_transition`;
revision 54's step 6 sub-step 1 persists exactly that to
`docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, and only afterwards runs sub-step 3's
exact staged-set assertion, sub-step 4's fifth-member blob re-verification,
and sub-step 5's `git commit`. Sub-steps 3 and 4 are explicitly fail-closed
refusals, and the commit can fail for ordinary local reasons. Revision 54
defined no rollback for any of them, and its own step 10 asserted only that
these branches "refuse before any commit exists" — true, and beside the
point, since the state write had already happened. Revision 52 had fixed
precisely this failure-atomicity class for the declaration-freshness branch;
revision 54 reintroduced it one transaction boundary later.

**Three further facts established while validating the finding**, each
independently reproduced, each fixed in this revision:

1. **The partial state is not inert.** The finding states that "the
   downstream durable-reachability logic fails closed, so this is not an
   approval bypass." That holds for `/milestone-implement`, which routes
   through `workflow_state.implementing_entry_reachable(...)` (it requires a
   discoverable `Workflow-Plan-Approval` commit reachable from `HEAD`, and
   so fails closed). It does **not** hold for `/bootstrap-workflow-v2`, the
   command that actually drives this work item's implementation: its step-2
   "durability guard" recomputes the plan-stage `review_content_id` and
   compares it against `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id`, never
   against a discovered approval commit. After the step-6 state write, that
   record field holds exactly the freshly recomputed value by construction,
   so the guard passes on a partially-written transaction and would resume
   implementation on a plan revision carrying no approval commit at all.
   Verified by reading `.claude/commands/bootstrap-workflow-v2.md` step 2
   and `.claude/commands/milestone-implement.md`, and by grepping every
   caller of `implementing_entry_reachable` in the repository (exactly one).
2. **An in-memory-only rollback cannot survive a hard interruption.** The
   pre-procedure `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` is uncommitted
   working-tree content — confirmed live, the file is currently modified
   relative to `HEAD` — so it cannot be reconstructed from `HEAD`, and
   `apply_plan_approval` overwrites the prior `plan_approval` and
   `last_transition` values in place, so it cannot be reconstructed from the
   post-write file either. A durable snapshot taken before the write is
   therefore genuinely necessary, not a stylistic preference.
3. **Revision 54's staged-set assertion constrains the index, not the
   commit.** Reproduced in an isolated scratch repository: with
   `approval.txt` staged and asserted as the complete staged set, an
   installed `pre-commit` hook that writes and `git add`s `sneaky.txt`
   causes the subsequent plain, pathspec-free `git commit` to produce a
   commit whose tree contains **both** files. Neither of revision 54's
   post-commit checks can see this — the declaration check inspects one
   path, and `verify_post_approval_manifest_match` recomputes the plan-stage
   projection, which by construction ignores every plan-stage-excluded path.

**Git semantics re-verified in isolated scratch repositories** before being
relied on, rather than reasoned from memory:

- `git reset --mixed HEAD` with `a.txt`/`state.json` staged restores the
  index to `HEAD` (`git diff --cached --quiet` clean) while leaving both
  working-tree files at their edited content — the exact property the
  rollback needs;
- a commit-signing failure (`commit.gpgsign=true`, unreachable
  `gpg.program`) fails with exit 128, leaves `HEAD` unmoved, and leaves the
  index staged;
- a `pre-commit` hook that mutates the index and then exits 1 fails the
  commit with exit 1, leaves `HEAD` unmoved, and leaves the hook's own
  staged path in the index — which the whole-index `git reset --mixed HEAD`
  then absorbs, where an enumerated per-path restore would not;
- `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r <commit>` yields exactly the
  commit's changed-path set against its first parent;
- `git commit --amend` preserves the commit's first parent, so an amended
  approval commit still satisfies the classifier's
  `first parent == pre_procedure_head` test.

**Fix**: the bootstrap becomes one failure-atomic transaction rather than a
sequence of individually-guarded steps. Three named contracts are added to
`D-Approval-Commits` — a **durable approval journal**
(`.ai-review/runtime/PLAN_APPROVAL_JOURNAL.json`, gitignored and
worktree-scoped, a sibling of D3's own `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json`, written
atomically and deliberately kept out of `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` because it
exists to restore that very file), an **approval-transaction outcome
classifier** (decides `COMMITTED`/`NOT_COMMITTED`/`AMBIGUOUS` from durable
Git state alone, via the existing scoped trailer lookup, never from a
command's exit status and never from `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`), and one
**approval-transaction rollback** (restores the captured state bytes and the
whole index to `HEAD`, touches no working-tree file, and verifies its own
completion before any refusal is reported). A new step 0 resolves an
interrupted transaction on a fresh session before anything else runs; a new
step 4a opens the journal before the first mutation of any kind; a new step
8a closes it only after post-commit verification passes. Step 5's pin
mismatch, step 6's two pre-commit assertions, and a `NOT_COMMITTED` commit
attempt all resolve through the one rollback. Step 7 gains an exact
committed-path-set assertion. Because the classifier and the rollback are
the same operations in-session and on recovery, the crash path is exercised
by every ordinary failure rather than only after a real crash.

### Bounded adversarial stress passes over the revised transaction

Three passes were run over the complete revised transaction, per the user's
own bounded-stress instruction; each found a further concrete defect in the
same contract, each was fixed in this revision, and the loop stopped at the
third repair/stress cycle.

**Pass 1** (invariant-directed): (a) step 4a could overwrite an existing
journal — destroying the only record of how to undo another in-flight
transaction — so it now refuses outright when one is present, and the
"a failed journal write leaves no journal" property of the atomic
`os.replace` sequence is stated explicitly; (b) missing-test item 347, the
permanent `.claude/commands/approve-review.md` obligation, required only the
five-file commit set, so retiring this bridge would have silently retired
its whole failure-atomicity contract — item 347 now requires the permanent
command to carry the index-isolation precondition, journal, classifier,
rollback, both staged-set and committed-path-set assertions, and the
pathspec-free commit before the bridge is retired; (c) the forced ordering
write → stage → assert → commit is now justified in place
(`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` is itself one of the staged members, so its
post-write bytes must exist before there is anything correct to stage or
assert — the rollback, not a reordering, is what makes that ordering safe).

**Pass 2** (input-provenance and time-of-check/time-of-use): (a) the
classifier's trailer lookup needs the work item's `base_commit`, which the
journal did not record, forcing step 0 to read it from
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` — the one file whose trustworthiness the classifier
exists to be independent of; `base_commit` is now a journal field and every
classifier argument comes from the validated journal or live Git; (b) the
rollback overwrote `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` unconditionally, so a writer
outside the transaction would have had its write destroyed rather than
detected — the rollback now requires the current file to be recognizably one
of this transaction's own two states (the captured pre-procedure bytes, or
its own step-6 write, identified by `phase == "IMPLEMENTING"` plus a
matching `approved_review_content_id`) and refuses otherwise; (c) the
reviewed fifth-member bytes were read from the mutable bundle copy three
separate times (step 5, sub-step 6.4, step 7) — three times-of-check against
one time-of-use — so the digest is now read **once** at step 4a into the
journal's `fifth_member_sha256` and every later comparison, including a
step-0 forward completion in a later session and the amend recovery's
pre-staging check, is made against that pinned digest.

**Pass 3** (fresh failure-mode perspective): step 7's `git commit --amend`
recovery assumed the approval commit was still `HEAD`, but the classifier
deliberately accepts a `COMMITTED` outcome where the approval commit is an
ancestor of `HEAD` rather than the tip (so that later unrelated commits do
not invalidate a real approval) — amending in that state would rewrite the
wrong commit. Sub-step (a) now requires `HEAD == C` explicitly and the
recovery does not apply otherwise.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 55 → 56) — external plan review returned one blocking and two important findings against the approval/bootstrap transaction; all three validated, all three applied as one system

Revision 55's external plan review (`GPT-R73-001`/`-002`/`-003`,
`Status: REVISE`) confirmed the revision-55 transaction correct at the
boundary it was built for, and found three defects in the same contract.
All three were validated against this repository before acceptance, none
was rejected, and — per the round's own instruction not to fix them
independently — they were treated as one transaction rather than three
patches. Doing so collapsed two of them into a single structural change.

### Validation performed before accepting anything

Every claim below was reproduced directly rather than taken on the
finding's word. Five reproductions in isolated scratch repositories or
against the bundled implementation:

1. **The installed command's guard.** `.claude/commands/bootstrap-workflow-v2.md`
   step 2 reads, verbatim, "compare it against the `Workflow-Plan-Approval`
   trailer value discovered in step 3 (or, once step 1 has run, against
   `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id`)". `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
   exists, so step 1 has run and the second branch governs. Against the
   live repository the guard's two inputs are currently
   `68eed7ec85fdaf9f…` (recorded) and `cb5e5ea43e8f62e0…` (recomputed), so
   it stops today — and revision 55's step-6 working-tree write would have
   set the first to exactly the second, making it pass. The command
   contains no journal check of any kind. `GPT-R73-001`'s premise is
   exactly right.
2. **Non-exclusive acquisition.** Two runs both observed the journal path
   absent, both `os.replace`d their own journal onto it, and the second
   silently won; the first transaction's undo record was destroyed.
3. **The two-field rollback predicate.** Applying a valid plan-approval
   record to the live state with the bundled `apply_plan_approval`, then
   advancing only `milestone-8.state_revision`, produced a file the
   revision-55 predicate still accepts as "this transaction's own step-6
   write" while differing in bytes — so the whole-file restore would delete
   `milestone-8`'s update. `apply_plan_approval` was also confirmed
   byte-deterministic for a fixed `now`, which is what makes an exact
   post-state binding possible at all.
4. **Same-path hook mutation.** A `pre-commit` hook that rewrote and
   re-staged `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` produced a commit carrying the hook's
   bytes while the committed path set stayed exactly the asserted set.
5. **The amend-retry stall.** Staging the corrected declaration and then
   re-entering step 7 made `git diff --cached --quiet` fail on precisely
   the staged path the interrupted recovery had correctly left behind.

Two further Git behaviours were validated because the fix depends on them,
not because a finding claimed them: `git hash-object -w --path` plus `git
update-index --add --cacheinfo` stages exact bytes while leaving the
working-tree file untouched, a pathspec-free `git commit` then commits the
pinned blob, and `git reset --mixed HEAD` clears such an entry without
touching the working tree.

### `GPT-R73-001` — blocking — the journal was a normative rule, not an enforceable lock

**Accepted.** Applied by removing the interval rather than guarding it.

The post-approval `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` is no longer written to the working
tree before the commit at all. Sub-step 6.1 pins the exact expected
post-state **into the Git index** as a blob; the commit is created from
that verified index; and a new step 8b materializes the working-tree file
only after every post-commit verification has passed. Throughout the whole
vulnerable interval the working-tree
`plan_approval.approved_review_content_id` is still the *previous*
approval's value, so the installed `/bootstrap-workflow-v2`'s own existing
step-2 guard stops — unchanged, unaware of the journal, and equally for the
second shape the finding names, a durable commit already rejected by step
7. This is the finding's own required-correction option 3 ("restructure the
temporary transaction so no intermediate working-tree state can satisfy
that command's existing durability guard"), chosen over editing the
installed command because a plan-only revision does not edit
`.claude/commands/`, and chosen over deferring to item 352 because that
defers enforcement past the event it guards.

Journal acquisition becomes `os.open(O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_WRONLY)`, whose
creation-if-and-only-if-absent is atomic, with the journal written into
that same descriptor so publication and ownership are one act. Item 352
survives as the permanent, general fix but is explicitly removed from this
bridge's critical path; item 347 gains a pairing rule forbidding a future
permanent command from adopting a working-tree-first state write without
landing item 352's commit-bound guard in the same change.

### `GPT-R73-002` — important — the exact post-state was never bound, and rollback could destroy a concurrent work item's write

**Accepted.** Applied in two halves, one of which the restructure above
resolves outright.

*Rollback.* The whole-file state restore is **deleted, not narrowed**. A
transaction that never writes the shared file has nothing to restore, so
the branch that could destroy another work item's update no longer exists.
This satisfies the finding's required corrections 5 and 6 by a route
neither offers: rather than requiring exact post-identity for a whole-file
restore or scoping the restore to one work item, it removes the write.
`D1`'s multi-work-item concurrency and this rollback are reconciled by
construction rather than by an unenforceable global write lock. What
remains is a read-only assertion that the state file does not already carry
this transaction's post-approval identity — an invariant check that can
never delete anyone's data. The revision-55 verification step requiring the
file to equal `pre_procedure_state_sha256` is deliberately dropped: it
would now fail on exactly the sanctioned concurrent write it exists to
protect.

*Binding.* The journal gains a pinned `approval_now` plus
`expected_post_state_b64`/`expected_post_state_sha256`, computed at step 4a
from the recorded pre-state, and the identity is checked as a
compare-and-swap before pinning, as a staged blob, as committed content
(step 7's new committed-`WORKFLOW_STATE.json`-bytes assertion, which closes
the hook case), and as materialized bytes. This required naming a
**canonical serialization** — `json.dumps(state, indent=2,
ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"` — which nothing in this repository stated
before: `scripts/workflow_state.py` has no state-file writer, and neither
`.claude/commands/` nor `REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` names one. It was verified to
round-trip the live state file byte-identically where `ensure_ascii=True`
and `sort_keys=True` both do not, and new missing-test item 353 makes it an
obligation on every writer.

### `GPT-R73-003` — important — the amend recovery was not interruption-idempotent, and step 8a's idempotence claim was false

**Accepted.** Step 7's single clean-index precondition becomes a three-way
classification: a clean index enters the ordinary path; an index holding
**exactly** the one declaration path with a staged blob already matching
`fifth_member_sha256` is recognized as an interrupted in-progress amend and
continues directly to the amend; anything else refuses. Step 8a's "the only
write among them is this deletion" is replaced by an exact enumeration of
the post-commit interval's three writes — step 7's amend, step 8b's
materialization, and the journal deletion — each individually idempotent
and re-runnable, with the reads between them trivially so.

### Bounded adversarial stress passes

Three passes were run over the complete revised transaction, each from a
different failure-mode perspective. The first two each found one concrete
defect, which was fixed; the third found one stale internal premise, also
fixed. The loop stopped at the third repair/stress cycle, as bounded.

**Pass 1 — step 8b's third branch deadlocked against `D1`.** A whole-file
materialization ("write if the file equals the pre-state, no-op if it
equals the post-state, otherwise refuse") is unreachable-by-retry when a
sanctioned concurrent operation updates a *different* work item between
sub-step 6.1a and step 8b: the user's only loss-free reconciliation
produces "expected post-state **plus** that update," which is neither
accepted state, so every retry refuses identically and the journal can
never close without discarding the other work item's write — `GPT-R73-002`'s
own loss reappearing one step later. Fixed by making step 8b
**target-scoped**: it replaces exactly `work_items["workflow-v2-1-core"]`
and carries every other entry through untouched. Reproduced both forms
directly: the whole-file form refuses permanently, the scoped form
completes, preserves `milestone-8`'s update byte-intact, and is a no-op on
re-run. Step 9's clean-tree confirmation gains the one permitted exception
this creates (a residual difference confined to other `work_items` keys),
and the general rule is stated: **before durability, refuse and let the
retry recapture; after durability, complete forward without clobbering.**
Two smaller hardenings landed in the same pass: sub-step 6.1b now takes the
index-entry mode from `HEAD` rather than assuming `100644`, and the
`git add -u`-style hook that reverts an index pin from the working tree is
documented as the vector the committed-bytes assertion exists to catch
(reproduced: the commit carried the pre-approval state and its path set
shrank; both step-7 assertions caught it).

**Pass 2 — the transaction-lifetime lock was a guarantee nothing held.**
An earlier draft of this revision held an exclusive `flock` from step 4a to
step 8a and used it to distinguish a live owner from an abandoned journal.
This procedure is a live checklist executed as a sequence of **separate,
short-lived processes** — item 348 says so explicitly — so no process spans
those steps. Reproduced: a second process acquired the supposedly held lock
the instant the writing process exited. A lock nothing holds is the same
category of defect as a journal rule no command reads, so the claim was
removed rather than left standing: acquisition is `O_CREAT | O_EXCL`, which
is exactly what the finding's required correction 4 asks for and which
works across process boundaries, with `flock` retained only to bracket a
single read or write against a torn read. The concurrent-session
interleaving the lifetime lock would have covered was then traced and shown
to fail closed: a second session's rollback runs only on `NOT_COMMITTED`,
its worst effect is resetting the first session's staged index, and that
session's own sub-step 6.3 assertion then catches it and refuses — no
interleaving produces a commit, a published approval state, or a lost
working-tree file. Journal deletion was made explicitly idempotent
(`FileNotFoundError` is success) so two sessions resolving the same
transaction do not produce a spurious failure report.

**Pass 3 — this section's own load-bearing premise had gone stale.** The
paragraph introducing the three named contracts still argued that
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` "is itself one of that commit's own members, so no
reordering can make the commit come first, and a real interval therefore
exists in which approval state is durable and the approval commit is not."
Revision 56 falsifies the middle step — the commit needs the post-approval
**bytes**, not a post-approval **working-tree file** — and that premise is
precisely what the whole revision turns on, so leaving it would have left
the section arguing against its own fix. Rewritten in place to state the
corrected reason and the narrower interval that genuinely remains (a staged
index, and an unverified commit on the far side of `git commit`). The same
pass reconciled the acceptance/test text that described superseded
behaviour as current: `WFR-63`'s revision-55 clause is marked superseded in
place, and item 348's sub-scenarios (q), (r) and (v) are corrected — (r)
now asserts the state file was **never written**, which is strictly
stronger than the byte-identical restoration it used to require, and (v)
confirms the dropped `pre_procedure_state_sha256` check is absent.

### Scope

Nothing outside this transaction contract was changed. The reviewer's
"Confirmed resolutions" for `GPT-R72-001`, `GPT-R71-001`, `GPT-R70-001`,
`GPT-R69-001`, `GPT-R68-001`, `GPT-R67-001`, `GPT-R65-001`, `GPT-R64-*`,
`GPT-R63-002` and the R62 corrections are left untouched, and revision 55's
validated journal, classifier, exact committed-path-set assertion, pinned
declaration digest, index-isolation precondition and pathspec-free commit
all survive intact except where strengthened above. `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s
own round-9 fields
(`reviewed_implementation_head`/`implementation_revision`/
`technical_approval`) are left exactly as recorded, not advanced or
reinterpreted, through revisions 28 through 56. No new `WFR` row and no
`WFR` description change: `WFR-63`'s acceptance/test column carries this
round, so `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json` is unaffected.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 56 → 57) — external plan review confirmed `GPT-R73-001` through `-003` resolved but returned three important findings against the same approval/bootstrap transaction: exclusive journal *creation* was never transaction *ownership*, the "target-scoped" materialization was still an unguarded whole-file read-modify-write, and the post-amend verification set had not grown with step 7 (`GPT-R74-001` through `-003`); all three validated, all three applied as one system

`Status: REVISE`, zero blocking findings, three important. The reviewer
independently reproduced the revision-56 bundle (`bundle_id`
`86eeafff…`, `review_content_id` `f5abb363…`), rebuilt the plan-stage
projection from first principles, and reran all 489 hermetic tests green.
Their "Confirmed resolutions" section closes `GPT-R73-001`'s principal
partial-state/bootstrap-command defect, `GPT-R73-002` before durability and
at committed-content verification, and `GPT-R73-003` at the
interrupted-staging boundary. What remained were three residual defects at
boundaries revision 56 itself created.

Per the round's own instruction the three were treated as **one
approval/bootstrap transaction**, not three patches, and each correction was
checked for its effect on journal ownership, shared-state concurrency, commit
durability, recovery, and fresh-session behavior before being written down.

### Validation performed before accepting anything

Every finding was reproduced against this repository or against isolated
scratch repositories before a word of the plan changed. Nothing was accepted
on the strength of the finding's own premise.

1. **`GPT-R74-001` A — a live journal can be deleted during its own
   publication.** Reproduced the exact revision-56 acquisition sequence: a
   writer performed `os.open(O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_WRONLY)`, paused in the
   unavoidable interval before its own write, while a resolver opened the
   same pathname, observed **zero length**, took revision 56's
   "crashed-at-acquisition" branch, confirmed a clean index, and `os.remove`d
   the journal. The writer then wrote and `fsync`ed its still-open
   descriptor — now referring to an **unlinked inode** — and completed,
   believing publication had succeeded. Final observed state: writer
   successful, journal path absent. `O_EXCL` makes *creation* exclusive; it
   does not make *publication* atomic, and revision 56's own recovery branch
   was what turned that gap into data loss.
2. **`GPT-R74-001` B — a fully-written live `NOT_COMMITTED` journal can be
   resolved by a stranger.** Confirmed by reading revision 56's own step 0
   against its own step ordering: after step 4a completes and before step 5's
   first `git add`, a second session validates the journal, the classifier
   returns `NOT_COMMITTED` (no commit, `HEAD` unmoved), and the rollback runs
   — a *verified no-op* on the index, followed by deletion of the journal.
   Revision 56's stress text covered only the opposite interleaving (a second
   session resetting an **already-staged** index, caught by sub-step 6.3). It
   did not cover recovery completing *before* the first mutation, which
   leaves the original transaction running with no durable recovery record.
3. **`GPT-R74-002` — step 8b's lost update.** Reproduced the reviewer's exact
   shape with the canonical serialization: step 8b read a state file in which
   `milestone-8.state_revision == 7`; a sanctioned concurrent writer updated
   only `milestone-8` to `8` and published atomically; step 8b then replaced
   only its own work item's entry **in its previously-read in-memory object**
   and atomically replaced the whole file; the published file carried
   `milestone-8.state_revision == 7` again. Logical scoping to one entry does
   not scope the filesystem operation.
4. **`GPT-R74-003` — the post-amend verification gap is mechanical, not
   cosmetic.** Reproduced in an isolated scratch repository: an approval
   commit with a wrong declaration, a `pre-commit` hook that rewrites and
   re-stages **only** `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` — an already-included path — and
   then step 7's amend recovery. The amended commit's path set was
   byte-identical to the pre-amend commit's, so the path-set check passed;
   the declaration check passed; and the amended commit carried
   `{"state": "HOOK-REWROTE-THIS"}` instead of the authorized bytes. Under
   revision 56's "re-run **both** of this step's checks" the transaction
   would have proceeded to step 8, whose plan-stage manifest recomputation
   cannot see that path at all.
5. **The primitives the corrections rely on were validated before being
   specified**, not assumed: `os.link` publication of a fully-written,
   `fsync`ed inode (twelve concurrent contenders, exactly one winner, and a
   concurrent observer polling the final pathname throughout that never once
   saw a zero-length or partial journal); the token-scoped `os.link` takeover
   claim (eight concurrent authorized takeovers, exactly one winner, token
   rotated, `takeover_count` incremented, superseded token recorded); the
   displaced owner's ownership check failing after rotation and the
   non-owner's deletion attempt refusing; and the never-merge step 8b on all
   four of its paths, including the reviewer's own lost-update reproduction
   now refusing fail-closed with `milestone-8` byte-intact, and the
   reconciliation terminating through the idempotent no-op branch.
6. **The installed command surface was inspected rather than assumed.**
   `/bootstrap-workflow-v2`'s step-2 durability guard does compare the
   recomputed plan-stage `review_content_id` against
   `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id` and reads no journal —
   confirming that a plan-level rule cannot bind it and that revision 56's
   *structural* defence (the index-pinned state write) remains the only
   enforceable one, unchanged by this revision. Eight installed
   `.claude/commands/` files write `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`,
   and **none** of them takes any lock — which is why `GPT-R74-002`'s fix
   could not be "make every writer cooperate" and had to remove the bridge's
   own merge instead.

### `GPT-R74-001` — important — exclusive creation is not transaction ownership

Accepted in full, and the correction is deliberately larger than the
finding's minimum, because the two reported shapes have one root cause:
revision 56 had no durable notion of *who owns this transaction*, only of
*who created this file*.

**Publication.** The journal is now written and `fsync`ed to a temporary file
in `.ai-review/runtime/` and installed at the final pathname by a single
`os.link` — the portable `RENAME_NOREPLACE`-style, fully-written, no-replace
primitive the finding's required correction (1) asks for. The final pathname
therefore only ever comes into existence already complete. Two consequences
are load-bearing and are stated as such: revision 56's zero-length shape
**cannot be produced by an interrupted acquisition at all**, and so step 0's
branch that *deleted* it is **removed rather than narrowed** — that branch is
now a fail-closed refusal that deletes nothing, because under the new
primitive the only way to observe that shape is corruption or a contract
violation, neither of which a resolver may repair by deletion. A crash before
the link leaves no journal and an inert temporary file, which is the correct
outcome: no mutation can have occurred.

**Ownership.** The journal gains `owner_token` (32 hex), `takeover_count`,
and `previous_owner_tokens`, and `schema_version` moves to `2`. A named
`assert_owner` check — re-read the journal, require its `owner_token` to
equal the token this session holds — runs immediately before **every** step
that mutates Git, the index, `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, or the journal, and the
list of those steps is enumerated exhaustively rather than described. Journal
deletion is ownership-conditional in both the rollback and step 8a. An owner
whose transaction was taken over therefore fails its very next assertion and
stops, which is the finding's required test 4.

**Refuse by default; takeover is explicit.** A session that does not hold the
token refuses at step 0 — no rollback, no forward completion, no replacement,
no deletion — and reports the token, the owner progress record, and the
read-only classification. Takeover is the only ownership transfer: the user
supplies a literal authorization quoting the observed `owner_token` and
`step_seq`, the session claims exclusively via a token-scoped `os.link`
(exactly one winner), re-verifies that neither value advanced (either having
advanced *proves the owner is live*), and only then rotates the token. This
replaces a wall clock with a mechanical staleness proof, which matters
because this checklist runs as separate short-lived processes and no
lease-by-time would be trustworthy across them. After takeover the *same*
classifier and the *same* rollback/forward logic run, unchanged — required
correction (5).

**`flock` is now used nowhere.** Revision 56 kept a `LOCK_EX`/`LOCK_SH` pair
for torn-read protection. Under link-publication a reader can only open a
complete inode, and the takeover's `os.replace` is atomic against readers, so
the lock protects nothing. Removing it also removes any temptation to read
process-lifetime `flock` semantics as ownership — the specific mistake
revision 56's own stress pass 2 had already identified in the abstract but
left the vocabulary for.

A crash *inside* a takeover is bounded: steps (1)-(4) mutate nothing and (5)
is a single atomic replace, so the journal carries either the old token or
the new one. A claim link left by a session that died before rotating is
resolvable by a fresh authorized takeover that unlinks it and re-claims,
where `os.link` again admits exactly one winner — bounded, with no ladder of
ever-longer names.

### `GPT-R74-002` — important — a "target-scoped" update is still a whole-file read-modify-write

Accepted in full. The fix removes the merge rather than guarding it.

The reviewer offered three coherent contracts: serialize all writers, define
a mechanically safe compare-and-swap/retry, or narrow `D1` explicitly. The
first is not available to this bridge — every writer lives in
`.claude/commands/`, which a plan-only revision does not edit, and none of
the eight installed writers takes a lock. The second cannot be made sound in
isolation, and the reviewer said so: no read-modify-write of a shared file
can be made atomic against a writer that does not cooperate, so a
merge-plus-retry would narrow the window without closing it while still
republishing another work item's bytes from a stale read — the precise
operation that lost the update.

So the fix is (3) plus a structural change that makes the bridge safe
regardless of whether (3) has landed:

> **Corrected by revision 58 (`GPT-R75-002`), recorded rather than rewritten
> because it was this section's load-bearing conclusion.** The structural
> change is real but narrower than stated here: it removes the class in which
> step 8b *itself* republishes stale foreign bytes, and it does not make the
> bridge safe regardless of (3). A whole-file `os.replace` is atomic
> publication, not conditional publication, so a foreign write landing after
> step 8b's final re-read is still overwritten. The count below is also
> wrong: the installed writer set is **twelve**, not eight. See `D1`'s
> corrected enumeration and `D-Approval-Commits` step 8b's temporary
> state-writer quiescence window.

- **`D1` is narrowed explicitly**, in a new "Serialized
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` writes" contract: exactly one authoritative writer of
  that file at a time, with a **named** primitive
  (`.ai-review/runtime/WORKFLOW_STATE.lock`, acquired by the same atomic
  no-replace `os.link` publication, owner-token-stamped, released on every
  exit path, subject to the same refuse-by-default/explicit-takeover
  discipline). Concurrent *work items* remain fully supported — that is
  `D1`'s point and it is unchanged; concurrent *writes to the state file* are
  not. New missing-test item 354 makes honoring it an obligation on every
  writer and requires the writer enumeration to be complete rather than
  sampled, and records the pre-obligation state explicitly so the gap is
  documented rather than assumed away.
- **Step 8b never merges.** It writes only bytes it already holds — exactly
  the `expected_post_state_b64` the journal bound and the verified commit
  carries — and only when the whole file is still byte-identical to the
  pre-state, compare-and-swapped on a **fresh** re-read immediately before
  the `os.replace`. When any other work item's entry has changed it **fails
  closed**, writes nothing, and reports a deterministic reconciliation
  (apply this work item's committed entry, available verbatim from `git show
  <commit>:…`, on top of the current file). A step that never reads-and-
  rewrites foreign content cannot lose foreign content, whether or not the
  other writer cooperates.

**Revision 56's deadlock argument is preserved and answered rather than
ignored.** That argument is correct *about whole-file classification*: if
both the "write" and the "no-op" tests compare the whole file, the user's
only loss-free reconciliation is neither, so every retry refuses and the
journal can never close. This revision keeps the classification on **this
work item's own entry** and moves the whole-file test inside the write
branch only. The reconciled file is therefore recognized by the "already
equal to the expected post-state" branch on the very next run, which no-ops
and closes the journal. Reproduced end to end, including the other work
item's value surviving byte-intact through the whole sequence. Same-target
races remain fail-closed, unchanged.

### `GPT-R74-003` — important — the post-amend verification set had not grown with step 7

Accepted in full. Revision 56 added a third load-bearing step-7 assertion
(committed `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` bytes) and left the amend recovery saying
"re-run **both** of this step's checks," so the state-bytes assertion was
omitted after an amend — directly contradicting revision 56's own item 348
`(jj)`, which already required all three.

The recovery now enumerates the three checks exhaustively, in order,
against the amended SHA, and states that **no amended commit may reach step
8, step 8b, or step 8a until all three pass**. A failure of the path-set or
state-bytes check does **not** trigger a second amend — an amend re-runs the
same hook, so repeating it either reproduces the violation or loops — and an
interruption between the amend and the re-verification resumes by re-running
all three checks rather than by re-amending. The reproduction above is
recorded inline as the reason the list is exhaustive rather than
count-worded, and a standing rule now requires this enumeration, item 348
`(jj)`, and `WFR-63` to be amended together whenever the set grows again,
since a count word is exactly how the omission arose.

### Bounded adversarial stress passes

Three cycles were run against the resulting transaction, each attacking
different boundaries, per the round's own bounded rule. Their findings are
recorded in the mechanism text above rather than only here.

**Stress pass 1** (ownership and publication boundaries) confirmed: exactly
one publication winner under contention with no observable partial journal;
exactly one takeover winner under contention; a displaced owner refusing at
its next assertion; a non-owner unable to delete; and the crash-inside-
takeover shape resolving deterministically. It also surfaced two corrections
applied here rather than deferred — journal deletion had to be made
ownership-conditional in the **rollback** as well as in step 8a (the rollback
is the path a stranger would actually have reached), and `previous_owner_tokens`
had to be validated for mutual consistency with `takeover_count` so a forged
or truncated ownership history cannot pass step 0's validation.

**Stress pass 2** (materialization, hooks, and amend boundaries) confirmed
the never-merge step 8b on all four paths and the exhaustive post-amend set
against a same-path hook. It surfaced one correction applied here: item 348
`(hh)`, written for revision 56's merge-and-complete behavior, asserted that
step 8b "is confirmed to complete" in exactly the concurrency case revision
57 now refuses. Left alone it would have been an acceptance obligation
contradicting the mechanism it tests, so it was rewritten in place to assert
the *terminating* outcome rather than a particular one of the two.

**Stress pass 3** (fresh-session entry, journal close, and the bridge's
relationship to the permanent fix) attacked the *resulting plan text* rather
than the design intent, and found five internal-consistency defects created
by this revision's own edits — the failure mode several earlier rounds were
flagged for. All five are fixed here rather than left for another round:
five surviving "a fresh session re-enters step 0" statements in steps 7, 8a,
8b and 10 implied automatic resumption, which refuse-by-default no longer
permits, so step 0 now carries one governing sentence covering every such
site; the ownership summary claimed a live owner's journal "cannot be
replaced by anyone, in any window," which overclaims — a user-authorized
takeover of a paused-but-live owner is exactly the permitted case, so the
claim is narrowed to *unauthorized* sessions and the residual is stated with
its staleness check and its fail-closed backstop instead of being papered
over; step 9's "one permitted exception" still described step 8b as carrying
another work item's update through, which the never-merge rule no longer
does (the residual is identical, but it is now reached by reconciliation, not
by this procedure writing another item's bytes); `D1`'s new lock was asserted
to be acquired by the bridge with no step actually acquiring it, so step 8b
now names its acquisition and release points explicitly and states plainly
that its correctness today rests on never merging, not on the lock; and the
publication contract assumed `.ai-review/runtime/` exists, which it must
create idempotently for `os.link` to have a same-filesystem temporary to
install. Beyond those, the pass re-confirmed the properties this revision
must not have broken:
the index-pinned state write still means no consumer can read a
`CURRENT`/`IMPLEMENTING` state without its commit, and the currently
installed `/bootstrap-workflow-v2` guard still stops throughout the
transaction; the exact expected-post-state binding, pre-pin
compare-and-swap, staged-state check, committed-state check, declaration
pin, and exact committed-path-set check are all intact; every excluded-from-
`review_content_id` datum that matters (`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` bytes, the
fifth-member declaration bytes) remains separately and durably bound; the
positive path still ends in exactly one approval commit with a clean
repository, index, and no journal; and the bridge remains compatible with
`workflow-v2-1-core` being permanently `governing_workflow_version: "1"`,
since the journal is a separate local-only file requiring no
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` schema change and therefore no `D3` validator change.

**Final verification sweep** (after pass 3's repairs): re-ran the four
hermetic suites (489/489), the 63-row plan/mapping conformance (identical ID
sets, zero description mismatches), and `validate_state` /
`validate_registry_mapping_coverage` / `validate_registry_topological_order`
against the edited documents; re-walked every cross-reference this revision
touched (steps 0, 4a, 5, 6.1b, 6.2, 6.5, 7, 8, 8a, 8b, 9, 10, 11, the three
named contracts, `D1`, `WFR-63`, and items 347-354) for the stale-count and
stale-mechanism classes that produced `GPT-R74-003` and pass 3's own
findings. No further blocking or important defect surfaced.

The stated bound is three repair/stress cycles, and all three were used —
cycle 1 (ownership and publication), cycle 2 (the item 348 `(hh)`
contradiction), cycle 3 (the five internal-consistency defects above), each
with its repairs applied in this revision. The sweep following cycle 3 found
nothing further, but it is reported as a verification sweep rather than
claimed as a fourth clean pass, and **no known blocking or important defect
in this transaction contract remains unfixed**. Two classes are recorded as
deliberate, stated residuals rather than defects, because neither is
closable by this bridge: a user-authorized takeover can displace a live but
paused owner (mechanically staleness-checked in front, fail-closed behind),
and a foreign writer that ignores `D1`'s lock can still race step 8b's
final re-read — which is why step 8b never merges.

> **The second half of that sentence is withdrawn by revision 58
> (`GPT-R75-002`)**, and is left here rather than erased because it was the

> It can cost exactly the foreign writer's content: not merging prevents step

> temporary state-writer quiescence window.

### Scope

Nothing outside this transaction contract was changed. The reviewer's

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 78 → 79) — external plan review found revision 78's consumer side correctly aimed and defectively built: a conformance arm that cannot be implemented as specified, a rule stated at a strength no mechanism in this design provides, and one consumer placed after its own authority-changing write; **zero blocking**, all six findings accepted (`GPT-OPUS-R97-001` through `-006`)

Revision 78's own corrections are confirmed resolved at their reviewed
boundaries — both `GPT-R96` findings closed. The reviewer independently
confirmed `GPT-R96-001`'s premise (`grep -rn REJECTED` over `.claude/commands/`,
`scripts/` and the three protocol documents still returns **zero** matches, so
revision 77's marker did have a writer and no owned consumer-side refusal) and
verified `GPT-R96-002` **by counting rather than by reading**: item 375's
revision markers, extracted mechanically, are `71, 72, 72, 72, 73, 72, 74, 73,
75, 74`, maximum **75**, and the corrected clause now reads 75 in the plan, in
`REVIEW_REQUEST.md` and in the byte-identical bundled `PLAN.md` alike. The
normative rule, the work-item scoping, the subject-boundary placement, the
generator writability carve-out, the bootstrap direct read, revision 77's
marker lifecycle, the four-field binding and the review-content live equality
were all re-verified clean, and six of revision 78's seven consumer placements
were confirmed to precede their command's first durable mutation against the
actual command files.

**All six findings were validated against this repository before anything was
edited. All six are accepted; none is rejected.** The three Important ones are
defects in revision 78's own text rather than gaps in what it set out to do,
and the pattern is worth recording as plainly as the fix was: the round that
finally attached readers to the marker specified the derivation, the ordering
and the concurrency of those readers in prose that had never been evaluated
against the live command set.

`GPT-OPUS-R97-001` — **accepted, and validated by executing the predicate
rather than by reading it.** Revision 78's arm derives the consumer set from
"every command file that resolves a bundle or feedback directory and advances a
gate". Run against `.claude/commands/`, `resolve_feedback_dir` appears in
`prepare-functional-review.md:11` and `apply-functional-review.md:10` — in each
file's own header text — and both advance a gate
(`AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`; `FIXING_FUNCTIONAL_FINDINGS` exiting to
`AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`). The derivation therefore classifies
as **required consumers** exactly the two commands part 3b exempts and the same
arm asserts name the assertion **nowhere**. Unimplementable as written, and the
only escape — hand-patching the exempt set back in as a literal — is precisely
the maintained caller inventory the arm exists to avoid.

**Applied by rekeying the derivation on the subject artifact, which is what
the exemptions were always reasoning about.** A command is a required consumer
iff it (A) reads `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`, (B) reads `MANIFEST.md` or recomputes or
compares `bundle_id` over a `<bundle_dir>` it did not itself generate in the
same invocation, or (C) presents `<bundle_dir>` or the canonical archive as
ready for external review. `FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW.md` satisfies none of the three,
which is the exemption paragraph's own stated reason and is now checkable
rather than assumed. The rule is stated **once**, in part 3b, and referenced by
item 376(t) rather than restated there.

**The reviewer's own suggested predicate was tested before being adopted, and
was not adopted verbatim.** It proposed "reads a `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` carrying
`Reviewed bundle ID:`, or resolves `<bundle_dir>` and reads `MANIFEST.md` /
recomputes `bundle_id`". Measured against the live directory that predicate
**drops a named consumer** — `milestone-implement.md` matches
`REVIEW_FEEDBACK|MANIFEST.md|bundle_id` zero times — and **selects an
unclassified file**, `bootstrap-workflow-v2.md`, whose two `bundle_id`
occurrences are its state-sync description of WF0's approving feedback and
which is the checkpoint driver rather than consumer #5's plan-approval
procedure. Disjunct (C) is added for the first, and the exemption list is
completed for the second. This is recorded rather than quietly corrected
because the finding's whole point is that a predicate must be evaluated against
the directory before it is written down.

**Two classification defects surfaced while performing the finding's own
required verification** — "verify it partitions today's thirteen command files
exactly as part 3b's prose does" — **and both are disclosed as extensions of
this finding rather than slipped in.** First, `/prepare-review` step 4 says
"Report the bundle location", which is disjunct (C) and is the identical act
consumer #7 exists for; revision 78 exempted it wholesale under the generator
heading, so a `/prepare-review` whose own generation refused and wrote the
marker would report the withdrawn bundle's location as the round's artifact.
The generator exemption is therefore scoped to the **generation path** — the
writing, updating and clearing that must never be blocked — and not to a report
presenting the result as review-ready; no deadlock is introduced, since a
generation that verifies its own end state clears the marker before its report
is reached. Second, `bootstrap-workflow-v2.md` was in neither list, which a
completeness-asserting arm would fail on immediately; it is named exempt with
its reason. Eight required consumers and five exempt commands now classify all
thirteen files.

`GPT-OPUS-R97-002` — **accepted, and the mechanism claim verified directly.**
`grep -c flock scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py scripts/workflow_state.py
scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh` returns `0` for all three. The race is concrete
rather than theoretical: a consumer reads the marker as absent, a second
operator's generation fails and its withdrawal writes the marker — which this
part requires it to write **first**, before any removal — and the consumer's
own first durable write lands anyway. The reviewer's observation that item
354's lock would not close it after landing is correct and is now stated in the
plan: that primitive's critical section is `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, the marker is
at `bundle_dir/../REJECTED` outside it, the withdrawal performs no state write
at all, and the plan already says the primitive "is not a compare-and-swap
against a non-cooperating writer".

**Applied as the finding's option (a), plus option (b)'s honesty, rather than
one or the other.** Each consumer asserts **twice**: at its existing
pre-mutation refusal point, and again immediately under its own mutation guard,
textually adjacent to the first durable write. That adds no new mechanism —
`/approve-review` step 5 already carries exactly this discipline for the
conditional fifth member, and for `/milestone-implement` the two points
coincide with `-003`'s correction. What the second assertion buys is stated
without euphemism: it removes every window spanning user interaction,
recomputation or generation, and it does **not** make the check atomic with the
write. That residual is disclosed on the same footing as the temporary bridge's
own post-final-re-read interleaving — outside the safe execution contract, with
a stated recovery — never as a loss-free race, on the precedent revision 75 set
when it withdrew a false quarantine claim rather than quietly editing it. The
reviewer's fair scoping of the **bootstrap** consumer is adopted and cited in
step 2 itself: that procedure runs inside the user-authorized state-writer
quiescence window it refuses to open a transaction without, and
`record_bundle_generation` is one of the twelve enumerated prohibited writers,
so a concurrent generation there is already a quiescence violation. That
coverage is stated as specific to consumer #5 and explicitly not extended to
the six permanent consumers.

than the summary.** `.claude/commands/milestone-implement.md:146` calls

advanced.

## WF8b finding disposition (revision 77 → 78) — external plan review found revision 77's marker lifecycle correct and the marker itself owned by a producer and by no consumer, so the fail-closed property it exists to establish was asserted of no reader; **zero blocking**, both findings accepted (`GPT-R96-001`/`-002`)

Revision 77's own corrections are confirmed resolved at their reviewed
boundaries — all five `OPUS-R94` findings closed: the marker is no longer

review-content-id function at all, listing each of the five protected paths' Git

literal and the per-row conformance re-derived at 67/67 in both directions, and
state, registry, mapping-coverage and config validation re-run independently.
The reviewer's evidence scoping is accepted as stated: the archive carries no
`.git` database, so the 698/698 stress aggregate is **not** treated as evidence
for any obligation this revision or its predecessor newly specified.

**Both findings were validated against this repository before anything was
edited. Both are accepted; neither is rejected.** The Important one is a gap
this plan left open in the same part it has been repairing for three
consecutive rounds, and it is worth recording as plainly as the repairs were:
each round closed the *producer* half more tightly, and none of them ever asked
who reads the result.

`GPT-R96-001` — **accepted, and validated at the mechanism rather than at the
summary.** Three checks, each run before anything was edited. First, the
normative text: part 3b's sentence "its presence beside a `current/` is always
sufficient to refuse treating that directory as reviewable, with no identifier
recomputation needed" is a statement about the marker, and nothing anywhere
requires a reader to perform that refusal. Second, ownership: `WFR-67`'s
implementation surface named `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh`,
`scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py`, `.claude/commands/milestone-plan.md`,
`.claude/commands/apply-plan-review.md` and
`docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` — the generator, the two commands that
*drive* generation, and the protocol document — and not one command that
*consumes* a bundle or a verdict; item 376(l) and (q) assert publication,
ordering, cross-generation persistence and clearing, and no arm of either starts
from a marked bundle and requires a consumer to refuse it. Third, the live
surface: `REJECTED` occurs **zero** times under `.claude/commands/`, `scripts/`,
`docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`
and `docs/ai-workflow/PLAN_REVIEW_WORKFLOW.md`. That third fact is expected
before `WF8b` implements anything and is not itself the finding; the finding is
that no *obligation* would ever make it change. The severity assessment is
accepted over the earlier Optional filing for the reason the reviewer gives: the
marker was introduced specifically to convert a fully self-verifying refused
artifact into a fail-closed one, and a producer-only marker converts it into a
*labelled* one, which is a different and weaker property.

**Applied as the required correction states, and slightly beyond it in one
respect that is named rather than slipped in.** Part 3b gains a consumer-side
bullet stating the rule once: while a work item is marked, every operation that
treats its `current/` bundle or a verdict bound to it as reviewable, ingestible
or approvable refuses before its first durable write, with no identifier
recomputation required and none sufficient. Three scoping decisions are stated
explicitly rather than left to an implementer, because each of them is a place
this plan has previously been found ambiguous. The rule is **work-item-scoped,
not stage-scoped** — the marker sits beside a `current/` that every stage
shares, so stage-scoping the effect would require a reader to decide which
stage a surviving `current/` belongs to at precisely the moment its manifest is
the thing not to be trusted; the clearing rule is unqualified by stage for the
same reason, and a completed, verified generation at any stage supersedes what
the marker names because it rewrites the manifest the residue's
self-verification depends on. The rule is enforced **at the subject boundary,
never in path resolution**, exactly as the finding requires: the generator must
be able to see, write, update and clear a marked location, and `/prepare-review`
is on that same generator side. And it is carried by **one** shared assertion
(`assert_bundle_not_rejected`) over **one** shared path resolver
(`resolve_rejected_marker_path`), used by the writer as well as by every reader
— the finding's own preference, and independently forced by this design's
history: `assert_local_generation_matches`' caller inventory was maintained as
prose and went stale in two consecutive finding rounds, the second of them
against the first's own correction.

**The consumer surface was audited rather than asserted**, since the finding
asks for the actual set. Seven call sites: `/review-plan` step 5,
`/record-manual-plan-review` step 6, `/apply-plan-review` step 1,
`/approve-review` step 2 at both stages, the bootstrap plan-approval procedure's
step 2, `/apply-implementation-review` step 1, and the hand-off report of
`/milestone-plan`/`/milestone-implement`. Two of these go beyond the finding's
own minimum and are named as such: `/apply-implementation-review` consumes the
identical bundle-bound `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md` shape one stage over, and the
hand-off report is what turns a surviving canonical archive into something an
operator attaches — the finding's own required test 4. Three exemptions are
stated **with proof rather than by omission**: the generator (writer and only
sanctioned clearer; blocking it would make the marker escapable only by hand),
`/prepare-functional-review`/`/apply-functional-review` (their subject is
`FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW.md`, a user-written checklist carrying no `Reviewed bundle
ID:` and binding to no bundle, so no refused bundle can reach them), and
`/accept-milestone` (consumes durable approval state, not a bundle). The
bootstrap step-2 call is additionally written so it is executable **in the
interval before the helper exists** — the identical read at
`.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/REJECTED` — because that procedure is the path
this very revision's approval takes and a step that cannot be performed is the
defect `OPUS-R93-001` found in the same place one round ago.

Item 376 gains **(t)** with all six required properties, over the fixture the
finding specifies: the marked-but-otherwise-fully-verifying residue, with each
consumer's refusal asserted before any write and with the repository, ledger,

**conformance arm** deriving the consumer set from the command files rather
than from a literal list, so a future marker-blind consumer fails the suite
instead of passing it silently.

`GPT-R96-002` — **accepted, and verified by counting rather than by reading the

`(new, revision 71)`, three `(extended in place, revision 72)`, one
`(extended in place, revision 73)`, one `(extended in place, revision 74,
OPUS-R91-002/-003)` and one `(extended in place, revision 75,

**On `OPUS-R95-001`/`-002`.** This round's feedback reports both as
