      commit already attests.

      **This step never merges** (rewritten, revision 57, `GPT-R74-002`).
      Revision 56 called this step "target-scoped" and implemented it as
      parse the whole file → replace one entry in the parsed object →
      serialize the whole file → `os.replace`. Logically scoping the change
      to one entry does not scope the *filesystem operation*: it remained a
      whole-file read-modify-write with no lock, version check, or
      compare-and-swap across the interval between its read and its replace.
      Independently reproduced (see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 56 →
      57)" below): with `milestone-8` legitimately advanced to
      `state_revision: 8` **after** this step's read and **before** its
      replace, the published file carried `state_revision: 7` again — the
      other work item's update silently lost, at the exact boundary
      `GPT-R73-002` had required this contract to make safe. Revision 56's
      own stress reproduction only exercised an update visible *before* the
      read, which this step already handled.

      The correction removes the merge rather than guarding it. This step
      now writes **only** bytes it already holds — the exact
      `expected_post_state_b64` the journal bound and the verified commit
      carries — and never republishes foreign content it read moments
      earlier.

      **What not merging does and does not buy (rewritten, revision 58,
      `GPT-R75-002`)**. Revision 57 concluded from this that "a step that
      never merges cannot lose an update it merged over," and then
      over-generalized it into "cannot lose foreign content, whether or not
      the other writer cooperates." The first sentence is true and is kept;
      the second is false and is withdrawn. Not merging removes exactly one
      class — **republishing stale foreign bytes this step itself read**. It
      does **not** make a whole-file `os.replace` conditional on anything:
      `os.replace` is atomic *publication*, not *compare-and-swap*. A
      foreign write that lands after this step's final fresh re-read and
      before its replace is overwritten wholesale, and the fresh re-read is
      a check, not a fence. Independently reproduced (see "WF8b finding
      disposition (revision 57 → 58)" below), with the bridge holding
      `.ai-review/runtime/WORKFLOW_STATE.lock` and without it, identically
      in both cases: `milestone-8.state_revision` observed as `7` at the
      final re-read, legitimately advanced to `8` by an unlocked installed
      writer, and `7` again in the published file. There is no available
      primitive that makes a whole-file replace conditional against a writer
      that does not cooperate — an advisory lock plus a fresh re-read plus
      `os.replace` is emphatically not one, and this plan does not pretend
      otherwise by assembling a "check hash, then replace" pair and calling
      it a CAS. The interval in which the installed writers still ignore
      `D1`'s primitive is therefore covered by an explicit **execution
      precondition**, not by a mechanical claim — see "Temporary
      state-writer quiescence window" below.

      Acquire the mutation guard (`step: "step-8b-materialize"`,
      `step_class: "destructive"` — **revision 59, `GPT-R76-001`**: this is
      the mutation whose delayed completion survives everything, since journal
      close *ends the quiescence window* and so legalizes exactly the foreign
      writes a stale `os.replace` would then overwrite; independently
      reproduced, a foreign `state_revision` went `8` → `7` after the
      displaced owner's delayed write, with the journal already gone) and run
      `assert_owner` inside it (revision
      57; guarded, revision 58), read and parse the current working-tree
      file (invalid
      JSON: stop, leave the journal, report), and classify **this work
      item's own entry**, exactly as before:
      - **Already equal to the expected post-state's own
        `work_items["workflow-v2-1-core"]` entry**: an interrupted earlier
        run of this same step — or a user reconciliation, below — already
        completed it. **No-op.** This is what makes the step idempotent and
        re-runnable under step 0's forward completion, and it is also the
        terminating exit for the refusal branch below.
      - **Equal to the journal's pre-procedure state's own
        `work_items["workflow-v2-1-core"]` entry**: this work item's state
        still needs publishing. Now branch on the **whole file**:
        - **Byte-identical to `pre_procedure_state_b64`** (the
          overwhelmingly common case — nothing wrote the file during the
          transaction): **publish `expected_post_state_b64` whole-file**,
          via the same atomic temp-file/`fsync`/`os.replace`/directory-
          `fsync` sequence the journal itself uses, having re-read the file
          and re-confirmed that digest immediately before the `os.replace`.
          The published bytes are exactly the committed blob, so step 9's
          clean-tree confirmation holds exactly, and no foreign content
          passes through this step at all. **That final re-read is a
          detection check, not a compare-and-swap** (revision 58,
          `GPT-R75-002`; revision 57 called it "a compare-and-swap on a
          **fresh** read," which named it as something stronger than it is).
          It closes every foreign write visible before it — which, under the
          quiescence window below, is the complete set of foreign writes the
          bridge's safe execution contract admits — and it is powerless
          against one landing in the instants after it. Naming it accurately
          is the point: it is the last of several detections, not a fence.
        - **Anything else** — the file differs from the pre-state somewhere
          outside this work item's entry, i.e. a sanctioned concurrent
          operation updated a **different** work item: **refuse, fail
          closed.** Write nothing, leave the journal in place, and report
          the durable approval commit's identity, exactly which
          `work_items` keys differ, and the deterministic reconciliation:
          apply this work item's own committed entry — available verbatim
          from `git show <commit>:docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` — on
          top of the current file, preserving the other item's update. This
          **terminates**: the next run's step 0 classifies `COMMITTED`,
          re-enters this step, finds this work item's entry already equal to
          the expected post-state, takes the no-op branch, and closes the
          journal. The other work item's bytes are never read, rewritten, or
          republished by this procedure at any point.
      - **Neither**: something outside this transaction rewrote **this work
        item's own** entry while the commit was being created. Stop, leave
        the journal in place, overwrite nothing, and report both the
        durable approval commit's identity and the divergence (`git diff
        HEAD -- docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`) for manual
        reconciliation. This is the one genuinely unresolvable shape: two
        writers disagree about the same work item's own state, and no
        automatic rule can prefer one. Same-target races therefore remain
        fail-closed, unchanged from revision 56.

      **Why not a merge with a retry loop** (revision 57, `GPT-R74-002`;
      count corrected, revision 58):
      because no read-modify-write of a shared file can be made atomic
      against a writer that does not cooperate, and this bridge cannot make
      the other writers cooperate — every one of them lives in
      `.claude/commands/`, which a plan-only revision does not edit
      (verified directly against this repository: **twelve** installed
      command files write
      `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, and none of them takes any
      lock; revision 57 said eight, an undercount corrected in `D1`). A
      merge-plus-retry would narrow the lost-update window without
      closing it, and would still be republishing another work item's bytes
      from a stale read — the precise operation that lost the update. Not
      merging is strictly stronger than merging carefully: it removes that
      class, at the cost of one deterministic, terminating manual
      reconciliation in the rare case where a different work item is written
      during this transaction's post-commit interval. It does **not**, on
      its own, make the whole-file publication conditional — see "What not
      merging does and does not buy" above.

      **Why this does not reintroduce revision 56's deadlock** (revision
      57): revision 56 rejected "whole-file" on the ground that a whole-file
      *classification* deadlocks — the user's only loss-free reconciliation
      produces "expected post-state **plus** the other item's update," which
      is neither the pre-state nor the expected post-state whole-file, so
      every retry refuses identically and the journal can never close. That
      argument is correct, and it applies to whole-file **classification**.
      This step classifies on **this work item's entry** and only then
      decides how to write, so the reconciled file is recognized on the
      first branch above and the transaction closes. Independently
      reproduced end to end: ordinary path writes the committed blob; re-run
      no-ops; a foreign `milestone-8` update lands the fail-closed refusal
      with that update byte-intact; and after reconciliation the next run
      no-ops and closes with `milestone-8` still at its own new value. The
      residual difference from `HEAD` is then confined to the other work
      item's entry, which is ordinary uncommitted work belonging to whoever
      made it, not a defect in this approval — step 9 states that exception
      explicitly.

      **The shared-state concurrency contract this depends on** is stated
      normatively in `D1` ("Serialized `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` writes"), which
      revision 57 narrows from an implicit "concurrent writers are fine" to
      a single named serialization primitive that every writer must acquire,
      with missing-test item 354 making that an implementation obligation
      (owned by `WF8b`'s continued scope as of revision 58, `GPT-R75-003`)
      and item 347 binding the permanent `/approve-review` to it.

      **This step acquires that primitive** (updated, revision 59,
      `GPT-R76-002`, to the corrected `flock` form). Concretely: `os.open`
      `.ai-review/runtime/WORKFLOW_STATE.lock` with `O_CREAT | O_RDWR` and
      take `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` **before this step's classification
      read**, hold it across the classification, the fresh re-read and the
      `os.replace`, and release it (`LOCK_UN`, then close) on every exit
      path — the write path, both refusal paths, and the no-op path. This
      satisfies `D1`'s "the read that feeds the write is inside the critical
      section" requirement literally: the classification read, the final
      re-read, and the publication are one critical section. The lock is
      held across this one step only, never across the transaction, so it
      introduces no cross-process lock and no abandonment problem — the
      kernel releases it if this session dies, which is exactly why `flock`
      is correct here and was correct to reject for the multi-process
      transaction as a whole. Every other step of this procedure is a reader
      of that file, not a writer (sub-step 6.1a's check reads, and refuses
      rather than writing), so this is the procedure's only acquisition
      point. **The lock is what makes this step correct once every writer
      honors it, and today none does** — so it is, for now, a
      forward-compatibility acquisition and nothing more. What makes this
      step safe *today* is not the lock and not the never-merge rule but the
      temporary execution precondition immediately below (rewritten,
      revision 58, `GPT-R75-002`; revision 57 said "the never-merge rule is
      what makes it correct **today**," which `GPT-R75-002` disproved).

      **Temporary state-writer quiescence window (new, revision 58,
      `GPT-R75-002`)**. Because a plan-only revision cannot retrofit the
      twelve installed writers before this plan is itself approved, the
      bridge's safety for the interval before item 354 lands is an honest,
      enforceable **execution precondition** rather than a mechanism:
      - **Authorization.** Before step 4a publishes the journal, this
        procedure requires the user's own current-turn literal **state-writer
        quiescence authorization**, naming `workflow-v2-1-core`, the `plan`
        stage, and stating that no other workflow session, command, or
        manual edit that can write `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
        will run until this transaction's journal is closed. It is recorded
        verbatim in the journal's `quiescence_authorization` field, so the
        window's authority is durable and a fresh-session forward completion
        inherits it. **Absent or malformed: refuse outright** — no journal is
        published, no index is touched, nothing is mutated, exactly like a
        step-3 or step-4 refusal. This is the "the bridge must refuse unless
        that temporary bootstrap precondition is explicitly established"
        requirement, and it is placed at step 4a rather than at step 8b so
        that no mutation of any kind occurs under an unauthorized window.
      - **Start.** At step 4a, the instant the journal is published. The
        journal's existence *is* the window's durable marker: while it
        exists, the window is open.
      - **End.** At step 8a, when the journal is deleted — or when the
        approval-transaction rollback deletes it. If any branch stops with
        the journal deliberately **left in place**, the window stays open
        through the manual resolution and closes only when a later session
        resolves the transaction and closes the journal. There is no branch
        on which the window ends silently.
      - **Prohibited during the window**, exhaustively: every installed
        command that writes that path — all twelve enumerated in `D1` —
        in any session and in any worktree sharing this repository, plus any
        manual or ad-hoc edit of the file. `/prepare-review` is the one
        installed command that never writes it and is therefore unrestricted.
      - **Reconciliation obeys the same rule.** Both manual reconciliations
        this step can require — the foreign-update branch's "apply this work
        item's committed entry on top of the current file" and the divergent
        branch's manual repair — are themselves writes of the shared file,
        so they are performed **inside** the same window, by the user, with
        no other writer running. Otherwise the identical read/modify/write
        race simply relocates to the reconciliation, which is exactly the
        outcome `GPT-R75-002`'s required correction (2) names.
      - **Violation behavior, stated without euphemism.** The window is an
        authorization, not a lock; nothing mechanically prevents a user from
        running a prohibited command. What the bridge does is (i) refuse to
        open a transaction without the authorization on record; (ii) detect
        every foreign write visible up to its final re-read and fail closed
        on it — the classification's "anything else" branch and the
        pre-`os.replace` re-read between them cover the whole window except
        its last instants; and (iii) treat a foreign write landing between
        that final re-read and the `os.replace` as **outside this bridge's
        safe execution contract**: it is a violation of the window, it can
        lose that writer's update, and it is reported as a state-loss
        incident to be recovered from Git (the approval commit carries this
        work item's entry verbatim; the other item's own writer must redo
        its update) — never described as a loss-free race. No in-contract
        execution of this bridge contains that interleaving, because no
        in-contract execution contains a concurrent writer at all.
      - **This bridge is temporary, and it is retired as a whole — it does
        not retire its own window** (rewritten, revision 61, resolves
        `GPT-R78-002`; revision 59's `GPT-R76-003` machine-readable
        retirement condition moves to the permanent command rather than
        being withdrawn). For **every** run of this temporary bootstrap
        bridge, the explicit user authorization above is required. This
        procedure evaluates no completion obligation, stores no commit in
        `quiescence_authorization`, pins no `HEAD`, and can produce no
        `PIN_MOVED`. Revision 60 specified the opposite and
        `GPT-R78-002` proved it unexecutable in three independent ways, each
        re-confirmed against the authoritative text here before acceptance:
        step 4a required the literal authorization unconditionally and had no
        branch for a derived `PASS`; `schema_version` 3 defines
        `quiescence_authorization` as the literal user text, validated at
        step 0 to name the work item and the `plan` stage, with no field and
        no encoding for a commit pin; and step 6 deliberately creates the
        `Workflow-Plan-Approval` commit **between** the pin and its use, so
        `HEAD` necessarily moves from the pinned `C` to the new commit `A`
        and step 8b's equality assertion deterministically returns
        `PIN_MOVED` on the *positive* path. That transition was independently
        reproduced in an isolated repository, exactly as the finding
        reported.
      - **Where retirement actually lives.** Item 347's permanent
        `/approve-review` may drop this authorization once, and only once,
        item 354 is implemented, **its implementation is independently
        reviewed and technically approved**, and
        `workflow_state.resolve_completion_obligations(...)` **derives**
        `PASS` for `WFO-STATE-SERIALIZATION` under an approved verifier
        identity, as defined in `D-Completion-Obligations`. Every other
        classification (`FAIL`, `DIVERGED`, `PIN_MOVED`,
        `VERIFIER_UNAPPROVED`, `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE`,
        `UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION`, `UNRESOLVABLE`) makes that permanent command
        fall back to requiring exactly this explicit window instead.
        **`complete_work_item` consumes that identical call under identical
        pinning, identical authority and identical refusal rules**, so "the
        window may be retired" and "`WF8b` may complete" cannot disagree in
        either direction. The lifecycle is therefore linear and has no state
        in which concurrent writes are called safe while any supported
        installed writer still ignores the primitive: temporary bridge under
        explicit quiescence → item 354 implemented → implementation review
        and technical approval → derived, verifier-authorized `PASS` →
        permanent command no longer needs the bootstrap-only authorization.
        See `D1`'s "Transition from temporary quiescence to permanent
        serialization."

      The asymmetry with sub-step 6.1a is deliberate and is the general
      rule this transaction follows: **before durability, refuse and let
      the retry recapture; after durability, complete forward without
      clobbering.** Refusing at 6.1a costs nothing (no commit exists, and
      rerunning from step 0 recaptures the new pre-state and recomputes the
      post-state on top of it), whereas refusing here permanently would
      strand a valid, verified approval commit behind an unclosable
      journal.
  8a. **Close the durable approval journal (new, revision 55,
      `GPT-R72-001`; renumbered after 8b and its idempotence claim
      corrected, revision 56, `GPT-R73-003`)**: only once step 7's checks,
      step 8's manifest
      verification, and step 8b's materialization have all passed against
      the final commit SHA, **acquire the mutation guard (`step:
      "step-8a-close-journal"`, `step_class: "destructive"`)** and run
      `assert_owner` inside it one final time (new,
      revision 57, `GPT-R74-001` — deletion is ownership-conditional, so a
      session that no longer holds the token closes nothing; made a
      guarded, unbreakable window, revision 58, `GPT-R75-001`, so a takeover
      can neither rotate ownership during the close nor be authorized to
      break the guard that covers it) and then delete
      `.ai-review/runtime/PLAN_APPROVAL_JOURNAL.json` (`os.remove`, then
      `os.fsync` the containing directory), followed by the owner progress
      record `PLAN_APPROVAL_OWNER.<owner_token>.json` and any
      `PLAN_APPROVAL_JOURNAL.claim.<token>` link for a token in
      `previous_owner_tokens`, and finally the guard itself — released last,
      so the close is atomic with respect to takeover from beginning to end.
      **The quiescence window ends here** (revision 58, `GPT-R75-002`).
      This is the transaction's
      commit point in the bookkeeping sense: before it, a fresh session
      re-enters step 0 and resolves the transaction; after it, the
      ordinary post-approval steady state holds. Both sides of that
      boundary are safe, because a crash before this deletion leaves a
      journal alongside a real approval commit, which step 0 classifies
      `COMMITTED` and completes forward.

      **The post-commit interval's writes, stated exactly** (revision 56):
      revision 55 claimed "the only write among them is this deletion,"
      which was already untrue of its own step 7 (`git add` plus `git
      commit --amend`) and is now also untrue of step 8b. The accurate
      claim, and the one each of these steps is held to, is that **every
      write in this interval is idempotent and re-runnable**, and there are
      exactly three:
      1. step 7's amend recovery (`git add` of the corrected declaration,
         then `git commit --amend --no-edit`) — re-runnable via the
         three-way index classification in (a), which resumes an
         interrupted amend instead of refusing on it, and re-verifies **all
         three** of step 7's checks against the amended SHA afterwards
         (revision 57, `GPT-R74-003`: committed path set, committed
         `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` bytes, declaration bytes — an interruption
         between the amend and that re-verification resumes by re-running
         the whole set, never by re-amending);
      2. step 8b's working-tree materialization — re-runnable via its
         classification of this work item's entry, whose first branch is an
         explicit no-op and whose fail-closed foreign-update branch
         terminates through that same no-op after reconciliation;
      3. this journal deletion — re-runnable because an absent journal is
         step 0's "no transaction in flight" case, and because the deletion
         itself treats `FileNotFoundError` as success rather than as an
         error (revision 56, stress pass 2), so two sessions that both
         resolve the same transaction both report completion instead of one
         of them reporting a spurious failure.
      Steps 7's and 8's verification checks are pure reads and are
      trivially re-runnable. An interruption at any boundary between them
      therefore either completes forward automatically on the next session
      or lands in one of this step 10's enumerated fail-closed states —
      never in a state the procedure has no rule for.
  9. **Report and stop (renumbered from step 8, revision 54)**: report the
     resulting phase (`IMPLEMENTING`)
     exactly as `/approve-review`'s own step 7 would, confirm the working
     tree is clean, and stop — never chaining into implementation in the
     same invocation, identical to the installed command's own step 7.
     **The one permitted exception** (revision 56, stress pass 1;
     re-derived, revision 57, `GPT-R74-002`): if a sanctioned concurrent
     operation updated a different work item's entry during this
     transaction, step 8b refuses rather than merging, and the user's
     reconciliation — applying this work item's committed entry on top of
     the current file — leaves that other entry present, after which step
     8b's next run no-ops. So `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` may
     still differ from `HEAD` in that other entry alone. (Revision 56
     reached the same residual by having step 8b carry the other entry
     through itself; revision 57 reaches it without this procedure ever
     writing another work item's bytes, which is the point of the
     never-merge rule. The residual, and this exception, are identical
     either way.) Confirm that the
     residual difference is confined to `work_items` keys other than
     `workflow-v2-1-core`, report it explicitly as another work item's
     pre-existing uncommitted change rather than as this procedure's own
     residue, and treat any other dirty path — or any difference touching
     this work item's own entry — as a failure. The
     clean-tree confirmation is meaningful only because step 8b has by now
     materialized `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` to exactly the
     committed bytes (revision 56); reaching this step with that file still
     unmaterialized is impossible, since step 8b either completes, no-ops,
     or stops the procedure. The
     journal never affects that confirmation: it is gitignored
     and so never appears in `git status --porcelain`, and by this point
     step 8a has deleted it in any case.
  10. **Failure-branch summary — no second commit, and no orphaned partial
      state, ever (renumbered from step 9, revision 54; extended
      revision 55, `GPT-R72-001`, to state each branch's exact residual
      state)**:
      - **step 0 validation failure or `AMBIGUOUS` classification**:
        nothing is mutated at all; the journal is left in place; manual
        resolution.
      - **step 0 zero-length/unparseable journal (rewritten, revision 57,
        `GPT-R74-001`; replaces revision 56's auto-delete branch)**:
        nothing is mutated, **nothing is deleted**, the journal is left in
        place, manual resolution. Under link-publication this shape cannot
        be produced by an interrupted acquisition at all, so deleting it
        can only ever destroy something this procedure did not create.
      - **step 0 non-owner refusal (new, revision 57, `GPT-R74-001`)**: a
        valid journal exists whose `owner_token` this session does not
        hold; nothing is mutated, nothing is deleted, the journal is left
        in place. Resolve by resuming in the owning session or by explicit
        takeover.
      - **step 0 takeover refusal (new, revision 57)**: the claim was lost
        to another taker, or the `owner_token`/`step_seq` advanced between
        authorization and claim (the owner is demonstrably live); nothing
        is mutated and the live owner is untouched.
      - **`assert_owner` failure at any mutating step (new, revision 57)**:
        the transaction was taken over while this session held it. Stop
        immediately, mutate nothing further, **release the mutation guard
        this session acquired** (revision 58 — its `holder_owner_token` is
        now a superseded token, so even an unreleased one is deterministically
        reclaimable by the new owner), leave the journal in place,
        and report the held and observed tokens. The new owner's own step 0
        resolves the transaction; this session never competes with it.
      - **mutation-guard acquisition refusal at a mutating step (new,
        revision 58, `GPT-R75-001`)**: the guard is held by the current
        epoch and this session is not its holder, so another operation on
        this same transaction is in flight. Mutate nothing, acquire nothing,
        leave the journal in place, and report the guard's
        `lease_id`/`step`/`step_class`. A superseded-epoch guard is instead
        reclaimed and acquisition retried once, with no report and no
        authorization.
      - **takeover guard refusal (new, revision 58, `GPT-R75-001`;
        destructive set widened, revision 59, `GPT-R76-001`)**: the
        takeover reached step (3a) and found the guard held in the current
        epoch. For `step_class: "destructive"` — the commit, the amend, the
        state-file materialization, the rollback's index reset, or a journal
        close — it refuses unconditionally and
        reports that no authorization can release it, naming the out-of-band
        manual guard clearance as the only alternative to resuming in the
        owning session; for `"ordinary"` (index-only staging) it
        refuses unless the guard-release authorization quoted this exact
        `lease_id`, and refuses again if the `lease_id` has since changed
        (the owner is live). Nothing is mutated and the live owner is
        untouched in every case; the claim link for `T` remains and is
        reusable by a fresh authorized takeover.
      - **step 4a quiescence-authorization refusal (new, revision 58,
        `GPT-R75-002`)**: the user's literal state-writer quiescence
        authorization was absent or did not name this work item and stage.
        Nothing written, index untouched, no journal opened, no token
        generated. Supply the authorization and rerun from the beginning
        (step 0).
      - **step 3 non-clean-index refusal**: nothing written, index
        untouched, no journal opened. Resolve the pre-existing staged
        content and rerun from the beginning (step 0).
      - **step 4a publication refusal (new, revision 56; primitive
        corrected, revision 57)**: a journal already exists, so the
        no-replace `os.link` publication fails; nothing written, index
        untouched, the existing journal untouched. An interruption *before*
        the `os.link` leaves no journal and an inert temporary file, and
        the next run is an ordinary fresh attempt.
      - **step 4 freshness refusal**: nothing written, index untouched, no
        journal opened. Correct the declaration and rerun from the beginning
        (step 0).
      - **step 5 pin mismatch**: journal open; the approval-transaction
        rollback restores the index to `HEAD` (state restore is a verified
        no-op) and closes the journal. Rerun from the beginning (step 0).
      - **step 6 sub-step 1a compare-and-swap refusal (new, revision 56)**:
        the shared state file changed after step 4a; the
        approval-transaction rollback restores the index to `HEAD` and
        closes the journal, writing no state bytes, so the other writer's
        content survives intact. Rerun from the beginning (step 0), which
        recaptures the new pre-state.
      - **step 6 sub-step 1c, 3 or 4 assertion failure, or sub-step 6
        `NOT_COMMITTED`**: journal open, index staged, **no approval state
        written anywhere a reader consults** (revised, revision 56: the
        post-approval state exists only as a staged blob, never as
        working-tree content); the
        approval-transaction rollback restores the index to `HEAD`,
        verifies it, and closes the journal, touching no working-tree file.
        No commit exists. Rerun from the beginning (step 0). This
        is the
        branch revisions 53/54 left undefined.
      - **step 6 sub-step 6 `AMBIGUOUS`**: no further mutation, journal
        left in place, manual resolution.
      - **step 7 exact-committed-path-set mismatch**: a durable commit
        exists with the wrong membership; the amend recovery does not
        apply; stop, journal left in place, manual resolution, never a
        second commit. The working tree still carries the **pre**-approval
        state (step 8b never ran), so no command can act on this rejected
        commit as though it were a valid approval.
      - **step 7 committed-state-bytes mismatch (new, revision 56)**: a
        durable commit exists whose `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` content is not
        the authorized post-state; the amend recovery does not apply (an
        amend re-runs the hooks that caused it); stop, journal left in
        place, manual resolution, never a second commit. As above, the
        working tree still carries the pre-approval state.
      - **step 7 declaration mismatch**: corrected by amending the single
        existing commit in place, per step 7's own defined recovery, never
        by creating a follow-up commit; an interruption inside that
        recovery resumes at (d) on the next session rather than stalling.
      - **step 8 manifest mismatch**: a durable commit exists; resolve the
        underlying state and rerun; journal left in place; never a second
        commit; working tree still pre-approval.
      - **step 8b divergent working-tree state (new, revision 56)**: this
        work item's own entry was rewritten by someone else; the approval is
        durable and valid; that change is preserved unwritten-over; journal
        left in place; manual reconciliation, then rerun from step 0, which
        classifies `COMMITTED` and returns to step 8b.
      - **step 8b foreign work-item update (new, revision 57,
        `GPT-R74-002`)**: this work item's entry is still the pre-state but
        the whole file is not, because a different work item's entry was
        legitimately updated during the transaction. Nothing is written —
        this step never merges, so that update cannot be lost — the journal
        is left in place, and the reported reconciliation (apply the
        committed entry for this work item on top of the current file)
        makes the next run's step 8b take its idempotent no-op branch and
        close the journal.
      - **step 7 post-amend check failure (new, revision 57,
        `GPT-R74-003`)**: the amended commit fails one of the three
        re-verified checks — committed path set, committed
        `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` bytes, or declaration bytes. No second amend
        is attempted, no second commit is created, the journal is left in
        place, and steps 8/8b/8a are unreachable, so the working tree still
        carries the pre-approval state.
      No path through this procedure ever creates a second commit after one
      already landed, and no path leaves a usable `CURRENT`/`IMPLEMENTING`
      state without the corresponding durable, verified approval commit —
      as of revision 56 this holds *structurally*, because the only write
      that publishes that state to any reader (step 8b) is itself
      downstream of every verification, not merely because a rollback is
      expected to undo it in time.
  11. **Scope (renumbered from step 10, revision 54)**: this procedure is
      scoped to `workflow-v2-1-core`'s own
      plan-stage approvals only; it does not apply to any other command,
      any other work item, or the implementation stage (whose commit
      contract is unaffected by this fix). `.claude/commands/approve-review.md`'s
      own prose is updated to state the corrected unconditional rule,
      retiring this procedure entirely, at the next checkpoint that touches
      implementation content — tracked by missing-test item 347, whose
      wording is updated (revision 51) to name this renamed procedure and
      extended (revision 55) to require that the permanent command carry
      this procedure's whole approval-transaction contract — index
      isolation, journal, classifier, rollback, both staged-set/committed-
      path-set assertions, pathspec-free commit — and extended again
      (revision 56) to add atomic `O_CREAT | O_EXCL` journal acquisition
      (**superseded by revision 57's `os.link` publication immediately
      below — the permanent command implements the link form, not this
      one**; recorded here only so the obligation's own history stays
      readable), the
      index-pinned state write with its compare-and-swap and deferred
      working-tree materialization, the exact expected-post-state binding
      with its canonical serialization, the committed-state-bytes
      assertion, and the interruption-idempotent amend recovery, and
      extended again (revision 57, `GPT-R74-001`/`-002`/`-003`) to add the
      atomic no-replace `os.link` journal publication, the durable
      `owner_token` with its `assert_owner`-before-every-mutation rule and

      ownership-conditional journal deletion, the never-merge
      materialization together with `D1`'s named `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`

      post-amend verification set, and extended again (revision 58,
      `GPT-R75-001`/`-002`) to add the transaction mutation/handoff guard —
      the fixed-path no-replace guard, the `acquire → assert_owner → mutate
      → advance progress → release` window shape, takeover's acquisition of
      that same guard across its re-verification and rotation, the
      refuse-never-wait rule, superseded-epoch reclamation, and the
      never-breakable `"destructive"` step class — **and, as the pairing
      rule that makes the window's retirement safe, to require
      that the permanent command may drop the quiescence precondition only
      in a change that also lands item 354's every-writer lock conformance;
      it may not drop the precondition while any supported writer still
      ignores the primitive, which would reintroduce `GPT-R75-002` exactly**,
      before
      this bridge is
      retired, so retiring it cannot silently retire the atomicity fix, the
      ownership barrier, or the shared-write protection.
      **Tightened, revision 61 (`GPT-R78-001`/`-002`)**: the pairing rule
      governs the **permanent** command exclusively — this temporary bridge
      never drops the precondition under any condition — and landing item
      354's conformance is necessary but not sufficient. The permanent
      command may drop it only when that landing is covered by a **current
      implementation-stage technical approval** and the gate derives `PASS`
      through the verifier that approval authorizes, since a command that
      accepted a `PASS` from an unreviewed verifier would let one commit
      change both the writers and their checker and then retire the very
      window protecting them (`GPT-R78-001`). On every other classification
      the permanent command falls back to requiring this same explicit
      window.
      **No transaction-safety property may be dropped in the process**: the
      permanent command supersedes this procedure only by carrying every
      one of these properties, and item 347's conformance assertion is what
      makes that mechanically checkable rather than a matter of intent.
      The obligation runs in the other direction too: because revision 56's
      structural enforcement (2) depends on nothing but this procedure's
      own ordering, the permanent command must either keep that ordering or
      land the item-352 commit-bound durability guard in the same change —
      it may not adopt a working-tree-first state write while leaving the
      installed guard bound to `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id`,

- **`/approve-review implementation`** (revised, `WF8B-003`; bare-equality
  branch removed, revision 29, `GPT-R45-003`; **exactly-one-commit gate
  generalized to a bounded, fully-enumerated provenance interval, revision
  30, `GPT-R46-001`/`-002`; terminal-commit classification strengthened to
  match every other interval member, revision 31, `GPT-R47-003`** — see
  D-Commit-Provenance's "Provenance interval" definition, below, and "WF8b
  finding disposition (revision 29 → 30)"/"(revision 30 → 31)" for why the
  exactly-one-commit rule could not represent recovery and why the
  terminal commit needed the same fail-closed check as every other
  member): requires no protected path dirty, and (derived-live) HEAD to
  equal `T`, the current (non-superseded)
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`
  commit for the work item's *current* `implementation_revision`,
  discovered by D-Commit-Provenance's trailer lookup and tie-break — where
  the **entire bounded provenance interval**
  `reviewed_implementation_head..T` (D-Commit-Provenance) validates: every
  commit in the interval enumerated in first-parent order, every
  non-terminal commit classified implementation-stage excluded-only (no
  protected, no unclassified path), and `T` classified identically (no
  protected, no unclassified path) **plus** matching its own
  role-specific provenance-mutation contract exactly (revision 31,
  `GPT-R47-003` — revision 30's weaker "touches no protected path" alone
  would have let a fabricated terminal commit carrying an unclassified
  path through). Ambiguous or missing discovery, or any failed interval
  element, refuses outright, naming the first offending commit. This
  replaces the plain SHA-equality rule stated
  by every revision from 6 through 27, which could never hold once the
  durability commit below is required to exist (worked counter-example in
  "WF8b finding disposition (revision 27 → 28)"). Bare equality (`HEAD ==
  reviewed_implementation_head`, zero intervening commits) is **never**
  accepted, not even as an alternative branch: under this section's
  mandatory provenance-commit-before-generation ordering (below), a
  durability commit lands between `reviewed_implementation_head` and every
  legitimate generated bundle, for every round without exception, so a
  state presenting bare equality can only mean that mandatory step never
  ran, and must refuse exactly like a missing-provenance descendant does
  (revision 29, `GPT-R45-003` — revision 28's own text still accepted this
  as a live alternative, silently bypassing the same requirement its own
  worked example proved necessary). For an **ordinary** round (no
  recovery), the interval is exactly one commit long (`T = S`, the
  durability commit created immediately before generation) — identical
  observable behavior to the pre-revision-30 rule, so items 215-230 are
  unaffected. Only a **recovered** round (WFR-62) presents an interval
  longer than one commit, and this generalized gate is what makes that
  interval acceptable instead of refusing it as an unconstrained-length
  provenance chain (`GPT-R46-001`). This remains a strictly narrower gate
  than unconstrained ancestor reachability (**Required invariant 8**): every
  element of the interval is individually enumerated and classified,
  never merely "reachable." Writes `technical_approval` and creates a
  metadata-only commit (zero production/test changes) carrying
  `Workflow-Technical-Approval: <full review_content_id>` +
  `Workflow-Work-Item: <id>` — **exact field-mutation contract, stated
  exhaustively (new, revision 35, `GPT-R51-001`)**: touches only
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, and within it changes exactly
  `technical_approval`, `phase` (durably,
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` → `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`
  — the **only** commit in this design that ever performs this
  transition; `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` itself is never durably
  written, D-States), `state_revision`, and `last_transition` — no other
  field. This is the same single commit `WF8B-003` already specified, not
  a second commit: the live-HEAD-`== T`-equality precondition above is
  checked and satisfied immediately before this commit is created, and
  nothing after it ever needs to re-satisfy the same equality against a
  later, different commit, because there is no later, different commit on
  this path — resolving the five-step contradiction `GPT-R51-001` raised
  (worked example in "WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35)").
- **`reviewed_implementation_head`'s sole writer** (resolves
  `OPUS-R6-013`; revision 28, `WF8B-003`, corrects the field's own
  durability/staleness self-invalidation; revision 29, `GPT-R45-002`,
  names the revision-advancement comparison source explicitly): the
  bundle generator, at `implementation`/`post-fix` stage only, sets it to
  the protected-content commit the round under review actually ends at —
  never to a later metadata-only bookkeeping commit, and never re-derived
  from live HEAD at some later moment. In the same write,
  `implementation_revision` advances by exactly one, and only when the
  freshly recomputed protected implementation-stage `review_content_id`
  genuinely differs from **the protected implementation-stage
  `review_content_id` recomputed directly from the commit
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s own `reviewed_implementation_head` field
  currently names** — never a separately stored content-id field, and
  never `.ai-review/current/MANIFEST.md` or the
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` trailer (which carries only
  `<work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`, no content hash, and is
  therefore not usable as this comparison's source). `reviewed_implementation_head`
  absent (no round has ever been recorded for this work item) is treated
  as vacuously differing — the first-ever round always advances from no
  revision to revision 1. Because this recomputes directly from the
  commit `reviewed_implementation_head` already durably names, written
  unconditionally by every prior round regardless of whether that round
  ever received `technical_approval`, it needs no provenance-commit
  discovery of its own and is unaffected by a prior `REVISE`-with-no-
  `technical_approval` round, a deleted `.ai-review/current/`, or a
  corrupted previous review directory (revision 29, `GPT-R45-002`; see
  "WF8b finding disposition (revision 28 → 29)" for the full edge-case
  analysis). A classification/artifact-declaration change between rounds
  is not specially handled: like every other protected-path projection in
  this document, the comparison always uses the currently governing
  classification rules, so a classification change can itself cause a
  genuine revision bump for otherwise-unchanged file content — intended,
  not a gap. **Regenerating with an unchanged protected `review_content_id`
  never bumps `implementation_revision`, but is not a single idempotent
  case — it splits into two (revised, revision 35, `GPT-R51-003`; see
  "WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35)" and D-Commit-Provenance's
  new "Same-content post-fix republication" subsection, below, for the
  full mechanism)**: if live HEAD is still exactly the already-recorded,
  content-verified current `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit `T`
  (nothing has been committed since `T`), this is an **exact retry** —
  create nothing, report existing success, exactly as every revision
  through 34 already specified. If live HEAD instead differs from `T` —
  legitimate excluded-only commits (this work item's own review-application
  bookkeeping, or an unrelated concurrent work item's) have landed since
  `T` was made — reusing `T` as-is would leave it historical rather than
  current, with no discoverable provenance tip from which a fresh external
  review can be requested; this is **same-content republication**, and
  `record_bundle_generation` instead performs the operation
  D-Commit-Provenance's "Same-content post-fix republication" subsection
  defines, producing a new, current, recovery-shaped commit without
  bumping `implementation_revision`. Nothing else ever writes either field — in
  particular, the functional-remediation cycle's bounded-change branch
  (D-Functional-Remediation) regenerates a `post-fix` bundle specifically
  so these fields advance, closing the loop `/approve-review
  implementation` depends on.
- **Provenance-commit-before-generation ordering, and `generation_head`**

  (survive a fresh session) before the bundle it describes is generated —
  but that durability commit is made **before** bundle generation runs,
  never after. It carries exactly the ordinary-role canonical trailer pair

  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`" wording, which never actually named

  that file changes **exactly** `phase` (**added, revision 34,
  `GPT-R50-001`** — see the new "Ordinary bundle-publication phase
  transition" subsection immediately below for `phase`'s own exact

  other field (the four non-`phase` fields **named exhaustively, revision

  `plan_approval`, `active_work_item_id`, a `checkpoints` entry,

  implementation-stage-*excluded* path by construction, therefore never a
  protected-path commit.

  **Ordinary bundle-publication phase transition** (new, revision 34,
  `GPT-R50-001` — the ordinary-path analogue of the `phase`-field fix
  revision 32, `GPT-R48-002`, already applied to recovery `S2`; see "WF8b

  the mandatory one-commit `P -> S` interval permits, and is therefore the
  only legal place the ordinary flow can durably enter
  `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` before the generated bundle is
  handed to an external reviewer
  (`docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md`'s own state reference: that
  phase's entry condition is "self-review and verification are
  complete"). No other commit in the interval can carry it: writing
  `phase` anywhere but `S` either violates the exact-field contract above
  (if folded into `S` without being named) or breaks the mandatory
  one-commit topology (a separate pre-`S` phase-only commit trips missing-
  test item 218's untrailed-metadata-commit refusal; a post-generation
  write moves live HEAD past `generation_head`, immediately staling the
  bundle under `assert_local_generation_matches`); and folding it into the
  final protected commit `P` instead is not a documented command contract
  and is not generally achievable, since self-review/testing can finish
  after `P` already exists and history is never rewritten merely to
  insert phase bookkeeping.

  - **Legal source phase** (governs the state-writer only, revision 37,
    `GPT-R53-002`; see the new "Bundle-publication resume" subsection
    below for the separate, non-phase-gated operation that replaces what
    a caller might otherwise expect a phase-gated "retry" to cover):
    `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` (the round's
    first bundle) or `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` (a `post-fix` bundle
    regenerated after a `REVISE` round) — the only two phases
    `docs/ai-workflow/MILESTONE_WORKFLOW.md` names as preceding bundle
    generation. `record_bundle_generation` invoked from any other current
    phase refuses outright, naming the actual phase and the two legal
    ones — unconditionally, with no retry-shaped exception: reaching
    either legal source phase itself durably requires a commit at or after
    the round's own current generation-record tip `T` (entering
    `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` for a fresh round happens only after
    any prior round's tip; entering `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` happens only
    via a real transition away from `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`,
    itself only reachable once `T` already exists), so live HEAD can never
    equal `T` while genuinely, currently in a legal source phase (proof
    worked through in "WF8b finding disposition (revision 36 → 37)").
  - **Target phase**: always `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`,
    regardless of which of the two legal source phases `S` ran from — the
    same uniform-destination-regardless-of-source-phase shape `WFR-62`'s
    post-recovery transition already uses.
  - **Post-commit validation**: immediately after `S` is created,
    `record_bundle_generation` re-reads `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` from the new
    commit and confirms `phase == AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
    before bundle generation proceeds — the operation does not trust its
    own write was applied correctly, the same re-derive-don't-merely-trust
    pattern `WFR-62`'s own post-commit validation already uses.
  - **`record_bundle_generation`'s own decision algorithm — two outcomes,
    not three** (**narrowed, revision 37, `GPT-R53-002`** — replacing
    revision 36's three-way "exact retry / same-content republication /
    genuinely new round" restatement, which `GPT-R52-002` itself corrected
    without noticing that "exact retry," as an outcome of *invoking this
    phase-gated function*, is impossible: the legal-source-phase bullet
    above proves live HEAD can never equal the current tip `T` while the
    function is legally invoked at all, so a branch keyed on that equality
    inside the function's own body can never execute; see "WF8b finding
    disposition (revision 36 → 37)"): defined by the
    "`reviewed_implementation_head`'s sole writer" bullet above and reused
    verbatim by `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Same-content post-fix
    republication" subsection's own "Operation" paragraph. On invocation
    (always from a legal source phase, per the gate above — a live HEAD
    equal to the round's current tip `T`, if one exists, is a **precondition
    the caller checks before ever invoking this function**, not a case
    this function classifies itself; see "Bundle-publication resume"
    below), `record_bundle_generation` recomputes the protected
    implementation-stage content and classifies exactly two ways: genuinely
    different from the value recomputed at `reviewed_implementation_head`
    → the ordinary new-round path, create `S`, advance
    `implementation_revision` by exactly one; identical, and live HEAD
    differs from the current tip `T` (always true here, per the legal-
    source-phase proof above) → same-content republication, create `S2`,
    `implementation_revision` unchanged. There is no third, no-commit
    branch inside this function.

  The bundle is then generated from the live HEAD
  that already includes this commit; `MANIFEST.md`'s `generation_head`
  (`D-Bundle-Manifest`, already diagnostic-only) records that HEAD, which
  now legitimately differs from `reviewed_implementation_head` by exactly
  this one provenance commit — the split `D-Bundle-Manifest` never made
  explicit until now. Bundle generation itself performs **no**
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` write and therefore requires no further commit:
  nothing lands between generation and `/approve-review implementation`,
  so `assert_local_generation_matches` (`D-Bundle-Manifest`) continues to
  hold by construction, and continues to correctly catch a genuinely
  later, unrelated commit (a different worktree, an out-of-band edit) as
  real staleness. This resolves the two questions the pre-revision-28 text
  conflated into one SHA-equality check: "is this still the implementation
  that was externally reviewed" is `reviewed_implementation_head`'s
  question, verified through the one-commit provenance interval above;
  "is this still the repository state the bundle was generated from" is
  `generation_head`'s question, verified by exact equality exactly as
  before — the two are never required to be the same SHA again once a
  durability commit exists.

  **Bundle-publication resume** (new, revision 37, `GPT-R53-002`, resolving
  the crash-recovery gap the now-removed "exact retry" branch left
  unfilled — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 36 → 37)" for the
  full derivation): writing the durability commit `S` (or `S2`) and
  generating the bundle's on-disk files from it are two separate
  operations — the sole `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` write is `S`/`S2` itself
  (`record_bundle_generation`); generating `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current/`'s
  files from live HEAD is a distinct, later step that performs **no**
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` write of its own, already true of every revision
  since 28. The caller-level operation "publish a review bundle for the
  current round" is therefore, itself, never phase-gated and never
  refuses based on current `phase`:

  1. Discover the current `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit `T`
     for the work item's current `implementation_revision`, if one exists
     (D-Commit-Provenance's trailer lookup).
  2. If `T` exists, its content is verified, and live HEAD equals `T`
     exactly (nothing committed since `T` — the case a fresh session
     resumed immediately after `S`/`S2` landed, but before the bundle's
     files were written, presents): **do not invoke
     `record_bundle_generation`.** Publish the bundle's files from live
     HEAD via `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s live "Bundle
     structure" section and `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh`'s live
     publication path — the design of record (`OPUS-R103-002`;
     the "Atomic bundle-file publication" contract below is superseded
     and is not to be implemented) — requires no phase check of its own
     (by the time `T` exists, `phase` is already durably
     `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, a consequence of `T`'s
     own commit, never an independent precondition this step re-checks).
     This is the resume path for the exact crash the removed "exact
     retry" branch could never actually serve, because reaching it
     required being in a legal source phase that, by the proof above, is
     never simultaneously true.
  3. Otherwise (`T` does not exist — a first-ever round in progress — or
     `T` exists but live HEAD differs from it, or the protected content
     genuinely changed): invoke `record_bundle_generation` from the
     current phase (refusing per the legal-source-phase gate if that
     phase is neither of the two legal ones), producing a fresh `S`/`S2`
     per its now-two-outcome algorithm above, then publish the bundle's
     files from the resulting HEAD via the same
     `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` "Bundle structure" /
     `scripts/prepare-ai-review.sh` publication path as step 2 above.

  This is the single caller-level algorithm every bundle-publication path
  (`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION`'s first bundle, an `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`
  post-fix bundle, and a fresh-session resume of either, interrupted at any
  point after `S`/`S2` lands or during publication itself) runs;
  `record_bundle_generation` is never invoked merely to discover whether
  step 2 applies, and step 2 never invokes `record_bundle_generation`. A
  fresh session resumed at step 2 performs no commit, no
  `implementation_revision` change, and no `phase` rewrite — it only
  (re)publishes bundle files, deterministically, from a HEAD that already
  durably reflects the completed round.
