    reproduced against this repository's own Python/Linux environment —
    see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 42 → 43)"). This same
    predicate, unchanged, is also what step 1c below invokes to validate
    an *already-existing* `current` symlink at fresh-session entry
    (`GPT-R61-002`) — one canonical implementation, never two independent
    copies that could drift apart on what "canonical" means:
    0. **Token grammar** (tightened, revision 46, `GPT-R62-003` — see "WF8b
       finding disposition (revision 45 → 46)" for the full derivation: the
       prior "one path component" rule alone permits characters with
       meaning to the exact `tar --transform` invocation "Atomic
       bundle-file publication" step 10 below builds from this same token,
       including a leading `-` (parsed by `tar` as an option), `,` (the
       `--transform` expression's own delimiter), and regular-expression
       metacharacters `tar --transform` interprets, e.g. `[`, `*`, `+`,
       `.`, `^` — independently reproduced against this repository's own
       environment: a token of literally `--version` makes the exact
       archive command below print `tar`'s own version and exit
       successfully without ever creating the archive): a version token
       matches exactly `^[0-9a-f]{32}$` — one lowercase-hex,
       fixed-32-character component, the exact form `uuid.uuid4().hex`
       produces in Python (never the hyphenated `str(uuid.uuid4())` form).
       This grammar is, by construction, still a valid single path
       component — non-empty, never `.` or `..`, containing no `/` — and
       additionally contains no character with any meaning to the shell,
       to `tar --transform`'s sed-style expression syntax, or to any other
       filename-adjacent parser this design interpolates it into.
    1. **Raw payload check**: `os.readlink(temp_link)` — the literal
       string stored in the symlink, never resolved — equals exactly
       `f"bundles/{token}"` for a token satisfying the grammar above,
       rejecting an absolute spelling, a repository/worktree-prefixed
       spelling, a `..`-escaping spelling, a multi-path-component token,
       and any other non-canonical spelling, even one that happens to
       resolve to the correct directory.
    2. **Direct-child reality check** (new, revision 45, `GPT-R61-002`):
       `lstat(.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>)`, using the
       exact token the raw payload check just extracted, identifies a
       real directory — never a symlink or any other filesystem object —
       rejecting `bundles/<token>` itself being an alias (e.g.
       `bundles/A -> bundles/B`) even when that alias happens to resolve
       somewhere otherwise valid.
    3. **Resolution check**: resolving the symlink
       (`os.path.realpath`/equivalent) yields exactly that same
       `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>/` directory the checks
       above already identified — not merely *some* real directory
       located somewhere inside this work item's own `bundles/`
       (tightened, revision 45, `GPT-R61-002`; the creation-time check
       already meant exact-target equality, since the creating step
       always already knows its own fresh token, but said so only in
       prose — this predicate is now the single, shared, textually
       precise statement of it) — rejecting a canonically-spelled-but-
       wrong-target payload, a target resolving outside this work item's
       own `bundles/` directory, and a broken/dangling target.
    Any check failing fails the promotion closed, leaving `current`
    untouched, before the rename onto `current` is ever attempted.
  An absolute payload could also resolve correctly under check 3 alone,
  which is exactly why check 1 exists — check 3 validates **where the
  link points**, never the required canonical **representation of the
  link payload itself** — the relative payload above is the sole
  canonical form. New item 334 (below, amended, `GPT-R59-002`) inspects
  both `os.readlink(current)` (the raw payload) and its resolved target
  directly after both migration and ordinary steady-state publication,
  and additionally exercises a deliberately corrupted **absolute** target
  pointing at the otherwise-correct intended directory, proving it is
  rejected by the raw-payload check even though it would incorrectly pass
  a resolution-only check.

  **Fresh-session `current`-absent recovery classifier** — **SUPERSEDED,
  revision 83** (`OPUS-R103-002`; carried under the same supersession, for
  the same reason, as "Atomic bundle-file publication" below — the design
  of record is `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s live "Bundle
  structure" section; retained as superseded historical text, no longer
  normative, not to be implemented). (labeled,
  revision 42, `GPT-R58-002` — the same classification revision 41
  already fully specified, now given its own named subsection and wired
  as "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1's own mandatory branch below,
  rather than left as narrative text a caller could read past without
  actually invoking): because an *ordinary* (non-migration) promotion only
  ever replaces one symlink name with another — a single, POSIX-atomic
  `os.replace` — a fresh session finding `current` observably absent from
  the filesystem knows unambiguously it is looking at either an
  interrupted migration, an interrupted first-ever publication, or a work
  item that has never published a bundle at all, and classifies which
  deterministically before doing anything else:
  - `bundles/` absent or empty: never migrated, never published — the
    ordinary, already-legal "no bundle exists yet" state; no recovery
    action — continue into "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1c
    below and build a fresh candidate.
  - Exactly one `bundles/<token>/` directory exists, `current` absent:
    either step 1.1 above completed and step 1.2 did not, **or** an
    ordinary first-ever publication's own step 4a (below) already
    promoted a verified candidate into `bundles/<token>/` and step 5
    (the symlink swap) did not yet run — both origins now guaranteed
    identical by construction (`GPT-R57-002`: "Atomic bundle-file
    publication" step 4a below never promotes a `staging/<token>/`
    candidate onto `bundles/<token>/` until it has already passed the
    same completeness/identity check migration step 0.2 requires of the
    legacy directory), so this branch performs **pointer recovery**,
    never by itself **publication completion** (revised, revision 43,
    `GPT-R59-001`, replacing the single-step "return immediately" this
    subsection previously specified for both origins alike, which let a
    stale migrated bundle from a *prior* round be mistaken for the
    *current* publication request's own round merely because it was the
    sole verified version directory on disk — worked failure scenarios in
    "WF8b finding disposition (revision 42 → 43)"):
    1. Create the `current` symlink pointing at this directory, using the
       exact canonical target payload above. The directory's own
       structural completeness is never re-verified in this step, since a
       directory occupying `bundles/<token>/` is, by this revision's own
       construction, always already complete and identity-verified —
       either because it arrived via migration's own
       validated-and-then-atomically-renamed legacy directory (step 1.1,
       preceded by step 0.2's validation), or because it arrived via a
       completed, POSIX-atomic promotion of an already-fully-verified
       staging candidate (step 4a below) — there is no path by which an
       unverified or partial directory can ever occupy `bundles/<token>/`.
    2. **Current-round binding check** (widened again, revision 45,
       `GPT-R61-001` — revision 44's seven-field comparison added
       `generation_head` but left it paired only with round/content
       identity, never with the other half of `generation_head`'s own
       local-staleness pair `D-Bundle-Manifest`'s "Worktree/HEAD
       staleness check" already defines: `generation_head` equality alone
       cannot distinguish a genuinely current bundle from one generated at
       the identical repository HEAD in a *different* (or
       since-relocated) worktree — two worktrees checked out to the same
       commit, with the same protected content, same work item, and same
       round number, can legitimately disagree only on `worktree_root`.
       Omitting it left recovery able to accept a bundle physically
       copied, moved, or replicated in from another worktree as the
       requested local publication, only for `/approve-review`'s own
       pre-existing `assert_local_generation_matches` check to then
       correctly reject that same bundle as stale — reporting publication
       success for a bundle the workflow's own next local gate already
       knows is stale — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 44 → 45)"
       for the full failure scenario; revised, revision 44, `GPT-R60-001`
       — widening revision 43's four-field comparison, which deliberately
       omitted `generation_head` on the reasoning that `generation_head`
       equality alone cannot distinguish two different rounds: that
       premise is correct, but the conclusion drawn from it was not.
       `generation_head` is required as one conjunct of the full binding
       below, never evaluated as a standalone distinguisher, and omitting
       it entirely left exactly the case same-content republication
       exists to produce unguarded — protected content genuinely
       unchanged across an excluded-only-commit gap, so every round/
       content field the revision-43 check compared still matches, while
       the regenerated bundle's own `generation_head` legitimately
       advances — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 43 → 44)" for
       the full failure scenario): read the restored directory's own
       `MANIFEST.md` and compare its full identity binding — `stage`,
       `work_item_type`, `work_item_id`, the stage's own round field
       (`plan_revision` for the plan stage, `implementation_revision` for
       the implementation stage), `base_commit`, protected
       `review_content_id`, `generation_head`, **and `worktree_root`** —
       against the values the publication request **currently in
       progress** already computed for the round it is trying to publish,
       before ever reaching this classifier (the same values
       "Bundle-publication resume," or the equivalent plan-stage caller,
       already has in hand). The **expected** `generation_head` for this
       comparison is never re-derived from the restored directory
       itself — it is supplied by the caller already in progress:
       - implementation-stage publication: the durable current
         `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` tip `T` for this
         `implementation_revision` ("Bundle-publication resume" step 1
         above);
       - plan-stage publication: live repository HEAD at the moment this
         publication attempt began — the value plan-stage candidate
         construction would itself bind a newly-built candidate's own
         `generation_head` to.
       The **expected** `worktree_root` is, identically, never re-derived
       from the restored directory — it is the publication caller's own
       current live Git worktree root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, run
       at the moment this publication attempt began), the same source
       `current_worktree_root_and_head`/`assert_local_generation_matches`
       already read (**corrected, revision 46, `GPT-R62-002`**: this
       sentence previously named `.ai-review/runtime/WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json`
       as that source; the bundled `current_worktree_root_and_head`
       implementation, which both manifest generation and
       `assert_local_generation_matches` already call, derives
       `worktree_root`/`generation_head` from live Git, never from that
       file — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 45 → 46)". `D3`'s
       `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` remains the source for dirty-`IN_PROGRESS`-
       checkpoint resume safety only, a separate lifecycle with no stated
       refresh-on-every-publication contract, and is never authoritative
       for bundle-generation/local-staleness identity).
       **Implementation note** (**corrected, revision 46, `GPT-R62-001`** —
       see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 45 → 46)" for the full
       derivation): the `generation_head` + `worktree_root` pair is not a
       second, independently-written comparison, but it is also **not**
       satisfied by invoking the existing `assert_local_generation_matches`
       predicate in its default, permissive form — that predicate's own
       bundled implementation, and its own bundled test
       `test_missing_manifest_metadata_is_not_a_local_mismatch`, establish
       that a `MANIFEST.md` missing either field passes with no comparison
       performed at all, a deliberate legacy-compatibility contract for
       bundles generated before this metadata existed. Reusing that
       permissive form directly here would let a restored directory that
       never recorded `worktree_root`/`generation_head` satisfy the claimed
       eight-field binding anyway, contradicting "all eight fields above
       must match exactly" below. Recovery therefore invokes
       `assert_local_generation_matches` (`D-Bundle-Manifest`) with its new
       `require_metadata=True` argument — the same function, not a second
       independent implementation, so this binding check and the two
       already-live permissive callers (`/approve-review`, `/review-plan`)
       cannot drift apart on what "the same worktree and HEAD" means
       (**corrected, revision 48, `GPT-R64-001`**, from "the two call
       sites," which predated `/review-plan`'s own revision-47 addition to
       this function's caller inventory — see "WF8b finding disposition
       (revision 47 → 48)") — which
       additionally requires exactly one well-formed `worktree_root:` line
       and exactly one well-formed, 40-hex `generation_head:` line in the
       restored `MANIFEST.md` (zero matches or more than one of either is
       itself a mismatch, never "nothing to compare"), before comparing
       both, as before, against the caller's own current values above. A
       raised `WorktreeOrHeadMismatchError` — for any reason, including
       missing or malformed metadata under `require_metadata=True` — is
       treated as "mismatch," never as a hard failure of the recovery
       attempt; the remaining six round/content fields are compared
       independently, as before. `/approve-review`'s and `/review-plan`'s
       own pre-existing repository-local staleness checks both continue to
       call the same function at their existing default,
       `require_metadata=False`, so an older bundle genuinely predating
       this metadata is unaffected by either check — this correction
       narrows only the current-round recovery binding's own new call,
       never either already-live permissive caller's established
       legacy-compatible behavior (**corrected, revision 48,
       `GPT-R64-001`**, from naming `/approve-review` alone — see "WF8b
       finding disposition (revision 47 → 48)"). This check remains, like
       `assert_local_generation_matches`
       itself, repository-local only (`D-Bundle-Manifest`'s portability
       split, `WFR-17`) — never asked of an external reviewer consuming a
       portable archive.
       All eight fields above must match exactly for the restored
       directory to be treated as the currently-requested publication.
       `generation_head` equality is still never sufficient **alone** —
       two genuinely different rounds can legitimately share a
       `generation_head` (a plan-only edit with no repository commit in
       between, or a metadata-only commit that does not itself change
       protected content), which is exactly why the six round/content
       fields above remain independently required — but that is an
       argument for requiring `generation_head` **conjunctively**, not for
       omitting it: a mismatch on `generation_head` alone, with every
       other field equal, is precisely the same-content-republication
       signature, and must fail this check rather than pass it.
       `worktree_root` is subject to the identical argument: two
       different worktrees can legitimately share every round/content
       field and even `generation_head` (both checked out to the same
       commit), which is exactly the case `worktree_root` alone
       distinguishes — never a standalone distinguisher either, but a
       required conjunct alongside the other seven.
    3. If every compared field matches exactly: the restored directory
       already **is** the bundle this publication request needs.
       Publication completion is not yet proven merely by the symlink now
       resolving correctly — continue directly into steps 9-10 below (no
       further candidate construction, no re-promotion, but archive
       generation/replacement still runs against the now-current target)
       and only then return success.
    4. If any compared field disagrees: the restored directory is a valid
       but **older** bundle — pointer recovery is complete as
       *representation* recovery only. Fall through to step 1c below and
       construct a fresh candidate for the round actually being
       published; the older `bundles/<token>/` directory this branch just
       linked is superseded by the new promotion in the ordinary course of
       step 4a/step 5 below, exactly like any other superseded version
       directory (step 9).
    "Atomic bundle-file publication" steps 2 through 4a are skipped only
    when case 3 above applies; case 4 enters them normally, identical to
    the "`bundles/` absent or empty" branch below except that the
    now-linked older directory is left in place as an ordinary superseded
    version rather than never having existed.
  - More than one `bundles/<token>/` directory exists, `current` absent:
    unreachable in conforming operation, since candidate construction is
    never permitted to begin while `current` is missing — a command
    encountering this anyway (a hand-edited or externally corrupted
    `.ai-review/` tree) fails closed and reports the inconsistency rather
    than guessing which directory is authoritative.
  Once migration completes (`current` resolves to a symlink), "Atomic
  bundle-file publication" runs completely unmodified from step 1c
  onward — migration is strictly a one-time precondition, never a
  recurring step, and the newly-migrated versioned directory becomes an
  ordinary superseded version the instant the very next promotion
  completes. Items 323-324 (amended, revision 41) exercise the migration
  mechanism, its own preconditions, and its interruption/recovery path
  end to end against the new unified model; item 330 (amended, revision
  42, wiring only — see below) exercises the collapsed
  migration-vs-first-publication recovery ambiguity, now driven through
  "Atomic bundle-file publication" step 1's own entry-point branching
  rather than described as a standalone scenario; new item 331 exercises
  legacy-content validation; new item 332 exercises the symlink-capability
  preflight.

  **Atomic bundle-file publication** — **SUPERSEDED, revision 82**
  (`OPUS-R102-001`'s "Answer to question 1", second condition; upheld on
  reconstructed evidence by external plan review, not on "it has worked so
  far"). **The design of record for bundle layout and publication is
  `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s live "Bundle structure" section
  (`:80-96`) — the flat `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current/` directory that
  has actually operated through all 81 plan revisions and the whole of
  `WF8b`'s multi-session dry run.** The entire contract below (steps 1-10,
  the `staging/<token>/` → `bundles/<token>/` → `current`-symlink promotion,
  the legacy migration, the token grammar, the canonical-symlink predicate)
  is **retained as superseded historical text, no longer normative**, and is
  not to be implemented. Revision 81 retired this design's *conformance
  items* (missing-test `314-317`, `319`, `323-327`, `329-338`) while leaving
  this section live and normative — which left the plan requiring a mechanism
  nobody owed and nobody would build, the exact "requirement with no owner"
  class the revision existed to eliminate; supersession is therefore applied
  here, at the layer where the design lives, in the same revision that
  supersedes its items. **The three invariants this design protected are
  genuinely not preserved by the flat layout, and each is named with its
  compensating mechanism rather than waved away**: (i) *torn read* — an
  interruption can leave `current/` holding the previous round's
  `MANIFEST.md` over new content, compensated by the round-identity preflight
  that runs before any write (`GPT-R43-003`, `prepare-ai-review.sh:164-285`,
  where a rejected generation mutates nothing but an idempotent `mkdir -p`)
  and by the three-way reproducibility check (`:416-462`), which requires
  `MANIFEST.md`'s recorded `bundle_id`, a fresh recomputation over the
  directory, and a fresh recomputation over the archive's extracted content
  to agree or exits non-zero — so a torn bundle cannot be *published*
  successfully; (ii) *the previously published bundle is destroyed in place
  rather than left byte-identical*, compensated by recomputation at every
  decision gate — `/approve-review` recomputes `bundle_id` and requires the
  feedback round's recorded `bundle_id` to equal it for `EXTERNAL_APPROVE`,
  so a torn `current/` recomputes to an id matching no feedback round and
  cannot yield an external approval; (iii) *non-atomic archive replacement*
  (`prepare-ai-review.sh:410-411` writes `tar -czf "$ARCHIVE"` straight over
  the previous archive) — the **one genuinely uncovered mode**, which is
  therefore **not** retired but carried forward as missing-test item 318,
  owned by `WF8c` (`OPUS-R102-011`). The residue is accordingly an
  **availability and wasted-review-round** risk, never a correctness one: an
  interrupted publication costs a deterministic regeneration, and the worst
  outcome is a reviewer's time spent on a torn directory read outside the
  archive. Noted for completeness: `compute_bundle_id` fails closed on any
  symlink or non-regular entry under the bundle directory
  (`workflow_fingerprint.py:2148-2156`) — a check this superseded design
  would itself have required relaxing for `current`. **Not superseded by
  this**: `D2a`'s durable `BLOCK`-verdict pin, whose conformance items
  (`320-322`, `328`) were mistakenly swept into this range by revision 81 and
  are restored to `WF8c` by revision 82 (`OPUS-R102-001`) — `D2a` remains
  fully live and normative.

         validation error and never auto-repairing or overwriting the
         existing link — leaving `current` exactly as found, the same
         discipline step 1d below already applies to a non-symlink object
         at this name. Only once every check passes does candidate
         construction proceed exactly as before: construct the
         complete candidate bundle inside a new, disposable staging
         directory — `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/staging/<token>/`
         (`GPT-R57-002`), `<token>` a fresh, collision-free identifier
         satisfying the token grammar above — `uuid.uuid4().hex` (32
         lowercase-hex characters; restated, revision 46, `GPT-R62-003`,
         from the prior "e.g. a UUID4 or `<pid>.<monotonic-timestamp>`"
         examples, neither of which is itself hex-32) — never reused and
         never itself treated as canonical by any reader — never inside
         `current`, `bundles/`, or any existing versioned directory.
     1d. **Any other `lstat` result** (new, revision 43, `GPT-R59-004`):
         a regular file, a FIFO/socket/device node, or any other
         unexpected filesystem object occupying the name `current` —
         refuses outright, before any candidate construction or mutation,
         naming a stable validation error and never auto-repairing or
         overwriting the unexplained object. This is the same
         "never trust an unexplained filesystem shape" discipline the
         migration recovery classifier's own "more than one
         `bundles/<token>/`" branch and `GPT-R57-001`'s parent-directory-
         type check already apply elsewhere in this design, now made
         explicit for `current` itself.
  2. Populate and validate every author-written and generated required
     artifact (`REVIEW_REQUEST.md`, `PLAN.md`/`IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md`,
     `TEST_RESULTS.md`, `CHANGED_FILES.txt`, `COMMITS.txt`, `DIFF.patch`,
     `CONTEXT_FILES.txt`, `files/`) inside the staging directory only.
  3. Write the staging directory's `MANIFEST.md` inside it.
  4. Independently reproduce `review_content_id`/`bundle_id` against the
     staging directory's own content before promotion is attempted — the
     same idempotency assertion `WFR-46` already requires of manifest
     generation, now checked pre-promotion rather than only post-hoc.
  4a. **Promote candidate to version store** (new, revision 41,
      `GPT-R57-002`): only once every check in steps 2-4 passes,
      `os.rename`/`os.replace` the now fully-populated, fully-verified
      `staging/<token>/` directory onto `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/<token>/`
      (the identical `<token>`) — an ordinary rename onto a
      previously-absent target name, the same primitive kind the
      migration contract's own step 1.1 already uses, and covered by the
      same POSIX atomicity argument: this rename can never leave a
      partially-built `bundles/<token>/` directory on disk. After this
      step, and only after it, the versioned directory referenced by
      steps 5-10 below exists under `bundles/`; before it, the (possibly
      still-incomplete) candidate exists only under the non-canonical
      `staging/` namespace, never mistaken for a version-store entry by
      any reader or recovery path.
  5. Promote: create a new symlink at a temporary path directly inside
     `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/` using the canonical target payload
     defined above (`bundles/<token>`, the versioned directory now under
     `bundles/` per step 4a — `GPT-R58-001`, never the fuller repo-relative
     spelling), then atomically replace the `current` name with it via a
     single `rename`/`os.replace` of the symlink itself (never of its
     target). Renaming one symlink name onto
     another existing name is a single directory-entry update on every
     POSIX filesystem this tooling runs on — this workflow's supported
     platforms, per `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `ubuntu-latest` and every
     documented local development environment, are POSIX/Linux only; no
     Windows support is claimed or required — unlike replacing a populated
     directory. This rename is the only moment which versioned directory
     `current` resolves to ever changes.
  6. On any failure or interruption before the symlink rename in step 5
     completes, `current` still resolves to whichever versioned directory
     it pointed at before promotion began — byte-identical to its
     pre-publication state — and the newly built, not-yet-promoted
     versioned directory is simply an unreferenced sibling, never mistaken
     for canonical content by any reader (a reader always resolves
     `current` through the symlink, never lists `bundles/` directly to
     guess which entry is current).
  7. A retry after an interrupted promotion is deterministic: it
     reconstructs the same candidate content in a fresh staging directory
     (a new `<token>` — the interrupted attempt's own `staging/` or
     `bundles/` directory, if any, is never reused or resumed in place)
     from the same live HEAD, and either completes a new promotion or,
     finding `current` already resolves to a versioned directory whose
     content matches the candidate exactly, promotes nothing further and
     leaves the redundant unpromoted directory/directories it just built
     unreferenced on disk — never deleted as a side effect of this retry
     (restated, revision 42, `GPT-R58-003`, from "discards," which read as
     deletion and contradicted step 9's own no-cleanup rule below; the
     same separate, explicit, later maintenance action step 9 describes is
     the only thing that ever removes it).
  8. Symlink creation or replacement failing closed for any reason
     (`OSError`, `NotImplementedError`, or any other failure from
     `os.symlink`/`os.replace` — including a filesystem or sandbox that
     does not support symlinks) aborts the promotion without touching
     `current`; this operation never falls back to a non-atomic in-place
     write or a two-step remove-then-recreate of `current` under any
     failure.
  9. **Automatic cleanup of superseded version directories is removed
     from ordinary publication entirely** (narrowed, revision 40,
     `GPT-R56-003` — replacing revision 39's "eligible for cleanup,
     opportunistically, by a later promotion" wording, which stated no
     retention guarantee for a version directory a slower multi-file
     reader might still be using; extended, revision 41, to `staging/`
     for consistency, though an abandoned `staging/<token>/` directory is
     never canonical and needs no retention guarantee at all): no
     promotion ever deletes a `bundles/<token>/` directory, nor any
     `staging/<token>/` directory, as a side effect of publishing a new
     one. Cleanup, if ever performed, is a separate, explicit, later
     maintenance action, run only when no workflow command is active —
     trading unbounded local disk growth under `bundles/`/`staging/` for
     the simplest correct concurrency story, with no reader-registration
     or reference-counting protocol needed. `.ai-review/` is fully
     gitignored and local-only (`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`), so this is a
     disk-hygiene tradeoff, never a correctness or repository-size one; a
     superseded directory left in place is never mistaken for canonical
     content regardless (only the `current` symlink's own target is
     canonical). New item 327 confirms ordinary publication never
     deletes a superseded version directory. Every "discard(ed/ing)" verb
     elsewhere in this document describing a redundant `staging/`/`bundles/`
     directory (step 7 above; missing-test items 314, 330) means exactly
     this rule — left unreferenced on disk, never actually deleted — a
     wording ambiguity closed explicitly, revision 42, `GPT-R58-003`, not a
     change to this rule itself.
  10. **Archive representation, exact** (restated, revision 41,
      `GPT-R57-005` — superseding revision 40's `-h`/`--dereference`
      mechanism, which resolved the archive's own top-level `current`
      name correctly for ordinary sequential use but handed `tar` the
      mutable `current` name directly rather than a target already pinned
      by the caller, so it did not itself obey the "Reader snapshot
      semantics" pin-once contract this same section requires of every
      other multi-file reader — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision
      40 → 41)"): archive generation first resolves `current` to its
      concrete `bundles/<token>/` target exactly once, per "Reader
      snapshot semantics" below, then generates the archive
      (`review-bundle.tar.gz`) directly from that already-resolved,
      concrete directory, remapping its top-level path component to the
      fixed archive name `current` via `tar`'s member-name transform:

      ```
      tar -czf review-bundle.tar.gz -C .ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles \
          --transform 's,^<token>,current,' -- <token>
      ```

      where `<token>` is the concrete directory name resolved from
      `current` at the start of this operation (the pinning step), never
      re-resolved during the `tar` invocation itself. Because the path
      handed to `tar` is already the resolved real directory rather than
      the mutable `current` symlink, no dereference flag is structurally
      necessary any longer — there is no symlink left anywhere in the
      path being archived. The positional `<token>` operand is preceded by
      `--` (added, revision 46, `GPT-R62-003`), so `tar` treats it strictly
      as a filename even were it to begin with `-` — defense in depth
      beyond the tightened token grammar above, which already forbids a
      leading `-` (or any other tar/regex-special character) for any token
      this design itself ever generates: by construction, a value reaching
      this command was already accepted by the canonical symlink validator,
      so the grammar alone already closes the vulnerability this
      independently reproduces (`GPT-R62-003`: a hand-constructed
      `bundles/--version` directory with a `current` symlink bypassing
      validation, archived with the pre-fix command above, prints `tar`'s
      own version and creates no archive) — but this command's own
      robustness should not depend solely on every caller already having
      validated its input first. The resulting archive contains only ordinary
      regular files/directories under a top-level `current/` name (via
      the `--transform` rename) — no symlink whose target exists only in
      the source worktree survives into the archive — so it extracts
      anywhere, on any machine, into an immediately self-contained,
      ordinary `current/` bundle directory: the identical guarantee
      revision 40's `-h`/`--dereference` mechanism provided, produced by a
      different, pin-respecting mechanism. This retains its own
      temp-file-plus-rename discipline for the archive file itself,
      unaffected by this change — a failed or interrupted archive write
      never replaces the previously valid archive. Item 325 (unchanged in
      intent) continues to extract a generated archive into an unrelated
      empty temporary directory and independently reproduce `bundle_id`
      from the extracted content, proving the round trip end to end under
      the restated mechanism; new item 333 additionally proves the
      pinning property itself: an archive generation pinned against one
      target, followed by a concurrent promotion to a different target
      before the `tar` invocation completes, still reproduces the
      originally-pinned bundle's `bundle_id`, never the post-promotion
      one.

  **Reader snapshot semantics** — **SUPERSEDED, revision 83**
  (`OPUS-R103-002`; carried under the same supersession, for the same
  reason, as "Atomic bundle-file publication" above — the design of
  record is `docs/ai-workflow/REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s live "Bundle
  structure" section, a flat directory with no `bundles/<token>/` target
  to resolve-once against; retained as superseded historical text, no
  longer normative, not to be implemented. Items 326/333 stay `SUPERSEDED`
  with owner `none`, unchanged from the "314-317, 319, 323-327, 329-338" row).
  (new, revision 40, `GPT-R56-003`; revision
  41, `GPT-R57-005`: the archive generator, step 10 above, is now also an
  explicit instance of this same rule, not an exception to it):
  atomic symlink replacement guarantees each single path lookup resolves
  to either the complete old bundle or the complete new one, but does not
  by itself give a *multi-file* reader — one that reads several paths
  under `current/` across one logical operation, the existing
  `compute_bundle_id`'s own shape, and now also the archive generator
  above — the same guarantee if it re-resolves `current` on every
  individual path access, since a promotion between two of those lookups
  could make one operation observe a mix of old and new files. Every
  reader of bundle content — `compute_bundle_id`/`MANIFEST.md`
  regeneration, `assert_local_generation_matches`, archive generation
  (`GPT-R57-005`), and any future multi-path consumer of `current/` —
  therefore resolves `current` to its concrete `bundles/<token>/` target
  **exactly once**, at the start of its operation, and performs every
  subsequent file read for that operation against the resolved, pinned
  path directly, never through the `current` name a second time and never
  re-resolving mid-operation. Combined with step 9's removal of automatic
  cleanup, a reader's pinned target is guaranteed to remain on disk, with
  its content unchanged, for the reader's entire operation regardless of
  any promotion that happens concurrently. Item 326 exercises this
  directly for `compute_bundle_id`: pin the old target, promote, finish
  reading the old target consistently, confirm a fresh reader started
  after promotion observes only the new target; new item 333 exercises
  the identical property for archive generation.

  This operation is the sole writer of `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/current`,
  `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/bundles/`, and `.ai-review/<work_item_id>/staging/`
  on this path; nothing else in this design mutates any of the three in
  place. `.ai-review/` remains fully gitignored (`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`), so
  `current` becoming a symlink and the new `bundles/`/`staging/`
  directories are not a tracked-content change.
- **Checkpoint completion** (resolves `OPUS-R6-014`): the checkpoint's own
  commit carries `Workflow-Checkpoint: <id>` + `Workflow-Work-Item: <id>`
  and updates `checkpoints[id].status = COMPLETE` in `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
  — the **sole** writable record of checkpoint status. The registry file
  (D-Registry) carries no status column; `ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md`'s
  per-checkpoint narrative is explicitly derived/non-authoritative for
  status and is updated at milestone boundaries, not required per
  checkpoint, so an interrupted session (state written, narrative not)
  resumes without a manual reconciliation stop. The commit trailer remains
  verification evidence — cross-checked against the state record, never
  trusted as a second source of truth.

### D-Commit-Provenance (revised again, revision 38: the "Same-content post-fix republication" subsection's "Authority and source phase" paragraph widened from "legal only... from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`" to legal from **either** of `record_bundle_generation`'s two legal source phases, closing the gap where an unchanged-content bundle regenerated from `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` (a no-op implementation pass, a plan-only correction requiring no protected implementation change, or a reverted-before-publication fix) had no legal outcome under either the general two-outcome algorithm (`D-Approval-Commits`, which never restricted this branch by source phase) or this subsection's own narrower restatement of it — the two normative sections directly contradicted each other for that exact repository state; condition 4's recovered-role "carries only" contract widened from two to three legal writer/source combinations to match; resolves `GPT-R54-002` — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 37 → 38)"; revision 37: the "Same-content post-fix republication" subsection's "Operation" contract narrowed to its two genuinely reachable outcomes (genuinely different content / same-content republication), removing the impossible "exact retry" outcome and deferring the crash-recovery case it stood in for to `D-Approval-Commits`' new "Bundle-publication resume" contract — resolves `GPT-R53-002`; see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35)"; revision 34: "Provenance interval" condition 3 redefined by role rather than terminal/non-terminal position, and condition 4's ordinary clause gains `phase` — resolves `GPT-R50-001`/`-002`; **`Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`**
(new, revision 28, `WF8B-003`): written by `record_bundle_generation`'s
own durability commit (D-Approval-Commits), before bundle generation runs.
Discovery reuses the exact same scoped, ancestry-limited, exactly-one-match
lookup every other trailer here already uses (`base_commit..HEAD`,
`Workflow-Work-Item`-scoped), with additional constraints specific to
this trailer, enforced by the discovering call site (`/approve-review
implementation`'s revised gate, D-Approval-Commits), not by the generic
lookup helper itself.

**Canonical provenance trailer set** (new, revision 33, `GPT-R49-001` —
resolves the contradiction between this trailer's own
`Workflow-Work-Item`-scoped discovery, just stated, and the terminal
role-specific "carries only" wording revisions 28-32 attached to each
role below, which never actually named `Workflow-Work-Item` and would
therefore make a correctly-scoped, correctly-discoverable commit fail its
own terminal-commit classification): every
`Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit — ordinary or recovered —
always carries the ordinary `Workflow-Work-Item: <work_item_id>` trailer
the scoped lookup above requires, in addition to its role-specific
trailer(s), and no other workflow provenance trailer. The exact set per
role, restated everywhere below and in `WFR-61`/`WFR-62`:

- **Ordinary generation-record commit `S`**:
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`
  + `Workflow-Work-Item: <work_item_id>` — exactly two trailers, no other.
- **Recovered generation-record commit `S2`**:
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`
  (the unchanged value `S` carried) + `Workflow-Supersedes: <S-sha>` +
  `Workflow-Work-Item: <work_item_id>` — exactly three trailers, no other.

Condition 4's role-specific "carries only" contracts, below, and the
recovery "Topology" paragraph are both stated against this same set —
neither ever again describes a two-trailer `S` or a two-trailer `S2`
missing `Workflow-Work-Item`.

**Provenance interval** (redefined, revision 30, `GPT-R46-001`,
generalizing revision 28's "first-parent child of `reviewed_implementation_head`"
single-commit rule, which could represent an ordinary round but not
`WFR-62` recovery — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 29 → 30)"):
given `P = reviewed_implementation_head` and a discovered current
(non-superseded, per the tie-break below) `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
commit `T` for the work item's current `implementation_revision`, the
interval `P..T` is valid only when **all** of the following hold:

1. `T` is reachable from live HEAD, and live HEAD **equals** `T` exactly
   (not merely a descendant of it) — the approval gate's own comparison,
   restated here as the interval's own closing condition;
2. every commit in `P..T` is enumerable in **first-parent** order —
   `C_1, C_2, ..., C_n = T` (`n >= 1`); a merge commit, or any commit
   reachable only through a non-first-parent edge, makes the interval
   unenumerable and the discovery refuses outright, exactly like a missing
   commit (no "widen the search" fallback);
3. every commit in `C_1 .. C_{n-1}` (there are none for an ordinary,
   non-recovered round, where `n = 1` and `T = C_1`) is classified **by
   role, not merely by terminal/non-terminal position** (corrected,
   revision 34, `GPT-R50-002` — revision 30's text classified every
   non-terminal commit only as generic excluded-only regardless of
   whether it was itself a generation-record commit, so a historical,
   already-superseded `S` (after one recovery) or `S`/`S2` (after two)
   was checked only for "no protected/unclassified path," never against
   its own role-specific contract, letting a malformed historical record
   hide behind a valid successor once superseded; see "WF8b finding
   disposition (revision 33 → 34)" for the two worked failure scenarios):
   - a commit carrying a `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` trailer for
     this exact `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` pair —
     necessarily historical/superseded when non-terminal, since the
     pair's current record is always `T` (the supersession-chain
     discovery, below) — must satisfy condition 4's role-specific
     provenance-mutation contract (the ordinary or recovered clause,
     matching whichever trailer set it actually carries), evaluated
     **exactly as strictly** as condition 4 evaluates `T` itself: a
     malformed historical record fails the whole interval, never
     rendered harmless merely because a later record has since
     superseded it;
   - every other commit — carrying no `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
     trailer for this pair at all (an ordinary, unrelated excluded-only
     commit `U_i`) — is classified implementation-stage
     **excluded-only** as before: its diff against its first parent
     touches no protected implementation path and no unclassified path

     `any_protected_path_dirty` already performs against a working-tree

     unclassified path anywhere in the interval refuses exactly like a

4. the **terminal** commit `T` — always itself a

5. if `T` carries a `Workflow-Supersedes: <sha>` trailer, that trailer

For an ordinary round, `n = 1` and this reduces to exactly revision 28's
rule (`T` is the sole, immediate first-parent child of `P`), strengthened
by condition 4's unclassified-path check and role-specific mutation match
— no behavior change for a well-formed round, items 215-230 unaffected; a
malformed or fabricated terminal commit that revision 30's weaker rule
would have accepted now refuses. A longer interval is reachable only
through one of exactly two authorized producers (**named explicitly,
revision 38, `GPT-R54-002`** — replacing the ambiguous "sole mechanism"
phrasing below, which predated `record_bundle_generation`'s own
same-content-republication writer and, once that writer existed, could be
misread as naming only one of the two): `WFR-62`'s
`/recover-implementation-provenance` recovery operation, below, or
`record_bundle_generation`'s own same-content-republication outcome
(legal from either `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` or
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`, D-Commit-Provenance's "Same-content post-fix
republication" subsection) — these two, and only these two, mechanisms can
legitimately place excluded-only commits between `P` and `T`.

A duplicate/ambiguous match for the same `(work_item_id,
implementation_revision)` pair follows the existing tie-break/recovery
rule below unchanged (first-parent-of-HEAD plus content-verification
tie-break; a `Workflow-Supersedes:` trailer or explicit
`WORKFLOW_STATE.json` annotation for genuine, user-approved ambiguity). A
missing discovery (no such commit reachable at all) is not a "gate
unreachable" outcome distinct from an ordinary missing-approval state —
it refuses with the same class of error `WF8B-003`'s worked example
depends on catching: a round whose durability commit was never made, or
was made but never gained this trailer, cannot reach
`AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` at all, by design (**Required invariant
8** in "WF8b finding disposition (revision 27 → 28)" — unconstrained
ancestor reachability is explicitly rejected in favor of this fully
enumerated constraint set).

Exact, scoped trailer lookup (unchanged from revision 6, and reused
verbatim by the new trailer type above): full identifiers
only, `Workflow-Work-Item`-scoped, ancestry-limited to `base_commit..HEAD`,
requiring exactly one match — **with one addition**. A legitimate rebase,
cherry-pick, or merge can copy a trailer onto a new commit while the
original remains reachable, producing two matches for what is really one
logical event (confirmed against this repository's actual state:
`milestone8-cp11-work` (`dc4381a`) has diverged from `162154d`, so its
required user-performed integration will be exactly such an operation):

- **Tie-break** (not a silent pick): among multiple matches for the same
  (trailer key, value, work-item) triple, prefer the one that is (a) a
  first-parent ancestor of HEAD, **and** (b) whose recorded state/content
  change verification (unchanged from revision 6 — the matched commit is
  checked against what it claims, not trusted on the trailer's word alone)
  passes. If more than one commit still qualifies after both filters, stop
  — this is genuine ambiguity, not a duplicate to resolve automatically.
- **Recovery for genuine ambiguity**: a user-approved `Workflow-Supersedes:
  <sha>` trailer on a new commit, or an explicit annotation in
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` naming which match is authoritative — either way a
  named, git-tracked, user-approved action (consistent with this
  repository's git restrictions), never a Claude-autonomous pick.
- **Stale-`generation_head` recovery after a later legitimate
  excluded-only commit** (new, revision 29, `GPT-R45-004`; topology,
  precondition, and operation contract corrected, revision 30,
  `GPT-R46-001`/`-002`/`-003` — see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 29
  → 30)" for why revision 29's `P → S2` framing was wrong): revision 28's
  exactly-one-commit provenance interval (`P → S`, `D-Approval-Commits`)
  is deliberately narrow, but the workflow explicitly permits concurrent
  work items with many implementation-stage *excluded* paths
  (`D-Fingerprint-Generalization`), so a legitimate commit `U` from
  unrelated work can land after `S` and move HEAD without changing this
  work item's protected implementation-stage `review_content_id` at all.
  Once that happens, `P → S → U` is two first-parent commits, not one, and
  the round's existing bundle/approval path is correctly stale
  (`generation_head == S != U`) with no automatic recovery.

  **Precondition** (checked first, before any commit is made; revision 30
  requires **both** of the following — revision 29 required only the
  first, which `GPT-R46-002` showed is not proof by itself):

  1. the protected implementation-stage `review_content_id` recomputed at
     the candidate HEAD is byte-identical to the one recomputed at
     `reviewed_implementation_head` (the same recomputation `GPT-R45-002`'s
     fix defines). This is a cheap, fast-refusal check: if it fails, this
     is not recovery at all — it is a genuinely new round, handled
     entirely by the ordinary path, and the operation refuses outright
     without performing check 2. If it passes, that proves only that the
     **endpoints'** protected projections agree — **not**, by itself, that
     no protected or unclassified commit occurred in between (a protected
     edit followed by a byte-identical revert, or a transient unclassified
     path added and removed, can both leave endpoint content identical
     while the interval contains a commit the operation must refuse —
     `GPT-R46-002`'s two failure scenarios);
  2. an **exhaustive, first-parent, commit-by-commit classification of the
     entire candidate interval** `reviewed_implementation_head..HEAD`:
     every commit is enumerated in first-parent order and classified under
     the **same role-based rule condition 3 of the "Provenance interval"
     definition above applies** (**corrected, revision 34, `GPT-R50-002`**
     — a prior recovery's own `S`/`S2` commit, already present in this
     candidate interval on a second or later recovery, must satisfy its
     own generation-record role contract, not merely the generic
     excluded-only rule revision 30's text applied here uniformly; an
     unrelated commit carrying no `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
     trailer for this pair is still classified excluded-only) — the same
     per-commit check the eventual approval gate performs, performed here
     as a precondition instead of at approval time, reused verbatim
     rather than a separately maintained duplicate rule. This check
     inspects **every intervening commit's own diff**; it never infers
     historical cleanliness from endpoint equality alone. A protected,
     unclassified, or (for a historical generation-record commit)
     role-invalid commit found anywhere in the interval refuses the
     recovery outright, naming the offending commit — even though check 1
     passed.

  Only when **both** checks pass does the operation create a commit.

  **Topology** (`GPT-R46-001`): once both precondition checks pass, the
  operation creates **exactly one** new commit `S2`, touching only
  `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s `phase`/`state_revision`/`last_transition`
  (**corrected, revision 32, `GPT-R48-002`**, naming the same fields
  condition 4 above and `WFR-62`'s row already require, rather than the
  bare-file wording that left this paragraph and condition 4 unaligned),
  as the **first-parent child of live HEAD** (not
  of `P` — Git ancestry is never rewritten), carrying **both** the
  unchanged `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record: <work_item_id>/<implementation_revision>`
  trailer value as `S` (this is not a new round — `implementation_revision`
  does not change), **and** a `Workflow-Supersedes: <S-sha>` trailer naming
  `S` explicitly (`S` is the previous, now-superseded
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit for this round — the sole
  commit in the interval besides `S2` itself that ever carried this
  trailer), **and** the ordinary `Workflow-Work-Item: <work_item_id>`
  trailer (**corrected, revision 33, `GPT-R49-001`** — the recovered-role
  canonical trailer set `D-Commit-Provenance`'s "Canonical provenance
  trailer set" defines above; never a two-trailer commit). The resulting
  real Git graph is `P → S → U → S2` (or, with
  multiple excluded-only commits, `P → S → U_1 → ... → U_k → S2`) — this
  is stated explicitly as the topology, never described as a
  `P → S2` one-commit interval, which does not exist in this graph and
  cannot be produced without rewriting history (revision 29's error,
  `GPT-R46-001`). `/approve-review implementation` accepts this graph not
  because it is one commit, but because D-Commit-Provenance's generalized
  **provenance interval** definition (above) accepts a bounded,
  fully-classified multi-commit interval whose terminal commit is the
  current trailer holder: `S` and every `U_i` are the interval's
  non-terminal members — `S` itself a historical generation-record
  commit, satisfying its own ordinary-role contract under condition 3's
  role-based classification (**corrected, revision 34, `GPT-R50-002`** —
  revision 30's text classified `S` here only as generic excluded-only,
  the same gap condition 3 itself had), and every `U_i` classified
  excluded-only as before (this reuses exactly the precondition-2
  classification just performed — the operation does not classify the
  interval twice with different logic; precondition 2 and the approval
  gate's own interval validation are the same check, one proving it
  before the commit, the other reproving it independently at approval
  time), and `S2` is the terminal, trailer-carrying, non-protected
  commit. This reuses the tie-break/recovery mechanism directly above
  rather than inventing a second one: on finding two matches for the same
  `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` trailer key/value, a
  content-verified `Workflow-Supersedes` match (the superseding commit
  itself touches no protected path — the same check every other trailer
  discovery here already performs) resolves the resulting duplicate
  deterministically — `S` is treated as superseded, `S2` as current —
  instead of stopping as genuine ambiguity. Without a `Workflow-Supersedes`
  trailer, two matching provenance commits remain genuine, refused
  ambiguity, exactly as the existing "Recovery for genuine ambiguity" rule
  already requires (missing-test item 221 is unchanged and continues to
  cover exactly that case).

  **Multiple sequential recoveries / supersession chain** (new, revision
  33, `GPT-R49-003` — defines what revisions 29-32 left unstated: what
  happens when a recovered round's own regenerated bundle goes stale
  again, from another legitimate excluded-only commit, before
  `technical_approval` is recorded against it): the recovery operation
  above is not limited to running once per implementation round. A second
  (or later) legitimate staleness event is recovered by the same command,
  the same precondition, and the same topology, applied again with `S2`
  playing the role `S` played the first time — the operation has no
  memory of "this is the second recovery" and needs none, since every
  precondition and topology rule above is stated in terms of "the current
  `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` commit" and "live HEAD", not in
  terms of a fixed, one-time relationship to `P`. The resulting
  supersession graph is governed by these explicit rules:

  - supersession is scoped to exactly one `(work_item_id,
    implementation_revision)` pair — a chain never spans a revision
    boundary, since a genuinely changed `review_content_id` is routed to
    the ordinary new-round path by precondition check 1, never to
    recovery, regardless of how many prior recoveries this revision has
    already undergone;
  - every `Workflow-Supersedes` edge names the immediately preceding
    **current** generation-record commit at the moment that recovery ran
    — never an arbitrary earlier commit in the chain, and never a commit
    that was itself already superseded at that moment;
  - supersession is therefore always a simple linked list, never a tree
    and never a cycle: **no fork** — at most one commit may ever carry
    `Workflow-Supersedes: <X>` for any given `X`. A second, different
    commit later found naming the same `X` is genuine, unresolved
    ambiguity, refused by the existing tie-break's "Recovery for genuine
    ambiguity" rule exactly like any other duplicate-trailer ambiguity,
    never auto-resolved by recency, commit order, or any other heuristic.
    **No cycle**: a chain in which some commit's `Workflow-Supersedes`
    edge, followed transitively, leads back to itself is malformed
    provenance, refused identically;
  - the **current** record for a `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)`
    pair is the unique commit — among every commit carrying that pair's
    `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` value — that is not itself named
    by any other such commit's `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer: the chain's
    tip. Discovery computes this by walking every `Workflow-Supersedes`
    edge among the matched set and confirming **exactly one** commit is
    never a target — zero such commits is the cycle case above, more than
    one is the fork case above, both refused identically to any other
    ambiguous/malformed provenance discovery this document defines;
  - a `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer targeting a commit outside the
    matched `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record` set for this exact pair,
    or targeting a commit that was not itself the immediately preceding
    current record at the time this recovery ran (e.g. a hand-authored
    trailer naming `S` directly when `S2` is already current and a third
    recovery is being attempted), refuses as malformed provenance — an
    edge may never "skip" a link in the chain;
  - every non-tip record in the chain remains historical (a real,
    never-deleted, never-rewritten Git commit) but is permanently
    non-current once a valid successor supersedes it — the tie-break
    never reconsiders a non-tip record once its successor's own
    provenance is content-verified;
  - concretely, a second recovery produces
    `P → S → U_1 → S2 → U_2 → S3`, with `S2 Workflow-Supersedes: S` and
    `S3 Workflow-Supersedes: S2`; `S3` is current, `S` and `S2` are both
    historical/non-current, and the provenance interval
    `/approve-review implementation` validates is
    `reviewed_implementation_head..S3` in its **entirety** — every one of
    `S`, `U_1`, `S2`, `U_2` individually classified under condition 3's
    role-based rule (**corrected, revision 34, `GPT-R50-002`** — `S` and
    `S2` each satisfying their own generation-record role contract;
    `U_1` and `U_2` classified excluded-only), `S3` classified as the
    terminal member under condition 4 — never a shorter interval computed
    by "jumping" directly from `P` to `S3` through the chain;
  - `implementation_revision` and `reviewed_implementation_head` are
    unchanged by any number of sequential recoveries, and each recovered
    bundle (`B2`, `B3`, ...) independently requires its own fresh external
    implementation review before `technical_approval` can be recorded
    against it, exactly as the first recovery already requires
    ("Post-recovery phase transition", above, applies identically to
    every recovery in the chain, not only the first) — the recovery count
    is otherwise unbounded and unremarkable past the first, not a
    distinct design case requiring its own command or state field.

  **Operation contract** (`GPT-R46-003` — revision 29 named no command,
  authorization boundary, or state mutation for this operation; revision
  30 defined them but left the phase scope and post-recovery transition
  wrong; revision 31, `GPT-R47-001`/`-002`, corrects both):

  - **Command**: a new, dedicated command, `/recover-implementation-provenance
    <work_item_id>` — never folded into `/prepare-review` (which only ever
    regenerates a bundle, never authors a Git commit on its own initiative)
    or `/approve-review implementation` (which only ever reads state and
    writes an approval commit, never a recovery commit), and never run
    automatically as a side effect of either. Keeping it a separate,
    explicitly-invoked command keeps its Git-authoring authority auditable
    and matches this repository's git restrictions (`CLAUDE.md`: commits
    require explicit authorization). **This is one of two legal writers of
    a recovery-shaped commit (new, revision 35, `GPT-R51-003`)**: the other
    is `record_bundle_generation` itself, invoked automatically (no
    separate command or additional confirmation) at `post-fix` stage from
    `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` — see "Same-content post-fix republication"
    below. The two are legal from disjoint phases and therefore never
    ambiguous about which one produced a given chain link; this command's
    own scope is otherwise unchanged.
  - **Allowed source phase** (narrowed, revision 35, `GPT-R51-001` — see
    "WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35)": `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`
    is never a durably stored `phase` value under any revision-35-conforming
    design, so it cannot be a legal source phase either; corrected,
    revision 31, `GPT-R47-002` — revision 30 permitted only
    `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`, leaving no legal recovery action for a
    bundle staled by a concurrent excluded-only commit while still in
    `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`): **only**
    `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` — the sole phase in which a
    generated implementation bundle can legitimately exist without
    `technical_approval.status == CURRENT` for the live
    `implementation_revision` already recorded — and only while the
    bundle is currently stale (`generation_head` staleness check,
    `D-Bundle-Manifest`, already fails). This single phase already covers
    every case revision 31's two-phase list covered: a bundle staled before
    any review, and a bundle staled after receiving a matching `APPROVE`
    but before the user invoked `/approve-review implementation` — both
    are, correctly, the same durable phase once `GPT-R51-001` removes the
    separate durable `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` value; recovery's own
    mechanics never depended on knowing whether a matching `APPROVE`
    existed (the "Post-recovery phase transition" paragraph below already
    makes any pre-recovery feedback automatically inert regardless of its
    verdict). Invoking it when the bundle is not actually stale, or from
    any other phase (including a hand-edited `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL`,
    which can now only mean corruption), is a no-op/phase refusal naming
    the actual phase and the one legal one, not a silent success.
  - **Post-recovery phase transition** (simplified, revision 35,
    `GPT-R51-001`, to match the single remaining legal source phase; new,
    revision 31, `GPT-R47-001` — revision 30 left the phase unchanged,
    incorrectly implying the recovered bundle could go straight to
    `EXTERNAL_APPROVE` under the *pre-recovery* round's feedback): a
    successful recovery always transitions the work item to (or leaves it
    at) `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` — now always a
    value-wise no-op, since that is both the sole legal source and the
    target, never a real transition (revision 31's "regardless of which of
    the two legal source phases" framing no longer applies: there is only
    one). This is not optional caution: `D2`'s `EXTERNAL_APPROVE` basis
    requires the current
    `REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md`'s `Reviewed bundle ID:` to equal the
    just-recomputed `bundle_id` **exactly**, and regenerating from `S2`
    necessarily changes `bundle_id` (`generation_head` moved, the bundled
    `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`/provenance content changed) even though the
    protected implementation `review_content_id` did not — so any feedback
    reviewing the pre-recovery bundle `B1` is automatically, correctly
    inert against the post-recovery bundle `B2` under the existing
    `WFR-03`/`D2` exact-match rule (no new staleness mechanism needed, only
    this explicit consequence, previously unstated). A fresh external
    implementation review of `B2` is therefore mandatory before
    `technical_approval` can be recorded via `EXTERNAL_APPROVE` — the
    ordinary computed `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` gate (`D-States`,
    `GPT-R51-001`) then becomes reachable against `B2` exactly as it would
    against any newly generated bundle. The reviewer
    of `B2` may observe that its protected `review_content_id` is
    byte-identical to the previously-approved round's (stated explicitly
    in `B2`'s own `REVIEW_REQUEST.md`/`IMPLEMENTATION_SUMMARY.md` so the
    reviewer can re-approve quickly), but the resulting `technical_approval`
    still binds to `B2`'s own exact `bundle_id`, never to `B1`'s, because
    `D2` makes that binding authoritative regardless of content identity.
    `implementation_revision` and `reviewed_implementation_head` remain
    unchanged throughout this whole round-trip — recovery, re-review, and
    re-approval never constitute a new implementation round.
  - **User confirmation**: **required**, exactly as D-Commit-Provenance's
    existing "Recovery for genuine ambiguity" rule already requires for a
    `Workflow-Supersedes` trailer generically (a "named, git-tracked,
    user-approved action ... never a Claude-autonomous pick") — this
    operation is that same category of action, not a narrower
    automatically-authorized one, so the existing requirement is preserved
    unmodified rather than carved out. The command refuses to write
    anything unless the user's own current-turn message supplies literal
    confirmation text naming the exact `work_item_id` and the exact
    superseded commit SHA `S` (mirroring `/approve-review`'s own
    `validate_user_confirmation` mechanism, D2).
  - **Exact `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` mutation** (corrected, revision 31,
    `GPT-R47-001` — revision 30 claimed only `state_revision`/
    `last_transition` changed; the post-recovery phase transition above
    is a real, additional field write this revision now states
    explicitly; **narrowed, revision 35, `GPT-R51-001`**, now always the
    value-wise-no-op case, since `AWAITING_TECHNICAL_APPROVAL` is never a
    legal source phase to run from): `phase` is set to
    `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, value-wise unchanged from
    its only legal source phase, and
    `state_revision`/`last_transition` update per D3's standing
    per-transition convention. **No other field changes**: in particular,
    `reviewed_implementation_head`, `implementation_revision`, and
    `technical_approval` remain byte-identical before and after — nothing
    in the tracked round-identity fields changes, because this is not a
    new round. The recovery's durable round-identity record is still the
    Git commit `S2` itself (its trailers), not a new `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`
    field — consistent with this document's standing principle that a
    durable commit, not a mutable state field, is the authority for round
    identity; `phase` is ordinary workflow-state-machine bookkeeping, not
    a round-identity field.
  - **Pre-commit validation**: both precondition checks above, in order
    (cheap endpoint check first, full interval classification second),
    plus the phase/authorization checks above — all before the commit is
    created.
  - **Post-commit validation**: re-run D-Commit-Provenance's trailer
    discovery and tie-break against the new live HEAD, confirming it
    resolves `S2` as the current commit and `S` as superseded, confirm the
    resulting `P..S2` provenance interval independently validates under
    the same "Provenance interval" definition the approval gate itself
    will apply (including `S2`'s own terminal-commit role-specific check,
    `GPT-R47-003`), and confirm the work item's phase now reads
    `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW` — the operation does not
    simply trust its own precondition checks were sufficient; it
    re-derives the same conclusions the way `/approve-review
    implementation` and a fresh-session phase read will.
  - **Interruption behavior**: this is a single-commit write, the same
    shape as every other durable state-mutating operation in this
    document (e.g. plan approval's "writes exactly one commit and nothing
    after it") — interruption before the commit leaves the repository
    state unchanged (safe to retry from the top); interruption after the
    commit is durable and requires no completion step (the commit either
    exists or it does not; there is no partial state, including the
    `phase` write, which lands in the same commit as the trailers).
  - **Replay/idempotency** (**corrected, revision 32, `GPT-R48-003`** —
    revision 31's text here described an impossible partial-commit branch,
    directly contradicting the atomic single-commit "Interruption
    behavior" immediately above: if `S2` exists at all, its `phase` write
    is part of that same commit; there is no committed-`S2`-but-uncommitted-
    phase state to complete, and "complete the phase transition without
    re-committing" would itself be an uncommitted, non-durable state
    mutation this document's standing model forbids). Replay is simple and
    fails closed: retrying the command against the same stale round first
    checks whether a content-verified `Workflow-Supersedes: <S-sha>`
    commit for this exact `(work_item_id, implementation_revision, S)`
    triple is already reachable from live HEAD.
    - If no such commit is reachable, this is not a replay — the ordinary
      precondition checks and commit-creation path run as a first attempt.
    - If one is reachable, its own committed state is verified, not
      trusted on the trailer's existence alone: the discovered `S2`'s
      committed `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` content is checked for the required
      post-recovery mutation (`phase == AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
      and the `state_revision`/`last_transition` advance the recovery
      contract requires). If it holds, the operation reports exact
      replay/idempotent success and creates no second commit, no working-tree
      write of any kind. If the discovered `S2` lacks the required state
      mutation — the only way that can happen is a hand-edited, corrupted,
      or otherwise malformed historical commit, never an in-progress
      recovery, since the commit is atomic — the replay path classifies it
      as malformed/conflicting recovery provenance and refuses outright,
      naming the discovered commit and the missing mutation; it never
      repairs it with an uncommitted state write.
  - **Conflicting duplicate**: if a *different* `Workflow-Supersedes`
    commit already exists naming a *different* prior current commit for
    the same `(work_item_id, implementation_revision)` (e.g. two divergent
    recovery attempts from different sessions), this is the existing
    generic-ambiguity case, unchanged: the tie-break's two matches remain
    genuine ambiguity, refused, requiring explicit user disambiguation —
    the recovery command does not attempt to auto-resolve it.

  Bundle generation then runs from `S2` (`generation_head == S2`,
  D-Bundle-Manifest's exact-equality staleness check unchanged), the work
  item is at `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, and a fresh
  external implementation review of the regenerated bundle `B2` is
  required before `/approve-review implementation` can use
  `EXTERNAL_APPROVE` — at which point it evaluates against the now-bounded,
  fully-classified provenance interval `reviewed_implementation_head..S2`,
  exactly the same gate every round (recovered or not) goes through, no
  separate approval code path. `implementation_revision` is untouched
  throughout the whole recovery → re-review → re-approval round-trip, and
  the recovery commit itself is idempotent per the replay rule above.

**Same-content post-fix republication** (new, revision 35, `GPT-R51-003`
— see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 34 → 35)"): the recovery
operation above fires only from `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`,
after some review cycle has already completed. It has no legal action for
the structurally identical staleness that can occur *during*
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`: the user (or the AI, applying `/apply-implementation-review`'s
own disposition of a `REVISE` round) rejects every finding with evidence,
or resolves them entirely in implementation-stage *excluded* content, so
the protected `review_content_id` never changes — but the round-trip of
applying and recording that disposition itself commits one or more
legitimate excluded-only commits, moving live HEAD past the round's
existing generation-record commit `T` (`S` or a prior `S2`/`S3`/...).
Reusing `T` as-is, unchanged, would leave it historical rather than
current the moment any such commit lands, with no discoverable current
provenance tip to request a fresh external review against — exactly
`GPT-R51-003`'s worked scenario.

**Authority and source phase** (**widened, revision 38, `GPT-R54-002`** —
see "WF8b finding disposition (revision 37 → 38)" for the full
derivation): this is not a new command and never requires the additional
user confirmation `/recover-implementation-provenance` requires. It is the
**second of `record_bundle_generation`'s two outcomes** (**restated,
revision 37, `GPT-R53-002`** — no longer "third branch": the removed
"exact retry" outcome was never reachable, so this was always the
function's second and last outcome, not its third; D-Approval-Commits'
"`reviewed_implementation_head`'s sole writer" bullet), legal when invoked
at `implementation`/`post-fix` stage from **either** of
`record_bundle_generation`'s own two legal source phases —
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` **or** `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` (widened
from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`-only, `GPT-R54-002`: revision 35-37's
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`-only restriction left no legal outcome for a
`SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION`-invoked call whose protected content turns
out identical to the prior reviewed round — a no-op implementation pass, a
plan-only correction requiring no protected implementation change, or any
fix reverted before publication — directly contradicting
`D-Approval-Commits`' own two-outcome algorithm, which was never phase-
restricted for the "Identical" branch in the first place). Both are
already `record_bundle_generation`'s own legal invocation phases (the
"Legal source phase" bullet, `D-Approval-Commits`, unchanged by this
widening); this paragraph only removes a narrower, contradictory
restriction this subsection alone had additionally imposed on one of
`record_bundle_generation`'s two already-legal outcomes.
`record_bundle_generation` already carries the authority to author a
commit automatically as part of ordinary bundle publication (the ordinary
`S` case); this adds no new Git-authoring authority, only confirms that
authority's existing *shape* (same-content republication) is reachable
from both of the function's own legal invocation phases, not one.

**Operation** (**narrowed to two outcomes, revision 37, `GPT-R53-002`** —
revision 35's three-way text included an "exact retry" outcome that,
reached only ever via an invocation of `record_bundle_generation` itself
at `post-fix` stage from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`, requires live HEAD to
already equal the round's current tip `T` — but entering
`APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` at all is itself only reachable through a real
transition away from `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`, which is
only reachable once `T` already exists, so live HEAD is always strictly
ahead of `T` by the time this function could legally run; that outcome
was never reachable, in any revision that stated it. The crash-recovery
case it stood in for — a fresh session resumed with live HEAD already
equal to `T` — is now `D-Approval-Commits`' "Bundle-publication resume"
contract, which explicitly never invokes `record_bundle_generation`; see
"WF8b finding disposition (revision 36 → 37)"): recomputes the protected
implementation-stage
`review_content_id` at candidate live HEAD and compares it, exactly as
already specified, to the value recomputed from the commit
`reviewed_implementation_head` currently names.

- **Genuinely different** → the existing ordinary path: create `S`,
  advance `implementation_revision` by exactly one. Unchanged.
- **Identical** (live HEAD always differs from the round's current tip
  `T` at this point, per the reachability proof above — there is no
  further sub-case to distinguish) → **same-content
  republication**: run the exact same two-part precondition the "Stale-
  `generation_head` recovery" rule above defines, over the interval
  `T..HEAD` in place of `reviewed_implementation_head..HEAD` — (a) content
  at live HEAD is byte-identical to content at `reviewed_implementation_head`
  (already established by the outer comparison); (b) an exhaustive,
  first-parent, commit-by-commit classification of `T..HEAD` finds no
  protected or unclassified commit, with any generation-record commit
  found in the interval (a prior, still-current `T` cannot appear here by
  construction, but a *malformed* extra one could) required to satisfy its
  own role-specific contract, reusing condition 3 of the "Provenance
  interval" definition verbatim, never a separately maintained duplicate
  rule. If both pass, create **exactly one** new commit, shaped identically
  to the recovery commit `S2` above: first-parent child of live HEAD;
  touches only `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`'s `phase`/`state_revision`/
  `last_transition`; carries the unchanged `Workflow-Bundle-Generation-Record`
  value, a `Workflow-Supersedes: <T-sha>` trailer naming `T`, and the
  ordinary `Workflow-Work-Item` trailer — the same recovered-role
  canonical trailer set. Its `phase` mutation is a real transition —
  `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK` → `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
  when invoked from `APPLYING_REVIEW_FEEDBACK`, or
  `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` → `AWAITING_EXTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEW`
  when invoked from `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION` instead (**new,
  revision 38, `GPT-R54-002`** — the second case did not previously exist,
  since this branch was not yet legal from that source phase) —
  **always a real transition either way**, never value-wise unchanged
  (unlike a recovery-authored `S2`, always value-wise unchanged after
