## Revision 91 — self-discovered: `WF8C-S372H-001` — the seventh lock-shaped primitive, `PLAN_APPROVAL_MUTATION.guardlock`, omitted from "The complete global partial order"

**This is a bounded correction, not a redesign.** Nothing about `D1`,
`D-States`, `D-Commit-Provenance`, `D-Approval-Commits`,
`D-Checkpoint-Ownership`, or `D-Completion-Obligations` changes here beyond
the one ordering section and the one missing-test item named below. It does
exactly four things: document the seventh live lock-shaped primitive the
code already acquires; state its position and edge in the global ordering
graph, derived from the actual acquisition code rather than invented;
rebuild item 372(h)'s completeness arm so a defect of this exact class — a
lock-shaped object the code acquires that this document never names — is
caught by construction rather than by a fourth manual discovery; and leave
everything else revision 90 left in place untouched.

### The finding this revision reconciles

`WF8C-S372H-001` (self-discovered,
`docs/ai-workflow/dry-run/WF8C_FINDING_plan_approval_guardlock_undocumented.md`,
found while designing item 372(h)'s own completeness-arm conformance test —
before any test code was written, so nothing shipped against the defective
spec): "The complete global partial order, in one place" states, as settled
text with no revision marker later than 76, that this design has six
lock-shaped primitives. `scripts/workflow_state.py:2147-2148` defines a
seventh — `PLAN_APPROVAL_GUARD_LOCK_PATH = Path(".ai-review/runtime/PLAN_APPROVAL_MUTATION.guardlock")`
— live since commit `eab14ec` ("item (g) part 2 -- WFR-63 mutation/handoff
guard, owner progress record, explicit-takeover contract"), a genuine
`fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` acquisition exercised by both
`acquire_plan_approval_guard` and `release_plan_approval_guard`, and already
exercised by `workflow_state_test.py`. It never appears in this document:
`grep -c PLAN_APPROVAL_MUTATION docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_V2_PLAN.md` returns
10 occurrences before this revision, all naming primitive (1) alone, none
naming `.guardlock`. Because item 372(h)'s completeness arm enumerated its
candidate set **from this document's own prose** — "every `.lease`, `.lock`
and `.guardlock` pathname the document names" — a primitive the document
never names could never become a candidate, so a test built exactly to the
item's pre-revision-91 wording would report the six-primitive list
"complete" while this real seventh lock stayed permanently invisible: the
same class of defect `OPUS-R92-004` and `OPUS-R93-002` each caught once
already (revisions 75 and 76), recurring a third time, in a form its own
specified mechanism structurally could not detect, because that mechanism's
source of truth was the (incomplete) prose rather than the code the prose
claims to describe completely.

### What this revision does

Three things, all inside "The complete global partial order, in one place"
and item 372(h) — see both for the full text:

- Adds primitive (7), `PLAN_APPROVAL_MUTATION.guardlock`, with its position
  and edge determined from the real acquisition graph rather than invented:
  `acquire_plan_approval_guard` and `release_plan_approval_guard` both wrap
  their entire body in `_plan_approval_guard_lock`, structurally identical
  in kind to (6)'s `guard_mutation_lock`/(5) relationship — the introducing
  commit's own message says so directly — so the recorded edge is
  `(1)→(7)`, labeled `[the release's compare-and-delete]` on exactly the
  same footing `(5)→(6)` already uses, and (7) is stated as a leaf below
  (1) exactly as (6) is a leaf below (5), verified by reading both guarded
  functions end to end: neither touches any other primitive in this list.
  The graph gains one new sink edge and stays acyclic by construction.
- Rebuilds item 372(h)'s completeness arm to derive its candidate universe
  from the live code — every pathname that feeds an `fcntl.flock`
  acquisition or an `os.link`-based guard's fixed target path in
  `scripts/workflow_state.py` — compared **in both directions** against
  this document's declared list, so that a primitive the code acquires but
  this document never names, and, symmetrically, a primitive this document
  still lists after the code stops acquiring it, are each caught and named.
  The existing graph arm's own mechanism (derive edges from nested
  acquisitions, compare by equality) and the existing direction arm are
  preserved verbatim in substance, extended only for the one new edge and
  one new primitive; the two existing live control arms (the inverted
  `(2)→(5)` acquisition, the extra `(1)→(3)` acquisition) are untouched.
- Corrects, in passing, one stale prose count the same drift class had
  already broken ("Two per-primitive properties" heading three bullets
  since revision 76 added the third without updating the word) while
  adding the fourth bullet, for (7).

### What this revision does not do

Reopen `WF8b` or the revision-81/82 reconciliation; touch any checkpoint's
`depends_on`, `complexity`, `session_target`, or `completion_obligations`;
add, remove, or renumber any `WFR` requirement row (this fix lives entirely
in missing-test item 372(h) and its supporting prose, not in the
requirements table, so `workflow-v2-1-core-mapping.json` is untouched);
touch the `## Checkpoint registry` table or its registry-JSON mirror's
per-checkpoint fields (revision 90's own repaired parity is unaffected —
only the registry's top-level `plan_revision` field changes, to 91); invent
an ordering position or edge not traceable to the actual code (the position
and edge above are read directly off `acquire_plan_approval_guard`/
`release_plan_approval_guard`'s own bodies, not guessed); or implement item
372(h) itself — no conformance test for it exists yet, against either the
old or the new wording, and none is written by this revision. That remains
`WF8c`'s own future implementation scope, now against a spec this revision
makes actually implementable.

### Required regression / acceptance check

Stated directly in item 372(h)'s own text, learning revision 90's own
lesson that such a check must be precise enough to actually verify, not
merely asserted: the completeness arm's forward direction, run against this
document's own revision-90 six-primitive text and the current
seven-primitive code, must fail, naming exactly
`PLAN_APPROVAL_MUTATION.guardlock`; both directions, run against the
current revision-91 text and code, must pass; the reverse direction, run
against a copy of the current list with any one live entry deleted, must
fail, naming that entry.

## Revision 81 — convergence: `OPUS-R101-002` ledger reconciliation and `WF8c` (corrected by revision 82, `OPUS-R102-*` — the reconciliation table below is revision 82's corrected form; the design and rationale are revision 81's, upheld in full)

**This is a convergence revision, not a redesign.** Revision 80 remains the
architectural baseline in full — nothing about `D1`, `D-States`,
`D-Commit-Provenance`, `D-Approval-Commits`, `D-Checkpoint-Ownership`, or
`D-Completion-Obligations` changes here. This section exists to do three
things, and no more: truthfully reconcile the ~210-item "forward-looking
obligations owed to `WF8b`'s continued scope" ledger (missing-test items
167-376) against what is actually installed today; assign the genuinely
remaining work to a new, reachable successor checkpoint, `WF8c`, without
reopening `WF8b`; and add a mechanically-checked completion obligation
(`WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE`, `WFR-68`) so that `WF8c`'s own eventual `COMPLETE`
status cannot repeat the exact failure this revision reconciles.

### The finding this revision reconciles

`OPUS-R101-002` (Blocking, `.ai-review/workflow-v2-1-core/feedback/
REVIEW_FEEDBACK.md:175-278`, filed against implementation round 10, commit
`c91234f`): `WF8b.status == "COMPLETE"` while a mechanically verified subset
of items 167-376 was absent from the installed implementation. The audit
verified seven concrete obligations absent by direct search (its own table,
`:192-200`) and explicitly disclaimed a full item-by-item pass: "the true
residue may be larger" (`:743-744`). The harm is structural, not merely
narrative: `scoped_remediation_gate_reachable` requires `not is_terminal`,
and a registry where every checkpoint reads `COMPLETE` is terminal —
`/accept-scoped-remediation`, the one non-terminal recovery path this plan
built for exactly this situation (`D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`,
`WF8B-002`), becomes permanently unreachable the moment `technical_approval`
is recorded and `complete_work_item` opens, since `WorkItemIdReusedError`
makes `work_item_id`s permanently non-reusable. Four of the audit's five
other findings (`OPUS-R101-001`, `-003`, `-004`, `-005`) were already fixed
by commits `d8882d0`/`b7fe7aa`/`29f4d03`/`acadba3` before this revision began
(the live entry's phase was also already repaired to `SELF_REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION`,
per the audit's own "Migration and data-integrity concerns" note); `WFR-65`/
`publish_plan_revision` (commit `a2949bf`) landed independently in the same
window. `OPUS-R101-002` itself — the structural finding — is what this
revision reconciles.

### `WF8b` is not reopened

Its completion is accepted as valid historical fact for everything it
genuinely delivered — a large, real body of work, not a false one. The two
independent classification passes below (items 167-270, items 271-376,
cross-checked against `scripts/workflow_state.py`, `scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py`,
`.claude/commands/*.md`, and the hermetic test suites by function/test name,
not by reading the plan for plausibility) found that `D-Scoped-Remediation-Acceptance`
(items 167-221), the ordinary-role half of `D-Commit-Provenance`'s
bundle-generation-record provenance-interval gate (229-241, 273-277), `D1`'s
state-writer lock and `D-Completion-Obligations` in full (354-361), and
`D-Checkpoint-Ownership` in full (362-375) are genuinely, carefully
implemented, with dense test coverage matching almost every named scenario.
This is the strongest-implemented slice of the whole range and it stays
credited to `WF8b`.

### Reconciliation table

Grouped by the item ranges the "Missing tests" section's own revision-history
preamble already ties to one feature/finding each (not renumbered or
individually rewritten, except where noted). `IMPLEMENTED` = IMPLEMENTED,
credited to `WF8b`, historical, no longer forward-looking. `PARTIAL`/`ABSENT`
= genuinely remaining, reassigned to `WF8c`. `DEFERRED` = judgment call,
flagged for external review, not silently decided. `INVALID`/repaired = the
requirement's own text was wrong and is corrected in place. `SUPERSEDED` =
the design the items test is itself marked superseded, at the design layer,
in the same revision — never a range-level retirement of items whose design
section is still live normative text (`OPUS-R102-001`).

**Totality (new, revision 82, `OPUS-R102-005`)**: the union of this table's
own `Items` column, parsed as ranges, is **exactly** `167-376` — no gap, no
duplicate, nothing outside it — plus one deliberately-listed
outside-the-umbrella row (item 166, pre-167, tracked because its drift class
recurred). The ranges are **disjoint as well as total**, so every item in
`167-376` resolves to exactly one `(status, owner)` pair, which is the form
item 355's clause (b) is now stated over (`OPUS-R102-007`); item 318 is
therefore excised from the superseded publication range and carried in its
own row rather than appearing in both.

**Per-item resolution rule (new, revision 82, `OPUS-R102-007`)**: clause (b)
is evaluated over *items*, not over table cells, so each item's `(status,
owner)` pair is resolved by these rules, in order. (1) An item in a row whose
status is a bare `IMPLEMENTED`/`ABSENT`/`SUPERSEDED` resolves to that status
and that row's owner. (2) An item in a **`PARTIAL`** row resolves to
`PARTIAL` and to the checkpoint owing the **remaining** work — never to the
checkpoint credited with the delivered core. That is deliberate and is the
whole point of the clause: a `PARTIAL` row's compound owner cell ("`WF8b` for
the delivered core; `WF8c` for the dependent sub-cases") records history *and*
obligation, and only the obligation half can strand. Under this rule the
three compound rows revision 81's cell-level reading flagged as violations —
`262-267`, `282-286, 297-303`, `368-372` — resolve to `(PARTIAL, WF8c)` and
pass, without the clause being weakened to let them. (3) A `SUPERSEDED` item
resolves to owner `none`, which clause (b2) admits **only** when the design
section it tests is itself marked superseded in this plan.

Revision 81's table failed this
property by exactly one item (272), which is precisely how that item became
owed by nobody, undetectably; the check is stated here as a property of the
table rather than left to inspection, and `WFR-68`'s `ledger-status.json`
totality requirement is the machine-checked half of the same rule. A future
revision that adds a row must re-derive this union rather than assume it.

**What this table is not**: a letter-by-letter re-audit of every lettered
sub-scenario inside every item (some items, like 348 or 356 or 374, carry
dozens of sub-clauses). `OPUS-R101-002` itself disclaimed that scope
("the true residue may be larger"); this reconciliation operates at the same
item/item-group granularity the audit did, cross-checked against real code
and test names rather than plan prose, and is itself subject to external
review — which is exactly why `WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE` below does not depend on
this table being perfectly correct today. An item this table marks
`IMPLEMENTED` that a future pass finds actually incomplete is not a crisis:
it gets reassigned to whatever checkpoint is then open, by the identical
mechanism this revision uses for `WF8c`, never by reopening a `COMPLETE` one.

### `WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE`: preventing a second false completion

The structural half of this fix needs no new code: `WF8c`'s mere presence as
a non-`COMPLETE` registry row already makes `registry_completion_status(...)`
non-terminal again, restoring `scoped_remediation_gate_reachable` for exactly
the reason `WF8b.status == "COMPLETE"` had removed it. That alone, though,
only fixes today's instance — the *next* checkpoint handoff could reproduce
`OPUS-R101-002` exactly the same way if nothing enforces that a checkpoint's
own assigned ledger obligations are actually discharged before it may read
`COMPLETE`. `WFR-68` (above) declares `WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE` on `WF8c`'s own
`completion_obligations`, reusing `D-Completion-Obligations`' existing
execution-based, Git-object-pinned, isolated-interpreter verifier
architecture — the same machinery `WFO-STATE-SERIALIZATION` already proves
out for `WF8b` — rather than inventing a second one. Until `WF8c` builds and
gets technical approval for that verifier, the obligation is declared but
unbound, which `D-Completion-Obligations` already defines as fail-closed
(`UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION`, permanently blocking `complete_work_item`) rather than
vacuously satisfied. This is deliberate and is the whole point: `WF8c`
**cannot** reach `MILESTONE_COMPLETE` merely by having every registry
checkpoint read `COMPLETE`, exactly the property whose absence let
`OPUS-R101-002` happen in the first place, one level up.

### Item 355 is repaired, not merely amended

Item 355's revision-58 form hardcoded `WF8b` as the umbrella's owner and
treated items 167-376 as the complete, permanently-correct set of what
remained owed — both became false the instant `WF8b.status` reached
`COMPLETE` while genuine items in that exact range were undelivered. It is
rewritten below (in place, in the "Missing tests" list) in checkpoint-agnostic
form: it now asserts reachability against *whichever* checkpoint
`select_next_checkpoint(...)` actually returns, and asserts no item's
reconciled owner is a `COMPLETE` checkpoint unless that item's reconciled
status is `IMPLEMENTED`. Its revision-58-through-80 text is retained
immediately after, unedited, as the historical record of what the check
asserted and why — not deleted, because it was a real, previously-load-bearing
conformance rule and this document does not erase its own history.

### Scope discipline

This revision touches: the title/status header (this section's own
existence, above); the checkpoint registry (`WF8c`'s row, the `After WF8c`
note); the requirements table (`WFR-68` new; `WFR-61`/`WFR-62`/`WFR-63`/`WFR-67`
amended in place); item 355 (rewritten); items 348-353 and 376 (owner suffix
reassigned from the now-`COMPLETE` `WF8b` to `WF8c`, the only individual item
suffixes edited — every other reassignment in the table above is carried by
this section and the umbrella-sentence correction alone, matching how the
umbrella already overrode individual `WF4c`/`WF5`/`WF4a-ii`/`WF4a-iii`
suffixes for the 167-376 range before this revision). It does **not** touch:
`WF8b`'s own registry entry, checkpoint status, or `completion_obligations`;
`technical_approval`/`plan_approval` history; any `D-`-prefixed design section's
normative text; or any item's own historical prose describing what was true
when it was written.

**Scope discipline (revision 82)**: revision 82 additionally touches, and
this is stated explicitly because revision 81's own scope note above declared
no `D-` section would be — the review's finding was precisely that
*declining* to touch them is what stranded the requirements. Two `D-`
sections are amended, both to **withdraw or retarget** normative text rather
than to add design: (1) `D-Approval-Commits`' "Atomic bundle-file
publication" contract is marked **superseded**, naming
`REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`'s "Bundle structure" as the design of record and stating
the three residual failure modes with their compensating mechanisms — the
second condition the external review attached to upholding revision 81's
supersession of that design's conformance items, without which the plan would
require a mechanism nobody owes; and (2) `D-Bootstrap`'s sole-driver range is
restated checkpoint-agnostically (`WF0` through the registry's terminal
checkpoint) in place of the hardcoded "`WF0` through `WF8b`" that revision
81's own appending of `WF8c` had falsified. `D2a` is explicitly **not**
touched and remains fully live and normative — revision 81 had effectively
retired its conformance items by range, which is the defect
`OPUS-R102-001` reports. Beyond those two withdrawals, revision 82 touches:
the title/status header; the reconciliation table (rows split, reclassified,
added, and a totality/disjointness rule plus a per-item resolution rule added
to its preamble); the requirements table (`WFR-19`/`WFR-53` gain `WF8c` as an
additional owner; `WFR-61`/`WFR-62`/`WFR-63`/`WFR-67`/`WFR-68` amended in
place, no row added or renumbered — still 68); item 355's clause (b); and
`WF8c`'s registry scope text. It does **not** touch `WF8b`'s registry entry,
status, or obligations; `plan_approval`/`technical_approval` history; any
item's own historical prose; or `.claude/commands/`, `scripts/`, or any other
implementation content — including the two edits this revision explicitly
assigns to `WF8c` rather than performing (`bootstrap-workflow-v2.md`'s stale
driver range, and item 166's stale row-count literal).
