352. **(new, revision 55, `GPT-R72-001`; retimed and re-scoped, revision 56, `GPT-R73-001`)** the cross-command obligation the journal creates: while `.ai-review/runtime/PLAN_APPROVAL_JOURNAL.json` exists for `workflow-v2-1-core`, no command may act on that work item's state until the bootstrap's step 0 resolves it, and `/bootstrap-workflow-v2`'s own step-2 durability guard is rebound to a discovered durable `Workflow-Plan-Approval` commit (or to `workflow_state.implementing_entry_reachable(...)`) rather than to `plan_approval.approved_review_content_id` alone — confirmed by a direct reproduction of the pre-fix behavior, in which a **working-tree** state write with no commit makes the recomputed plan-stage `review_content_id` equal that record field by construction, so the unfixed guard passes and would resume implementation on a plan revision carrying no approval commit at all, while `/milestone-implement`'s `implementing_entry_reachable(...)` route correctly fails closed on the same state. **As of revision 56 this item is no longer the temporary bridge's only protection and is explicitly no longer on its critical path**: the index-pinned state write means the bridge never produces the working-tree state this guard would misread, so item 348(bb) — not this item — is what proves the *currently installed* command is safe during the bridge's own approvals, and this item covers the permanent, general fix for every future round, every other Workflow-v1-governed work item, and any future implementation that departs from the index-pinned ordering (see item 347's pairing rule). Its coverage additionally includes a journal precondition in the installed command and an explicit check that a durable approval commit rejected by step 7's committed path-set/state-bytes assertions is likewise not treated as a valid implementation entry while the journal remains unresolved. **Extended, revision 57 (`GPT-R74-001`)**: the journal precondition must be an **ownership-aware** one — a command that finds a journal it does not own refuses and reports, and never resolves, replaces, or deletes it, so the permanent fix cannot reintroduce the automatic-recovery-by-any-session shape this revision removed. **Extended again, revision 58 (`GPT-R75-001`)**: the ownership-aware precondition must be **guard-aware** too — a command that finds the transaction mutation guard held reports it and refuses rather than treating an unheld journal token as the whole ownership picture, and the permanent fix may not reintroduce a check-before-mutation ordering in place of the guarded `acquire → assert_owner → mutate → advance progress → release` window → WF8c (reassigned, revision 81, `OPUS-R101-002` — the now-`COMPLETE` `WF8b` never delivered this item).

353. **(new, revision 56, `GPT-R73-002`)** the canonical `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` serialization — `json.dumps(state, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"`, UTF-8 encoded — is asserted to round-trip this repository's own live state file byte-identically, and the two obvious neighbours are asserted **not** to (`ensure_ascii=True`, the `json.dumps` default, escapes the file's non-ASCII characters; `sort_keys=True` reorders `work_items`), so the check fails loudly if a future edit makes the live file non-canonical rather than silently accepting either form. Because `scripts/workflow_state.py` deliberately has no state-file writer of its own — the state file is written by the commands, and `apply_plan_approval`/`apply_technical_approval`/the phase-transition helpers all return a new state object for the caller to persist — this obligation is a conformance assertion over **every** writer: each `.claude/commands/*.md` step that persists this file must name the canonical form, so two commands cannot alternate between serializations and leave the file oscillating. The obligation is load-bearing for `D-Approval-Commits`' exact expected-post-state binding, which is meaningless without a single agreed byte-level form. The "every writer" set is the complete twelve-command enumeration `D1` names (revision 58); a sampled list would leave the file free to oscillate through whichever writer was omitted → WF8c (reassigned, revision 81, `OPUS-R101-002` — the now-`COMPLETE` `WF8b` never delivered this item).

354. **(new, revision 57, `GPT-R74-002`; primitive corrected and completion binding added, revision 59, `GPT-R76-002`/`GPT-R76-003`; (c) rewritten around live writer discovery and (d) rewritten from a recorded success fact to a gate-derived verdict, revision 60, `GPT-R77-001`/`-002`/`-003`)** `D1`'s shared-state concurrency contract — "Serialized `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` writes" — is real rather than advisory, and its primitive has correct live-writer and crash semantics. **(a) The primitive.** `.ai-review/runtime/WORKFLOW_STATE.lock` is opened `O_CREAT | O_RDWR` and held under `fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX)` across the **complete** read → mutate → canonical-serialize → atomic-publish critical section, released by `LOCK_UN`/close on every exit path including refusals and exceptions. **Revision 58's persistent `os.link` lock with owner-token takeover is superseded and must not be implemented**: it was reproduced losing an update — writer A took the lock and read `{a:0,b:0}`, ownership was taken over, writer B read and published `{a:0,b:1}`, and the still-live A then published its stale `{a:1,b:0}` — because a generic state writer has no journal, no owner-progress record and no mutation guard, and therefore no mechanical way to tell a crashed holder from a paused one. **(b) The asserted properties**, each exercised with real processes rather than asserted: writer B cannot enter the critical section while A holds it (B blocks until A releases); if A crashes mid-section the kernel releases ownership and B proceeds with **no** manual "break a possibly-live writer" step, with A's partial update absent; after B proceeds, A cannot publish, because no live writer is ever displaced and a crashed one is gone — the implementation is asserted to contain **no takeover, no owner token, and no user authorization** for this lock at all; two (and sixteen) concurrent writers serialize with **every** update present in the final file and none lost; a naive same-process second acquisition is confirmed to block (`LOCK_EX | LOCK_NB` raises `BlockingIOError`), so nested state writes are asserted to **raise an explicit re-entrancy refusal** rather than deadlock; and the lock file is confirmed to carry no ownership at rest, being immediately acquirable once the holder exits. **(c) The every-writer conformance.** A conformance assertion enumerates every writer of that path **through `discover_state_writers(repo_root, C)` — the single live-discovery implementation `D-Completion-Obligations` defines, whose return value is simultaneously what this conformance validates and what the obligation identity binds** (revision 60, `GPT-R77-002`) — never from this plan's own list, and over every declared writer surface rather than `.claude/commands/` alone: surfaces are recursive (namespaced `.claude/commands/<ns>/<name>.md` commands are supported and were found undiscovered by a one-level rule) and extension-agnostic (a `.markdown`/`.bash` file escaped an extension-keyed rule), and every file on a surface must carry an explicit `state_writer` declaration, with a missing or contradictory one failing closed. The conformance confirms each discovered writer (i) acquires the primitive, (ii) performs the read that feeds its write **inside** the critical section, and (iii) holds it through the publish — the shape it must specifically reject is a command that locks only around its final write while publishing a value derived from its preflight read. The enumeration is asserted complete rather than sampled, since a single unlocked writer voids the contract for all of them. **Twelve is a recorded observation of today's repository, never an input and never a hard-coded invariant** (revision 60, `GPT-R77-002`'s acceptance criterion 13): the conformance compares discovery's result against the live declarations, and item 357 asserts that no code anywhere compares a writer count against a literal. The twelve writers discovery returns today are `/accept-milestone`, `/accept-scoped-remediation`, `/apply-functional-review`, `/apply-implementation-review`, `/apply-plan-review`, `/approve-review`, `/bootstrap-workflow-v2`, `/milestone-implement`, `/milestone-plan`, `/prepare-functional-review`, `/record-manual-plan-review`, `/review-plan` (`/prepare-review` is the sole non-writer, and no file under `scripts/` writes the path — `workflow_state.py` has no state-file writer, which is why every writer is a command file). A writer that cannot acquire the lock is asserted to refuse and report rather than proceed. The pre-obligation state is asserted explicitly, so the gap is recorded rather than assumed away: all twelve perform a plain, unlocked read-modify-write today, which is why `D-Approval-Commits` step 8b additionally never merges and runs under a temporary quiescence window instead of depending on this obligation having landed. **(d) The authoritative success fact (new, revision 59, `GPT-R76-003`; rewritten from a recorded fact to a derived one, revision 60, `GPT-R77-001`/`-002`/`-003`).** This item's conformance **is** the authority, and it is executed by the gate rather than reporting to it. There is no evidence record: revision 59's `status: "PASS"` + `obligation_content_id` artifact is withdrawn, because a hand-written record carrying the exact current digest was reproduced classifying `CURRENT_PASS` — with an arbitrary `produced_by`, with a copied one, and by editing a `FAILED` record to `PASS` without rerunning anything. Instead, `resolve_completion_obligations(...)` pins one commit `C`, reads every input out of Git objects at `C` (with replace-object resolution disabled), discovers the writer set through the single `discover_state_writers(repo_root, C)` implementation, runs this item's conformance against exactly that discovered set, and derives `PASS`/`FAIL` from the execution. The verdict is a pure function of `(obligation_id, subject_identity, verifier_identity)` (**corrected, revision 61, `GPT-R78-001`** — revision 60 called it a pure function of `(obligation_id, C)`, which pins the subject but not the checker, so a later implementation could silently change the answer for an unchanged `C`); the subject cannot change between derivation and use because Git objects are immutable, and the verifier cannot change because it is materialized and executed from the blobs a **current implementation-stage technical approval** covers -- resolved, **as of revision 62 (`GPT-R79-001`), through the obligation owner's durable `Workflow-Technical-Approval` commit** rather than through `approval_is_current(..., stage="implementation", head=C)` alone: that predicate proves freshness of a mutable record and never that the record came from an approval event, so the gate now recomputes the implementation-stage identity at `C`, discovers the reachable, unambiguous approval commit carrying *that* identity, reads the authoritative `technical_approval` record out of the `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` that commit committed, and refuses whenever a live copy disagrees with it on any authority-bearing field. The verifier it materializes is the **complete execution-complete repository-local dependency closure** of the declared entry point (`GPT-R79-002`), not a single recorded file, and it is executed in a fresh isolated interpreter with the live repository removed from module lookup. An unreviewed protected change to the conformance, to the obligation-to-conformance binding, to discovery, or to any state writer classifies `VERIFIER_UNAPPROVED` and refuses before any verdict is derived, and a currency evaluation that cannot complete at all classifies `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE`; the obligation identity it carries binds the surface definitions, the complete surface census, the discovered writer set, the publisher, the helper and the conformance implementation, so adding, removing, renaming or rewriting a writer — or adding an *undeclared* file to a writer surface — recomputes it rather than leaving a prior result current. **That single derived verdict is what both the temporary quiescence window's retirement and `WF8b`/work-item completion consume**, through the identical call under identical pinning and refusal rules — they cannot disagree, because there is only one derivation. The conformance never touches the live state file or the live lock, so the gate is safe to run from inside the terminal critical section that already holds it. **Owner (revision 58, `GPT-R75-003`): `WF8b` continued scope**, not `WF4a-iii` — revision 57 suffixed this item `→ WF4a-iii`, which `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` records as `COMPLETE`, while the "Missing tests" continued-scope umbrella stopped at item 353, so the one obligation that turns `D1`'s serialized-write contract from prose into a mechanism had no reachable implementation owner at all; `select_next_checkpoint(...)` was run against the live state and registry and returns `WF8b`. This follows this plan's own standing `GPT-R29-003` precedent exactly — item 166 was found assigned to already-complete `WF8a-ii` and reassigned to `WF8b` continued scope rather than reopening the completed checkpoint — and `WF4a-iii` is deliberately **not** reopened. **`WF8b` cannot complete while this item is unsatisfied**, and as of revision 59 that is a machine-enforced dependency through `D-Completion-Obligations` rather than a statement in prose → WF8b.
355. **(new, revision 58, `GPT-R75-003`; rewritten to test a real dependency, revision 59, `GPT-R76-003`; rewritten a second time, revision 81, `OPUS-R101-002`, after the checkpoint-agnostic form below replaced the hardcoded-`WF8b` form this note used from revision 58 through 80)** **Revision-81 disposition, read first.** Clauses (a)-(d) as revision 59 left them hardcoded `WF8b` as the umbrella's owner and asserted the umbrella's item range (167-376) was itself the complete set of what remained owed — both became false the moment `WF8b.status` reached `COMPLETE` while genuine obligations from that exact range were still undelivered (`OPUS-R101-002`, the finding this whole revision reconciles). A conformance that hardcodes today's open checkpoint as tomorrow's assumed-still-open owner is exactly the "convention with no owner" class this item exists to reject, one level up from what revision 58 caught the first time. The rule is restated below in checkpoint-agnostic form, and this item's own historical text (the paragraph beginning "every forward-looking obligation…") is retained immediately after, unedited, as the record of what the check asserted from revision 58 through 80 and why revision 59's stress pass corrected clause (b) — it is superseded prose, not current the rule.

    **The corrected rule.** Every forward-looking obligation this plan adds has a **reachable, non-terminal** implementation owner, asserted mechanically against the live registry and state rather than by reading suffixes or assuming which checkpoint that owner is: (a) for the currently-open umbrella owner — `workflow_state.select_next_checkpoint(<work item entry>, <registry>)`'s return value, whatever checkpoint that resolves to today — every item this revision's own reconciliation table assigns to it is confirmed to have that checkpoint as a real, `depends_on`-reachable, non-`COMPLETE` registry entry; run against the live state and registry immediately after this revision's own registry write, this resolves to `WF8c`, and `WF8b` — the prior umbrella owner — is confirmed `COMPLETE` and *not* reused (`D-Checkpoint-Ownership`'s origination reference forbids it structurally, independent of this item); (b) **restated per item, revision 82 (`OPUS-R102-007`)** — revision 81 stated this clause over the reconciliation table's `status`/`owner` *cells*, which made it simultaneously unsatisfiable on the three rows carrying compound cells (`262-267`'s "`WF8c` (267 only)", and the two `PARTIAL` rows reading "`WF8b` for the delivered core; `WF8c` for …", each naming a `COMPLETE` checkpoint against a non-`IMPLEMENTED` status on a literal read, where the substance was fine and only the encoding was wrong) and **fail-open on exactly the rows that mattered**, since "no owner" is not "a `COMPLETE` checkpoint" and so an owner-`none` row passed unexamined — which is precisely how `OPUS-R102-001`'s four stranded pin items, and item 272's absence entirely, slipped through the check written to catch stranding. That is the same defect class this item's own retained history records revision 59's stress pass 5 withdrawing: a conformance that can never pass is worse than none, because it either blocks forever or gets quietly weakened during implementation. The rule is therefore stated over **per-item resolved `(status, owner)` pairs**, which the reconciliation table now guarantees exist and are unique (its totality-and-disjointness property, added the same revision): every item in `{166} ∪ {167..376}` — the identical universe `WFR-68` property (i) now names, corrected here to match, revision 87, `OPUS-R109-003` — resolves to exactly one status and exactly one owner. Two limbs, both required: **(b1) negative** — no item whose resolved status is not `IMPLEMENTED` names a `COMPLETE` checkpoint as its resolved owner; **(b2) positive** — every item whose resolved status is not `IMPLEMENTED` names a **real, non-`COMPLETE`** owner, and a resolved owner of `none` is a violation *unless* that item's status is an explicitly argued `SUPERSEDED` **and** the design section whose behaviour it tests is itself marked superseded in the plan. (b2) is the limb revision 81 lacked entirely, and it is what makes the check non-vacuous: `WFR-68`'s `ledger-status.json` is the natural carrier for the per-item pairs, so this conformance is a read of that artifact rather than a markdown parser; (c) the umbrella range's own upper bound (currently item 376) equals the highest-numbered item in the "Missing tests" list, unchanged from revision 59 — adding an item without extending the range still fails the check; and (d) unchanged from revision 59: a corresponding requirements-row's `checkpoint_ids` never implies that a newly discovered obligation inherits an already-complete historical checkpoint merely because that checkpoint's row happens to mention the same design thread. **The structural half of this revision's own fix is independent of this item's conformance test**: `WF8c`'s mere presence as a non-`COMPLETE` registry entry already makes `registry_completion_status(...)` non-terminal again today, for the same structural reason `WF8b.status == "COMPLETE"` made it terminal — this item's conformance is what keeps that property from silently regressing at the *next* umbrella handoff, not what establishes it at this one.

    **Superseded historical text (revision 58 through 80, retained for the record, no longer the rule — see above):** "every forward-looking obligation this plan adds has a **reachable** implementation owner, asserted mechanically rather than by reading suffixes: (a) `workflow_state.select_next_checkpoint(<the work item's own authoritative `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` entry>, <the protected registry>)` is run for real and the checkpoint it returns is confirmed to own item 354 — the run performed at revision 59 returns `WF8b`, and `WF4a-iii`, item 354's revision-57 owner, is confirmed `COMPLETE`; (b) **every item numbered ≥ 167 — the continued-scope era — falls within the umbrella range**, checked across the whole list rather than for the newest item only, since revision 57 demonstrated that a single item falling one past the umbrella's upper bound is enough to strand it; and no item is *added* carrying an owner suffix that resolves to a `COMPLETE` checkpoint unless the umbrella covers it. **(Scoping corrected, revision 59, stress pass 5.)** The first draft of this clause said "no missing-test item whose owner resolves to a `COMPLETE` checkpoint is left without an overriding umbrella entry, checked across the whole list," which is **unsatisfiable**: run against the live plan and state it flags 83 items, every one of them numbered below 167 — historical obligations that the checkpoint named in their suffix actually implemented before completing. A conformance that can never pass is worse than none, because it either blocks `WF8b` forever or gets quietly weakened during implementation; the corrected form flags exactly the items the umbrella is responsible for, and returns empty against the live plan; (c) the "Missing tests" continued-scope range's upper bound equals the highest-numbered item in the list, so adding an item without extending the range fails the check rather than silently orphaning it; and (d) the corresponding requirements-row wording is confirmed not to imply that a newly discovered obligation inherits the already-complete historical checkpoint of the row that happens to mention it — `WFR-63`'s `WF4a-iii` ownership covers the revision-50 five-member commit property it was written for, never item 354's future serialization work." **Revision 58's own clause (d) is withdrawn and replaced by item 356** (`GPT-R76-003`): it claimed `WF8b` was confirmed unable to reach completion while item 354 remained unsatisfied, "exercised through `registry_completion_status(...)` / `resolve_own_registry_completion_status(...)`" — but those helpers know only checkpoint status. Independently re-confirmed against the bundled implementation: forcing `WF8b.status = "COMPLETE"` on the live work item makes `registry_completion_status(...)` return `(True, None)` and `select_next_checkpoint(...)` return `None`, with no item-354 evidence consulted anywhere. This item therefore asserts **reachability and orphan-freedom only**, which is what it can actually prove; the completion *dependency* is item 356's subject (now generalized by `WFO-LEDGER-COVERAGE`, revision 81, to cover this item's own reconciliation table rather than only item 354), and this item additionally asserts that no plan text claims a completion guarantee from a registry-only helper → WF8c.
356. **(new, revision 59, `GPT-R76-003`; sub-scenarios (a)/(b)/(c)/(h)/(i) rewritten in place for the derived-verdict model and (k)-(p) added, revision 60, `GPT-R77-001`/`-002`/`-003`; (q)-(v) added, revision 61, `GPT-R78-001`; (w)-(z) added for durable approval provenance, live-record non-authority, verifier execution closure and executable replay, revision 62, `GPT-R79-001`/`-002`)** `D-Completion-Obligations` is a real, machine-enforced dependency rather than a declaration: (a) the verdict classifications are each exercised against `WF8b` with **every** ordinary registry checkpoint marked `COMPLETE` — a conformance that genuinely `FAIL`s, a working tree that has `DIVERGED` from the pinned commit, a caller-asserted pin that has moved (`PIN_MOVED`), an obligation with no bound conformance (`UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION`), an unresolvable commit (`UNRESOLVABLE`), and a genuine `PASS` — and `complete_work_item(...)` is confirmed to raise `UnsatisfiedCompletionObligationError` in every case but the last, naming the obligation, its classification and (for `FAIL`) the failing conformance assertions, and to succeed only on `PASS`; (b) the same set is exercised against the **temporary state-writer quiescence window's retirement** and confirmed to produce the identical verdict from the identical helper call under identical pinning, so the two consumers cannot disagree in either direction; (c) **the verdict is confirmed to be derived from execution, never read from a record**: with the conformance in a state that genuinely fails, a hand-written `docs/ai-workflow/registry/<work_item_id>-completion-evidence.json` carrying `status: "PASS"` and the exact current `obligation_content_id` is confirmed **not** to satisfy either consumer — with an arbitrary `produced_by`, with a `produced_by` copied verbatim from a legitimate run, and after editing an existing `FAILED` entry to `PASS` — and, in the other direction, a legitimate passing conformance is confirmed to satisfy both consumers *while such a file is present, absent, or says `FAILED`*, proving the file is not an input to any verdict or to the obligation identity; (d) setting `WF8b`'s registry checkpoint status to `COMPLETE` by hand, via `complete_checkpoint(...)`, or by any other route is confirmed **insufficient by itself** to reach `MILESTONE_COMPLETE`; (e) the set of functions that can write the terminal phase is enumerated from the bundled implementation and asserted to be exactly `complete_work_item(...)`, so no alternate acceptance path — `/accept-scoped-remediation` and `apply_scoped_remediation_acceptance(...)` in particular, whose whole purpose is the **non**-terminal continued-scope round — can bypass the same dependency; (f) `select_next_checkpoint(...)`/`registry_completion_status(...)` are confirmed to retain their registry-only semantics unchanged, and the higher-level gate is confirmed to reject their terminal result when an obligation is outstanding, which is the division `GPT-R76-003`'s required correction (3) permits; (g) a **second, synthetic** obligation declared on a checkpoint is confirmed to be enforced by the same code path with no new special case, proving the mechanism generalizes rather than hard-coding item 354; (h) an obligation declared in the registry with no conformance bound to its id is confirmed to classify `UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION` and block completion permanently rather than defaulting to satisfied — the fail-closed direction; (i) the gate is confirmed to be evaluated **inside** the same `WORKFLOW_STATE.lock` critical section that publishes the terminal transition, and **separately** confirmed not to depend on that lock for its stability: with a verdict derived at pinned commit `C`, rewriting the serialization helper, deleting a discovered writer, and planting or mutating an evidence-shaped file in the working tree are each confirmed to leave the derived verdict and its `obligation_content_id` bit-for-bit unchanged, while a fresh resolve is confirmed to refuse the same working tree as `DIVERGED` — revision 59's claim that the state-file lock made unrelated evidence immutable is confirmed false by the same test and is asserted nowhere; (j) where both the transaction mutation guard and the state-file lock are held, the acquisition order is confirmed to be guard-then-`flock` on every path, so no lock-order inversion exists; (k) **(revision 60)** the gate is confirmed to accept **no caller-supplied commit**: handing it an ancestor commit at which the conformance passed, while `HEAD` genuinely fails and the working tree has been restored to that ancestor's content so the divergence precondition stays silent, is confirmed **not** to satisfy either consumer — the pin a caller may pass is confirmed to be an assertion that refuses (`PIN_MOVED`), never a redirection of the derivation; (l) **(revision 60)** the conformance is confirmed to run against the **exact identity later accepted**: the terminal transition's recorded `source_commit`/`obligation_content_id` are confirmed to be the ones the passing derivation produced, and re-deriving at the recorded `source_commit` is confirmed to reproduce both exactly, including after arbitrary later commits have landed; (m) **(revision 60)** the terminal state is confirmed to carry `completion_obligations_accepted` in the same atomically published bytes as `MILESTONE_COMPLETE`, sufficient for a later audit to name which obligation result and implementation identity authorized the transition; (n) **(revision 60)** the conformance is confirmed to touch neither the live `docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json` nor `.ai-review/runtime/WORKFLOW_STATE.lock`: the whole gate is exercised **with that lock actually held by the calling process**, confirmed to complete without deadlock or re-entrancy refusal, and the lock is confirmed still held by the caller afterwards; (o) **(revision 60)** the behavioural sub-suite is confirmed **deterministic** rather than probabilistic — a publisher that reads outside the critical section is confirmed to fail the barrier-based interleaving test on every run, not merely to be likely to lose a race; and (p) **(revision 60)** every Git object read the gate performs is confirmed to disable `git replace` resolution, exercised in both directions: substituting broken bytes over a bound blob is confirmed not to change the verdict, and substituting honest bytes over a failing blob is confirmed **unable** to launder that identity into a `PASS`; (q) **(revision 61, `GPT-R78-001`)** the verdict is confirmed **unusable without a current implementation-stage technical approval**: with a genuinely converted repository and a legitimate prior approval, a single unreviewed commit that changes a state writer *and* rebinds `WFO-STATE-SERIALIZATION` to an unconditional-`PASS` conformance is confirmed to classify `VERIFIER_UNAPPROVED` for **both** consumers, with the working tree clean and byte-equal to that `HEAD` so the divergence precondition is silent — the exercise is repeated separately for a discovery changed to omit the writer it just broke, for a conformance changed to return `PASS` unconditionally with nothing else touched, and for a protected writer changed with the verifier untouched, and each is confirmed to refuse *before* a verdict is derived rather than to derive one and discard it; (r) **(revision 61)** a fresh implementation review and technical approval of the **exact** changed content is confirmed to make the same repository eligible again and to derive `PASS`, and the recomputed `verifier_identity_id` is confirmed **unchanged** when only the subject changed, proving the two identities are separate rather than one digest wearing two names; (s) **(revision 61)** commits touching only implementation-stage **excluded** paths (`docs/ai-workflow/WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, this plan document, the registry/requirements artifacts) after the approval are confirmed **not** to create refusal, so provenance-permitted metadata activity produces no false staleness; (t) **(revision 61)** every incomplete authority is confirmed to refuse rather than to pass — absent record, `status: "STALE"`, a `LEGACY_V1` record whose `review_content_manifest`/`approved_review_content_id` are null, a null `reviewed_content_commit`, an approved manifest covering no verifier path, and a manifest entry whose verifier blob does not equal the content at the pinned commit — while a work item declaring **no** obligation is confirmed satisfied vacuously **without** its `technical_approval` being consulted at all, so `D-Legacy`'s imported `LEGACY_V1` entry is not made permanently uncompletable by a mechanism that does not apply to it, and an `UnclassifiedPathError` from the implementation-stage classifier is confirmed to classify `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE` rather than to propagate out of the gate; (u) **(revision 61)** **historical replay executes the recorded verifier, not the live one**: after a terminal completion, changing the live verifier to an unconditional-`PASS` binding and then renaming its derivation entry point entirely is confirmed to leave replay from the recorded `verifier_census` bit-for-bit unchanged — verdict and `obligation_content_id` both — including after arbitrary later history, and a recorded verifier blob that is no longer reachable is confirmed to classify `REPLAY_UNRESOLVABLE` rather than to fall back to whatever implementation is running; and (v) **(revision 61)** `completion_obligations_accepted` is confirmed to carry the verifier identity and its technical-approval provenance (`verifier_identity_id`, the ordered `verifier_census`, `technical_approval_commit`, `approved_review_content_id`) alongside the subject identity, in the same atomically published bytes, sufficient for (u)'s replay to run from the state file alone; **(w)** **(revision 62, `GPT-R79-001`)** the verifier authority is confirmed to come from a **durable approval commit**, exercised across the full attack set with the working tree clean and byte-equal to `HEAD` so the divergence precondition stays silent: a genuine reachable technical-approval commit plus unchanged approved implementation authorizes; a hand-written `status: "CURRENT"` record carrying the **exact** recomputed `approved_review_content_id` and the **exact** current verifier manifest but no approval commit refuses; the same record with a plausible copied `reviewed_content_commit` still refuses; an approval commit reachable only on a foreign branch refuses; two same-identity approval commits that survive the existing first-parent tie-break refuse as ambiguous rather than resolving to either; an approval commit whose committed `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` is malformed or carries no record for the owner refuses; and an approval trailer naming a **different** work item does not authorize this one; **(x)** **(revision 62)** the **live record is never independently authority-bearing**: with a genuine approval commit present, editing the live `review_content_manifest` afterwards refuses, and so does divergence on any other authority-bearing field, with the refusal **naming the diverging fields** rather than silently choosing a side; repairing the divergence is confirmed to restore authorization, so the rule is an equality check and not a one-way trap; the live `base_commit` is confirmed pinned to the approval commit's own recorded value, since it is folded into the authority-bearing digest; **(y)** **(revision 62, `GPT-R79-002`)** the recorded verifier is confirmed **execution-complete**: the derived closure is materialized into a scratch tree and executed in a **fresh interpreter** with `sys.path` reset to that tree plus the standard library, and it imports and runs; omitting `scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` fails closed with `ModuleNotFoundError` rather than importing it live, **including with `PYTHONPATH` pointed deliberately at the live `scripts/` directory**; a newly added repository-local import that is not censused fails closed; a lazily imported dependency is nonetheless censused; a dynamic-import construct classifies `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE`; a package dependency is censused with its subtree and executes, and fails closed when dropped; every loaded module is confirmed to resolve inside the scratch tree, asserted from **inside** the isolated process so `sys.modules` cannot hide a leak; and **(z)** **(revision 62)** historical replay is confirmed **executable rather than descriptive**: after later history rewrites both live verifier modules to raise on import, adds unrelated commits, and then **deletes both modules from the tree entirely**, replay from the recorded census is confirmed bit-for-bit unchanged; a `git replace` ref planted over a recorded verifier blob is confirmed defeated by `--no-replace-objects`, with the same read *without* the hardening confirmed laundered in the other direction; and a recorded blob that is genuinely unreachable is confirmed to classify `REPLAY_UNRESOLVABLE` rather than to fall back to current code — the verdict staying tied to the originally approved verifier identity in every case → WF8b.

357. **(new, revision 60, `GPT-R77-002`)** State-writer discovery is a single, complete, dynamically-evaluated implementation, and the obligation identity binds exactly what it discovers: (a) `discover_state_writers(...)` is confirmed to be the **only** writer inventory in the bundled implementation — no second list, no prose-derived constant, and no comparison of a writer count against a literal anywhere in the code — so the 8-vs-12 drift `GPT-R75-002` found cannot recur; (b) the writer projection the conformance validates and the projection hashed into `obligation_content_id` are confirmed to be the **same object**, not two computations asserted to agree; (c) discovery is confirmed to return exactly the twelve installed writers against this repository's own live content, as an observation rather than an assertion about the number; (d) each of adding a thirteenth state-writing command, converting `/prepare-review` (today's sole non-writer) into a writer, adding a state writer under a supported non-command surface, renaming a writer, and removing a writer is confirmed to change the obligation identity **and** to be correctly accepted or refused on its own merits — a properly converted thirteenth writer passes as a recomputed thirteen-writer verdict, an unconverted one fails; (e) an **undeclared** file added to a writer surface is confirmed to change the identity as well as to fail the conformance, so surface membership is bound and not merely its declared-writer subset; (f) a namespaced `.claude/commands/<ns>/<name>.md` writer and a writer named with an unexpected extension are each confirmed to be discovered, the two escapes a non-recursive and an extension-keyed surface rule respectively permitted; (g) a file declaring `state_writer: false` while referencing the state path or the publisher, and a file whose declaration is missing or self-contradictory, are each confirmed to fail closed rather than being guessed at; (h) exactly one file is confirmed to be permitted to declare itself the publisher, and it is confirmed to be the path the projection names; (i) a declared writer that delegates its state write to a module outside the writer surfaces — a `*_test.py` module in particular, the one deliberate surface exclusion — is confirmed to fail the routing check, so the exclusion is not a hiding place; and (j) changing unrelated non-writer content — the state file itself, product documentation, an excluded test module — is confirmed **not** to change the obligation identity or the verdict, so the mechanism does not manufacture false staleness → WF8b.

358. **(new, revision 61, `GPT-R78-001`; (a)/(b) rewritten and (c)/(e) extended, revision 62, `GPT-R79-001`/`-002`)** The completion-obligation gate's **verifier authority** is a real consumer of the workflow's existing implementation-stage approval machinery, not a second approval system and not a claim in prose. **(a)** **(rewritten, revision 62, `GPT-R79-001`)** The authority resolution is asserted to be sourced from a **durable `Workflow-Technical-Approval` commit**, not from the mutable `technical_approval` record: the gate is asserted to recompute the implementation-stage identity at the pinned `C` for the work item that **owns** the obligation, to look that recomputed identity up through `discover_technical_approval_commit(...)` (**the search key is asserted to be the recomputed identity, never any field of any record**), to require the discovered commit reachable and an ancestor of `C`, to read the authoritative record out of the `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` that commit committed, and to require any live copy to equal it on every authority-bearing field (`status`, `basis`, `approved_review_content_id`, `review_content_manifest`, `reviewed_content_commit`, `reviewed_bundle_id`, `user_confirmation`, `legacy_evidence`, `waived_guarantees`) and the live `base_commit` to equal the one that commit committed. It is asserted structurally too, by confirming the gate defines no status field, record, ledger, freshness rule or approval format of its own for completion obligations, and that it reuses the existing trailer/ancestry/ambiguity helpers rather than a parallel provenance system. **(b)** **(rewritten, revision 62, `GPT-R79-002`)** The approved verifier identity is asserted to be derived as an **execution-complete repository-local dependency closure**: a static `ast` import closure over the pinned blobs, seeded at the declared verifier entry point, transitively following every tracked module or package on the declared verifier source root, including imports inside function and class bodies. Each closure path is asserted to be bound either to its blob in the **durable** `review_content_manifest` or, where that manifest legitimately does not cover it, to a blob proven equal at `C` and at `base_commit`. The census is an ordered `{path, mode, blob, source}` list, `verifier_identity_id` is a sha256 over `{verifier_entry, verifier_source_root, verifier_census}` and **not** over `approved_review_content_id`, and **both** directions are asserted — a subject-only change (a state writer) leaves `verifier_identity_id` byte-identical, while a change to **any** executable verifier dependency, `scripts/workflow_state.py` and `scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` alike, rotates it. The first is the property that makes historical verifier replay possible at all; the second is the property that makes the closure load-bearing rather than decorative. **(c)** **(extended, revision 62, `GPT-R79-002`)** The executing verifier is asserted to be materialized from the **approved** blobs via `git cat-file` (with `--no-replace-objects`/`GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`, as everywhere else in this mechanism) into a scratch directory **preserving the module/package import layout**, and executed there in a **fresh interpreter process** — never in-process, so `sys.modules` cannot mask a leak — launched in Python's isolated mode (`-I`, which ignores `PYTHONPATH` and user site directories), with `sys.path` reset to the scratch module tree plus the standard library alone, so **the live repository is not a module source**. Omitting any required repository-local dependency is asserted to fail closed with an import error rather than resolving live, and that is asserted to hold even with `PYTHONPATH` pointed deliberately at the live `scripts/` directory. And, independently, the verifier content at `C` is asserted to be proven equal to those approved blobs per path, with the refusal naming the specific file. **(d)** `VERIFIER_UNAPPROVED` and `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE` are asserted to be non-satisfying classifications for **both** consumers, with the second reserved for a currency evaluation that could not complete — `UnclassifiedPathError` above all — so no exception from the classifier escapes the gate. **(e)** **(extended, revision 62, `GPT-R79-002`)** The verifier **entry point and source root** are asserted to be declared constants of the implementation rather than caller parameters, an empty derived closure is asserted to fail closed rather than to authorize vacuously, and the closure is asserted to be **derived rather than maintained**: adding a new repository-local import to the verifier without binding that dependency is asserted to fail closed, and a dynamic-import construct static closure cannot follow (`importlib.import_module`, a bare `__import__`, `exec`, a relative import) is asserted to classify `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE` rather than to be censused optimistically. That today's closure is exactly `scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` and `scripts/workflow_state.py` is asserted as a **recorded observation** of this repository, never as an input and never as a hard-coded pair — the same discipline item 357 applies to the twelve-writer count. **(f)** The ordering claim is asserted mechanically rather than assumed: `milestone_complete_gate_reachable` is confirmed `True` only for `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW`/`AWAITING_USER_ACCEPTANCE`, and the set of functions writing `AWAITING_FUNCTIONAL_REVIEW` is confirmed to be exactly `apply_technical_approval` and `promote_legacy_work_item` (the latter refusing via `LegacyAdoptionStaleApprovalError` on a changed protected path), so a technical approval provably precedes the completion gate on every reachable path and this binding adds no unreachable state → WF8b.

359. **(new, revision 61, `GPT-R78-001`, self-discovered while validating it; scope corrected from one prefix to two, revision 62, self-discovered while validating `GPT-R79-001`)** The **implementation-stage classification is total over this repository's own tracked content**, so `approval_is_current(stage="implementation")` returns a boolean rather than raising. Reproduced directly against the live repository before this item was written: it raises `UnclassifiedPathError("docs/ai-workflow/dry-run/WF8B_FINDING_continued_scope_remediation_no_nonterminal_return_path.md")`. **Revision 61 recorded that single path and thereby understated the gap.** Re-derived exhaustively this revision rather than from the first exception the classifier happened to raise: all 85 tracked paths changed in `base_commit..HEAD` were classified against the live declaration, and **four** fail, across **two** prefixes — the three `docs/ai-workflow/dry-run/` files and `docs/improvements/FUNCTIONAL_FEATURE_AUDIT.md`. Both prefixes are **plan**-stage `excluded_prefixes` entries that appear in neither implementation-stage set — an asymmetry that predates revision 61 and that item 358's verifier authority now makes load-bearing, since until it is closed the honest gate answer for this repository is `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE` (reproduced through the revision-62 authority chain itself, stress pass 3). A conformance asserts that every tracked path changed in `base_commit..HEAD` classifies under the implementation-stage declaration without raising, that **both** `docs/ai-workflow/dry-run/` and `docs/improvements/` in particular are classified (excluded, with their reasons stated: this work item's own throwaway dry-run execution evidence, and product improvement notes outside this process work item's scope, neither an implementation deliverable), that the enumeration is **exhaustive over all changed paths rather than stopping at the first exception** — the editing error that produced revision 61's undercount — and that the fail-closed `UnclassifiedPathError` discipline itself is **not** weakened to a default in the process. The declaration edit is implementation-stage protected by its own exact path, so it correctly stales `technical_approval` and lands through the ordinary implementation-review round rather than being applied silently — which is why this is an implementation obligation and not a plan-revision edit → WF8b.

360. **(new, revision 62, `GPT-R79-001`)** The completion-obligation gate's technical-approval authority is **durable Git provenance**, and the ways it can be forged or faked are enumerated and refused rather than reasoned about. **(a)** The authority chain is asserted in order: recompute the implementation-stage identity at the pinned `C`; discover the `Workflow-Technical-Approval` commit carrying **that recomputed identity** for the obligation owner; require it reachable, an ancestor of `C`, and unambiguous; read `technical_approval` from the `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` that commit committed; validate that durable record on its own terms; require any live copy and the live `base_commit` to agree with it; derive the verifier census from it; execute; derive the verdict. **(b)** The **search key** is asserted to be the recomputed identity and never a record field, which is the structural reason a fabricated record is irrelevant rather than merely insufficient; a test that mutates only the live record is asserted not to change which commit is discovered. **(c)** Every fail-closed direction is exercised individually and named in the refusal — absent approval commit, unreachable/foreign-branch commit, ambiguous commits surviving the first-parent tie-break, malformed or missing committed record, `status != "CURRENT"` durably, durable `approved_review_content_id` not the recomputed identity, null/malformed `reviewed_content_commit`, empty durable manifest, absent live record, live/durable divergence on any authority-bearing field, live `base_commit` divergence, and an approval trailer naming another work item. **(d)** The **non**-refusal directions are asserted with equal weight, because a gate that only ever refuses is not a gate: commits touching only implementation-stage **excluded** paths after the approval keep it usable and leave `verifier_identity_id` unchanged; repairing a live/durable divergence restores authorization; and a fresh implementation review plus a new durable approval of the exact changed content makes a previously refused repository eligible again. **(e)** The mechanism is asserted to introduce **no new approval format and no parallel provenance system**: the discovery, ancestry and ambiguity semantics are asserted to be the existing `discover_approval_commits`/`_is_ancestor` ones, shared with plan-approval provenance, and the `AmbiguousApprovalTrailerError` is asserted to be **caught and classified**, never to escape the gate. **(f)** The durable approval commit's own SHA is asserted to be what `completion_obligations_accepted` records as `technical_approval_commit`, distinct from the record's `reviewed_content_commit`, so a later audit can name the approval **event** and not merely the content it approved → WF8b.

361. **(new, revision 62, `GPT-R79-002`)** The recorded verifier is an **execution-complete repository-local dependency closure**, and its completeness is a mechanically checked property rather than a maintained list. **(a)** The closure is asserted to be **derived**, by static `ast` import analysis over the blobs at the pinned commit, seeded at the declared verifier entry point and transitively following tracked modules and packages on the declared verifier source root; the derived result for this repository is asserted to be exactly `scripts/workflow_fingerprint.py` and `scripts/workflow_state.py`, **as an observation**. **(b)** Imports inside function and class bodies are asserted to be followed, so a lazily imported dependency cannot escape the census. **(c)** Constructs static closure cannot follow are asserted to **fail closed**, not to be skipped: `importlib.import_module(...)`, a bare `__import__(...)`, `exec(...)` and relative imports each classify `VERIFIER_UNRESOLVABLE`, and today's two modules are asserted to contain none of them. **(d)** Package dependencies are asserted to contribute their whole tracked subtree and to be materialized preserving import layout, with the package's absence from the census asserted to fail closed. **(e)** Isolated execution is asserted to be the backstop that makes (a) checked rather than assumed: the census is materialized to a scratch tree and executed in a **fresh interpreter process** in isolated mode with `sys.path` reset to that tree plus the standard library, and the process asserts **from inside itself** that no loaded module resolves to the live repository. **(f)** Omitting any required dependency is asserted to fail closed with an import error rather than resolving live, asserted to still hold with `PYTHONPATH` pointed at the live `scripts/` directory, and a live module of the same name is asserted **not** to win over the recorded one. **(g)** Identity rotation is asserted in both directions: changing **any** executable verifier dependency rotates `verifier_identity_id`, while changing only a state writer leaves it byte-identical. **(h)** Census binding is asserted to handle the legitimate case the manifest cannot cover: where the durable `review_content_manifest` covers a closure path the blob at `C` must equal the approved one, and where it does not the path must be proven byte-identical at `C` and at `base_commit`, with each entry recording which source bound it — the direct regression test for `R62-S3-001`, where requiring manifest coverage unconditionally was reproduced permanently refusing a repository whose dependency had simply not changed since `base_commit`. **(i)** Historical replay is asserted to execute the recorded closure after arbitrary later history, including both live verifier modules rewritten to raise and then deleted outright; a planted `git replace` ref over a recorded blob is asserted to be defeated by `--no-replace-objects`/`GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1`; and a genuinely unreachable recorded blob is asserted to classify `REPLAY_UNRESOLVABLE` rather than to fall back to current code → WF8b.
362. **(new, revision 63, `WF8B-S14-001`)** The defect itself is a standing regression test, not only a fixed bug. **(a)** Against a real two-worktree fixture where worktree A holds a checkpoint `IN_PROGRESS` with the transition **uncommitted**, worktree B's full step-1 procedure is asserted to refuse rather than to select that checkpoint as a fresh start — and the pre-fix procedure is asserted, in the same fixture, to fresh-start it, so the test proves the fixture reproduces the defect rather than merely passing. **(b)** B's refusal is asserted to leave every authoritative byte unchanged: A's `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, A's `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json`, A's dirty working files, both worktrees' `HEAD`s, both `git status` outputs, B's own `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`, and the claim record — byte-compared, not inspected. **(c)** B is asserted never to have required a copy of A's `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`: B's copy is asserted byte-identical to its own committed bytes throughout. **(d)** The same refusal is asserted from a third worktree, from a worktree checked out at an **older** commit than the claim, and from a linked worktree nested inside the primary checkout (this repository's own layout). **(e)** A **committed** `IN_PROGRESS` marker is asserted to have been refused even by the pre-fix procedure, which is the property that scopes this contract to the uncommitted transition `/milestone-implement` writes and excludes the trailer-derived bootstrap driver → WF8b.
363. **(new, revision 63, `WF8B-S14-001`)** Acquisition and release ordering are asserted **with control arms**, because an ordering claim no test can fail is not a contract. **(a)** Claim-before-state: a crash between the two step-1d writes is asserted to leave the claim behind and to keep a foreign worktree refused; the **state-first** arm is asserted to let the foreign worktree fresh-start, proving the ordering load-bearing. **(b)** Release-after-durable-completion: releasing after the checkpoint commit is asserted to drop the claim only once `committed_checkpoint_status(...) == "COMPLETE"`; the **release-before-commit** arm is asserted to hand the work item to another worktree while the completion is still uncommitted. **(c)** A release that cannot complete is asserted to raise a typed ownership error with a defined recovery, never a bare `OSError`, and the next invocation from the same worktree is asserted to self-heal the leaked claim — because, and only because, the completion is durable. **(d)** **(amended in place, revision 64, `GPT-R81-003`)** Every one of `/milestone-implement`'s outcomes is asserted to name the checkpoint id it applies to, and the assertion is made by running the **real** step-1 procedure to the point of mutation rather than by inspecting a helper's return value: a `CONTINUE_CLAIM` or durable-release outcome reached while selection returns `None` is asserted to resolve to the terminal `NO_CHECKPOINT` outcome, to be unable to reach step 1d at all, to leave the state file byte-identical, and to leave the work item at the same post-checkpoint boundary the command's existing no-checkpoint path reaches; the non-final case is asserted separately to release checkpoint X and return a concrete next checkpoint Y that step 1d then claims and writes. **(extended in place, revision 67, `OPUS-R84-001`; rewritten in place, revision 68, `OPUS-R85-001`, after the mechanism the revision-67 wording assumed was withdrawn — the discipline is unchanged, what it is applied to is not)** The same real-caller discipline is required of step 1c's **single** proof of origination and of step 1d's ordering. `verify_dirty_resume_safety` is asserted **through the real step-1 procedure** to run on every contended path — claim absent, foreign or self-owned alike, adoption included — and to refuse before any authoritative mutation on each of them. A worktree whose ownership key matches the claim but whose **worktree instance does not** is asserted refused through that same caller, in both path-reuse constructions, with the post-refusal `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` asserted byte-identical and the claim record asserted untouched; the revision-67 resolver is carried as the live control arm that admits it and mutates, so the assertion fails if the withdrawal is reverted. And step 1d's identity-before-claim ordering is asserted the same way: the crash window it opens is asserted to always carry this worktree's identity record, so `CONTINUE_CLAIM` is reachable without relaxing anything, with the **claim-first** ordering carried as the control arm that reproduces the lockout. **(extended in place, revision 69, `OPUS-R86-001`)** The same real-caller discipline is required of adoption's own origination test, which is a *second* proof rather than a restatement of the first: adoption is asserted, through the real step-1 caller in a real two-worktree fixture, to refuse a checkpoint whose `IN_PROGRESS` is present in the origination reference and to admit one whose `IN_PROGRESS` is not, with the **unguarded** adoption carried as the live control arm that admits a worktree holding none of the originator's work — so the assertion fails if the guard is reverted, exactly as (a) and (b) require of the other two orderings. **(extended in place, revision 70, `OPUS-R87-001`/`-002`)** The same real-caller discipline is required of the *reference* the test is evaluated against, which revision 69 left selectable by the worktree being tested: the reference is asserted to be derived from every commit reachable from **every ref**, asserted unchanged by every ref operation the adopting worktree can perform on its own refs (`git reset --soft`/`--mixed`, `git checkout <commit> -- <path>`, `git cherry-pick -n`, `git stash pop`), and asserted to still admit an interrupted checkpoint whose transition is committed nowhere — with revision 69's `HEAD`-relative reference carried as the live control arm that admits under each of those operations and locks the true originator out. The read is asserted **fail-closed** over its own total partition, with the `return None`-on-undecidable behaviour carried as the control arm that admits, and the ordering asserted a second time at **publication** and not only at evidence time → WF8b.
364. **(new, revision 63, `WF8B-S14-001`)** The crash windows each have a defined, asserted outcome, and none of them locks out the legitimate owner — **and that preamble is asserted in the state every work item actually starts in, not only in states a worktree reaches after it has already completed a checkpoint** (corrected, revision 67, `OPUS-R84-001`: through revision 66 this item was satisfiable only because no arm had ever been run against a worktree with no prior `WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` entry for the work item, which is precisely the state in which the lockout occurred; the same discipline `OPUS-R82-002` and `OPUS-R83-002` established for items 372(f) and 365(c), where an obligation was rewritten to assert what the mechanism actually does rather than what it was hoped to do). **(a)** Claim published, `IN_PROGRESS` state not yet written: the owner is asserted to **continue its own acquisition**, to complete the interrupted state write, and to leave the original claim record intact rather than republishing it; a foreign worktree is asserted still refused throughout that window. **(a) is asserted for a brand-new work item in a worktree that has completed no checkpoint anywhere** — so nothing about the work item is inherited from any other worktree — **by running the real step-1 procedure to the point of mutation**, never by inspecting a helper's return value, with **the claim-first 1d ordering carried as a live control arm** that is asserted to lock the owner out, so the assertion fails if the correction is reverted (**rewritten in place, revision 68, `OPUS-R85-001`**: through revision 67 this arm required the owner to be admitted while holding *no* identity record, which is exactly the state a replacement worktree at the holder's path presents; the property being asserted is the same — the legitimate owner is never locked out of its own claim — but it is now asserted of the ordering that makes the record present, not of a relaxation that stops requiring it). **The two path-reuse constructions are asserted as first-class arms**: (i) the holder relocated by `git worktree move` and a different worktree created at the vacated path, and (ii) the holder removed and recreated at the same path **with the same name**, which is additionally asserted to reuse the dead holder's admin directory — so the assertion also records that binding the check to `worktree_git_dir` would not close it. In both, the replacement is asserted refused through the real caller with zero authoritative mutation, and **the revision-67 resolver is carried as the live control arm** that admits it, mutates state, and does so under the original holder's unrotated `owner_token`. **A fencing assertion accompanies them**: no path may leave two worktrees presenting the same `owner_token` for one claim without a recorded rotation — `takeover_count` incremented, the displaced token appended, `taken_over_from` recorded — and the replacement's only sanctioned route in is asserted to be the explicit takeover, which is asserted to satisfy all three. **A corrupt-`WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json` arm is asserted for both flavours** — unparseable bytes, and parseable but schema-invalid — asserting that step 1c refuses with the declared `CorruptJsonError` **before** any `WORKFLOW_STATE.json` write, with the revision-67 shape carried as the control arm that mutates first and then fails, in the schema-invalid case with an undeclared `TypeError`; and asserting that the corrupt record cannot survive a successful checkpoint start unreported, with the control arm's silent `RESUME`-over-it behaviour carried as the shape the assertion must fail if it holds. Four further arms make the property total. **No hand repair is required**: in that same state the work item is asserted recoverable without deleting or editing any file by hand, and `clear_malformed_guard` and `recover_abandoned_destructive_guard` are each asserted to refuse as not applicable (there is no guard). **The state a lost identity record leaves behind is asserted to have exactly one documented exit** (**rewritten in place, revision 68, `OPUS-R85-001`**; through revision 67 this sub-clause asserted that a takeover by the *owning* worktree rotates the claim and still does not clear the state, which was true of a takeover that established nothing and is the incompleteness revision 68 closes): the explicit takeover is asserted to rotate the claim **and** to establish the taking worktree's own identity record, so the work item is workable immediately afterwards through the real step-1 caller, with the revision-67 takeover — which established nothing — carried as the control arm that leaves the refusal standing. **The refusal is not weakened**: in the identical state a *foreign* worktree is asserted still refused with `WorktreeIdentityMissingError`/`WorktreeIdentityMismatchError` as applicable, performing zero authoritative mutation and leaving no guard residue, so `S14a`/`S14b` both remain distinguishable and remain the classes a foreign worktree sees **in the states `S14` is written against** — with the one further foreign case asserted separately rather than left implied (**added, revision 68, `OPUS-R85-001`**): a foreign worktree carrying a valid identity record of its own *with* an entry for this work item, reachable only for a worktree that has itself held this claim, is asserted to pass `verify_dirty_resume_safety` and to be refused one line later by the foreign-claim row with `CheckpointOwnedByOtherWorktreeError`, still before any mutation, so the enumeration is asserted at the strength it actually has. **Both `WorktreeIdentityMissingError` branches are asserted separately** — the missing-file case and the file-exists-but-carries-no-entry-for-this-work-item case — since only the second is reachable for a worktree that has already worked on a *different* work item, and the two are distinct code paths in `verify_dirty_resume_safety`. **Diagnosis is asserted**: any refusal raised while a decidable claim is present is asserted to carry the ownership evidence and to name the escape that applies, for a self-owned claim as well as a foreign one, so no refusal can again describe resuming an `IN_PROGRESS` checkpoint that does not exist while naming no way out. **(b)** `IN_PROGRESS` written but the checkpoint not committed — the ordinary interrupted case — is asserted to resume for the owner and refuse for everyone else. **(c)** Checkpoint committed but the claim not released is asserted to auto-release on the next invocation from the owning worktree, and **only** when the completion is `COMPLETE` in the state committed at `HEAD`; the same fixture with the completion present only in the working tree is asserted to refuse instead. **(d)** Two work items with interleaved `IN_PROGRESS` work are asserted not to disturb each other's claim in any of these windows, preserving `OPUS-R10-008` → WF8b.
365. **(new, revision 63, `WF8B-S14-001`)** The record's integrity properties are asserted against hostile and accidental inputs. **(a)** Two genuinely concurrent OS processes claiming the same work item are asserted to produce exactly one winner and one `CheckpointOwnedByOtherWorktreeError`, with the surviving record complete and parseable; a deliberately injected stale pre-read is asserted not to overwrite the winner. **(b)** A partially written record is asserted **not producible by this writer** — publication is a same-directory temp file plus `os.link` — and no staging temp file is asserted to survive a successful publication. **(c)** A record corrupted by anything else (torn, wrong `schema_version`, wrong `work_item_id`, unparseable) is asserted to fail closed for **every** worktree including the owner, never to be read as "unclaimed", and to be recoverable **only** by an explicit, observation-bound operation — **which one depending on the guard, asserted against the guard-held case and not only the guard-free one** (corrected, revision 66, `OPUS-R83-002`: through revision 65 this item named the explicit takeover unconditionally, which is true only when no `"destructive"` guard is held and the record is byte-readable, so the conjunction that had no exit at all could satisfy this item while being unrecoverable). 366. **(new, revision 63, `WF8B-S14-001`)** No claim is released on an assumption, and the takeover is the only exception. **(a)** A claim whose holder worktree has been **deleted** is asserted still not released automatically — no age, heartbeat, liveness probe or `claimed_at` comparison is asserted to appear anywhere in the resolution path. **(b)** `takeover_evidence` is asserted to **report rather than conclude**: the claim record, whether the holder's recorded path still exists, and whether a currently registered worktree still corresponds to it, matched on the stable `worktree_git_dir` as well as the recorded path — so a **live** holder is asserted reported as live rather than shown as a false orphan, and a **relocated** holder (`git worktree move`) is asserted distinguishable from a deleted one. **(c)** Takeover is asserted refused without its literal authorization naming both work item and checkpoint — absent, empty, truthy-but-wrong, and naming a different checkpoint are each asserted individually — with the existing claim asserted untouched after every refusal. **(d)** An authorized takeover is asserted to publish by **atomic replace**, so a takeover that fails to publish leaves the previous claim in force rather than leaving the work item unclaimed; to record the displaced holder in `taken_over_from`; and to write **no** authoritative workflow state. **(e)** Takeover is asserted unreachable from `/milestone-implement` on every path → WF8b.

369. **(new, revision 64, `GPT-R81-002`)** Takeover authorization is bound to the exact claim the human reviewed. **(a)** An authorization naming checkpoint X while the installed claim holds Y is asserted refused, with the revision-63 literal asserted — as a control arm — to have displaced exactly that claim. **(b)** A claim that changes between the evidence presentation and the takeover is asserted to produce a stale-evidence refusal with **zero** mutation, the surviving claim byte-compared. **(c)** The same authorization is asserted non-replayable against the claim its own rotation produced. **(d)** `taken_over_from` is asserted to describe the record **atomically** displaced — its `claim_observation_id` asserted equal to the digest of the bytes present at rotation and unequal to an earlier read's — together with the displaced `owner_token` and `checkpoint_id`, and the `takeover_count`/`previous_owner_tokens` chain. **(e)** The unreadable/corrupt-record recovery is asserted to carry an equally explicit observation binding rather than a reusable generic authorization: a generic literal is asserted refused, an authorization for one corrupt record is asserted not to carry over to a different one, and the correctly bound literal is asserted to recover it and to record the recovery. **(f)** The `"absent"` observation is asserted to be an observation like any other, so authorizing a takeover of "no claim" is asserted not to survive somebody publishing one in the meantime → WF8b.

**Direction semantics of every edge, restated precisely** (revision 93, `OPUS-R117-007`): `X → Y` means a thread that already holds `X` goes on to acquire `Y` — for `(1)→(2)`, `(5)→(2)` and `(5)→(3)`, `X` is a **guard whose acquire/release bracket is the outer, long-lived window**: `plan_approval_guarded_mutation`/`owner_mutation` acquire the guard, run the caller's whole mutation inside that open window, and release it only at the end, so a `WORKFLOW_STATE.json`/identity-document write nested anywhere inside that window is genuinely reached while the guard is still held. `(7)→(1)` and `(6)→(5)` are the opposite shape, not the same one restated: `(7)`/`(6)` are single-purpose guardlocks whose *entire* reason to exist is to bracket one create-or-remove operation on their own paired lease — `acquire_plan_approval_guard`/`acquire_guard` open `(7)`/`(6)` first and publish `(1)`/`(5)` inside that open window (both the ordinary path and the reclaim branch); `release_plan_approval_guard`/`release_guard` open `(7)`/`(6)` first and remove `(1)`/`(5)` inside that same open window. In both directions the guardlock's critical section is the one that is open when the lease is touched, never the reverse, which is why revision 91's `(1)→(7)` and revision 76's `(5)→(6)` had the direction backwards: they read the lease as the long-lived container because that is its role everywhere *else* in this graph, but relative to its own guardlock specifically, the guardlock is the container, and it closes — releasing `(7)`/`(6)` — long before the lease's own later, separately-acquired nested operations (`(1)→(2)`, `(5)→(2)`, `(5)→(3)`) ever run. This is also why the correction does not make `(6)`/`(7)` transitively reach `(2)`/`(3)`: `(6)`/`(7)`'s own critical section has already closed by the time `(5)`/`(1)` goes on, later and separately, to nest those — the four "per-primitive properties" bullets below state this as the literal, checked fact it is (never held simultaneously with `(2)`), not as a consequence of graph reachability, since a bare transitive-closure reading of `(6)→(5)→(2)` would wrongly suggest otherwise. `(8)→(5)` is the long-lived-container shape, not the guardlock shape, and the discriminator is *why* `(6)`/`(7)` get the guardlock reading and `(5)` does not: `(6)`/`(7)` exist *for no other reason* than to bracket one create-or-remove instant of their own paired lease, so every time either is entered it is, by construction, to touch that lease and nothing else. `(5)` is not a dedicated bracketing lock for `(8)` — it is `D-Checkpoint-Ownership`'s general-purpose mutation guard, acquired and released independently, for unrelated reasons, at both step 1d (the fresh-claim state write) and step 1f (the commit-and-release), and `(8)` is present, unremoved, across both: `claim_checkpoint` creates it *unguarded*, before any guard exists (`D-Checkpoint-Ownership`'s own "claim acquisition itself needs no guard"), and it is not removed until `release_checkpoint`, at the far end of step 1f. So `(8)` is genuinely the outer, longer-lived object with respect to `(5)` — two *separate*, independently-triggered `(5)` acquisitions nest inside `(8)`'s one lifetime, the identical relationship `(5)` itself has to `(2)`/`(3)` — and `(8)`'s own removal, which happens to be the second of those two nested `(5)` windows, does not change which object is outer any more than `(5)`'s own eventual release changes whether `(2)`/`(3)` nest inside it. Stated from `(8)`'s side, consistently with how `(5)→(2)`/`(5)→(3)` are stated from `(5)`'s side and not `(2)`'s/`(3)`'s. **`(8)→(2)` and `(8)→(3)`, added revision 95, `OPUS-R119-001`, are the identical long-lived-container shape one level further out**: at step 1d, `(8)` is genuinely the outer object not only with respect to `(5)` but with respect to `(2)`/`(3)` too, since `(8)` is published *before* `owner_mutation` opens at all — the state write and the identity refresh that nest inside that window are reached while `(8)` has already been held for longer, the same relationship `(5)` itself has to `(2)`/`(3)`, one containment level further out; `(8)→(2)` recurs at step 1f for the identical reason `(8)→(5)`/`(8)→(6)` do. **`(6)→(8)` and `(8)→(6)`, added revision 94, `OPUS-R118-001`/`-002`, are each the same shape as an edge already derived above, not a new shape**: `(6)→(8)` is the guardlock shape — `adopt_claim` opens `(6)` first and publishes `(8)` inside that window, exactly as `acquire_guard` opens `(6)` first and publishes `(5)` inside it for `(6)→(5)`, so `(6)`'s critical section closes — releasing `(6)` — before `(8)` goes on, separately and later, to nest anything else, the identical guarantee `(6)→(5)` already has. `(8)→(6)` is the long-lived-container shape `(8)→(5)` already has, restated at `(6)` instead of `(5)`: `owner_mutation`'s `acquire_guard` opens `(6)` while `(8)` is durably published and unremoved, so `(8)` is genuinely the outer object with respect to `(6)` the same way it already is with respect to `(5)`. Neither derivation is new; what is new is that `(6)` is the target of one and the source of the other, which is precisely the `(6)↔(8)` two-cycle "Blocking vs. non-blocking edges" (above, in "The complete global partial order") resolves by classifying `(6)→(8)`'s target `(8)` as non-blocking (`os.link`, never a wait) and `(8)→(6)`'s target `(6)` as blocking (`fcntl.flock`, a real wait) — the same two edges, two different kinds, never a contradiction and never an ad-hoc exception. **(Strengthened from a subset check to an equality, revision 77, `OPUS-R94-002`.)** Revision 76 asserted only that the four recorded edges *hold*, which a new edge cannot contradict: an implementation that made `write_worktree_identity` reachable from inside the plan-approval transaction's guard would add `(1)→(3)` — acyclic, contradicting no recorded edge, and outside `(4)`'s negative — and pass, leaving the single ordering site documenting five of six real edges. That is the third recurrence of the class of error `OPUS-R92-004` and `OPUS-R93-002` each found once, so the arm is stated at the strength that closes it rather than at the strength that merely records today's answer. Deriving the set from acquisitions rather than comparing a hand-maintained list is forced by the control arms and is the right design in any case — a hand-maintained list is the thing that went stale twice.
